318: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits do not repeat along the marked diagonal. The marked diagonal reflects odd/even parity on each side. (Eg if r6c2 is odd then r2c6 must also be odd.) Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Each purple line contains a set of consecutive, non-repeating digits.
319: Normal sudoku rules apply. Blue dots join cells with a difference equal to the grey central digit of their box. (For example, if r2c5=4 then r2c4 - r3c4 = ± 4)
320: Normal sudoku rules apply. Find the path of the marble run (from R1C1 to the hole in R9C1). The marble can only drop down or go sideways. It cannot visit a cell more than once. Digits in cages sum to the given total. Cells on the marble's path do not contribute to the sum. No digits can repeat in a cage.
321: Normal sudoku rules apply. You must find the path of the marble run (from R1C1 to R9C9). The marble can only drop down or go sideways. It cannot visit a cell more than once. Digits in cages sum to the given total. Cells on the marble's path do not contribute to the sum. No digits can repeat in cages.
322: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Odd/Even parity is reflected across the purple mirror. eg if r6c2 is odd, r2c6 must also be odd.
323: Digits along the lines add up to the number in the circles.
324: Blacken some white cells and then draw a single closed loop (without intersections or crossings) through all remaining white cells. Blackened cells cannot share an edge with each other. Some cells are outlined and in gray and cannot be part of the loop. Numbered arrows in such cells indicate the total number of blackened cells that exist in that direction of the grid.
325: Draw a single closed loop passing through some empty cells in the grid. The grid contains some bordered/coloured cells that cannot be part of the loop. Black cells must be outside the loop. White bordered cells must be inside the loop. Numbers and arrows refer to the total sum of the lengths of the loop segments in the given direction.
326: Connect dots with lines to make a single loop. A number shows how many loop lines border that cell.
327: Normal sudoku rules apply. In addition, there are some special CTC rules in this puzzle: There are 7 pairs of variants in this sudoku, totalling to 14 different rules. For each pair, one area will follow one variant and the other area will follow the other variant. It is up to the solver to determine which variant gets used where. Throughout there will be no converse rules like “all possible dots are given” etc.
328: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the number given in the top left of the cage. Digits cannot repeat in a cage. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. Digits can repeat along these diagonals. One of the digits from 1-9 is a joker – wherever it appears in the grid, it can count as any digit from 1-9 for cage and diagonal sums, and it can be DIFFERENT for both – but (as in normal killer sudoku) it can only appear once in each cage.
329: Normal sudoku rules apply except that the regions are irregular. Additionally, a snake has to be drawn into the grid. The head and tail of the snake are in the two cells with the grey circles. The snake may not touch itself orthogonally, but it can touch itself diagonally. In the correct solution, the cells without snake form exactly eight areas, one of each size from 1 to 8. Such an area of size n contains each digit from 1 to n exactly once.
330: Normal sudoku rules apply; for 1-8, each marked number N appears N cells away in either a horizontal or vertical direction (not both). 9’s obey the king’s move constraint, both as regards each other and marked 9’s.
331: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the clue in the top left of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage.
332: Place the letters A,B,D,H,I,M,P,R,Y and/or the digits they are assigned to in every row and column. (NOTE no 3x3 boxes!)The nine letters used in the puzzle represent a different number from 1-9. The letters outside the grid are all Skyscraper clues. ie each number represents the "height" of a skyscraper in that cell. Numbers outside the grid indicate the number of visible skyscrapers from the direction (where taller buildings obscure smaller buildings "behind" them). After substitution within the grid, the digits 2 and 6 are "stars", and cannot touch orthogonally or diagonally with other instances of themselves or each other. The numbers outside the grid give the number of cells between the stars in that row. Stars cannot be on cells with red squares. Red squares give a message in the finished grid. Grey Circles contain odd digits and grey squares contain even digits.
333: Normal Sudoku rules apply. Each digit inside the grid and its perimeter (rows 0&10 and columns 0&10) represents the height of the Skyscraper in that cell. Taller Skyscrapers hide shorter ones (and ones of the same size). The numbers beside diagonal lines give the number of Skyscraper clues seen in the corresponding directions in rows0&10 and columns 0&10 respectively and all the digits placed there give the number of Skyscrapers seen in the corresponding row or column inside the grid. A clue in a circle is the sum of the digits in the two cells on either side of the clue. [For the avoidance of doubt: the perimeter cells do not obey the rules of sudoku ie they can repeat. So eg along r10 it would be fine for digits to repeat.]
334: Normal sudoku rules apply. If two orthogonally adjacent cells sum to 10, there must be an X between them. If two orthogonally adjacent cells sum to 5, there must be a V between them. The digits in each circle must appear at least once in the four surrounding cells.
335: Enter a single digit from 1 to 9 into each white cell so that the sum of digits in each Across entry equals the value given to the left of the entry, and the sum of digits in each Down entry equals the value given above the entry. No digit may be repeated within a single entry.
336: Same as Kakuru (Prasana) but, additionally, some cells are shaded and the digits in these shaded cells also act as Kakuro clues for subsequent white cells (ie until the next grey cell, black cell or grid boundary). It is up to the solver to determine if the shaded cell digit is an across or a down clue and it could be both.
337: Normal sudoku rules apply. Numbers must not repeat in a killer cage, and the numbers in the cage must sum to the given total, BUT there is exactly one cage in the grid where the condition is broken (either the sum is incorrect, or digits are repeated, or both). It is up to the solver to find out which cage is lying. The purple lines in the grid are incomplete arrows. The digit on one end of the line is the sum of the other digits on the same line.
338: Normal sudoku rules apply. Every 5 in the grid must have a 1 directly above it or a 9 directly below it. It may have both, but it doesn't need both. A camel’s move in fairy chess is a jump of three squares horizontally and one square vertically or three squares vertically and one square horizontally. Any cell a camel’s move away from a camel cell has to contain a digit that is either consecutive or in a 2:1 ratio with the digit in the camel cell. There are exactly seven camel cells in the grid. Two of them are shown; the others are hidden. All the hidden camels are in odd-numbered boxes and contain the digit of the box that they live in. The 3x3 boxes are numbered in normal reading order.
339: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits do not repeat in cages. Adjacent cages share at least one edge. If adjacent cages have sums that are consecutive, there is a white dot between the cages. If adjacent cages have sums that are in a 1:2 ratio, there is a black dot between the cages.
340: Within the main 9x9 grid, normal sudoku rules apply. Numbers along an arrow must sum to the number in the circle. Shade cells within the main 9x9 grid so that the clues outside the grid in order equal the sums of the digits in contiguous blocks of shaded cells in that row/column. Blocks must be separated by at least one unshaded cell.
341: Fill some cells in the grid with the digits 1–9 such that no digit repeats in a row or column. Cells containing a circle, square, or arrow must have a digit in them. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in the circle. Gray squares contain even digits and gray circles contain odd digits. A region is a collection of orthogonally connected cells. A region of size n contains the digits 1 through n once each. Regions may not touch each other orthogonally, although they may touch each other diagonally.
342: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a circle appear at least once each in the four surrounding cells. Adjacent digits on a green line differ by at least 5. Any set of three sequential cells on an orange line contains a low digit (1-3), a middle digit (4-6), and a high digit (7-9). Digits on a purple line form a set of non-repeating consecutive digits (in any order).
343: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a circle appear at least once in the four surrounding cells. Adjacent digits on a green line differ by at least 5. Any set of three sequential cells on an orange line contains a low digit (123), a middle digit (456) and a high digit (789). Digits on a purple line form a set of non-repeating consecutive numbers (which can appear in any order).
344: Normal sudoku rules apply. Once in each row, column, and box, the Thing assimilates a number, thereby negating it (e.g. if the Thing is in R5C7 and the cell appears to contain a 3, its actual value is –3). Values on the blue line have the same sum in each 3x3 box the line is in. Values along a thermo increase from the bulb end. Adjacent values on a green line differ by 5 or more. Numbers in a circle appear once in the four surrounding cells; they may be genuine (positive) or they may be the Thing (negative). To successfully escape, you must travel from the now destroyed Outpost #31 (R2C2) to the helicopter (R8C8). Your path is one cell wide and may not go outside of Antarctica's boundary (blue line). The path which travels orthogonally may not contain nor be orthogonally adjacent to any of the Thing's cells. Adjacent values on the escape route differ by 5 or more.
345: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is covered mostly in darkness. Placing correct digits in cells will illuminate more of the grid. Cells are either wall or cave cells. Walls are orthogonally connected to the edge of the grid and the cave is one orthogonally connected area. A 2x2 area cannot be fully wall nor fully cave. White circles are cave cells and the value in a circle is the number of cave cells “seen” in that row and column, including the cell itself. Walls obstruct vision. A cage contains no repeated digits, and the values of the cave cells sum to the given total. Wall cells don’t count towards the sum. (Note: A cage’s clue doesn't necessarily appear in the uppermost nor leftmost cell.) A doubler appears exactly once in each row, column, and 3x3 box. For purposes of circles and cage sums, such cells’ digits are doubled in value. Each digit is doubled once.
346: There are five overlapping 6x6 grids. Within each grid, place the digits 1–6 once each in every row, column, and region. Clues outside the grids refer to the sum of the digits between two 1's in that row/column.
347: Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a loop (which never intersects with itself) through the centres of some cells. The loop moves from cell to cell orthogonally. Every cell in the grid is one of three types: fully inside the loop, fully outside the loop, or part of the loop. A 2x2 area cannot be entirely one cell type. A green circle is inside the loop, a blue circle is outside the loop, and a yellow circle is part of the loop. A digit placed in a circle is the number of cells of its own type that it “sees” horizontally and vertically, including itself. (Other cell types obstruct vision.) Cells inside the loop form one orthogonally connected area and cells outside the loop are orthogonally connected to the edge of the grid. Adjacent non-loop cells contain digits that differ by 5 or more.
348: Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a non-intersecting loop along some edges of the grid. Aliens are inside the loop and cacti are outside the loop. A digit in a white square indicates the number of that cell’s edges that are part of the loop. A digit in a white circle is inside the loop and indicates the number of cells inside the loop “seen” horizontally and vertically, including the circled cell itself. Cells outside the loop obstruct vision. The loop passes through a white dot in a straight line, then makes a 90-degree turn on one or both of the nearest cell corners along the loop. The loop makes a 90-degree turn on a black dot, and does not turn at the next opportunity in either direction. Diagonally adjacent cells joined by a white dot contain consecutive digits and by a black dot contain digits in a 1:2 ratio.
349: Fold the grid into a cube, and then fill each row with the digits 1-8. Cells separated by a white dot are consecutive, and cells separated by a black dot have a ratio of 1:2. All possibly dots are given, including between different faces of the cube.
350: Normal Sudoku rules apply. Arrows indicate the sum of digits along their respective diagonals. Digits can repeat on these diagonals. Identical digits cannot be in the same position in different 3x3 boxes. (Eg cells like r1c2 and r4c5 cannot contain the same digit as both occupy the same position in their 3x3 box).
351: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal (digits can repeat along these diagonals). Along thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb end.
352: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage.
353: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. Digits on blue lines must be strictly between the digits in the circles at either end.
354: Divide the grid into pentominos (orthogonally connected 5-cell regions). Cells on either side of a given border must belong to different pentominos. Two pentominos of the same shape (including rotations and reflections) cannot share an edge.
355: Normal sudoku rules apply. Circled numbers must appear in at least one of the four cells touching that circle. Small circles (without a number in them) link cells containing consecutive digits.
356: Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a single closed loop that travels orthogonally through the centres of some cells. The loop does not use any cell more than once and must travel through each dot. The two loop segments extending from both sides of a dot must be balanced ie the sum of the digits up to and including the digit in the cell containing the first turn must be the same. ALL possible dots are given.
357: Normal sudoku rules apply. A clue outside the grid shows the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. None of these individual clues is given in this puzzle but the sum of all the "?" clues together is 178.
358: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along grey "fast" thermometers must increase by at least 2 at a time starting from the bulb end. The large red ring is made up on 5 normal thermometers glued tip-to-bulb. ie travelling clockwise around it, digits must increase with no more than 5 exceptions.
359: Divide the grid into pentominoes, such that no two pentominoes of the same shape (including rotations and reflections) touch orthogonally. Clues outside the grid indicate the number of borders between pentominoes present in that row or column. [A pentomino is a set of 5 orthogonally-connected cells.]
360: Normal sudoku rules apply. Considering all rows and columns as 9-digit numbers read from the direction of the clue and ranked from lowest (1) to highest (36), a clue represents where in the ranking that row/column lies.
361: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a blue line sum to the same value in each 3x3 box the line passes through. Different lines may have different sums. eg r1c2 + r2c2 + r3c2 = r4c3 + r5c3 + r6c3 = r7c2 + r8c2 + r9c2. Cells separated by a black dot contain digits in a 1:2 ratio (ie one digit must be double the other). Cells separated by a white dot must contain consecutive digits. Not all dots are given.
362: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a black dot contain digits with a 1:2 ratio (ie one digit is double the other). Cells separated by a white dot must contain consecutive digits. Not all dots are given. The grey squares contain even digits. Digits along a blue line sum to the same value in each 3x3 box the line passes through.
363: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells connected by a V must sum to either 5 or 15. Cells connected by an X must sum to either 10 or 15. Not all possible Vs and Xs are given. Cages are psycho look-and-say cages. In these cages, the digits in the cage point to boxes in the grid, and provide a referred cell which is in the same position in both boxes. The number in the top left corner should be read as a look-and-say number, which says the number of times a digit appears in the cells referenced by that cage (eg, a '23' clue means there are two 3s in the referenced cells). Digits placed within cages do NOT count towards the look-and-say total unless they are self-referencing, and digits may NOT repeat in cages. For example, if r1c5 were a 4 and r2c5 were a 5, then exactly one of the referenced cells in box 4 or box 5 (r4c2 or r5c5, respectively) would need to contain a 2 to satisfy the look-and-say clue of '12' (ie, one 2 in the referred cells).
364: Normal sudoku rules apply. Also the numbers outside the grid show the sum of the first X numbers from that direction where the Xth number is the first to change parity (odd/even). Also, each line shown has unique content and sums to 23.
365: Normal sudoku rules apply and on the marked blue diagonal no digit may repeat. The digits along an arrow sum either to the number in the circle (x) or to the square of that number (x times x). (The circled digit does not contribute to the sum in either case).
366: Normal sudoku rules apply. Normal killer sudoku rules apply (ie digits in cages must sum to the clue given in the top left corner of the cage; digits cannot repeat within a cage.)
367: Normal sudoku rules apply, and the two lines in the grid are palindromes (on which the same sequence of numbers runs both ways along the line). Outside the grid are Parity Party clues, which show the sum of the digits seen from that direction up to and including the first change of parity (odd/even).
368: Normal sudoku rules apply. The digits along an arrow sum either to the number in the circle (x) or to the square of that number (x times x). The circled digit does not contribute to its own sum. There are also 3 instances of paired cells in a circle (pill). Here, the two cells should be read as a two digit number, reading from left to right.
369: Normal Sudoku rules apply. Where a small square appears between cells in a row, the difference between those cells is the digit in the first cell in the row. Where a small square appears between cells in a column, the difference between those cells is the digit in the first cell in the column. All possible small squares are marked.
370: Normal sudoku rules apply, and any two cells directly connected by a line must have a difference of at least 5.
371: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cages may not include repeated digits. Each cage should be treated as a “building” with a height equal to the sum of the digits in the cage. (Eg a cage containing the digits 2, 6 & 8 would equate to a building of height 16.) Cells outside of cages are completely ignored for the purposes of the clues outside the grid. The clues outside the grid give the number of buildings that can be "seen" along that row or column, whereby (1) taller buildings obscure shorter buildings and (2) in a row/column with a clue outside the grid, there can never be two buildings of the same height. Note that a row/column without a clue does not necessarily have repeated building heights but may do.
372: Normal sudoku rules apply. The reddish kitty on the left is made of two German Whispers lines. Ie Each successive pair of digits on a line must be at least 5 apart, e.g. 839. The hazy grey kitty on the right (red kitty's Astral Projection :tm: ) is made of two palindrome lines. They read the same backward as forward, e.g., 12321. The circled digits are quadruples, meaning that the four cells surrounding the circle must contain the given digit or digits at least once.
373: Normal sudoku rules apply. A clue outside the grid shows the sum of the digits sandwiched between the 1 and the 9 in that row/column. Digits along an arrow (which may repeat) average exactly to the digit in the attached circle.
374: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits do not repeat in cages, which show their sums. A clue outside the grid show the sum of the indicated diagonal, which may include repeated digits.
375: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages do not include repeat digits, and sum to the indicated total. Digits along indicated diagonals must add to the indicated total. Repeats are permitted along such diagonals. Each row, column, and 3x3 box contains exactly one 'negator' cell. Digits in these cells must be subtracted, rather than added, to achieve the given cage or diagonal totals. The nine 'negator' cells are also a set of the digits 1-9.
376: Normal sudoku rules apply. The cell with the grey circle must contain an odd digit. Every single cage in the grid must contain digits summing to an odd number. Arrows with numbers outside the grid give the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. All other arrows point to diagonals that, although unclued, also sum to an odd number.
377: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on an arrow can repeat, and sum to the number in the circle. The grey line is a palindrome, reading the same either way. The black dot joins two digits with a 1:2 ratio. Digits in grey cells are larger than their orthogonal neighbours. Prime numbers can never be orthogonal neighbours.
378: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on a line must be between the numbers in the circles of that line. Also each line acts as an arrow, so that the number in one circle is the sum of all the other digits on the line, including the other circle.
379: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each grey dot represents one of the following 4 constraints: a White Dot connects two consecutive digits; a Black Dot connects two digits with a ratio of 1:2; a V connects two digits that sum to 5; an X connects two digits that sum to 10. If a cell is connected to different cells via multiple grey dots, each such grey dot must have a different property in terms of which constraint it represents. Every single grey dot represents exactly one constraint (eg 2 and 3 cannot be connected via a grey dot, since the grey dot would be a valid white dot and a valid V clue). Not all possible dots are given.
380: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a purple line must be a set of consecutive, non-repeating digits, in any order. Clues outside the grid give the multiplication of the box sums that the diagonal passes through.
381: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each of the following clue types has exactly one liar in the puzzle: Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow’s circle; adjacent digits separated by a black dot have a ratio of 1:2; cells with a grey square contain even digits; adjacent digits along a green line have a difference of at least 5; clues outside the grid indicate the digit which has to be placed in the Nth cell in the corresponding direction, where N is the digit placed in the first cell in that direction; cells with a grey circle contain odd digits; digits in a white circle must appear in at least one of the four surrounding cells (for this clue type to be correct, all digits in the circle must satisfy this condition); cells along a purple line must be a set of consecutive digits; digits along a thermometer must increase from the bulb end; cells separated by a V must contain digits summing to 5; cells connected by a white dot have to contain consecutive digits; and cells separated by an X must contain digits summing to 10.
382: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle.
383: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage.
384: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a line must have values between the digits on the circled ends of that line. Digits in a white circle must appear in at least one of the cells touching that circle.
385: Normal sudoku rules apply. All friendly cells in the grid form a single one-cell-wide orthogonally-connected snake, which cannot touch itself, even diagonally (a cell is 'friendly' if it has a value identical to its row-, column- or box-number). Cells connected by a dot are both friendly; if they are the same 'type' of friendly (that is, both match the row-number, both match the column-number, or both match the box-number) the dot is white, and otherwise the dot is grey.
386: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a V contain digits summing to 5. Cells separated by an X contain digits summing to 10. All possible Vs and Xs are given.
387: Normal sudoku rules apply. In addition, draw a one-cell-wide snake (ie a non looping or branching string of orthogonally connected cells with two ends - head and tail) that may not touch itself orthogonally such that: the snake divides the rest of the grid into orthogonally connected regions, each of which sums to the same total and contains no repeated digits; and, all given digits belong to the snake and may not decrease when read along the snake from head to tail.
388: Normal Sudoku rules apply. Battlefield rules apply: Consider the first X cells and the last Y cells of a row or column where X is the number in the first cell and Y is the number in the last cell. A clue outside the grid gives the sum of the digits where these groups overlap, or the sum of the digits in the gap between the groups if they don't overlap.
389: Normal sudoku rules apply. Normal killer sudoku rules apply (ie digits in a cage must sum to the small clue given in the top left corner of the cage. Digits may not repeat within a cage.)
390: Normal sudoku rules apply. However, every clue is lying to you! The thermometer bulb is not where it says it is (but is still on the thermo, and each thermo cannot contain a repeated digit). Killer cages don't sum to the number in the corner. Little killer arrows do not give the sum of cells on their diagonal. X and V clues mean the adjoining cells don't add to 10 or 5 respectively. The palindrome line does not contain a palindrome. Black kropki dots mean neither adjoining cell is half of the other. Maximum cells (in blue) are not greater than all four adjacent cells.; Cells touching “quadruple circles” do not include all digits within the circle (but may include some of them).
391: Normal sudoku rules apply. Two cells separated by a knight's move (in chess) may not contain the same digit. In cages digits sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat in a cage. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the cells on the indicated diagonal. Digits may repeat along the diagonal.
392: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage.
393: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat in a cage. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. Digits may repeat along a diagonal.
394: Normal sudoku rules apply. Additionally, when two arrows face each other, they are crusts of a “sandwich”. Ie The digits in the crust cells must be the sum of the sandwich INCLUDING the crusts, in some order.
395: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. Cells along an arrow must strictly increase towards the circle and must sum to the digit in the circle.
396: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a king's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. Cells with circles contain the sum of all diagonally adjacent digits.
397: Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid are "X-Snake sums". X-Snakes are basically bendy X-Sums: orthogonally connected 1-cell wide paths that begin in the cell next to the clue (the 'tail' cell). Snakes are X cells long, where X is the digit in the tail cell, and sum to the value of the clue without repeating any digits. Snakes may not touch themselves OR ANY OTHER SNAKE orthogonally. The snakes are racing to the grey rock in the centre of the pit (grid!). Exactly one cell of exactly one snake must touch the rock orthogonally or diagonally to win the race. (ie there is only ONE snake cell in box 5). Snakes don't eat rocks so neither the rock cell nor its digit may appear in any snake.
398: Normal sudoku rules apply. Progressive Divisor numbers are numbers where the first digit is divisible by 1, the first two digits taken as a two-digit number are divisible by 2, and so on. There is a nine digit Progressive Divisor number in row 1 of the grid, written from left to right. Each of the digits in row 1 is also in a distinct non-overlapping invisible region that sums to 3x the digit's value. These regions may branch, and digits may repeat in regions if allowed by other rules. The size and shape of these regions must be determined by the solver. Clues outside the grid indicate the first N cells in the row/column, read from outside-in, are a Progressive Divisor number, where N is the digit in the cell next to the clue. The cages hold two digit numbers that are either divisible by both digits (eg 24) or neither digit (eg 98).
399: Normal Sudoku rules apply (yay!). Digits along a purple or red “renban” line MUST ALL repeat, and MAY NOT be chosen from consecutive digits (i.e. 445577 is valid but 445566 is not). Digits along a grey palindrome line MUST NOT read the same in both directions. Digits along a thermometer MUST NOT increase from the bulb end. Digits along the negative diagonal (marked in blue) MUST ALL repeat. Diagonals indicated by arrows outside the grid MUST NOT sum to the indicated value. Clues outside the grid MUST NOT be valid X-Sum or Skyscraper clues, as defined below. In a valid X-Sum clue, the first X digits seen by the clue, where X is the first seen digit, sum to the number in the clue (i.e. 382xxxxxx would be a 13 clue). In a valid Skyscraper clue, consider the digits as heights of buildings, where taller buildings hide smaller buildings behind them. The clue outside the grid indicates how many buildings can be "seen" from the clue (i.e. 462187593 would be a 4 from the left (4 → 6 → 8 → 9) and a 2 from the right (3 → 9).
400: In a standard sudoku grid, the boxes are numbered by convention from left to right and top to bottom such that the top left box is box 1, top middle is box 2, and so on. Within each box, the cells are numbered the same way. In this puzzle, the boxes have been separated and shuffled around, and it is up to the solver to determine their actual placement in the solution. Each box must have its box number in that position within the box (i.e. box 1 has 1 in position 1, box 2 has 2 in position 2, etc). No other digit in any box may be in its self-numbered cell. Fill each box with the digits 1-9 so that when the boxes are restored to their proper positions, each digit appears exactly once in each box, resulting row, and resulting column. Digits in a cage must sum to the indicated number. For a clue outside a box with no arrow, the first X cells, where X is the first seen digit, sum to the value of the clue. ? sums must be deduced by the solver. Sums do not cross box gaps. A clue with an arrow shows the sum of the indicated diagonal. Diagonals do not cross box gaps.
401: Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid indicate the sums of the digits in contiguous blocks in that row/column. Cells in blocks should be shaded. Blocks must be separated by at least one unshaded cell. Cells separated by a white dot must contain consecutive digits.
402: Normal sudoku rules apply. Additionally, shade some cells such that the clues outside the grid indicate the sums of the digits in contiguous blocks of shaded cells in the respective row or column. Blocks have to be separated by at least one unshaded cell. So a 6 clue in a row could mean a single-cell 6 is shaded, or a 2/4 pair is shaded, or a 1/2/3 triple is shaded. There must be a 3x3 magic square completely in the shaded region of the correct solution.
403: Normal sudoku rules apply, and shading cells will help you solve the puzzle! Clues outside the grid show the sums of digits in shaded cells. The groups of shaded cells must be separated by at least 1 unshaded cell. In addition - one of the following rules applies: Rhino rule (cells that are n cells over and n+1 cells up cannot have the same digit for each value of n); Camel rule: identical cells cannot be an extended knight's move apart (a regular knight's move is 1:2 , a camel move is 1:3); Elephant rule (cells 1 or 2 steps diagonally apart cannot have an identical digit).
404: Irregular/region sudoku rules apply. The are 4 6x6 grids (separated by the cages) that each use the digits 1-6 each. Japanese sums rules apply. Colors used in this puzzle are Red, White (green clues), Blue, and Pink. Red and white clues appear on the top and left side of the grid, while blue and pink appear on the right and bottom. There are no unshaded cells. The clues outside the grid indicate the sums of the contiguous runs found in that row or column that must be shaded the color of the clue (green clues represent white!). If a clue is black, then both colors must be present in the row or column. There must be a different color between runs of the same color. If a row or column is unclued, those colors do not appear in that row or column. Clues read left to right (or top to bottom) in both cases.
405: 1-9 must be placed in each row, column and marked region. The clues outside the grid indicate the sums of the contiguous runs of cells in that row or column that must be shaded black for black clues and gray for blue clues. If a clue is red, then both colors must be present in the row or column. There must be an unshaded cell between runs of the same color, though there is no need between runs of differing colors.
406: Normal sudoku rules apply - but the grid has been torn apart and scrambled. The clues outside the grid indicate the sums of the contiguous runs of digits found in that 3x3 box's row/column- these digits must be shaded. There must be an unshaded cell between runs of shaded cells. If a row/column is unclued, there is NO shading in that row/column. 3x3 boxes are numbered by convention from left to right and top to bottom such that the top left box is 1, top middle is 2, and so on. Within each box the cells are numbered in the same way. Each box must have its box number in its correct position within the box (ie box 1 of the untorn sudoku has a 1 in position 1, box 2 has 2 in position 2, etc). NO other digit in any box may be in its self-numbered cell. When finished, the shaded cells create a picture if put together in the correct order.
407: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Each purple line contains a set of non-repeating consecutive digits, which can be in any order.
408: Normal sudoku rules apply. The digit in the red cell (r1c1) is high [6,7,8 or 9]. The digit in the blue cell (r9c9) is low [1,2,3 or 4]. Digits along a purple line form a set of non-repeating consecutive digits (which can be in any order). Adjacent digits along a green line must have a difference of at least 5. A digit in a yellow cell must be greater than all of the orthogonally adjacent cells.
409: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Digits along a purple line cannot repeat and form a consecutive set in any order.
410: Normal sudoku rules apply. A circle with a number in it that connects two cells shows the remainder when the bigger digit is divided by the smaller digit. Eg 9 and 2 would have 1 in a circle between them since 9 divided by 2 is 4 with *1* as the remainder.
411: Normal Sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. For each blue line in the grid, digits on the line have an equal sum N within each box the line passes through.
412: Normal sudoku rules apply. (ie place the digits 1-9, once each, in every row, column and 3x3 box). Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow's circle.
413: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent cells on a green line must contain digits that have difference of at least 5. Adjacent cells on an orange line must contain digits that have difference of at most 2. Note that due to its nature, digits can repeat along an orange line if allowed by other rules. Digits on the grey line have an equal sum N within each box it passes through
414: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle.
415: Normal sudoku rules apply, and the clues outside the grid show the sums of the indicated diagonals, which may include repeats. The grey cells must be larger than any orthogonal neighbour.
416: Shade exactly four connected cells in each region to form an L, I, T or S tetromino. All shaded cells in the grid must connect to each other without forming a 2x2 block of shaded cells. Two tetrominoes of the same type must not share an edge.
417: Normal sudoku rules apply. Both main diagonals (marked in blue) must also contain the digits 1 to 9 once each. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal, and digits may repeat on these diagonals. Grey lines form palindromes (ie the digits thereon read the same forwards and backwards).
420: Normal sudoku rules apply. A cell with a grey square must contain an even digit. A cell with a grey circle must contain an odd digit. Cells separated by a black dot must contain digits in a ratio of 1:2. (Not all black dots are given.)
422: Place 1-9 in each row, column and marked region. A purple line contains a set of consecutive digits in any order.
423: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each line consists of one or more contiguous groups of cells, each of which sums to 10. These groups of cells cannot overlap. Digits may repeat freely on lines and even within sums.
424: Normal sudoku rules apply. A number outside the grid indicates the sum of the digits in the cells sandwiched between the 1 and 9 in its column. A number in a circled cell indicates the total number of cells sandwiched between the 1's and the 9's in the row and column containing the circle. If a cell is simultaneously in a row sandwich and column sandwich, it is only counted once. Not all circles are necessarily given.
425: Normal sudoku rules apply. Divide the entire grid into killer cages, each of which is a set of orthogonally connected cells. Each cage contains exactly one clue, which may be in any position in the cage, and gives the sum of the digits in that cage. Digits may not repeat in a cage. Single cell cages are allowed. Draw a single loop through the centres of some cells with no branches or crossings, which visits each cage exactly once. The loop moves orthogonally from cell to cell. If two cells share an edge but are in different cages, at least one of them must be visited by the loop. The digit in a clued cell equals the number of cells in that cage which are visited by the loop.
426: Normal sudoku rules apply. Blue lines in the grid are Region Sum Lines. For each blue line, digits on the line have an equal sum N within each 3x3 box the line passes through. Multiple entries to a 3x3 box sum separately
427: This is a puzzle that must be solved twice! Normal sudoku rules apply. Normal Killer, Little Killer, Quadruple, Kropki, Thermometer, Palindrome, Maximum, Minimum, and XV rules apply (see below for detailed rules). Red clues are each at least one of normal Skyscrapers, X-Sum, or Sandwich clues. After solving the puzzle, save your solution, because it's time to solve it again as a Wrogn puzzle! All clues in the grid must be made invalid in the finished solution, and red clues cannot be ANY of valid Skyscrapers, X-Sum, or Sandwich clues. To be considered invalid, the maximum cell must be less than AT LEAST one adjacent cell, the minimum cell must be greater than AT LEAST one adjacent cell, thermometers must NOT increase from bulb to tip, and quadruple circles may have some BUT NOT ALL listed digits in the surrounding cells. A "less than" sign effectively becomes a greater-than-or-equal-to sign. A "greater than" sign effectively becomes a less-than-or-equal-to sign. ADDITIONALLY, when solving the Wrogn version, no digit may be the same as it was in the Right version. i.e. if R1C1 was a 1 the first time, it may not be a 1 the second time. IT IS IMPOSSIBLE TO SOLVE THE WROGN VERSION WITHOUT FIRST SOLVING IT NORMALLY
428: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along blue lines sum to the same total in each region they pass through. Different lines may have different totals. Each instance of a single line that passes through a box is counted separately. The area outside the grid is counted as a region for these lines. A clue outside the grid (to be deduced) indicates the digit in the Nth cell in that direction, where N is the first digit seen by the clue.
429: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits increase along thermometers from the bulb(s) to the end. Disjoint subset rules apply: a digit can never appear twice in the same cell within different 3x3 boxes.
430: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cages show their sums. The two grey shapes are exact clones of each other.
431: Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells in the grid such that clues outside the grid show the sums of consecutive runs of shaded cells in that row/column (each run separated by at least one unshaded cell). On each blue line, numbers must be consecutive and cannot repeat (but can appear in any order).
432: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue given in the top left corner of the cage. Digits may not repeat within a cage. A black dot between two cells means that one of the digits in the cells is exactly double the other. A white dot between two cells means that the two digits in the cells must be consecutive. Not all black and white dots are given.
433: Normal sudoku rules apply, and identical digits cannot be a knight's move apart. Digits on arrows, which may include repeats, sum to the number in the circle.
434: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells along arrows must sum to the digit in the attached circle. Clues outside the grid indicate the sum of digits "sandwiched" between the 1 and 9 in that row or column.
437: I’m sorry, the rules seem to have been invaded by pickles. I hope you can still make pickle of them. Normal pickle rules apply. Two adjacent pickles on a pickle line have a difference of at least 5. Pickles separated by a light pickle dot are consecutive. Pickles separated by a dark pickle dot are in a 2:1 pickle. Not all pickles are necessarily shown. Have pickle!
438: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. Digits along an arrow path must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle.
439: Normal Sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits must not repeat within a cage. Along thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb end.
440: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along thermometers, digits increase from the bulb. A number in a circle must appear in one of the cells touching that circle.
441: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cages are ‘putteria’ cages. Each cage of size N has to have the number N contained in it. Putteria numbers (Ns) cannot repeat in a cage, and cannot orthogonally neighbour other putteria numbers. Other numbers may repeat in cages.
442: Normal sudoku rules apply, and the grid divides fully into polyominos, each containing one circle and no repeated digits. The circle digit indicates the number of cells in that polyomino. White boxes separate adjacent, consecutive digits that share a polyomino. Black boxes separate adjacent numbers with a 1:2 ratio that are in different polyominos. All such boxes of both types are given. Three of the polyominos have been filled in, including the unique largest and the unique smallest.
443: Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits “sandwiched” between the 1 and the 9 in the respective row/column. Cells along arrows sum to the digit in that arrow’s circle. Digits can repeat along arrows if allowed by other rules. X and y need to be deduced by the solver. The row labelled "min" is the unique lowest sandwich sum across the entire grid.
444: Every row/column contains the digits 1-9 exactly once each. Digits may not repeat along the marked (blue) diagonal. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. Every cage must be entirely shaded or unshaded, and every row and column contains at least one shaded cell. In each row and column the cell that contains the number of shaded cells in that row/column is indicated either by a square or a circle. Circles indicate that all shaded cells in that row/column are orthogonally connected; squares indicate those shaded cells are not all orthogonally connected (though some may be). Whether a particular square/circle corresponds to its row/column (or both) is to be determined.
445: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits may not repeat along a main diagonal (marked in blue). In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage (which is always given). Digits cannot repeat within a cage. Placing correct digits in the grid will clear the fog.
446: Normal sudoku rules apply. Every row, column and 3x3 box contains exactly one "doubler" cell. A digit in a doubler cell counts for twice its value for the purposes of all cage sums. Digits in doubler cells form a unique set of the digits 1 to 9. Digits may not repeat in cages, though values might. (eg a cage may not contain a doubled 2 and a regular 2 but may contain a doubled 2 and a regular 4). Caged cells must sum to the value indicated in the top left corner of the cage. The cell with a grey circle contains an odd digit. The cell with the grey square contains an even digit.
447: Normal sudoku rules apply, and digits increase along thermos from the bulb. Each digit is represented by a different letter, and the clue outside the grid shows the sum of the indicated diagonal.
448: Normal sudoku rules apply. Red cells cannot border with a consecutive digit, in blue cells squares are even and circles are odd. Somewhere in the white cells is a 3x3 magic square (the digits 1-9 arranged so that each row, column and diagonal adds to the same number).
449: Divide the grid, along its lines, into regions. Regions of the same size cannot share an edge, and each given digit must be in a region of that size. Regions may not have any given digits in them, or may have more than one.
450: Normal Sudoku Rules apply but, instead of the usual 3x3 boxes, each irregularly-shaped 9 cell region must contain the digits 1 to 9. Digits in two orthogonally adjacent cells may not be consecutive. Cells separated by a knight’s move or a king’s move in chess cannot contain the same digit. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage.
451: Normal Sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid show the sums of the indicated diagonals. Dots mark neighbouring consecutive digits – all possible dots are shown.
452: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. Similarly coloured dominoes are clones of each other and must contain the same digits in the same orientation.
453: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits increase along thermometers from the bulb(s) to the end.
454: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits may not repeat along the main diagonals (which are marked). Digits in cages must sum to the total in the top left corner and may not repeat.
455: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the number in the associated circle. Clues outside the grid indicate the sum of the digits between the 1 and the 9 in that row or column.
456: Normal sudoku rules apply, and each cage shows the sum of its digits, which cannot include repeats.
457: Each row and column contains 1-9. Each outlined white area and each connected grey area also contains each of 1-9.
458: Normal sudoku rules apply. Blue lines are Region Sum lines. In each box visited by such a line, the digits must sum to the same total, to be determined. The target sum will potentially be different for each line. XY Difference Pairs rules apply. If two cells are separated by a diamond, the digits must exhibit a difference equal to the leftmost or topmost digit sharing a row or column with them. For example, the difference between R9C34 = R9C1, and the difference between R23C1 = R1C1. Not all possible diamonds are necessarily given.
459: Rows, columns and 3x3 boxes all contain 1-9.
460: Normal sudoku rules apply, and digits along an arrow sum to the number in the 'circle' (which in some cases is a 2-digit number reading left-to-right or down).
461: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits cannot appear in the same position in different 3x3 boxes. In box 1: Digits separated by a white dot must be consecutive. (No negative constraint.) In box 2: Digits along the thermometer must increase from the bulb end. In box 3: Digits along the indicated diagonal sum to the given total. In box 4: Digits in the circle must appear in one of the surrounding four cells. In box 5: Digits separated by an X must sum to 10; digits separated by an V must sum to 5. (No negative constraint.) In box 6: Digits along the arrow must sum to the circled digit. In box 7: Digits in the cage must sum to the given total. In box 8: Digits in a circle must be odd. In box 9: Digits separated by a black dot must have a 2:1 ratio. (No negative constraint.)
462: Normal sudoku rules apply. A friendly cell has a value identical to its row-, column- or box-number, counted in the standard way. The green "lawn" cells are friendly. (For example, r1c7 must be either 1 to match the row, 3 to match the box, or 7 to match the column.) Additionally, an orthogonally-connected one-cell wide path (so the path cannot touch itself orthogonally) must be found between the cells marked with circles, such that every cell on the path - including the marked cells - is friendly but not lawn. (Note: there could be friendly cells other than path or lawn in the puzzle.) Along the marked arrows, the digits in the friendly cells (any friendly cells - whether lawn, path, or otherwise) sum to the same total as the digits in the cells that are not friendly.
463: Normal sudoku rules apply. Black dots connect cells with a ratio of 2:1, and white dots connect cells with a difference of 1. Not all dots are shown.
465: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along thermometers must increase from bulb to tip.
466: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage.
468: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along grey lines will read the same when you roll out the grey line along the row or column, e.g. the line in box 1 would 'unroll' along column 1 and would read the same down column 1 as it does r1c1 to r2c2.
469: This puzzle is an 11x11 grid with a normal 9x9 Sudoku centered inside. Within the 9x9 Sudoku grid, normal sudoku rules apply: place the digits 1 to 9 in every row, column, and 3x3 box. Draw a snake (non-looping, non-branching 1-cell wide path of orthogonally connected cells) that may touch itself diagonally but not orthogonally. The two ends of the snake are given as large white circles (UFOs). Within the 9x9 Sudoku, all of the odd digits (and none of the even digits) belong to the snake. The snake may appear in any cell within the 11x11 grid, and may move in and out of the 9x9 Sudoku as necessary. Cells outside the 9x9 Sudoku have no numerical value—they exist only for the snake. Digits separated by a white dot (sun) must be consecutive. Digits separated by a black dot (moon) must have a ratio of 2:1. Not all dots are given.
470: Normal 4x4 sudoku rules apply (1-4 appear in each row, column and 2x2 box). Arrows indicate the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. Digits may repeat if allowed by other rules.
471: Normal sudoku rules apply. Some Japanese sums rules apply: There is a 6x6 grid in boxes 5/6/8/9. Blue cells in boxes 2/3/4/7 act as Japanese sum clues for this 6x6 grid, giving the sum of contiguous runs of blue-shaded cells within the grid. Two-digit clues are read top-to-bottom or left-to-right. There must be an unshaded cell between runs of the same color. A black dot separates digits with a 1 to 2 ratio. A white dot separates digits with a difference of 1 (or the given number when given). Not all dots are given. Fog rules apply. The fog will clear as you place digits correctly.
472: 1-9 appear in each row and column. Japanese Sums rules: The clues outside the grid indicate the sums of the contiguous runs found in that row or column that must be shaded. There must be at least one unshaded cell between runs. If a row or column is unclued, there is no shading in that row or column. Regions, which each contain 1-9 orthogonally connected, must be determined. Either all or no cells within a region are shaded. 620: Normal sudoku rules apply. Consider the first x and last y cells of a row/column where x is the value of the first cell and y is the value of the last cell. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits where these groups overlap or the sum of the digits between these groups.
621: Renban Sudoku: Normal sudoku rules apply; also, all coloured shapes (green or grey) contain a run of (5) consecutive digits, though not entered in a particular order
622: Normal sudoku rules apply. There are some Killer Sudoku clues given. They are part of a group of connected cells and give the sum of the digits in this group. Digits may not repeat within these groups and groups for different clues cannot overlap. Each group is completely contained in one coloured orbit of the puzzle grid. Otherwise, placement and size of the groups is not known. There may be cells that are not part of any group.
623: Normal sudoku rules apply. Little killer (Arrow) clues show the sum of the indicated diagonal. Sandwich product clues above the grid show the product of digits between the 1 and the 9 in that column. 'Parity Party' clues beside the grid show the product of the digits in that row as far as (and including) the first change of parity (odd/even). X-Factor clues below the grid show the product of the first X digits reading up, where X is the first digit.
624: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in the first and second cell from the top and from the left are A and B. Clues outside the grid tell something about A and B: The clue closest to the grid gives the sum of A and B. The sum of the digits on positions A and B from that side is given in the clue in the grey bar.
625: Normal sudoku rules apply. The first two cells in each row and column are A & B, and clues outside the grid show the sum of A + B (white) and the sum of the digits in position A and position B in the row/column (grey). Odd/Even digits in these sums are shown by O/E.
626: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. In addition, each cage contains a standard "arrow" clue, which is hidden. (In an arrow clue, cells along arrow must sum to the digit in the circle from which the arrow emerges.) The 'circle' part of the arrow will be at one end of the cage with the arrow extending along the cage all the way to the other end. The circle may be any number of digits and multi-digit totals are read in the direction of the arrow.
627: Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid show the total of the first X digits from that direction, where X is the first digit seen.
628: Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a circle in one of the cells of each line. The digit in the circle gives the sum of the digits towards (each of) the remaining end(s) of the line.
629: Normal sudoku rules apply. The clues outside the grid indicate the sum of the first X digits placed in the corresponding row/column, where X is equal to the first digit in that row/column. In these clues, odd digits have been replaced by O. (Zero is even. Multi-digit clues may not start with zero.)
630: Normal sudoku rules apply. The clues outside the grid indicate the sum of the first X digits placed in the corresponding row/column, where X is equal to the first digit in that row/column. In these clues, even digits have been replaced by E. (Zero is even. Multi-digit clues may not start with zero.)
631: Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid are X-Sum clues. Ie They give the sum of the first X digits where X is the first digit from that direction. Some friendly Aliens helped me creating this puzzle, but each alien uses his own number system with an unknown base, and I can't remember which alien wrote which clue anymore.
632: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits outside the grid show the first odd and even digits seen in the direction of the clue.
633: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits increase from the bulb to the tip along thermos.
634: Normal sudoku and killer rules apply.
635: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits outside the grid show the first odd and even digits seen in the direction of the clue.
636: Normal sudoku rules apply. The leftmost and rightmost cells of a row are considered orthogonally adjacent for the purposes of all rules below. Cells joined by a white dot contain consecutive digits. Not all white dots are given. Shade some cells in the grid and leave the rest unshaded such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected and no 2x2 region is entirely shaded. A cell containing Pac-Man, Blinky, Pinky, Inky, or Clyde (yellow, red, pink, blue, and orange)—or part of a white dot—must be shaded. A cell containing a killer clue must remain unshaded. Digits may not repeat within an orthogonally connected area of unshaded cells, and they sum to the killer clue. (Note: Unshaded regions may not touch each other orthogonally and not all regions necessarily have a killer clue.) Starting in R5C2, Pac-Man must travel orthogonally through the grid. His path may not touch itself orthogonally, although it may do so diagonally, and the path cannot intersect or overlap itself. Pac-Man must go directly through each white dot; his path is completed immediately after going through the final dot. Pac-Man’s path cannot be orthogonally adjacent to any of the ghosts (red, pink, blue, and orange) nor can the path enter unshaded cells.
637: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grey lines and the diagonal must sum to 50.
638: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits outside the grid show the sum of the diagonals.
639: Normal sudoku rules apply. Queens rules apply to the digit 9.
640: There are three identical shaded regions in the grid. Two of them are clones, and the third is an extra region. In the cloned regions, the same digits must appear in corresponding locations. In an extra region each digit 1-9 must appear exactly once.
641: Normal sudoku rules apply. Additionally the digits on an arrow either sum or average to the digit in the circle.
642: Normal Sudoku rules apply. Digits outside the grid are either frame or x-sum clues or both. Frame gives sum of first 3 digits. X-sum gives the sum of the first X digits where X is in the first position.
643: Normal sudoku rules apply. Find the clone shown by grey squares.
647: Normal sudoku rules apply. Grey circles are odd. Grey squares are even.
650: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb end.
651: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grey cells must be cloned somewhere else in the grid in same shifted positions.
653: Normal sudoku rules apply. The cells touched by each circle must sum to the total given in the circle. Digits can repeat around a circle.
654: Normal sudoku rules apply, and each cage shows the sum of its digits, which cannot include repeats.
656: Normal Sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid show the sums of the indicated diagonals.
658: Normal sudoku rules apply. Start with any digit from 1 to 7 in centre cell.
659: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits outside the grid show the sums between the digits 1 and 9 in that row or column.
663: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cell with an arrow must repeat at least once in the direction of the arrow.
665: Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid indicate the sum of the first X digits in the corresponding direction, where X is the first digit placed in that direction.
666: Enter a single digit from 1 to 9 into each white cell so that the sum of digits in each Across entry equals the clue to the left of the entry, and the sum of digits in each Down entry equals the clue given above the entry. No digit may be repeated within a single entry.
669: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage.
670: Place 2 stars in each row, column and region. Stars cannot be placed in adjacent cells that share an edge or corner.
671: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. The digits in a cage must sum to the small clue in the cage’s top left corner. The digits on a purple “Renban” line have to form a non-repeating set of consecutive digits – these digits can appear in any order.
672: Normal sudoku rules apply. Additional each line has the same sum and digits may repeat on a line.
673: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb end.
674: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb end.
675: Normal sudoku rules apply. Lines must be all even or all odd and no other lines in a box must be all odd or all even.
676: Normal sudoku rules apply, arrows outside the grid show the ascending direction of the first three digits, weherever that applies.
677: Normal sudoku rules apply. If the sum of digits in two orthogonally adjacent cells is 10 then they are separated by an X. If the sum of digits in orthogonally adjacent cells is 5 then they are separated by a V. All possible X & V are marked (which means if two orthogonally adjacent cells are not separated by an X or a V then they cannot sum up to 10 or 5).
678: Normal sudoku rules apply and the grey cells show accurate multiplications with the factors in the top row and the product below them.
679: Normal sudoku rules apply, and cells surrounding a black dot must contain consecutive digits.
680: Normal sudoku rules apply. Additionally, the grey lines represent incomplete 'arrows'. The digit on one end of each line is the sum of the other digits on the same line.
681: Normal sudoku rules apply. Lines in the grid form palindromes ie the string of digits on these lines reads the same backwards and forwards.
682: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits increase along thermometers from the bulb. Cages show their sums, and outside clues show the total of the indicated diagonals (which can include repeat digits).
684: Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues with arrows show the sum of the indicated diagonal, which may contain repeats. Other clues show digits which must appear in the first three cells, looking from that direction.
685: Normal sudoku rules apply. Some cages show their sums. Clues outside the grid show the sum of indicated diagonals, which may include repeat digits.
686: Normal sudoku rules apply. The circled number between two cells represents the difference between the two cells.
687: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each of the given equations must be satisfied, reading left-to-right or downwards. Addition (+), subtraction (-), multiplication (x), division (/) and powers (^) may be used, so that 3^2=9 for instance.
688: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. Digits can repeat along such diagonals if allowed by the other rules. Each purple line must contain a set of non-repeating, consecuitive digits. These digits can appear in any order.
689: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Adjacent digits along a green line must differ by at least 5. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. Digits may repeat along such a diagonal if allowed by other rules.
690: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along green lines, neighbouring digits differ by at least 5. A purple line shows a sequence of consecutive digits, not necessarily in order.
691: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each grid marking 'points' at the lower digit in the connected cells.
692: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits along a green line must have a difference of at least 5. Digits in cages sum to the indicated total. Digits along indicated diagonals must add to the indicated total. Repeats are permitted along such diagonals.
693: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits outside the grid must appear in the first three cells in that direction.
694: Normal Sudoku rules apply. Also: Digits along an arrow in the grid must sum to the digit in its circle.; Along thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb end; The green line is a palindrome, it reads the same from both directions. Each different digit must appear at least once on the palindrome; The black dot means that the ratio of the two connected cells is 2; The white dot means that the difference of the two connected cells is 1; In cages, digits must sum to the small clue given in the top-left of the cage; There are no negative constraints.
695: Normal sudoku rules apply. Numbers along arrows sum to the number in the circle/pill, BUT for blue pills, the numbers on the arrow are 2-digit numbers (reading away from the pill) and the number in the pill is a 2- or 3-digit number reading left-to-right or downwards.
696: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits must increase along grey thermos, from the bulb(s). Double-digit numbers must increase along green thermos, starting with the ‘plant’s root’ and always with the tens digit appearing first, and double-digit numbers on arrows similarly must sum to the 3-digit number in the central pill.
697: Normal Sudoku rules apply. Digits in two cells separated by an X sum to 10. Digits in two cells separated by a V sum to 5. For any pair of orthogonally adjacent cells where both cells are coloured yellow: The digits cannot add to 5 or 10; the digits cannot be consecutive (ie cannot have a difference of 1); and the digits cannot have a ratio of 1:2 (so one digit cannot be double the other).
698: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage (if given). Along each main diagonal (marked in blue) digits cannot repeat.
699: In each row and column the digits 1-9 must appear exactly once. Each cell is part of a “galaxy”. There are big galaxies of exactly 9 cells and island galaxies which are smaller than 9 cells. Digits can't repeat in galaxies. Each galaxy is 180 degrees rotational symmetric. In the centre of each galaxy there is exactly one circle either between 2 cells or in a cell. A circle in a cell is odd and a circle between 2 cells is a consecutive pair. Some of the circles are given, the other circles must be deduced (but all circles must have the circle properties listed above). Island galaxies can't touch each other, not even diagonally. Clues outside the grid sum the digits of the island galaxies in that row or column.
700: Normal sudoku rules apply. Furthermore, there are two snakes (snake A and B) in the grid. One is an 'Equal Sum Line' Snake (see below) and the other is a 'German Whisper Line' Snake (again, see below). The solver must determine which is which. Each snake is an orthogonally connected set of cells (the starts and ends are marked) and each snake MUST visit every 3x3 box. The snakes cannot touch themselves, even diagonally. The snakes may touch each other but they do not cross each other. The outside clues give the sum of the NON-snake cells in that direction. The squares give the number of the NON-snake cells in that box. On an 'Equal Sum Line', digits have an equal sum N within each box the line passes through. On a German Whisper Line, adjacent digits must have a difference of at least 5.
701: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each grey (fortress) cell must be higher than any white cell it borders. Along thermometers, digits increase from the bulb.
702: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage.
703: Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade the grid according to the following rules: all odd digits are 'water' and should be unshaded; all even digits must be shaded to form islands; all water cells must be orthogonally connected but there cannot be any 2x2 areas of water. An island is formed of orthogonally connected cells. Islands cannot touch each other orthogonally but they can touch diagonally. Digits may repeat on an island. A cage cell is representing the leftmost cell in the top row of an island and the clue of the cage cell is equal to the sum of digits of the island. Not necessarily all cage cells are given.
704: Normal sudoku rules apply. In the grid, every cell is part of an 'Omino', consisting of all 12 different Pentominoes, all 5 different Tetrominoes and 1 Monomino. Ominoes cannot overlap and digits cannot repeat within an Omino. The sum of the digits in each Omino must be divisible by the number of cells in that Omino. The 1-cell cage clues each mark the leftmost cell of the top row of an Omino, and this Omino sums to the value of that clue. The digits along a grey line form a sequence of consecutive digits but may appear in any order. Each line cannot be part of more than one Omino.
705: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the number in the circle. Clues outside the grid show the sum of the indicated diagonal, which can include repeats.
706: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle.
707: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each line in the grid is one of the three types of line: Renban (a series of consecutive digits, including no repeats, appears on the line, not necessarily in order); Whisper (digits next to each other on the line must have a difference of at least 5); Palindrome (the line reads the same forwards and backwards). You must decide which lines have which property.
708: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a white dot contain consecutive digits. Not all white dots are given. The grey line is a "Double Digit Thermometer" where it alternatives tens digits and units digits. Starting at the bulb the double digits increase along the thermometer. All double digits added together sum to 400. Digits along each purple line multiply to 400. [NB Some people have questioned whether r3c2 should be counted twice in doing the multiplication. It should NOT be. It only counts once.]
709: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Each purple line must contain a set of consecutive, non-repeating digits (in any order). Adjacent digits on a green line must have a difference of at least 5. Cells containing opaque grey circles must contain odd digits. Grey lines are palindromes ie they must read the same forwards and backwards.
710: Normal sudoku rules apply. Furthermore there are 3 snakes hidden in the grid. Each snake is a set of cells sharing an edge or a corner; each snake cannot branch; touch itself (orthogonally or diagonally) or touch another snake (orthogonally or diagonally). Each snake's cells contain digits which, when multiplied together, give exactly 500. Parts of some or all the snakes are shown as grey lines in the grid. No snake can start or end in the digit 1. NB as cells on the same snake cannot touch diagonally r2c4, for example, in this puzzle cannot be snake (as the snake cell r3c3 touches r2c4 diagonally).
711: Normal sudoku and killer rules apply.
712: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits may not repeat along the two main diagonals.
713: Normal sudoku and killer and little killer rules apply.
715: Normal sudoku and killer rules apply.
716: Normal sudoku and little killer rules apply.
717: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in circles must appear in at least one of the 4 cells surrounding it
718: Normal sudoku rules apply. No two cells that share an edge can sum to 15.
719: Normal sudoku rules apply. All the digits located on same side of diamond must be different. The digits are the same for the four sides.
720: Add light bulbs to the grid so that each white cell is lit up. Each light bulb illuminates the cell it is in as well as any horizontal or vertical adjacent cells stopping at any black cells or the grid perimeter. No bulb can illuminate another bulb. Numbers in the cells indicate how bulbs in orthogannly adjacent cells.
721: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in circles must appear in at least one of the 4 cells surrounding it
722: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat in a cage.
723: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage.
724: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits sum to the small clue in the top-left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. A digit in a shaded cell must be greater than all the digits in orthogonally-adjacent unshaded cells.
725: Normal Sudoku rules apply. In each cage, two of the three digits shown appear and the other does not. Digits may repeat in cages.
726: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits sum to the small value in the top-left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. Digits on a line must be strictly smaller than one of the two corresponding circled digits, and strictly larger than the other.
727: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each 18-cell grey region must contain the digits from 1 to 9 exactly twice.
728: Normal sudoku rules apply. A cell with a circle contains an odd digit. A cell with a square contains an even digit. HOWEVER exactly one of the given symbols is a liar. It may be a square containing an odd digit or a circle containing an even digit.
729: Normal sudoku rules apply. Numbers increase from the bulb end of the thermometers. Cells separated by a white circle are consecutive. Cells separated by a black circle are in the ratio 1 to 2. Completing the dots between neighbouring yellow cells will allow you to detect the weapon and murderer, using Morse code (white = dot, black = dash).
730: Normal sudoku rules apply, and digits increase along thermometers from the bulb. No pair of neighbouring cells adds to 5 or 10.
731: Normal sudoku rules apply, and digits increase along thermometers from the bulb to the end(s). The black dot marks a pair of neighbouring cells with a ratio of 2:1 - other such pairs may be unmarked.
732: Normal sudoku rules apply, and digits increase along yellow thermometers from the bulb to the end(s). Clues outside the grid show the total of the indicated diagonal, which may include repeats. Blue, green and purple 'balloons' are odd digits.
733: Normal sudoku rules apply, and digits increase along thermometers from the bulb to the end. The '0' thermometer has a bulb on one end, to be discovered. An arrow clue shows the sum of the indicated diagonal, which may include repeats.
734: Normal sudoku rules apply, and digits ascend along thermometers from the bulb to the end(s). Black dots mark connections between cells with a ratio of 1:2, but not all possible dots are marked.
735: Normal sudoku rules apply. A clue outside the grid shows the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. Grey circles are odd numbers. The grey line is a palindrome, reading the same from both directions.
736: Normal sudoku rules apply. Numbered arrows outside the grid indicate the sum of the digits along that diagonal path (which could repeat). The gray square is an even number. Adjacent digits along the lines alternate between odd and even numbers. Cells separated by a black dot are in the ratio 1 to 2. Cells separated by a white dot are consecutive. Not all possible dots are given.
737: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a thermometer must increase from the bulb to the end. Cells joined by a white dot contain consecutive digits. Not all dots are given. The three “2” thermometers are clones, with the same digits in the same positions.
738: Normal sudoku rules apply. Numbers along an arrow must sum to the number in the arrow's circle. Two of the orange dots are thermometer bulbs and the third is the beginning of a palindrome. Which dot is which is to be determined. The palindrome is 10 digits long and goes around one of the heart shapes. Numbers increase from the bulbs of the thermometers on both sides of the heart shapes to the common end point at the base of the heart (r5c3 and/or r9c3 and/or r7c7).
739: Normal sudoku rules apply. The numbers in the balls (circles) must appear in the four surrounding cells. One racquet (grey line) must consist of all odd numbers and the other racquet (grey line) must have all even numbers. Digits do not repeat on each marked diagonal.
740: Normal sudoku rules apply. The digits on lines of the same colour sum to the same total. The four different totals are prime numbers. Digits may repeat on a line if allowed by other rules. Cells separated by a black dot contain digits in a 1:2 ratio (ie one digit is double the other). Not all possible black dots are shown.
741: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells joined by black dots have a ratio of 1: 2. Not all possible dots are shown. Identical digits cannot be a chess knight’s move apart. Neighbouring digits along the orange line have a difference of at least four.
742: Normal sudoku rules apply. The purple/blue lines are "equal sum lines". ie The sum of the digits on a line within a particular 3x3 box must be the same for all the boxes the line passes through.
