Different lines may have different sums. eg r9c1 + r9c2 + r9c3 = r9c4 + r8c4 + r7c4 = r6c4 + r5c4. Digits along each line are also a set of non-repeating consecutive numbers (which can appear in any order).
743: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits along the line have a difference of at least 4. A digit in a coloured cell must form at least one sum of 5 or 10 with a digit in an orthogonally adjacent cell. A digit in a white cell must not form any sum of 5 or 10 with a digit in an orthogonally adjacent cell. For example r2c5 and r3c6 cannot be a 3 or an 8. However, one or both of r2c7 and r1c6 must be a 3 or an 8.
744: Normal sudoku rules apply. Identical digits cannot be a chess knight's move apart. Digits along each purple (renban) line are a set of consecutive numbers in any order. Purple lines which are joined by grey connecting lines are also equal sum lines, so the sum of the digits on a purple line within one 3x3 box must be the same as the sum of the digits on a connected purple line. Different joined lines may have different sums.
745: Normal sudoku rules apply. The sum of the digits on a blue line within a particular region must be the same for all of the regions the line passes through. Different lines may have different sums. Pairs of adjacent numbers on a line must sum to a prime number. The digits in each cage sum to the same total (which is to be determined).
746: Normal sudoku rules apply. A clue outside the grid indicates the sum of the digits along that diagonal path (which may include repeat digits). Digits increase from the bulb to the end(s) of a thermometer. Cells separated by a white dot are consecutive. Not all possible white dots are shown.
747: Normal sudoku rules apply. Neighbouring digits along green lines have a difference of at least five. Digits along a purple line are a set of consecutive numbers in any order with no repeats. Cells joined by black dots are in the ratio of 1:4.
748: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits do not repeat on the marked diagonal. Digits in a cage do not repeat and their sum is given. Each digit inside a cage is consecutive with its orthogonally adjacent neighbours outside the cage.
749: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow's circle.
750: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along the diagonals must not repeat. The two grey regions are clones.
751: Each row, column and 3x3 box xontains digits 1 to 9. The green cells sum to 75, and the blue cells sum to 75.
752: Numbers in the perimeter (ie outside the 9x9 sudoku grid) are "sandwich sudoku clues" - they give the sum of the cells sandwiched between the 1 & 9 in their row/column. Along thermometer shapes, digits must increase from the bulb end. Any thermometer cell in the perimeter cannot contain a 0 but need not be a digit from 1 to 9.
753: Normal sudoku rules apply; cages show the sum of their digits, which are different; lines are palindromes and therefore read the same in each direction.
754: Normal sudoku rules apply. In addition, the digits 1 to 9 must appear on both main diagonals. Along thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb end.
755: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each row/column begins with a number X, and 1 is in the Xth cell of that row/column.
756: Normal sudoku rules apply, and digits along arrows sum to the numbers in the circles – some of the ‘circles’ contain 2-digit numbers.
757: Normal Sudoku rules apply. Digits placed along an arrow must sum to the number in the corresponding circle. If the sum is multiple digits, the digits are read left to right as a two-digit total. Digits can repeat along an arrow.
758: Normal Sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a dot must contain consecutive digits. Not all possible dots are given. Digits with a 1:2 ratio may not appear in orthogonally adjacent cells, even if separated by a dot.
759: Shade some cells so that each connected region of shaded cells is a perfect square. No two squares of the same size are allowed to "see" each other (have a horizontal or vertical line of unshaded cells connecting them, unobstructed). A number in the grid represents how many cells are shaded in a cross shape around it, consisting of the cell itself and the four orthogonally adjacent cells.
760: Normal sudoku rules apply. Additionally, cells separated by a single knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal; digits may repeat along these diagonals.
761: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue given in the top left corner of the cage. Digits may not repeat within a cage. The purple line represents a 21-digit palindrome the ends of which have to be deduced (i.e. the first digit and the last digit lie adjacent to each other on the purple line).
762: Normal Sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a single knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. Digits may not repeat within a cage and the clue in the top left corner of a cage indicates the sum of all the digits in that cage. Also, note the inequality sign in the grid. (The killer cage without the sum is not required for the solution. It's just there to maintain the symmetry.)
763: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits may not repeat within a cage. Within every 3*3 box (marked by thick black lines), all the killer cages have the same sum. Also, killer cage sums are unique for every 3*3 box i.e if box 1 (top left box) had killer cages each of which sum up to 10, then none of the other boxes can have killer cages with a sum of 10. The killer cage sums are not given and have to be deduced.
764: Normal Sudoku rules apply. Shade cells using the following rules: do not shade cells containing digits in their top left corner (“TLC”); the digit in the cell with a number in its TLC gives the number of contiguous white cells in that area (i.e. it represents a Nurikabe clue); the number in the TLC also equals the sum of all the digits in that area; digits cannot repeat within a white area; no two different areas of white cells can share an edge (though they can touch at a point); the shaded cells are all orthogonally-connected BUT cannot occupy a 2x2 square (or larger); all the Nurikabe clues have been given. Note the inequality sign in the grid. Unlike in normal killer sudoku, the cell with the number in its TLC may not be the leftmost cell of the highest row of that white area.
765: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cages show either the sum or product of their digits, which include no repeats. So a 2-cell 16-cage could contain 7 & 9 (7+9) or 2 & 8 (2x8).
766: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. Cells separated by a knight’s move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit.
767: Normal Sudoku rules apply. The digits on an arrow add up to the digit in the corresponding circle. Numbers may repeat along an arrow. Each marked main diagonal cannot have a repeated digit. Ie each contains every number from 1 to 9 exactly once.
768: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. The green lines are "renban" lines. ie each line contains a set of consecutive, non-repeating digits, in any order.
769: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage (if given). Digits cannot repeat within a cage. Each grey line contains a set of consecutive, non-repeating digits, in any order.
770: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits on a purple line must be between the values placed in the circled ends of that line.
771: Normal sudoku rules apply. Three of the four digits touching a circle sum to the fourth digit. Not all circles are necessarily given.
772: Normal sudoku rules apply. Grey squares are walls and green squares are cave. Some of the cells must be coloured grey so that all grey cells (the walls) are orthogonally connected to the edge of the grid and all other (green) cells form an orthogonally connected area (the cave). A clue in the top left corner of a cell indicates the sum of the digits that are seen from this cell looking to the north, south, east and west. The cell with the clue counts once towards this sum. Walls obstruct the view. A cell with a clue must be part of the cave. Within the field of vision of a clue, digits may not repeat.
773: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. Odd digits(1, 3, 5, 7, 9) can appear consecutively for more than two cells vertically, but not more than two cells horizontally. Even digits(2, 4, 6, 8) can appear consecutively for more than two cells horizontally, but not more than two cells vertically.
774: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle.
775: Normal sudoku rules apply. The cells with a clue in the top left corner represent one end of a snake. Each clue belongs to a different snake. The value of the clue gives the sum of all the digits that lie on a snake. These snakes behave as region sum lines. As a snake passes through different 3 x 3 boxes, digits on the snake have an equal sum N within each box it passes through. If the snake passes through the same box more than once, then each individual segment within that box sums to N separately. The snake must pass through at least two 3 x 3 boxes. If '?' is given as a clue, then its value has to be deduced. The snakes can't touch themselves orthogonally or diagonally. Two snakes can't share a cell together.
776: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits may not repeat within a cage. Numbers outside the grid are X-Sums clues. They indicate the sum of the first X cells in the row/column from that direction, where X is the first number in that row/column. A double-digit X-Sums clue inside a cage prevents BOTH of its digits from appearing anywhere else in the cage (this does mean 11, 22, 33, and 44 are disallowed as X-Sums clues, as those would repeat digits in a cage). A double-digit X-Sums clue may include zero (10, 20, 30, and 40 are valid X-Sums clues).
777: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along thermometers must increase from the bulb end. In addition, digits along thermometers must be consecutive, such as 23456.
778: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb end.
779: Normal sudoku rules apply! Digits seperated by a knights move must be different.
780: Normal sudoku rules apply! Digits seperated by a knights move must be different.
781: Normal sudoku rules apply! Digits seperated by a knights move must be different.
782: Normal sudoku rules apply. In X-Sums sudoku, the clues outside the grid show the sum of the first X digits looking into the grid from the clue, where X is the first clue. In this puzzle, all clues inside and outside the grid are incorrect by 1.
783: Draw a closed loop that consists of horizontal and vertical lines between cells (from cell centre to cell centre), and that doesn’t cross or touch itself. The loop visits each boldly outlined area exactly once. Clues indicate how many cells within an area are used by the loop. Non-loop cells are not allowed to touch orthogonally if they are in different areas. [Also see the video for an example puzzle.]
784: Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid show the total of the first X cells from that direction where X is the first of those cells from that direction.
785: Place two stars in each row, column and region.
786: Place three stars in each row, column and region.
787: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb end. Digits on an arrow must sum to the digit in the arrows circle.
788: Normal sudoku rules apply, and clues outside the grid show the total of all digits in the indicated diagonal after the largest digit in it (or its first appearance).
789: Divide the grid into regions and place a number in each cell. The numbers within a region must all be the same and equal to the size of the region. Regions of equal size must not touch orthogonally, but may touch diagonally. A region may contain zero, one or more of the given numbers. In addition, it must be possible to shade some regions fully, such that two shaded regions or two unshaded regions never touch orthogonally.
791: Normal sudoku rules apply. In addition cells connected by a white dot are consecutive.
792: Shade some cells so that each circled number represents the total count of shaded cells in connected groups sharing an edge with that number. Cells with circles cannot be shaded.
793: Digits on each arrow sum to the number in the circle
794: Place two stars in each row, column and region.
796: Normal sudoku rules apply. In addition, if a grey bar is given between two adjacent cells then the two numbers in these cells must be consecutive. (Note: not all possible grey bars are given: adjacent cells without a bar may contain consecutive or non-consecutive numbers).
797: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb end.
798: Normal Sudoku Rules. The sum of the digits along the path of each arrow must equal the digit in the circled cell (digits can repeat on an arrow). Along thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb end. The sum or product of the digits in each cage must be either 20 or 21. The sum or product of the digits along the marked diagonals outside the grid must be either 20 or 21 (digits can repeat on a diagonal).
800: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb end.
801: Normal sudoku rules apply. Some numbers are given on the edges between two adjacent cells. Treating those cells as a two-digit number (reading left-to-right or downwards), the two-digit number must be a multiple of the clue (eg around a 7 clue, the two digits could be 14, 21, 28, 35, …).
802: Normal sudoku rules apply within the 9x9 grid. Digits along a thermometer must increase from the bulb end. Each digit in the 9x9 grid represents a skyscraper with a height corresponding to its value. Clues outside the 9x9 grid indicate how many skyscrapers can be seen, in total, when looking along that row or column from that direction. Taller skyscrapers block smaller skyscrapers from view.
803: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a small white dot are consecutive. Hashiwokakero rules apply, ie: Draw lines between the circles such that all circles are connected; the lines must be drawn in straight lines that are horizontal or vertical, and that do not cross any other lines or circles; at most two lines can connect a pair of circles; the number of lines connected to each circle must match the digit on that circle.
804: Normal sudoku rules apply. Any instance of neighbouring cells adding to 5 or 10 in the grid are marked by V (5) or X (10). A black dot deparates cells with a ratio of 2:1 and a white dot deparates cells with a difference of 1. Not all black and white dots are given but all V's and X's are given. The identity of tne Secret Santa is revealed late in the video.
805: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on an arrow sum up to the digit in the circle of that arrow. Clues outside the grid indicate the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. Digits can repeat along such a diagonal.
806: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along thermos increase from the bulb. Blue (renban) lines contain a sequence of consecutive, non-repeating, digits, not necessarily in the right order.
807: Normal sudoku rules apply. The square bulb and line form a 'thermometer' which must be populated by double-digit numbers. Each number starts with the tens-digit followed by the units digit (seen from the bulb end) ie tens and units digits alternate along the line. The numbers must increase moving away from the bulb.
808: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a white dot must contain consecutive digits. Cells separated by a black dot must contain digits in the ratio 1:2. Not all dots are given. The red line is a palindrome for which the start cell and end cell must be determined. The line must read the same in either direction. Neighbouring digits along the line cannot be further apart in value than two steps (so a 5 would have to be next to 3,4,5,6 or 7). For this purpose 1 and 9 are considered to be consecutive. (E.g., a 1 can have the digits 8, 9, 1, 2 or 3 as neighbours along the line.)
809: Normal sudoku rules apply. Grey circles represent odd digits. Digits along thermometers ascend or repeat from the bulb (slow thermo rules). The black and yellow lines are seven segments long.
810: Normal sudoku rules apply. A clue outside the grid shows the sum of the digits sandwiched between 1 and 9 in that row or column. Digits on a line must be between the digits in the circles connected by the line.
811: Normal sudoku rules apply. The digits in a cage sum to the number in the upper left corner. Neighbouring digits along a line have a difference of at least 5.
812: Normal sudoku rules apply. White dots separate two consecutive numbers. Black dots separate two numbers with a ratio of 1:2. Not all dots are given. Numbers outside the grid (which must be deduced) indicate the sum of the x first digits in that row or column seen from the direction of the clue, where x is the first of those digits.
813: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits along a green line must differ by at least 5. Each purple line contains a set of non-repeating consecutive digits (which can appear in any order).
814: Normal sudoku rules apply. The sum of the digits on a line within a particular 3x3 box must be the same for all of the 3x3 boxes the line passes through. eg r9c5+r8c6 = r7c7 = r6c8+r5c9
815: Normal sudoku rules apply. The two lines are equal sum lines ie The sum of the digits on a line within a particular 3x3 region must be the same for all the regions the line passes through. Different lines may have different sums. Each letter represents a unique digit. If a letter is in the grid, that digit must be put in the same cell. Clues outside of the grid are x-sums clues ie they indicate the sum of the digits of the first x cells in its row or column, where x is the digit placed in the first cell in that direction.
816: Divide the grid into regions of orthogonally connected cells so that no two regions of the same size share an edge. Enter a number into each cell equal to the size of its region. Digits on a thermometer must increase from the bulb end.
817: Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid indicate the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal.
818: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits on a green line differ by 5 or more. Divide the grid into non-overlapping rectangular regions so that each region contains exactly one small clue (found in the top left corner of some cells). Four regions cannot share the same cell corner. Digits may not repeat within a region and sum to that region's small clue. The digit placed in a small clue cell gives information about that region: 1–4: The region has a greater width than height. 5: The region is a square. 6–9: The region has a greater height than width.
819: Normal sudoku rules apply and digits on a thermometer increase from the bulb end. Digits in a cage sum to the given total and do not repeat. The clue outside the grid shows the sum of the digits on the indicated diagonal. Digits in cells joined by a white dot are consecutive, and those in cells joined by a black dot have a 1:2 ratio. Not all possible dots are given.
820: Normal sudoku rules apply, and digits on thermos increase from the bulb.
821: Normal sudoku rules apply. Identical digits cannot be a knight’s move apart. Digits along arrows sum to the number in the circle.
822: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb end. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Arrowed clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits on the indicated diagonal. The (unarrowed) 21 clue outside the grid is the sum of the digits sandwiched between the 1 and 9 in its column. Cells separated by a white dot must contain consecutive digits. Not all possible white dots are given.
823: Normal sudoku rules apply. Some cells have been pencilmarked with all of their possible candidates.
824: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Cells separated by a knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit.
825: Normal sudoku rules apply. Identical digits cannot be a knight's move apart. X joins two cells that sum to 10, V joins two cells that sum to 5. Not all X's and V's may be given. The marked diagonal sums to the given number.
826: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Cells connected by a white dot contain consecutive digits. Cells connected by a black dot contain digits in a 1:2 ratio. Not all possible dots are given.
827: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the number in the attached circle. A black dot joins two cells with a 1:2 ratio. All possible black dots are given.
828: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages cannot repeat and must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Neighbouring digits on a green line have a difference of at least 5.
829: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along a thermometer, digits must increase from the bulb end. An orange line is either 1) a sequence of non-repeating consecutive digits, in any order; or 2) a line on which neighbouring digits differ by at least 5. In r8c5, the two lines cross each other.
830: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits do not repeat on the marked diagonal. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage.
831: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Cells separated by a knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. On the diagonal (marked in blue) digits cannot repeat.
832: Normal sudoku rules apply. Identical digits cannot be a knight's move apart. Identical digits cannot be a king's move apart. Orthogonally adjacent cells may not contain digits that sum to 5 or 10.
833: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on a line must have values strictly between those of the digits in both connected circles. Shade some cells such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected and all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected. No 2x2 area may be fully shaded or fully unshaded. The circles act as "minesweeper" clues. Cells containing a circle are always unshaded, and their value is the number of shaded cells in the surrounding 3x3 area (i.e. the up to eight cells that touch the circle either orthogonally or diagonally).
834: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each purple line contains a set of non-repeating consecutive digits. These digits can appear in any order.
835: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells connected by an X contain digits summing to 10. Cells connected by a V contain digits summing to 5. Not all possible Xs and Vs are given. The clue outside the grid gives the sum of the first X cells in the corresponding column, where X is the digit in the cell nearest to the clue.
836: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a king's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. Some cells contain a two-digit clue in their corners: these clues give the sum of the cells a knight's move (in chess) away from the clued cell. Digits can repeat in these sums.
837: Normal sudoku rules apply. In the thermometer shape, digits must increase from the bulb end. The central grey 3x3 is a magic square (each of its rows/columns/main diagonals must sum to the same number). Cells connected by a knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit.
838: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue given in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat in a cage. Clues outside the grid give the sum of cells along the indicated diagonal. Inequality signs in the grid point to the lower of the two cells involved.
839: Normal sudoku rules aplly, and identical digits cannot be a chess knight’s move apart. Cages show their sums and digits increase along thermometers from the bulb to the end(s).
840: Normal sudoku rules apply, and identical digits cannot be a knight's move apart. Clues outside the grid show the sums of indicated diagonals. Lines in the grid each contain identical digits (odd for orange, blue for even). The central 3x3 box is a magic square.
841: Normal sudoku rules apply. Grey lines are palindromes, reading the same in each direction. Black dots join cells with a ratio of 1:2; white dots join cells with consecutive digits. Not all dots are given. The inequality sign 'points' at the lower digit.
842: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along the thermo, 2-digit numbers increase from the bulb - any 2-digit numbers beginning with 2 or 8 must have an odd second digit. The black dot joins digits with a 1:2 ratio
843: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grey lines are palindromes and must read the same forwards and backwards. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. A black dot separates cells containing digits with a 1:2 ratio. (Not all dots are necessarily given.)
844: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Along the indicated main diagonal (marked in blue) digits cannot repeat. Inequality signs between two cells point to the lower of the digits in those cells.
845: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Each purple line contains a set of consecutive digits. Cells separated by a black dot contain digits with a 1:2 ratio. Cells separated by a white dot contain consecutive digits. Not all possible dots are given. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. Digits may repeat along such diagonals if allowed by other rules. Digits along the thermometer must increase from the bulb end.
846: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each purple line contains a set of consecutive digits. Along a thermometer, digits must increase from the bulb end. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. Cells separated by an X contain digits summing to 10.
847: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb end. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Cells separated by an X must contain digits summing to 10. Cells separated by a white dot must contain consecutive digits. Cells separated by a black dot must contain digits in a ratio of 1:2. Not all possible dots/Xs are given. The cell with a grey circle contains an odd digit. The cell with a grey square contains an even digit.
848: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a thermometer must increase from the bulb end. A black dot separates cells containing digits with a 1:2 ratio. A white dot separates cells containing consecutive digits. Not all dots are given. Digits on a blue line must be numerically in between the two circled cells at the line's ends. The orange line contains three consecutive digits in any order. The biggest of those digits is divisible by 3. The inequality sign points to the lower of the two digits.
849: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. These digits may repeat if allowed by other rules. The coloured dominoes are clones and must contain the identical digit in the identical position. (eg r4c1=r1c7=r7c4). A black dot separates cells containing digits in a ratio of 1:2 (ie one digit must be double the other). A white dot separates cells containing consecutive digits. Not all possible dots are given. The purple line contains a set of non-repeating consecutive digits, in any order. On the grey line, the sum of the digits in box 1 is equal to the sum of the digits in box 2.
850: Normal sudoku rules apply. The marked diagonal contains 9 different digits in ascending or descending order. Along the thermometer, digits must increase from the bulb end. The sum of the digits in every possible straight triomino (orthogonal or diagonal) is divisible by 3.
851: Normal sudoku rules apply. Identical digits cannot be a chess knight's move apart. Neighboring digits along a yellow line must sum either to 5 or 10. A purple line contains a set of consecutive digits in any order. A black dot separates digits with a 1:2 ratio. Not all dots are given.
852: Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. Digits may repeat along the diagonal. Grey lines are palindromes (ie must read the same in both directions). No two cells in the same position of their box (e.g. R1C1 and R4C4) may contain the same digit.
853: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat in a cage. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow’s circled cell. Along thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb end.
854: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in the circle, and may repeat (if allowed by the other constraints).
855: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage.
856: Normal Sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits must not repeat within a cage. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle.
857: Normal Sudoku rules apply. Along thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb end.
858: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Cells separated by a black dot have a ratio of 1:2. Cells separated by a white dot have a difference of 1. Not all dots are given.
859: Normal sudoku rules apply. Grey lines are palindromes and must read the same in both directions. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. Digits may repeat along such a diagonal (if allowed by other rules). No two cells in the same position relative to their box (eg r1c1 and r4c4) may contain the same digit.
860: Totally normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits must not repeat in a cage. There is exactly one cage in the grid where the cage is broken ie either the sum is incorrect or digits are repeated or both. The pink lines are "incomplete arrows". The digit on one end of the line is the sum of the other digits on the same line.
861: (Totally) Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. A cell containing an opaque grey square must contain an even digit. A cell containing an opaque grey circle must contain an odd digit.
862: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along thermometers, digits increase from the bulb end.
863: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage.
864: Normal sudoku rules apply (ie place the digits 1-9 once each in every row, column & 3x3 box). Digits on a grey line must be between the digits in the circles at either end of the line.
865: Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a one-cell wide snake of orthogonally connected cells which doesn't touch itself orthogonally; the path begins in r9c1 and ends in r9c7. Adjacent snake cells must differ by at least 5. A digit in a circle is equal to the number of snake cells in the (up to) 9 surrounding cells, including itself. The snake must visit each circle.
866: Normal sudoku rules apply. Normal Yin Yang rules apply (ie shade some cells in the grid such that all shaded cells are connected and all unshaded cells are connected. No 2x2 box may be fully shaded or fully unshaded.) Clues outside the grid give the sum of the first continuous block of shaded cells seen from that direction.
867: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by either a knight's or king's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. The grey cells must all contain different digits and form a magic square (ie each row/column/main diagonal of grey cells must sum to the same number).
868: Normal sudoku rules apply, and marked diagonals multiply to the product shown. Marked regions, which may include repeats, have a product of 24. Apart from the given digits, the two-digit numbers 24, 48 and 96 do not appear in any row.
869: Normal sudoku rules apply and clues outside the grid give the sum of the first X digits seen in the row/column, given that X is the first digit seen from the clue. The grid must be filled with the 12 different pentominoes (allowing rotation/reflection), all of which cross a box boundary. Digits in shapes cannot repeat, and sum to an odd number for pentominoes, and an even number for tetrominoes. The three placed bar lines act as shape boundaries.
870: Normal Sudoku rules apply, and cages show the sums of their digits. Digits along arrows sum to the number in the circle.
871: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is completely covered by 17 killer snakes! One snake of length 9, and two snakes each of length 1 through 8. A snake is 1 cell wide, and has exactly one single bend somewhere along its length (except the 1- and 2-length snakes). Numbers don't repeat within a snake. The nine given numbers in the corners give the total sum of digits in the snake that occupies that cell. These 'killer clues' apply to nine differently-sized snakes. Find the snakes and solve the sudoku.
872: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. The grey lines are palindromes (ie they must read the same in both directions). The indicated diagonal sums to 45 - digits may repeat along this diagonal. Cells a "camel move" apart may not contain the same digit. A camel move is like an elongated knight in chess - it makes a {1,3} jump.
873: Normal sudoku rules apply. In the finished grid, every cell will be part of a group of orthogonally connected cells that share the same parity (ie an odd or even group comprising every orthogonally connected cell of the same parity). Such a parity group can be as small as a single cell, or large enough to span multiple boxes and include repeating digits. Corner clues give the sum of all cells in the parity group containing that cell. Black dots separate cells with a 1:2 ratio. Not all possible black dots are given.
874: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along thermometers, digits increase from the bulb end. Digits in column 1 indicate the column in which the digit 1 appears in that row. (eg if r4c1 is a 6, r4c6 is a 1). The applies to columns 5 and 9 with the digits 5 and 9 respectively.
875: Normal sudoku rules apply. There are two snakes in the grid, the endpoints of which are given (as circles). Snakes cannot touch themselves or each other orthogonally but they can touch diagonally. Adjacent digits along a snake must differ by at least 5. The non-snake cells form several regions. In regions, digits cannot repeat. Some region totals have been indicated by small corner clues. The given digits indicate the number of snake cells within the 3x3 square centered on that digit.
876: Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a "simple loop" in the grid ie a single closed loop that visits all cells except the ones containing a 5. The loop must go horizontally or vertically from cell to cell without branching or intersecting itself. Grey-cell clues outside the grid give the sum of the all the cells between the border and the 5 in that row/column containing straight line segments. White-cell clues outside the grid give the sum of all cells between the border and the 5 in that row/column containing corner segments.
877: Normal sudoku rules apply. Black dots join digits with a 1:2 ratio; white dots join consecutive digits. Not all dots are shown. There are 18 'crust cells' in the grid, 2 in each row and column. Crust cells can have any value, and can differ in each row and column. An outside clue gives the sum of the digits between the crust cells in that row or column.
878: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a white dot must contain consecutive digits. Cells separated by a black dot contain digits in a 1:2 ratio. Digits in cages cannot repeat and sum to the indicated total. However, one of the digits from 1 to 9 is an imposter. Whenever that digit appears in a cage, it counts as any value from 1 to 9 towards the cage total. This value can be different for each cage that the imposter appears in.
879: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages do not include repeat digits, and sum to the indicated total. Digits along an arrow sum to the number in the circle.
880: Normal sudoku rules apply. Neighbouring digits along a green line differ by at least 5. Neighbouring digits along an orange lines differ by at least 4. The digits in the indicated cage sum to 18.
881: Normal sudoku and killer rules apply. Cells outside the grid give the sum of the digits between 1 and 9 in that row or column.
882: Cages contain different numbers adding to sums which, if given, have their digits shown as Even, Odd or Unknown. All coloured cages contain consecutive runs of numbers in some order; white cages don’t (but could be e.g. 1278). The blue cell is even; normal sudoku rules apply.
883: Thermo sudoku rules apply. Coloured lines are palindromes; of the red and purple lines, one's sum is more than 35, the other's less than 15. Ignore the green shapes, which represent an 'accolade message' for Mark.
884: Normal sudoku rules apply, and digits increase along thermometers from the bulb to the end. Clues outside the grid total the digits between the 1 and the 9 in that row/column, and the value of the letters used are to be deduced.
885: Normal sudoku rules apply, and clues outside the grid show the sum of digits sandwiched between the 1 and the 9 in that row/column. Identical digits cannot be a knight's move apart.
886: Normal sudoku rules apply. Normal killer sudoku rules apply (ie in cages digits must sum to the clue given in the top left of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage).
887: Normal sudoku rules apply except that the regions are irregular. Additionally, a snake has to be drawn into the grid. The head and tail of the snake are in the two cells with the grey circles. The snake may not touch itself orthogonally, but it can touch itself diagonally. The clues outside the grid indicate the sum of the digits located on the snake. Considering "Snake" and "non-snake" as two colors, the given digits show how many cells orthogonally connected to the given are of a different color to the color of the given cell itself. All such possible digits are shown. Givens can be on or off the snake.
888: Normal Sudoku Rules apply. 10 different pentominos must be placed in the grid, not over given digits. Each pentomino touches exactly two other pentominos orthogonally and they form a loop, so a path could be traced orthogonally around all 10, but each pentomino may only touch another on one edge of one cell. Pentominos act as killer cages in which digits may not repeat, and corner clues in the grid indicate the sum of the pentomino’s digit or its shape.
889: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits sum to the small clue in the upper left corner of the cage. Two cells separated with an X must sum to 10; two cells separated by a V must sum to 5. NOT all XV clues are shown. Digits on the arrow sum to the number in the oval read from top to bottom.
890: Normal Sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by an X sum to 10. Cells separated by a V sum to 5. All XV clues are given. Digits along thermometers must increase from the bulb end.
891: Normal Sudoku rules apply. Digits cannot repeat in cages, which show their sums. The grey square marks an even digit.
892: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. Cells that appear in the same relative position in their 3x3 box must not contain the same digit. eg the digit in r1c3 cannot appear in r7c6 as this would cause a repear in the North-East corner cell of the 3x3 boxes.
893: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits cannot repeat on the marked diagonals. Digits cannot repeat in cages, which sometimes show their sums.
894: Normal Sudoku rules apply. The given filled circles indicate the start of a palindrome line (with the same order of digits from either end) The number in the circle indicates the sum of all the digits on the palindrome line. The arrows indicate the starting direction of the line. Empty circles are the ends of lines. The line paths and lengths must be discovered by the solver. Lines can cross each other but can not share cells. No digit repeats on a palindrome more than once.
895: Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells in the grid. Those cells are part of the "coral". The rest of the cells are "water". All coral cells are orthogonally connected. All bodies of water connect to the edge of the grid. No 2x2 is entirely water or entirely coral. Digits do not repeat within cages, and the sum of the coral cells within each cage must equal the sum of the water cells within that cage. The digit in a circle gives the number of cells within its cage which match its colour (coral or water). The total includes itself.
896: Normal sudoku rules apply. Where arrows point from the same cell, the sum of the digits along the two indicated diagonals (from that cell to the edge of the grid) is the same.
897: Normal sudoku rules apply. The black dot joins digits in a 1:2 ratio (ie one digit is double the other). Not all dots are given. The sum of the digits along a grey line is equal to the sum of the digits in the circles at either end of the line. Shade some cells such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected and all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected. No 2x2 area may be fully shaded or fully unshaded. The circles act as 'minesweeper' clues. Ie Cells containing a circle are always unshaded, and their value is the number of shaded cells in the surrounding 3x3 area (i.e. the up to eight cells that touch the circle either orthogonally or diagonally).
898: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits cannot repeat on each main diagonal (marked in blue). Digits along arrows sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. Digits may repeat along such a diagonal if allowed by other rules.
899: Normal Sudoku rules apply. A digit in a circle must appear in at least one of the four cells surrounding that circle. Every even digit must see at least one identical digit via a knight's move (in chess).
900: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each main diagonal (marked in blue) must contain the digits 1 to 9 once each. Cells separated by a black dot must contain digits with a 1:2 ratio. Not all possible dots are given. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. Digits may repeat along such diagonals if allowed by the other rules.
901: Normal sudoku rules apply. For each line, digits on that line have an equal sum within each box the line passes through. Cells separated by a white dot contain consecutive digits. Cells separated by a black dot contain digits in a 1:2 ratio.
902: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grey highlighted regions contain the digits 1 to 9 once each. Cells separated by a knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle.
903: Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw two closed loops in the grid that don't intersect themselves or each other. A loop travels horizontally or vertically between cell centres. Each loop must be situated entirely on one side of the highlighted diagonal and is a mirror image of the other with respect to that diagonal. A digit in a grey cell gives the number of cells in its row (or column, because of the symmetry) that are NOT part of either loop. Adjacent digits along either loop must have a difference of at least 5.
904: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grey line in the central box is a thermometer. Digits along that thermometer must increase from the bulb to the tip, but the positions of the bulb and the tip are hidden. In the outer three rings, the sum of the digits along a ring between two 9s must always be the same throughout the puzzle. For the avoidance of doubt, those two 9s could be the same 9 if a ring has only a single 9 in it.
905: Normal sudoku rules apply. On the marked diagonal, digits cannot repeat. A clue outside the grid gives the sum of the first N digits from that direction, where N is the first of those digits. In this puzzle, all clues outside the grid are the same number X, which has to be determined by the solver.
906: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells marked with a circle contain an odd digit; cells marked with a square contain an even digit. Two neighbouring digits along a green line have a difference of at least 5. You must put this pattern of clues into the grid 7 times: □ ⟋ □ ⟋ 5 ○ □ ○ ○ The patterns may overlap with each other or the given clues. If there is an overlap all clues must still be valid. Digits may repeat within a pattern. You may not rotate or mirror the pattern or put it partially off the grid.
907: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in column 1 indicate the column in which the digit 1 appears in that row (eg if r4c1 is a 6, r4c6 is a 1). The same is true of column 5 and the digit 5; and column 9 and the digit 9. Cells separated by a white dot contain consecutive digits. Cells separated by a black dot contains digits in a ratio of 1:2 (ie one digit is double the other). Not all possible dots are given. Digits may not repeat on either of the main (blue) diagonals.
908: Put the digits 1-3 twice each and the digits 4-6 once each in every row, column and 3x3 box. Cells separated by a king's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. Digits in the cage sum to the small clue in the top left corner of that cage.
909: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits may not repeat on either of the main diagonals (marked in blue). Digits on each purple line form a set of non-repeating consecutive digits, which can be in any order. Neighboring digits on a green line have a difference of at least 5 OR a sum of at most 5.
910: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on a purple line form a set of consecutive, non-repeating digits in any order. Along thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb end. Adjacent digits on a green line must differ by at least 5.
911: Place the digits 1-8 once each in every row, column and region. A digit in a cell with a circle must be odd. A digit in a cell with a square must be even. There are invisible thermometers in this grid. Every empty cell (the 6x6 in the center) gets visited by one of those thermometers. Digits on a thermometer increase from the bulb on one end to the tip on the other end. The thermometers are orthogonally connected and don't fork or overlap. A thermometer may have length 1 if it's bulb and tip are the same cell. The difference between bulb and tip must be unique for each thermometer.
912: Normal sudoku rules apply. Identical digits cannot appear a chess king's move away from each other. Along thermometers, digits increase from the bulb to the ends.
913: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a thermometer increase from the bulb end.
914: Fill the grid with digits 1-6, such that each digit appears exactly once in each row, column and marked 3x3 box. There will be 3 blanks in each row, column and 3x3 box. Wherever two vertically adjacent cells are occupied by digits, the top digit must always be greater than the bottom one.
915: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on outside of grid give the sum of the groups of cells in row or column.
916: Place given dominoes into the grid.
917: Draw a single closed loop passing through some empty cells in the grid. The grid contains some bordered/coloured cells that cannot be part of the loop. Black cells must be outside the loop. White bordered cells must be inside the loop. Numbers and arrows
918: Draw a snake in the grid whose head and tail are given by the circles. The nine white areas must contain 1 to 9 cells with the numbers from 1 up to the size of the region.
919: Shade cells to create a single orthogonally-connected group of black cells. No 2×2 region can contain all black cells. Numbers outside the grid represent the groups of consecutive black cells in that row/column in order, either from left to right or from top to bottom. A question mark (?) represents a single group of consecutive black cells whose size is unknown (but cannot be zero); an asterisk (*) represents any number of unknown groups of black cells, including none at all.
920: Normal sudoku rules apply, and digits in cages sum to the total shown, including no repeats. Digits in marked diagonals sum to the totals shown, and can include repeats. 3, 1 and 4 can never be in neighbouring cells (orthogonally), and the unshown totals of cages and diagonals can never be made up of only 3s, 1s and 4s.
921: Shade some empty cells grey to create a single connected wall. The shaded cells cannot form a 2x2 square anywhere in the grid. Numbers in a circled cell indicate the length of consecutive shaded blocks in the neighboring cells. If there is more than one number in a circled cell, then there must be at least one white (unshaded) cell between the grey cell groups. Also, all unshaded cells of the grid should contain all digits from 1 to 7 in each row and column. All cells marked with circles should contain at least one digit (and therefore they are not shaded). The digits in circles are valid clues for Tapa and pencilmark clues for sudoku. You should place one or more digits in the empty circles but you cannot make additions to given circle clues. All possible circled cells may not be given (ie there may be some cells without circles that are valid clues for both the Tapa and sudoku.)
922: Normal sudoku rules apply. 10 cities have been affected by two major earthquakes (7.7 and 7.6 on the Richter Scale) in Turkey. Place each city’s name along a grey line, one letter per cell. For lines without arrows, the city can be read in either direction, otherwise it must read in the arrow's direction. The sudoku works as follows: If a cell’s letter is included in the spelling of one of the digits 1 to 9 (eg ONE, TWO, etc), such a digit is a valid candidate for that cell. If a cell’s letter is not included in the spelling of ANY of the digits 1 to 9, any digit can be placed in that cell. One of the red (earthquake) lines is 7.7 and the other 7.6. The cities to be placed are: ADANA, ADIYAMAN, DIYARBAKIR, GAZIANTEP, HATAY, KAHRAMANMARAS, KILIS, MALATYA, OSMANIYE and SANLIURFA.
923: Normal sudoku rules apply. The digits on the arrow path add to the digit in the circled cell. Digits can repeat on the arrow if allowed by the other rules.
924: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage.
925: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each grey and red line contains a set of consecutive, non-repeating digits, in any order. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. Digits may repeat along such a diagonal (if allowed by the other rules).
926: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb end. Cells separated by a knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit.
927: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage.
928: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Odd digits (1,3,5,7,9) can appear consecutively for more than two cells vertically but not more than two cells horizontally. Even digits (2,4,6,8) can appear consecutively for more than two cells horizontally but not more than two cells vertically.
929: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits along a green line must have a difference of at least 5. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage.
930: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow’s circle. Shade some cells so that all shaded cells form one orthogonally connected area. Arrow circles are the clues for a “Canal View” puzzle. Ie These clues cannot be shaded, and represent the number of shaded cells connected in a straight line horizontally or vertically to the clue. No 2x2 region may be entirely shaded. Additionally, digits cannot repeat within unshaded regions.
931: Normal sudoku rules apply. In each cage, at least one of the following conditions must apply: the sum of the digits is a square number (ie 1,4,9,16,25,36); and/or the sum of the even digits equals the sum of the odd digits. Digits cannot repeat within a cage.
932: Normal sudoku rules apply. For each line, digits on the line have an equal sum N within each 3x3 box it passes through. If a line passes through the same box more than once, each individual segment of such a line within that box sums to N separately. eg R1c4+r2c4+r3c4+r3c5 = r4c5+r4c6 = r3c6+r3c5+r2c5.
933: Normal sudoku rules apply. Some of the cells must be coloured grey so that all grey cells (the walls) are orthogonally connected to the edge and all other (green) cells form an orthogonally connected area (the cave). Grey cells may not form 2x2 blocks. A number in the top left corner of a cell indicates the sum of the digits that are “seen” from this cell looking to the north, south, east, and west. The cell with the clue counts once in this sum. Walls obstruct the view. A cell with a clue must be part of the cave. Within the field of vision of a clue, digits may not repeat. In addition, grey walls act as “Region Sum lines”: Meaning that each wall (ie group of connected grey squares) must visit at least two boxes and the sum of the digits in each box must be equal.
934: Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells using the following rules: cells containing clues in their top left corner must be unshaded (white); the digit in the cell with a “clue” in its top left corner gives the number of white cells orthogonally connected to that clue cell; the clue in the top left corner gives the sum of all the digits in that white area; digits cannot repeat within a white area; each area of white cells is separated by black cells; the black cells are linked to form a continuous orthogonally-connected wall; black cells cannot form a 2x2 square; and all possible clues have been given. Note: the given clues are NOT necessarily located in the leftmost cell of the highest row of that white area.
935: Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells so that the outside clues indicate the sums of the contiguous shaded cells in that row or column. A number indicates the sum of a complete contiguous block. A question mark (?) indicates that a contiguous block sum to a single-digit number and a double question mark (??) indicates that a contiguous block sums to a double-digit number. An asterisk implies that any number of blocks may exist, including zero. The clues are provided in the correct order (left-to-right, or top-to-bottom), and there is at least one unshaded cell between each pair of clued blocks. The shaded cells form a single orthogonally connected group. No 2×2 area within the grid can be totally shaded.
936: Normal sudoku rules apply, and cages show the sum of their digits, which cannot include repeats. EASY VERSION rules at the bottom of this description field.
937: Normal sudoku rules apply, and identical digits cannot be a knight’s move apart. Cages show the sums of their digits, which cannot include repeats.
938: Normal sudoku rules apply. Two cells directly connected by a line must have a difference of at least 5. The inequality sign 'points' to the lower of the two digits.
939: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow’s circle. The grey squares are even numbers. The grey circles are odd numbers.
940: Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. Digits along such a diagonal may repeat if allowed by other rules. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage.
941: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits cannot repeat in cages, which show their sums. Identical digits cannot be within a king's move of each other (i.e. cannot touch diagonally).
942: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits along arrows sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Cells separated by a white dot must contain consecutive digits. Not all possible dots are given.
943: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Each grey line is a palindrome ie the string of digits on it reads the same in both directions (eg 1374731).
944: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages must sum to the total in the top left corner, if given. Clues outside the grid show the sums of the indicated diagonals, which may contain repeats, BUT the numbers for these clues are hidden in the cages as 2-digit numbers, reading left-to-right or downwards. One clue outside the grid maps to exactly one cage and vice versa. Digits along the thermo increase from the bulb.
945: Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. These digits may repeat if allowed by other rules. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage.
946: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an indicated diagonal from each question-mark may repeat and sum up to a two-digit number hidden in a killer cage (read from left to right or downwards). One killer cage belongs to exactly one diagonal clue and vice versa. Each diagonal clue is only valid in ONE of the two possible ways. White dots between two cells indicate that those cells contain consecutive digits. Not all dots are given.
947: Normal sudoku rules apply. A number outside the grid shows the sum of the digits sandwiched between the 1 and the 9 in that row or column. A purple line contains a set of consecutive digits in any order, without repeats.
948: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow in the grid must sum to the digit in its circle. Except: The circles and the arrow lines are separated. One circle belongs to exactly one arrow line and vice versa. Digits along the two indicated diagonals can repeat and sum to X and Y. The sum of these diagonals (X+Y) equals the sum of the digits in the circles.
949: Normal Sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage.
950: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each number placed into the grid represents the height of a building. Clues outside the grid tell you how many buildings can be 'seen' along the indicated diagonal when looking from that direction; buildings which are shorter or the same height are hidden from view. For example, a 4 clue along a 7-cell diagonal might be satisfied by 3141592 or 4455567.
951: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along thermometers, digits increase from the bulb to the end. The clue outside the grid indicates the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal (40). Digits on the blue line have an equal sum N (to be determined by the solver) within each box it passes through. In the centre box the two segments of the line sum to N separately.
952: Normal sudoku rules apply. A purple line must contain a set of non-repeating consecutive digits (which can appear in any order). Adjacent digits along a green line must differ by at least 5. Cells separated by a black dot must contain digits in a 1:2 ratio (ie one digit must be double the other). In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow’s (grey) circle. Digits along a thermometer must increase from the bulb end. A digit in a black circle must appear in at least one of the four cells surrounding that circle. Digits along a blue line have an equal sum within each 3x3 box the line passes through.
953: Divide the grid into polyominoes so that polyominoes of the same size (ie with the same number of cells) don't share an edge. Each cell contains a number equal to its polyomino's size. For each line, one circle contains an odd number, and the other an even. The odd circle gives the amount of odd numbers on the line (excluding itself), while the even circle gives the amount of even numbers (excluding itself). If an odd number is in a cell with an arrow, it gives the amount of odd numbers in that direction (excluding itself) and if the number is even, it gives the amount of even numbers (excluding itself).
954: Normal sudoku rules apply, and whenever a digit is larger than the one on its right, a dot joins the two cells, black if the difference is odd and red if the difference is even.
955: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages sum to the total given, EXCEPT: for each given cage total, one such cage is telling the truth and sums to the given number, but the other is lying and does not. The solver must detect which cages are telling lies.
956: Nonogram rules apply: clues outside the grid give the lengths of sequences of coloured cells in the row/column. Normal sudoku rules apply. Coloured cells are either higher than each neighbour or lower than each neighbour, and have no consecutive neighbours (a neighbour is a cell sharing an edge).
957: Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid show the sum of the indicated diagonal, which may include repeat digits.
958: Normal sudoku rules apply. The marked diagonal contains no repeated digits. The grey lines are palindromes, reading the same each way. Clues outside the grid mark diagonals, which sum to a 2-digit number given by the first two digits in the direction of the arrow.
959: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along thermometers, digits increase from the bulb to the tip.
960: Normal sudoku rules apply. The digits in white circles must appear in at least one of the four cells touching the circle. The digit in the grey cell must be higher than its four orthogonal neighbours. Additionally every edge of the cube sums to the same two-digit number and this number is given in the grid by the 3 two-cell cages (all of which are filled identically), with the tens digit as the top number and the units digit below that.
961: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along thermometers, digits increase from the bulb. Purple lines are palindromes, which read the same both ways. A number in a circle must appear in at least one of the four surrounding cells.
962: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits along arrows sum to the digit in that arrow’s circle. In large circles (without arrows) the indicated digit must appear in one of the surrounding cells. Cells separated by a small white dot must contain consecutive digits.
963: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages add up to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage, if given. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. The main diagonal (in blue) must include the digits from 1 to 9 once each. Digits within the white circles must appear at least once in the four cells touching the circle. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow’s circle. The two digits on the two-cell-palindrome grey line must be the same. The cell with the grey square must contain an even digit. Cells separated by an X must contain digits that sum to 10. Black dots separate cells containing digits with a ratio of 1:2. White dots separate cells containing consecutive digits.
964: Normal sudoku rules apply. Identical digits cannot be a knight’s move apart. Consecutive digits cannot be (orthogonal) neighbours. A number in a white circle must appear at least once in the four surrounding cells. A number outside the grid appears in the first four cells of that row/column from that direction.
965: Normal sudoku rules apply. The numbers in white circles must appear in the four surrounding cells. Cells separated by an X contain digits summing to 10. Cells separated by a white dot must contain consecutive digits. Not all possible Xs/dots are given.
966: Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid are either Sandwich, X-Sums or Little Killer, one type each being red, blue and green - grey clues may be any of the types. Sandwich: the sum of the digits between the 1 and the 9 in that row/column is 15; X-Sums: the first X digits from that direction sum to 15, where X is the first digit; Little Killer: 15 is the sum of a diagonal pointing away from the clue, which may include repeats.
967: Normal Sudoku rules apply. Grey circles indicate odd numbers, grey squres indicate even numbers. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. The digits in the cage sum to the cage total. The digits of the cage total indicate how many odd and even digits are in the cage (in no particular order).
968: Normal sudoku rules apply, and numbers shown in cages are the sums of the digits in those cages. For one cage, the sum is not shown.
969: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells containing a grey circle must contain an odd digit. Cells containing a grey square must contain an even digit. Digits in a cage may not repeat. The digits in the cage sum to the cage total. The digits of the cage total indicate how many odd and even digits are in the cage (in no particular order).
970: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each grey line contains a set of consecutive, non-repeating digits, in any order. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. Digits may repeat on such a diagonal if allowed by other rules.
971: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on a line must fall 'outside' the range of their yellow endpoints (eg endpoints of 1 and 8 only allow 9 on the line connecting them.) Each endpoint value must differ by at least 4 from other directly connected endpoints. Digits on a line may repeat if allowed by other rules.
972: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. Digits in column 1 indicate the column in which the digit 1 appears in that row (eg if r4c1 is a 6, r4c6 is a 1). The same is true of column 5 and the digit 5, and column 9 and the digit 9.
973: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Additionally, the digit in an arrow's circle will repeat in a cell pointed at by that circle's arrow tip. This repeat can be one or more cells away from the arrow tip (but not the arrow tip cell itself).
974: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow in the grid sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. Digits can repeat along such diagonals if allowed by other rules.
975: Place the numbers 1-9 once each in every row and column and region. Regions must be determined by the solver and each consists of nine orthogonally connected cells. Every arrow in the grid corresponds to an “arrow total” in one of the bulbs (ie the digits on that arrow sum to the digit in that arrow’s bulb). Both the arrow and the corresponding bulb have to be in the same region. The direction of the arrow is of no importance.
976: Place the digits 1-9 once each in every row, column and region. The nine regions are to be constructed by the solver and each contains 9 orthogonally connected cells. Additionally every region contains cells from exactly two cages and cells in one cage are distributed across exactly two regions. In cages, digits sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage.
977: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells containing a grey square must contain even digits. Along a red line, digits must alternate parity (so, if the first digit is odd, the next digit must be even, etc). The sum of the digits along a blue line must be the same total N within each 3x3 box the line passes through.
978: Normal sudoku rules apply; digits along arrows sum to the number in the circle.
979: Normal sudoku rules apply; digits along arrows sum to the number in the circle.
980: Normal sudoku rules apply, and digits increase along arrows, in the direction of the arrow, and sum to the 1- or 2-digit number in the circle or pill. 2-digit numbers always read left-to-right or downwards.
981: Normal sudoku rules apply. Numbers along the green line must alternate between odd and even digits. The black dots connect cells with a 2:1 ratio. The white dots connect cells with a difference of one. Not all black and white dots are shown.
982: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a thermometer must increase from the bulb end. Cells connected by an X or V must sum to ten or five, respectively. Not all Xs and Vs are shown. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits, which may repeat, along the indicated diagonal.
983: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along the green Christmas tree line alternate between odd and even numbers. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in the connecting circle. (The bottom two arrows represent garland and the top arrow is a star.) Digits connected by a white Kropki dot must be consecutive. (These represent tree lights.) The digit in the large quadruple circle must be in at least one of the four connecting cells. (This represents a large ornament.) And the gray square at the base of the tree is an even digit. (This represents the tree stand.)
984: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on a gray line must be between the digits in the circled ends. A clue outside the grid gives the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal, which may include repeats. Digits connected by an X sum to ten. Digits connected by a V sum to five. Digits connected by a white circle must be consecutive. Not all X’s, V’s and white circles are shown. Digits along the blue diagonal cannot repeat and must alternate between odd and even.
985: Normal sudoku rules apply. The digits along an arrow must sum to the number in the connecting pill (read left-to right or downwards) or circle. Each number in the four highlighted pills must be a perfect square, none of which can be repeated among those four pills. Digits connected by a white dot must be consecutive. Not all white dots are shown.
986: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along thermometers must increase from the bulb end. Digits connected by a black dot have a 2 to 1 ratio. Digits connected by a white dot are consecutive. Not all black and white dots are shown. Any two cells separated by a chess knight’s move cannot contain the same digit.
987: Normal sudoku rules apply. Exactly one of the nine 3 x 3 boxes is a minimum square (i.e., the digits in its three rows, three columns and two diagonals sum to the smallest number possible). Exactly one of the nine 3 x 3 boxes is a maximum square (i.e., the digits in its three rows, three columns and two diagonals sum to the largest number possible). Digits connected by an X sum to ten. Digits connected by a V sum to five. Not all Xs and Vs are shown. Digits in gray squares are even.
988: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits within a cage may not repeat and sum to the number in its upper left-hand corner. Digits along an arrow sum to the number in the connected circle. Digits along a thermometer increase from the bulb end. Digits along each marked diagonal may not repeat.
989: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a thermometer must increase from the bulb end. Digits along the marked diagonal may not repeat. Digits within a cage may not repeat and must sum to the number in the top left corner. Digits within the four highlighted regions may not repeat.
990: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells joined by an X sum to 10; cells joined by a V sum to 5. Digits increase along thermometers from the bulb. A clue outside the grid gives the sum of the digits in the indicated diagonal.
991: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the number in the connecting circle. Digits connected by a black dot have a 2:1 ratio. Digits connected by a white dot are consecutive. A grey square contains an even digit. Digits along a marked diagonal may not repeat.
992: Normal sudoku rules apply, and clues outside the grid show the sum of digits sandwiched between the 1 and the 9 in that row/column.
993: Normal sudoku and killer rules apply.
994: Normal sudoku rules apply. The clues outside the grid show the sum of the first X digits from that direction, where X is the first of those digits.
996: Normal sudoku rules apply. Japanes sum rules apply.
997: Each row and column contains digits 1-5 and two blanks. Clues in the grid show the sum of surrounding cells. Clues outside the grid show the sum of the digits between the blanks in that row/column.
998: Divide the grid along the dotted lines into regions called polyominoes so that no two polyominoes with the same area share an edge. Inside some cells are numbers; each number must represent the area of the polyomino it belongs to. A polyomino may contain zero, one, or more of the given numbers. In addition, the numbers in the cages must form these hands in any order: four of a kind, straight, full house, three of a kind, one pair, one pair. Use the conversion 1 = ace, 11 = jack, 12 = queen, 13 = king.
999: Shade exactly four connected cells in each outlined region, to form an L, I, T, or S tetromino, so that the following conditions are true: (1) All shaded cells are connected with each other; (2) No 2×2 group of cells can be entirely shaded grey; (3) When two tetrominoes in adjacent regions share an edge, they must not be of the same type (L, I, T, or S), regardless of rotations or reflections. [See the video if you are unsure what an L, I, T or S tetromino looks like.]
1000: Enter a single digit from 1 to 9 into each white cell so that the sum of digits in each Across entry equals the value in grey to the left of the entry (if given), and the sum of digits in each Down entry equals the value in grey above the entry (if given). No digit may be repeated within a single entry. A white circle between two cells shows that the digits in those cells are consecutive (i.e., they differ by 1). A black circle shows that the digit in one of the cells has twice the value of the other. If there is no circle between adjacent cells, neither of these properties holds. (Note: between 1 and 2, either a white or a black circle can be given.)
1001: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. The digits on a line must increase from one end to the other.
1002: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along thermometers, digits increase from the bulb. Clues outside the grid show the sum of digits between the 1 and the 9 in that row/column.
1003: Normal sudoku rules apply. Neighbouring digits on an orange line have a difference of at least 5. Digits on a blue line form a set of consecutive, non-repeating digits in any order.
1004: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells with opaque grey circles must contain odd digits. Cells with opaque grey squares must contain even digits. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle.
1005: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along thermometers, digits increase from the bulb end. Each purple line must contain a set of non-repeating consecutive digits, which can appear in any order.
1006: Normal sudoku rules apply. The digits in two cells joined by a white dot have a fixed difference; those joined by a black dot have a fixed ratio (the ratio is not necessarily an integer, it could be any rational number); those joined by a blue dot have a fixed sum; those joined by a red dot have a fixed product.
1007: Normal sudoku rules apply. ie Place the digits 1-9 once each in every row, column and 3x3 box. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage (if given). Digits cannot repeat within a cage.
1008: Normal sudoku rules apply. (ie place the digits 1-9 once each into every row, column & 3x3 box). In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage.
1009: Normal sudoku rules apply. Neighbouring digits on a green line have a difference of at least 5. Cells separated by an X contain digits summing to 10. Not all possible Xs are shown.
1010: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb end. Each purple line contains a set of non-repeating consecutive digits. These digits can appear in any order.
1011: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each purple line contains a set of non-repeating consecutive digits. These digits can appear in any order. Neighbouring digits on a green line have a difference of at least 5.
1012: Normal sudoku rules apply. The digits in a cage sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. Neighbouring digits along a green line have a difference of at least 5.
1013: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits within a cage must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage (if given). Digits cannot repeat within a cage.
1014: Normal sudoku rules apply. Thermometers act like accelerometers: the difference between two consecutive digits on a thermo must increase from the bulb end (e.g. 1-2-4-9 is a valid thermo but 1-2-3-9 is not).
1015: Normal sudoku rules apply. A clue outside the grid shows the sum of the indicated diagonal, which may include repeat digits.
1016: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb end. Along blue lines, successive digits must differ by at least 6.
1017: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Purple lines must contain a string of consecutive digits, in any order.
1018: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits may repeat in cages and along indicated diagonals. Every given clue should be read as a "look-and-say" number. Each number says which digits are in the respective cage or on the respective diagonal. Eg if a cage clue is 1221, this means there is one 2 and two 1s in the cage. If a diagonal says 33 then there are three 3s along the diagonal.
