1019: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along the thermometer, digits increase from the bulb. Digits next to each other along a green line must have a difference of at least 5.
1020: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb end. Digits along arrows must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. The cages in the grid are either killer cages or look-and-say cages (or both). It is up to the solver to determine which cage is which. In a killer cage, digits cannot repeat and must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. In a Look-and-Say cage, digits CAN repeat and the small clue in the top left corner should be read as a look-and-say number (ie it says which digits are in that cage). For example, if a look-and-say cage has the clue "12" then it means there is one 2 in the cage. If it has the clue "33" then it means there are three 3s in the cage.
1021: Normal sudoku rules apply. Diagonals and cages are NOT standard. Digits MAY repeat in cages and along indicated diagonals. The numbers should be read as a "look-and-say number". Each number says which digits are in the respective cage or on the respective diagonal. For example, if a cage clue is 1221, this means there is 1 two and 2 ones in the cage. If a diagonal says 33, then there are 3 threes along the diagonal.
1022: Normal sudoku rules apply. Successive digits along the green line must differ by at least 5. Each marked diagonal (in blue) must contain the digits 1 to 9 exactly once each. The inequality sign points to the smaller of the two digits.
1023: Normal sudoku rules apply. Neighbouring digits along a green line must differ by at least 5. Digits in cages cannot repeat and must sum to the number in the top left corner of the cage.
1024: Normal sudoku rules apply. Purple lines and white dots connect two digits that are consecutive. Black dots connect two digits that are in a 1:2 ratio. Not all dots or lines are necessarily given.
1025: Normal sudoku rules apply. Fog is covering the grid. Your task is to remove the fog by placing correct digits in the grid (no guessing is required). Digits along a grey arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Along blue thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb end. Cells separated by a white dot must contain consecutive digits. Cells separated by a black dot contain digits in a ratio of 1:2 (one digit is double the other). Not all dots are necessarily given.
1026: 1 to 9 must appear in each row, column, and 9-cell region. The grey square indicates an even digit. Any two orthogonally adjacent digits must have a difference of two or less.
1027: Normal sudoku rules apply. Entropy: The low digits (1, 2, 3), middle digits (4, 5, 6), and high digits (7, 8, 9) form three different groups. Every 2x2 region within the cage must contain at least one digit from each group. Climbing Ropes: Adjacent digits along orange lines must have a difference of 3 or less.
1028: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells with grey squares must contain even digits. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle - except all arrows are hidden! Each circle has exactly one hidden arrow that is 3 cells long and extends from its circle in a straight line, either horizontally or vertically. Arrows may not cross, overlap or share cells with other arrows/circles.
1029: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each cage must extend into an orthogonally adjacent cell so that it contains a total of three digits (ie dominoes become trominoes!). Cages cannot extend into the same cell or into other cages (ie cages do not overlap). The small clue in the top left corner of a cage gives the sum of all three of the digits it contains. Digits cannot repeat within cages.
1030: Normal sudoku rules apply. (Within the 9x9 grid, place the digits 1 to 9 in every row, column and 3x3 box). Each of the ten cells outside the 9x9 grid must contain a digit from 1 to 9 inclusive. The outer digits can be repeated as necessary. Each outer digit gives the sum of the digits sandwiched between the 1 and 9 in its corresponding row/column. Adjacent digits along a green line must have a difference of at least 5.
1031: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along lines, adjacent digits must be consecutive and/or in a ratio of 2:1.
1032: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each gray dot is the midpoint of a single, 3-cell long line segment that must be drawn into the grid. Line segments are fully straight, and can be oriented horizontally, vertically, or diagonally. The three digits along a line segment cannot repeat, and they sum to the value shown in the corresponding midpoint cell. Line segments do not cross, overlap, or share cells with each other.
1033: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each blue circle in the grid is a Snowball. Snowballs roll in straight lines—either horizontally or vertically—through a set of orthogonally connected cells. The total length (in cells) of a Snowball's path is given by the number in the top left corner of its starting cell. The digits along a Snowball's path behave as follows: after the first two digits, each digit is the sum of the two preceding digits (just like the Fibonacci Sequence). Snowballs may cross paths, and therefore may share one or more cells with other Snowballs.
1034: Normal sudoku rules apply. Every 3x3 box contains one hidden 2x2 region called a Whisper Square. In a Whisper Square, orthogonally adjacent digits must have a difference of 5 or greater. Whisper Squares must not touch each other orthogonally, but they may touch diagonally. Within each cage, the sum of digits inside Whisper Squares equals the sum of digits outside Whisper Squares.
1035: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Numbers in the corner of cages indicate the number of cells in that 3x3 Box that form "wormholes" with other boxes. A cell in a cage in Box A forms a wormhole with the central cell of Box B when the cell's position in Box A (eg top right cell) matches the position of Box B in the grid (eg top right box). Two cells in a wormhole relationship both contain the same digit. Note: Cage totals only count the number of wormholes that look out of that box and into the central cells of other boxes ie A wormhole from another box that looks into the central cell of a cage is not counted.
1036: Shade some cells to form an orthogonally-connected, 1-cell wide snake that does not branch, does not loop, and does not touch itself orthogonally—but may touch itself diagonally. One end of the snake is given as a white circle. The remaining non-snake cells form ten, distinct, orthogonally-connected areas—one each of sizes 1 to 10. Areas of different sizes do not touch orthogonally, but they may touch diagonally. Each number in the grid must be part of an area of that size. A '?' represents any number from 1 to 10. [To enable the software to check your solution, in each non-snake cell write the size of that region. Use "0" instead of 10 for the 10 region!].
1037: Normal sudoku rules apply. A purple line contains a set of consecutive digits in any order. Cells separated by a black dot contain digits with a 1:2 ratio. Cells separated by a white dot contain consecutive digits.
1038: Normal sudoku rules apply. Pink lines must contain a set of consecutive, non-repeating digits in any order. Digits in a white circle must appear at least once in the four surrounding cells.
1039: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages cannot repeat and must sum to the total given.
1040: Normal sudoku rules apply, and digits in thermometers must increase strictly (and not necessarily consecutively) from the bulb
1041: Normal sudoku rules apply, and digits increase along thermometers from the bulb to the end(s).
1042: Normal sudoku rules apply, and digits increase along thermometers from the bulb to the end. Clues outside the grid show the sum of digits between the 1 and the 9 in that row/column. Bonus puzzle: find the two palindromic T-shaped 'hammers' in the grid, one of them near the 'nail'.
1043: Normal sudoku rules apply, and digits increase along thermometers from the bulb. Cages show their sums and contain no repeated digits.
1044: Normal sudoku rules apply, and digits on thermos increase from the bulb.
1045: Normal sudoku rules apply, and identical digits cannot be within a king's move of each other. Digits ascend along thermometers, starting from the bulb. The marked diagonal contains no repeated digits.
1046: Normal sudoku rules apply, and the same digit cannot appear twice in the same position within two 3x3 boxes. Digits increase along a thermo from the bulb. Digits do not repeat in cages. A black dot joins digits with a 1:2 ratio. Not all dots are given.
1047: Normal sudoku rules apply. The arrow outside the grid shows the sum of the indicated diagonal. Other clues outside the grid are the sum of digits sandwiched between the 1 and the 9 in that row/column. Grey circles show odd digits. White dots join consecutive digits. Digits on thermos increase from th ebulb. Digits on arrows sum to the number in the attached circle. Digits next to each other on the green line have a difference of at least 5. The purple line joins a set of consecutive digits, not necessarily in order. The cage shows its sum.
1048: Normal sudoku rules apply. Neighbouring digits on a green line have a difference of at least 5. Digits on a grey line must be between the digits in the attached circles. Black dots join digits with a 1:2 ratio. Not all dots are given.
1049: Normal Sudoku rules apply. Digits cannot repeat along the marked diagonals. Digits along a thermometer must increase from the bulb. Neighbouring digits along a green line have a difference of at least 5. Digits along a purple line form a sequence of consecutive digits, not necessarily in order. Digits joined by a black dot have a ratio of 1:2. Not all dots are given.
1050: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage may not repeat and must sum to the total in the top left corner of the cage (if given). Cells with a grey sqaure must contain even digits. Adjacent digits along a green line must differ by at least 5.
1051: Normal sudoku rules apply. Placing correct digits in the grid will clear the fog. Adjacent digits along a line must differ by at least 5. Cells separated by an X must contain digits summing to 10. Cells separated by a V must contain digits summing to 5. All X/V clues are given, but may be hidden in the fog.
1052: Normal sudoku rules apply, and cells touching diagonally cannot contain consecutive digits. Arrows in the gfrid add up to the number in the 'circle', and clues outside the grid show the total of the indicated diagonal. Sums can include repeats.
1053: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits cannot repeat in cages, which show their sums. Clues outside the grid show the sum of the indicated diagonal, which may include repeat digits.
1054: Normal sudoku rules apply. A single, orthogonally connected region must be shaded. Circles are not shaded - digits in circles show the number of surrounding cells that are shaded. Squares are shaded; the digit in a square is the number of shaded cells that cell "sees" (up/down/left/right), including itself, until reaching an unshaded cell.
1055: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along thermometers must increase from the bulb. Diagonally adjacent digits joined by a white dot must be consecutive; those joined by a black dot must have a 1:2 ratio (1 and 2 might be joined by a white or black dot). No other diagonally adjacent digits in the grid can be consecutive or have a 1:2 ratio.
1056: Normal sudoku rules apply. For each line, digits have an equal sum within each box it passes through.
1057: Normal sudoku rules apply. For each line, digits have an equal sum within each box the line passes through. eg For the line starting in r6c1, the sum of the box 4 digits must equal the sum of the box 7 digits ie r6c1 + r6c2 = r7c2 + r8c2 + r8c3.
1058: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits cannot repeat in a cage. The digits in a cage must sum to the given total in the top left corner.
1059: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on an arrow sum to the value in the diamond. If the arrow is horizontal, then the digit in the diamond indicates where the column number of the diamond appears in the row, e.g. if r9c5 is a 7 then r9c7 is a 5. Similarly, if the arrow is vertical, then the digit in the diamond indicates where the row number of the diamond appears in the column, e.g. if r2c7 is a 5 then r5c7 is a 2. If a diamond has arrows in both directions then it follows both rules.
1060: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a Quadruple circle must be placed at least once in the four cells touching that circle. Digits on a Region Sum Line have an equal sum within each box that the line passes through.
1061: Normal sudoku rules apply. Entanglement: A digit must share a row, column, or box with exactly two instances of each digit that it is consecutive with. Digits on an arrow sum to the value in the connected circle.
1062: Normal sudoku rules apply. Arrows in the grid can be correct or incorrect. On correct arrows the digits on the arrow sum to the value in the circle. Incorrect arrows do not sum to the value in the circle. It is up to the solver to determine which arrows are correct or incorrect. A number outside the grid is the sum of the circles in the row or column that are for correct arrows. Incorrect arrow circles do not contribute to the sum.
1063: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits cannot repeat in cages. The difference between the sums of the digits in any two orthogonally adjacent cages is exactly 1. The two cells joined by a white dot contain consecutive digits.
1064: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cages show their sums, and digits cannot repeat within a cage. On thermometers, digits increase from the bulb. But! One of the digits from 1-9 is a ghost, and is not bound by those constraints. The ghost digit still follows normal sudoku rules (appearing once in each row/column/box), but does not count toward cage sums, can repeat within a cage, and can appear anywhere on a thermometer (other digits on the thermometer must still increase from bulb to tip; the ghost digit is simply ignored).
1065: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. The grey lines are palindromes which contain the same sequence of digits forwards and backwards. Digits in cells separated by a white dot are consecutive.
1066: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Along thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb end. Each purple line contains a set of non-repeating consecutive digits, in any order. Adjacent digits along a green line must differ by at least 5.
1067: Normal sudoku rules apply. For each pair of arrows outside the grid, the digits along the two indicated diagonals have equal sums. Digits can repeat along these diagonals if allowed by other rules.
1068: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. A digit inside a white circle must appear in at least one of the four cells surrounding that circle. Along green lines, digits must differ from their neighbors by at least 5.
1069: Normal sudoku rules apply. Numbers in the grid represent the heights of skyscrapers, and clues outside the grid indicate the number of skyscrapers visible in that row or column, looking in that direction. The purple line contains a non-repeating set of consecutive digits, in any order. On thermometers, digits increase from the bulb. The gray line is a palindrome, which contains the same sequence of digits in either direction. Digits in cells separated by a V sum to 5. Digits in cells separated by an X sum to 10. Digits in cells separated by a white dot are consecutive. Digits in cells separated by a black dot have a 1:2 ratio.
1070: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is covered with fog, with an initial light source in the centre cell. Digits also act as light sources and, when placed correctly, illuminate the cells around them. The sum of the digits within a cage is given in the left-most cell of the top row reached by the cage (all cage sums are given). Digits cannot repeat within a cage. Digits on arrows sum to the number in the connected circle, and can repeat if allowed by other rules. All arrow sums are single-digit, and arrows do not overlap or intersect. Digits in cells with a grey circle must be odd. Digits in cells with a grey square must be even. Cells separated by a knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit.
1071: Normal sudoku rules apply. ALL clues are wrong. A clue is "wrong" if it is not 100% correct Ie Along purple lines, digits cannot form a consecutive, non-repeating set. Along green lines, at least one pair of adjacent digits must have a difference of less than 5. Along thermometers, digits cannot increase from bulb to tip. (Digits can repeat along purple/green lines and thermometers if allowed by other rules.) Digits on arrows cannot sum to the digit in the attached circle. At least one of the digits inside a (larger) white circle must not appear in any of the four cells surrounding that circle. Digits in cells separated by a V cannot sum to 5, and digits in cells separated by an X cannot sum to 10. Digits in cells separated by a white dot are not consecutive. Digits in cells separated by a black dot do not have a 1:2 ratio.
1072: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is covered with fog, except for two initial light sources. Digits also act as light sources and, when placed correctly, illuminate the cells around them. Cages show their sums, and digits cannot repeat within a cage. Digits on arrows sum to the single-digit number in the connected circle, and can repeat if allowed by other rules. Along green lines, digits must differ from their neighbours by at least 5. Digits in cells with a grey square must be even. Digits in cells separated by a black dot have a 1:2 ratio.
1073: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits cannot repeat along the blue diagonal. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. A pink line contains a set of non-repeating consecutive digits. These digits can appear in any order. Cells separated by a white dot must contain consecutive digits.
1074: Normal sudoku rules apply. All clues are standard, and all clues are wrong. A clue is 'wrong' if it is not 100% correct.
1075: Fill the grid with nine non-overlapping 3x3 square regions, such that each region contains the digits 1-9 once each and no digit repeats in any row or column. Correctly entered digits clear the fog around them. Cells outside regions do not contain digits. Cages show the sum of their digits in the left-most cell of the highest row reached by the cage, and digits cannot repeat within a cage. Cells with a shaded square must contain an even digit. Cells with a shaded circle must contain an odd digit.
1076: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cages show their sums, and digits cannot repeat within a cage. Digits on arrows sum to the two-digit number in the connected pill, which reads from left to right. These digits can repeat if allowed by other rules. A digit in a cell with a shaded square must be even.
1077: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Digits in cells separated by a white dot are consecutive. Digits in cells separated by a black dot have a 1:2 ratio (ie one digit is double the other).
1078: Normal sudoku and killer and little killer rules apply.
1079: Normal sudoku rules apply. Numbers along an arrow must sum to the number in the arrow's circle.
1081: Normal sudoku rules apply, and digits on thermos increase from the bulb.
1082: Normal sudoku rules apply. One or two digit numbers read left to right or top to bottom will be separated by L or C if numbers add to 50 and 100 respectively.
1083: Normal rules apply, and identical digits cannot be a knight’s move apart
1084: Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues between cells indicate the difference between the digits in the two cells.
1085: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in circles must be found on one of the four cells touched by the circle.
1086: Normal sudoku rules apply, and digits increase along thermometers, from the bulb end.
1087: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages sum to a number that ends in 5. Digits cannot repeat within a cage.
1088: Classic sudoku rules apply. Outside clues show the sum of the nearest X or (X-1) numbers, where X is the number in the first cell from that direction.
1089: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a knight's move (in chess) cannot contain identical digits. Digits along a thermometer increase from the bulb end. Digits in a cage sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage.
1090: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each circle marks the head of a familiar line constraint which takes the form of a snake of length from 2 – 9 cells. The specific constraint is indicated by the colour of the circle (and by a letter on the colourblind friendly version). The circle contains the length of the snake. The snakes move orthogonally through the centres of some cells, and do not touch themselves orthogonally. Snakes may freely touch each other, but do not share cells. The grey cells in box 4 are not part of any snake. The featured clue types are as follows: Renban (purple/R): The digits on a renban line form a sequence of consecutive digits in any order; Region Sum Lines (Blue/ S): The cells along a region sum line in each 3x3 box it passes through sum to the same total. Region sum lines always occupy at least two regions; German Whispers (Green/W): Adjacent digits along a German whispers line differ by at least 5; Modular Lines (Yellow/M): Each string of three adjacent cells along a modular line contains one of 147, one of 258, and one of 369. Length two modular lines contain one of each of two of these groups; Entropic Lines (Orange/E): Each string of three adjacent cells along an entropic line contains one of 123, one of 456, and one of 789. Length two entropic lines contain one of each of two of these groups; Parity Lines (Red/P): Adjacent digits along a parity line have opposite parity; Ten Lines (Gray/T): Digits along a ten line must be entirely divided into non-overlapping groups of adjacent cells which sum to 10. Digits may repeat within these sums if allowed by other rules.
1091: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cages show their sums. On thermometers, digits increase from the bulb. Digits in cells separated by a V sum to 5, and digits in cells separated by an X sum to 10. All possible V's and X's are given. Digits in cells with a gray square must be even.
1092: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. Clues outside the grid indicate the sum total of the digits in the cage that contains the Nth cell from that direction, where N is the first digit from that direction.
1093: Each row, column and region must contain the digits 1 to 9 once each. Each region is a set of 9 orthogonally connected cells and each region's position must be determined by the solver. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Digits may repeat along an arrow if allowed by other rules. Digits on an arrow (excluding its circle) have an equal sum N within each region it visits. It is possible that some arrows visit only one region. At any intersection between arrows, both arrows continue straight and they cannot overlap.
1094: Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells in the grid such that all shaded cells are connected orthogonally and all unshaded cells are connected orthogonally. No 2x2 area may be fully shaded or fully unshaded. Digits in cages cannot repeat and must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. However, shaded cells are treated as negative. In other words, the cage total is the sum of unshaded cells minus the sum of shaded cells.
1095: Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade a single group of orthogonally connected cells in each dashed cage. Shaded groups may not share a dashed border. Each cage must contain at least one shaded cell, and two cages which share a border cannot contain the same number of shaded cells. Digits MAY REPEAT in cages. Some cages have one or two sums indicated. The first value given is the sum of all digits in shaded cells in that cage and, if given, the second is the sum of all digits in unshaded cells in the cage. A cage sum given as "X" is to be determined by the solver and is the same value in all appearances.
1096: Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells in the grid such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected and all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected. No 2x2 area may be fully shaded or fully unshaded. Along the red line, each run of cells with the same shading contains a non-repeating set of consecutive digits in any order. Along the red line, digits in each pair of adjacent cells with different shading must differ by at least 5. The grey cell is shaded.
1097: Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells in the grid such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected and all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected. No 2x2 box may be fully shaded or fully unshaded. Digits in a cage cannot repeat and must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. In cages, all shaded cells must contain even digits, and all unshaded cells must contain odd digits.
1098: Shade some cells in the grid so that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected. No 2x2 area can be fully shaded. Place some digits from 1 to 9 in unshaded cells such that no repeating digits occur in any row or column. Shaded cells do not contain digits. Groups of orthogonally connected unshaded cells form islands, which do not touch orthogonally, but may touch diagonally. An island of size N must contain the digits 1 to N once each. Cells with arrows contain a digit that indicates the total number of unshaded cells (including itself) in the indicated directions combined. Caged cells contain a digit that indicates the size of the corresponding island. All possible cages are given.
1099: Divide the grid into regions and enter into each cell the size of its region (ie how many cells large it is). No two regions of the same size may share an edge. A number in a cell with an arrow indicates the distance to the nearest copy of that same number in every indicated direction. Not all arrows are necessarily given.
1100: Normal sudoku rules apply. Divide the grid into cages, i.e. non-overlapping areas of one or more orthogonally connected cell(s) with no repeating digits. A clue in the top-left corner of a cell indicates the sum of digits in that cage. Some cages do not contain any clues. For these other cages, the sum must be determined by the solver. Some cells may be outside cages. No two cages can share the same sum. Each cage represents a building whose height equals the sum of its digits. Clues outside the grid indicate the number of buildings “seen” from that direction. Taller buildings block the view of smaller buildings. Cells outside cages cannot be seen.
1101: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. All low digits (12345) must be orthogonally connected with each other. Each 2x2 group of cells must contain at least one high digit (6789).
1102: Divide the grid into regions of orthogonally connected cells. Two regions of the same size may not share an edge. Enter a number into each cell equal to the size of its region (ie the number of cells in its region). Consider N the number in the top-left corner of a cell with arrows. Arrows indicate ALL the directions (up, down, left, and right) where the NEAREST occurrence(s) of N is/are located. The number placed in that cell indicates the distance to the first occurrence of N in the indicated direction(s).
1103: Normal Sudoku rules apply. Digits 1-4 are pawns, 5's are kings, 8's are rooks. Rooks can 'see' all cells orthogonally until their view is blocked by a pawn. Kings are not allowed to be seen by a rook from outside their own 3x3 box. Digits in grey cells act as clues, (those in column 1 for their row and those in row 1 for their column), indicating how many cells the rook in their row/column can see in total, including cells with pawns blocking its way, but not including the cell with the rook itself.
1104: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells in the same relative position with respect to a box cannot contain the same digit (so eg r1c1 and r4c4 cannot contain the same digit). The marked main diagonals also contain no repeated digit. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the cells along the indicated diagonal. Digits may repeat along these diagonals (if allowed by the other rules).
1105: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along (blue) thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb end. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage.
1106: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb end. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. The clue outside the grid gives the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. These digits may repeat if allowed by other rules. The main diagonal marked in blue cannot contain a repeated digit. Digits on the diamond endpoints of a purple line must have a difference of at least 4 and the remaining digits on the line cannot be between or equal to the digits on the endpoints.
1107: Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid equal the Xth digit in their row/column seen from the side of the clue, with X being the 1st digit in their row/column seen from the side of the clue.
1108: Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells to form a snake (a one-cell wide path that does not branch, cross itself or touch itself orthogonally. It can touch itself diagonally.) The snake consists entirely of odd digits and its head and tail are given by the grey circles. Clues outside the grid are skyscraper clues that ignore any snake cells in their row/column. ie Each digit that is not snake indicates the height of a building in that cell. Clues indicate the number of buildings that can be seen in their row/column from the side of the clue, where higher buildings obscure the view of lower buildings. Digits separated by an X sum to 10; digits separated by a V sum to 5. Not all Xs and Vs are necessarily given.
1109: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each purple line contains a set of non-repeating consecutive digits (which can appear in any order). Adjacent digits along a green line must differ by at least 5.
1110: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the number in the attached circle.
1111: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along thermometers, digits increase from the bulb end.
1112: Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid indicate the sum of the first X digits from the Nth cell from that side, where X is the digit in the Nth cell and N is the digit in the first cell from that side.
1113: Normal sudoku rules apply. A purple line contains a set of consecutive digits in any order. Along arrows, the digits add up to exactly one more or less than the digit in the circle.
1114: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages cannot repeat and must sum to a prime number. (For the avoidance of doubt, 1 is not a prime number!)
1115: Normal sudoku rules appy. Identical cells cannot be a knight's move apart. Identical cells cannot appear within the same position in two 3x3 boxes. Grey lines are palindromes. A clue outside the grid shows the sum of the indicated diagonal, which may include repeats.
1116: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along purple lines, digits must form a sequence of non-repeating consecutive digits, in any order. Along thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb end. Cells separated by an X must contain digits summing to 10. Not all possible Xs are given.
1117: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage must not repeat, and sum to the number in the top left corner. Adjacent digits along a green line have a difference of at least 5.
1118: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage (if given). Digits cannot repeat within a cage.
1119: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along the blue lines must have an equal sum within each box they visit.
1120: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits along the green lines must have a difference of at least five. Along each blue line, digits on the line have an equal sum within each box they pass through.
1122: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along lines, the region sums form a consecutive ordered sequence. For example, the sum of the digits along the blue line within box 3 must be consecutive with the sum of the digits along that line in box 2 – and the sum of the digits along that same line in box 6 must be consecutive with the sum from box 2. And these sums must be ordered from lowest to highest (so the box 2 sum would always be the middle of that sequence).
1123: Normal sudoku rules apply. The dots given in the grid are the centres of (rotationally) symmetric "galaxies" (non-overlapping sets of orthogonally-connected cells), which function as "Region Sum Areas". Cells in Region Sum Areas have an equal sum N within each 3x3 box they visit, and they must visit more than one 3x3 box. Not every cell in the grid has to be part of a galaxy.
1124: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along “renbanmometers”, digits must increase from the bulb end and form a non-repeating consecutive sequence. The renbanmometers in this puzzle are all hidden, only their bulbs and tips are given. Bulbs are larger circles while tips are smaller circles. Corresponding tips and bulbs share the same colour (and letter). Renbanmometers can move diagonally or orthogonally, but renbanmometers cannot ever cross and different renbanmometers cannot share a cell.
1125: Normal sudoku rules apply. A number outside the grid is an X-sum for both its column or row, and also a Little Killer clue for the indicated diagonal. The number shows the sum of the first X digits in the row/column from that direction, where X is the first of those digits, and also indicates the sum of the indicated diagonal.
1126: Normal Sudoku rules apply. Digits may not repeat in a cage. Cage sums are all 2-digit numbers, which may be written xy, signifying that the digit at row x column y must equal n, where n is the size of the cage, e.g. if a 5-cage sums to 28 that means that R2C8 is a 5.
1127: Normal sudoku rules apply. Travel around the world following the international whisper lines from Berlin to Moscow. The arrival hall at each airport (red) tells you the minimum difference between digits along the next leg of the journey, starting from the departure lounge (green). A terminal with a white control tower must contain consecutive digits. A black control tower indicates the digits are in a ratio of 1:2.
1128: Place the digits 0-9 in the grid so that every row, column and 3x3 box contains every digit exactly once. To enable this, there is a single Schrödinger cell in each box, containing a superposition of two different digits. Every Schrödinger cell contains a unique pair of digits. No Schrödinger cell can see another Schrödinger cell by a Queen's move in chess (i.e. any distance horizontally, vertically or diagonally). Digits in a cage may not repeat and must sum to the indicated total. Schrödinger cells contribute the average of their two digits to the cage total.
1129: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. The digits in a cage sum to the 'cage total'. Along each line, the cage totals form a palindrome, reading the same from each end. eg R1c1 + r1c2 + r2c1 = r6c1 + r7c1.
1130: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits cannot repreat within a cage. The sum of the digits in a cage is its cage total. Along each purple line the cage totals form a set of consecutive numbers in any order.
1131: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each number in a circle must be the total of at least one of the cages touching that circle. Digits may not repeat in a cage.
1132: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage.
1133: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a red line sum to the product of the digits in the two connected squares. Digits may repeat on a line if permitted by other rules.
1134: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits may not repeat in a cage. Every cage sums to 16.
1135: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits may not repeat in a cage. The totals of individual cages of the same colour form a set of consecutive numbers, in any order.
1136: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each cage forms a line, the number on the top left shows the sum of the numbers sandwiched between the smallest number and the largest number of the line. Digits cannot repeat in a cage.
1137: Normal Sudoku rules apply. Each cage forms a line (ie a one-cell wide path with no 2x2 region). The number at the top left of a cage shows the sum of the numbers between the smallest and the largest number of the line. For clarification the smallest and largest digit do not have to be at the ends of each cage. Numbers cannot be repeated in a cage.
1138: Normal Sudoku rules apply. Each cage forms a line with a one-cell width. Digits cannot repeat in a cage. Each cage is either a killer cage or a “lunch box”. For killer cages, the number on the top left shows the sum of all digits in the cage. For lunch boxes, the number at the top left shows the sum of the numbers sandwiched between the smallest and the largest number of the line.
1139: Normal Sudoku rules apply. The circles shown in the grid are the centres of point-symmetrical “galaxies”. Each galaxy forms a line with one-cell width that must contain at least 3 cells. Each line cannot touch itself and does not form any loop. Galaxies cannot overlap. The number next to a circle shows the sum of the numbers between the smallest and the largest number of the galaxy line. Numbers cannot be repeated along galaxy lines. Not every cell in the grid has to be part of a galaxy.
1140: Normal sudoku rules apply, Each cage forms a line with a one-cell width. The number on the top left of a cage shows the sum of the numbers sandwiched between the smallest number and the largest number of the line. Digits cannot repeat in cages. Digits have been encrypted such that each letter represents a unique digit. Bold letters in cells indicate the digit that must appear in that cell in the solution. The number AB represent the number for which A is the tens digit, and B the units. It does not mean A*B.
1141: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each cage forms a line with the small clue in the top left showing the sum of the digits sandwiched between the smallest digit and the largest digit of the line. Digits cannot repeat in a cage.
1142: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage must sum to the small clue given in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat in a cage. Clues outside the grid show the sum of digits sandwiched between 1 and 9 in that row/column.
1143: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a thermometer increase from the bulb end. There are 8 identical clones in the grid which consist of 3 cells each. (Clones cannot be rotated or reflected). Clones have an orthogonally connected shape. No two clones overlap. Digits on clones cannot be the same if they are separated by a knight's move (in chess).
1144: Normal sudoku rules apply but in the final grid, every clue is wrogn (aka invalid)... Clues are valid if: [Everything is "totally standard" Undar promises...] Digits in a killer cage sum up to the small clue in the top left of the cage; Clues outside the grid are correct X-sums. ie Clues show the sum of the first X digits in that direction where X is the 1st digit. Clues outside the grid are correct skyscraper clues. ie The digits in the grid represent the "heights" of skyscrapers. Clues represent the number of skyscrapers seen from that direction. Taller skyscrapers block shorter ones. Digits on a thermometer increase from the bulb end. Digits separated by a black dot has a ratio of 1:2. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Digits separated by X have a sum of 10. Digits separated by V have a sum of 5. All digits in a circle appear in the 4 cells touching it. Maximum cells are larger than all 4 adjacent cells. Not all clues are necessary and some of them are just there to "throw you off".
1145: Normal sudoku rules apply. Neighbouring cells are marked with a white dit if they are consecutive, and with a black dot if they have a 1:2 ratio. Grey dots can represent white dits or black dots, and must be decrypted to give the final step. All possible dots are marked.
1146: Each row column and irregular region must contain two stars. Stars cannot touch each other.
1147: You can solve it as either an ODD or an EVEN Sudoku (ie grey squares must either all be ODD or all EVEN!!).
1148: Normal sudoku rules apply and digits on a thermometer increase from the bulb end.
1149: The two grey shapes are identical.
1150: Normal sudoku rules apply, and all shaded cells must be even.
1151: Normal sudoku rules apply, and all shaded cells must be even. Add in digits from No. 1 circles.
1152: Normal sudoku rules apply, and all shaded cells must be even. Add digits from No. 2 same position as No.1 circles.
1153: Normal sudoku rules apply, and all shaded cells must be even. Add digits from No. 3 same position as No.1 circles.
1154: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb end. Cells separated by a knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit.
1155: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each line must contain a set of consecutive, non-repeating digits, in any order. For each line, digits on it have an equal sum N within each box it passes through.
1156: Normal sudoku rules apply. Consecutive digits cannot be orthogonal neighbours. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in the attached circle/pill; two digit pills read from left to right or top to bottom. Purple lines contain a string of consecutive digits in any order. [All arrows (including attached circles/pills) fully overlap purple lines.]
1157: Digits on an arrow sum to the digit in the attached circle. (Digits can repeat along arrows if allowed by other rules). In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. This puzzle is solved in two stages: 1. Normal 9x9 sudoku rules DO NOT apply. Solve each 3x3 box within the grid independently (so ignoring the rest of the grid). ie Three digits (selected from 1 to 9) need to be placed in each row/column of that 3x3 box once each. 2. Erase all digits within the grid whose box number does not match their row number (eg you'll keep the digits in r4c1c2c3 within box 4). Then solve the puzzle as a regular killer arrow sudoku using the remaining digits as givens (ie normal sudoku rules will apply at this point).
1158: Normal sudoku rules apply. Every string of 5 consecutive cells along the continuous purple line must form a non-repeating, consecutive set of digits. The 3-cell purple lines must each comprise a set of consecutive digits (in any order). Cells separated by a black dot must have a 1:2 ratio (ie one digit must be double the other). Cells separated by a white dot must contain consecutive digits.
1159: Fill the grid with the digits 1-9 such that no digit repeats in any row, column, 3x3 box, or coloured region. Divide the grid into coloured regions so that no two coloured regions of the same size (ie containing the same number of cells) shares an edge. Numbers that match a coloured region’s size CANNOT be placed into the cells in that region. Eg a coloured region of size 3 cannot contain any 3s within it. The small clue in the top left corner of a cage indicates both the total size in cells of any coloured regions that overlap the cage, as well as the sum of the digits within that cage. Digits can't repeat within a cage. The indicated diagonals show both the total size in cells of any coloured regions that overlap the cells on that diagonal, as well as the sum of the digits along that diagonal. Eg a diagonal clue of 7 would indicate that the digits in/along it would either come from the same 7 cell coloured region, or multiple coloured regions whose total size equals 7.
1160: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. All cages are “aquariums”. Cells within aquariums are either air cells or water cells, with cells outside of cages not being air or water. Water cells fill the bottoms of cages and must have digits greater than all the air cells in their cage. Rows in cages must be either all air cells or all water cells. Cages must have at least one row of air cells and one row of water cells. Additionally, the cages are “pressurized”: The air cells within any cage must have a higher average value than the number of rows above that cage in the grid.
1161: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Along thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb end.
1162: Normal sudoku rules apply. The dots are the centres of rotationally symmetrical “galaxies” of orthogonally connected cells. (ie If you rotate the shape of the galaxy around 180 degrees you must get the same shape.) Each cell in the grid belongs to exactly one of these galaxies. Each row, column, and 3x3 box contains exactly 2 stars, and every galaxy contains exactly 1 star. Stars can't be within a kings move (in chess) from each other. Each galaxy with a small number clue in it sums to the number indicated. Digits can't repeat within a galaxy and “star” cells do not contribute to the totals shown.
1163: Normal sudoku rules apply. Divide the grid into coloured regions, so that no two orthogonally adjacent regions have the same size (in terms of number of cells they contain). The regions must be rotationally symmetrical. Digits may not repeat in a region, and regions with a small number clue sum to the number indicated. (Not all number clues are given, and these number clues DON'T have to be in the top, leftmost cell of their region.)
1164: Divide the grid into coloured regions along cell boundaries such that no two equally sized regions share an edge. Place the region size (in number of cells) into each cell within those regions. Digits on lines must be numerically between the digits in the attached circles.
1165: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits cannot repeat within a cage and must sum to the digit in the top left corner if given. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Digits cannot repeat along either of the diagonals.
1166: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. Cells separated by a white dot must contain consecutive digits. Cells separated by a black dot must contain digits in the ratio of 1:2. Not all possible dots are given.
1167: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. Digits can repeat along such a diagonal if allowed by other rules.
1168: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. Cells separated by a white dot contain consecutive digits. Cells separated by a black dot contain digits in a 1:2 ratio (ie one digit is double the other). Not all possible dots are given. Grey lines are palindromes and must read the same forwards and backwards.
1169: Normal sudoku Rules apply. In cages, digits cannot repeat and must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage (if given). Cells separated by a white dot must contain consecutive digits. Grey lines are palindromes that read the same forwards and backwards.
1170: Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. Cells separated by a white dot must contain consecutive digits. Cells separated by a black dot contain digits in a 1:2 ratio (ie one digit is double the other). Not all dots are given.
1171: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage sum to the digit in the top left corner of the cage. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. Cells separated by a knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. Grey lines are palindromes ie they read the same forwards and backwards.
1172: Normal sudoku rules apply. A clue outside the grid shows the sum of the diagonal it indicates. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Identical digits cannot be within a (chess) king's move. Grey lines are palindromes that read the same forwards and backwards. Note: All palindromes are straight lines with no bends.
1173: Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. Grey lines are palindromes, which must read the same backwards and forwards. Cells separated by a white dot must contain consecutive digits. Cells separated by a black dot contain digits with a 1:2 ratio (ie one digit must be double the other). Not all dots are given.
1174: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cages show their sums, and digits cannot repeat within a cage. The digits along each arrow sum to the digit in the circled cell. Cells joined by a white dot contain consecutive digits.
1175: Normal sudoku rules apply. The digits on an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Each purple line contains a set of non-repeating consecutive digits (which can appear in any order).
1176: Normal sudoku rules apply, in honour of International Sudoku Day. Digits in cages do not repeat and sum to the given total. Digits along indicated diagonals may include repeats, and sum to the given total.
1177: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Each purple line must contain a non-repeating set of consecutive digits (in any order).
1178: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle.
1179: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each purple line contains a set of non-repeating consecutive digits (which can appear in any order). Each main diagonal (marked in blue) cannot contain a repeated digit. The sum of the digits on an orange line within a single box must be the same for each box that line passes through.
1180: Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells in the grid such that all shaded cells form a single orthogonally-connected region and no 2x2 square is fully shaded. Each unshaded region must contain exactly one clue cell. Each unshaded region is an “X-killer cage”. Digits within a cage may not repeat and must sum to the total given in the corner of the clue cell. Additionally, the digit placed in the clue cell must equal the number of cells in the cage. The cell with a grey circle must contain an odd digit.
1181: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in circles must appear at least once in the surrounding four cells. Digits in cages may not repeat. In each cage, digits are grouped into pairs of adjacent cells - each cell used exactly once. Each pair is a two-digit number, read left-to-right or top-to-bottom. The sum of the two-digit numbers is given in the upper left corner of the cage.
1182: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Each coloured shape is a clone. Digits must appear in identical positions in each copy of a clone.
1183: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Digits given in one of the circles in the grid must appear at least once in the four surrounding cells.
1184: Normal sudoku rules apply. In addition, the sum of digits along a line must be the same within each 3x3 box the line passes through. eg r9c1+r9c2+r8c3 [line cells in box 7] = r9c4+r8c5 [line cells in box 8]. Furthermore, each line is either an Entropic Line or a Modular Line. Along an entropic line any run of three cells contains exactly one low {1,2,3}, one medium {4,5,6}, and one high {7,8,9} digit. Along a modular line, the digits in any run of three cells must all have different remainders under division by 3. (ie So one digit must be from the set {1,4,7}, one from {2,5,8} and one from {3,6,9}).
1185: Normal sudoku rules apply. [Fillomino] Divide the grid into regions along grid lines such that no two regions of the same size share an edge. Cells divided by a green wall are in different regions. Given digits specify the size of the region in which they appear. [Renban] Each region must include a digit equal to its size. Each region contains a non-repeating set of consecutive digits that may appear in any order.
1186: Normal sudoku rules apply. A number outside the grid is both a frame sum for its column or row, and also a Little Killer clue for the indicated diagonal. The number shows the sum of the first three digits in the row/column from that direction, and also indicates the sum of the indicated diagonal.
1187: Each row, each column and each region must contain the digits 1 to 9 once each. Regions consist of nine orthogonally connected cells and must be determined by the solver. Clues outside the grid indicate the sum of digits in each contiguous segment of cells that belong to the same region in that row/column, in ascending order (not necessarily in the order of appearance). Ie the largest clue will appear in the pill closest to the grid. For a given row or column, either all clues or no clues are given. Note that the same region can be represented in multiple pills in a row/column, as long as there's at least one cell in another region between.
1188: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along thermos, digits increase from the bulb to the tip. Adjacent digits on a green line differ by at least 5. A purple line contains a set of consecutive numbers in any order. The digit sum on a blue line is equal in every box. A black dot joins digits with a 1:2 ratio; a white dot joins consecutive digits.
1189: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Cells separated by a white dot contain consecutive digits. Not all dots are given. Cells separated by a knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit.
1190: Normal sudoku rules apply. There must be 2 ‘stars’ in each row, column, and box. Stars cannot touch each other (including diagonally). A clue outside the grid gives the total of the digits between the stars. Stars can have any value! Two digits separated by a knight’s move cannot be the same.
1191: Normal sudoku rules apply. Every grey line that connects two cells shows a prime number, read from left-to-right, top-to-bottom or bottom-left-to-top-right.
1192: Divide the grid into ominoes (regions of orthogonally connected cells), so that no two ominoes of the same size share an edge. Each cell contains a number equal to its omino's size. After the regions are placed, it must be possible to shade the regions one of two colours such that any two regions touching on an edge have different colouring. One or more arrows in a cell indicate that the number in the cell equals the number of cells of the same shading in all of the directions combined.
1193: Normal sudoku rules apply, and digits increase along thermometers from the bulb to the end.
1194: Normal sudoku rules apply, and identical digits cannot be a knight's move apart. The central (blue) 3x3 box is a magic square - each row, column and diagonal must add to the same sum.
1195: Normal sudoku rules apply. Larger white circles are surrounded by factors of 12. White dots join neighbouring cells with consecutive digits; black dots join neighbouring cells with a 1:2 ratio. Not all dots are given.
1196: Normal sudoku rules apply. The “goose path” from r9c2 to r1c8 is orthogonally connected, visits every cage and box and does not touch itself orthogonally or diagonally. Cages contain no repeated digits and show the total of the cells in the cage that are not on the goose path. Grey squares are not on the goose path, and show even digits which count the goose path cells in the adjacent (including diagonal) cells.
1197: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on a line must be strictly between the values of the digits in the associated circles. Clues outside the grid show the sum of the indicated diagonal, which may include repeats.
1198: Normal Sudoku Rules Apply. Digits along lines must form palindromes. Digits in white circles must appear in the four surrounding squares. Digits along indicated diagonals must sum to the given total and may repeat.
1199: Normal sudoku rules apply. Some cells have been pencilmarked with all of their possible candidates.
1200: Each row, column, region and cage contains 1-9.
1201: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grey lines are palindromes that read the same in both directions. Digits in cages sum to 12; negative constraint applies -- no unmarked dominoes sum to 12. Digits separated by a V sum to 5 (not all V's are shown).
1202: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along the thermometer ('4') must increase from the bulb end. The grey line ('9') is a palindrome that reads the same in both directions. Digits in cages sum to 7; negative constraint applies -- no unmarked dominoes sum to 7. Digits separated by a white dot differ by 1 (not all dots are shown).
1203: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits along a green line must differ by at least 5. The digits in each cage sum to 11 and all such dominoes are shown. (ie it is not possible for a domino to contain digits summing to 11 in this puzzle unless they are in a cage).
1204: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive; not all such dots are shown. The indicated 60-cell white region contains one each of the twelve standard pentominoes. Each pentomino contains exactly one given digit. That digit indicates the number of cells of the pentomino that are 'seen' orthogonally from that position (including itself). Once placed, each pentomino behaves like a 5-cell killer cage: digits do not repeat and must sum to the value listed below (using standard pentomino labeling): F=30, I=26, L=24, N=17, P=33, T=17, U=15, V=25, W=26, X=25, Y=23, Z=31
1205: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages do not repeat and must sum to the small clue in the top left corner, if given. Adjacent digits along a green line must differ by at least 5.
1206: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages do not repeat, and must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. A path consisting of the digits 1 to 9, in order, crosses from left to right across the grid with each digit in its corresponding column (1 in column 1, 2 in column 2, etc.) The cells along the path are connected orthogonally or diagonally. A similar path crosses the grid from top to bottom, starting with a 1 in row 1, then a 2 in row 2, ending with a 9 in row 9. Again, cells along the path are connected orthogonally or diagonally. The paths (which do not share cells, nor appear in any cage) are to be determined by the solver.
1207: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages sum to the clue in the top left corner. Two race cars (blue and green) start in box 1 and race around the track to the chequered flag line in box 2 (in the 16 cage). Draw green and blue lines to show the paths that the cars take. Each checkpoint (cage) shows which cell each car passes through. The cars may not enter grey shaded cells, and must avoid all oil slicks (given digits). The paths cross exactly 3 times during the race. The paths do not share cells. Digits along the blue path have an equal sum N within each 3x3 box the path passes through. Adjacent digits along the green path must differ by at least 5.
1208: Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected and all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected and no 2x2 area may be fully shaded or unshaded. White dots lie on the border between the shaded and unshaded regions. Additionally, white dots separate consecutive digits. Not all possible dots are shown. Digits in caged cells show the number of cells of the same color (shaded or unshaded) seen orthogonally from that position, including itself. The 'other' color blocks vision. Cells a (chess) knight's move apart cannot contain the same digit.
1209: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a blue line have an equal sum N within each 2x2 box the line passes through. Different lines may have different values for N.
1210: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in column 1 indicate the column in which the digit 1 appears in that row (e.g. if r4c1 is a 6, r4c6 is a 1). The same applies to columns 5 and 9, with the digits 5 and 9 respectively. Digits along a blue line have an equal sum N within each 3x3 box the line passes through. Different lines may have different values for N.
1211: Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells (the “hedges”) such that the unshaded cells (the “trails”) form an orthogonally connected area (with no loops) where no 2x2 group of cells is either fully shaded or unshaded. Different parts of the trail may touch diagonally (so checkerboard patterns ARE allowed). Note that hedges do not need to connect to the edge of the grid. The trails are completely tiled with non-overlapping dominoes. Caged cells are always trail cells and indicate two things: (a) the digit placed in the cage shows how many trail cells (including itself) can be seen orthogonally from that position (where hedges obstruct the view); (b) the small clue in the corner of the cage shows the total sum of the corresponding domino. Not all dominoes are marked with a cage.
1212: Place 1-6 in every row, column, and 2x3 box. Digits cannot repeat along the two marked diagonals. A digit outside the grid shows the sum of the digits on the indicated diagonal.
1213: Normal sudoku rules apply. Odd-even parity is reflected across the diagonal running NW-SE. (For example: if R6C2 is odd, R2C6 must also be odd.) The other diagonal running SW-NE must contain the digits 1 to 9 once each. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle.
1214: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each line consists of one or more non-overlapping groups of consecutive cells, each of which sums to 10. No two of these groups may have the same fill (including permutations), even if they are on different lines. For example, if one line had a group with digits 1315, and another line had a group with digits 5113, this would be invalid.
1215: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits along a green line must differ by at least 5. Digits on a purple line must form of a set of non-repeating consecutive digits. These digits can appear in any order. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Along a thermometer, digits must increase from the bulb end. Golden lines are "nabner" lines: No two digits selected from the set of digits on a nabner line can be consecutive.
1216: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. Digits in cells separated by an X sum to 10. All possible Xs are given.
1217: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages may not repeat, and must sum to the total shown.
1218: Normal sudoku rules apply. Neighbouring digits along a green line must have a difference of at least 5. Cells along a purple line must be a set of consecutive digits in any order. Cages read as 6, 8, 17, and 26 in an order that must be determined by the solver (reading order is left-to-right or up-to-down).
1219: Normal sudoku rules apply. The digits along each blue/purple line multiply to 200. Draw a 1-cell wide, non-branching, orthogonally-connected road that does not touch itself orthogonally (but may diagonally). The two ends of the road are given as circles. The road contains only odd digits, and the digits along the road sum to 200. Except for the circles, the road CANNOT visit any cell that contains a given clue ie the road cannot visit the given digits in R2C9 and R9C1, nor any cell that contains a line segment.
1220: Normal sudoku rules apply. The digits on the arrow path add to the digit in that arrow’s circled cell. Digits can repeat on the arrow if allowed by the other rules. Digits on a grey line form a palindrome i.e. the sequence reads the same whether read forwards or backwards.
1221: Normal sudoku rules apply.In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top-left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. The digits on a grey line must form a palindrome ie the string of digits must read the same forwards and backwards. Digits on the palindrome can repeat if allowed by other rules. Grey circles can only contain odd digits.
1222: Normal sudoku rules apply.Small circles show the difference between the cells they join. Large circles show digits that each must appear in a touching cell. Lines are palindromes, that can be read as the same each way.
1223: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells in the same relative position with respect to a box cannot contain identical digits. (So eg, r1c1 and r4c4 cannot contain the same digit). Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. Digits along such a diagonal may repeat if allowed by other rules. The digits along lines in the grid must be BETWEEN the two digits in that line’s circles (eg if the circles contained 2&7 then the digits on the line could only be from 3/4/5/6). Digits on the lines may repeat if allowed by other rules.
1224: Normal sudoku rules apply.Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. Digits along the diagonal may repeat if allowed by other rules. In the grid, the digits along the path of an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow’s circled cell. Digits along the arrow path may repeat if allowed by other rules. Digits along a grey lines form a palindrome
1225: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by white dots must contain consecutive digits. Cells separated by black dots must be in the ratio of 1:2. Not all white and black dots are given. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage, if given. Digits cannot repeat within a cage.
1226: Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. Digits along the diagonal may repeat. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. . Digits on a grey line form a palindrome i.e. they read the same forwards and backwards.
1227: There are nine 9-cell regions in the grid. Each region contains each digit from 1-9 exactly once. Each row and column also contain the digits from 1-9 exactly once. The digits on an arrow path add up to the digit in that arrows circle. Digits on an arrow may repeat if allowed by other rules.
1228: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells that have an X between them add to 10, and cells that have a V between them add to 5. Not all Xs and Vs are marked. A grey line of length n contains n sequential (ie consecutive) digits, but they may be arranged in any order on the line.
1229: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by the black dot contain digits in a 1:2 ratio (ie one digit will be double the other). The golden lines are “nabner” lines. Digits cannot repeat on a nabner line, and nabner lines cannot contain consecutive digits - regardless of order. Eg. if a line has a 3 anywhere on it, 2 and 4 cannot appear on that line. The blue lines in the grid are Region Sum Lines. The sum of digits on a blue line must be the same within each 3x3 box the line passes through.
1230: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along thermometers must increase from the bulb. Digits in cages sum to the given total. Digits along the indicated diagonal must sum to the given total and may repeat. Green cells are Sujiken (no digit is repeated in any diagonal in any direction in this area).
1231: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on a purple line form a set of consecutive, non-repeating digits in any order. Digits in circles must appear at least once in the four cells touched by the circle. Adjacent digits on a green line must have a difference of at least 5. Digits in a cage must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage.
1232: Normal sudoku rules apply. Consider the low digits (1, 2, 3), middle digits (4, 5, 6) and high digits (7, 8, 9) as three different groups. Each 2x2 box in the grid has to contain at least one digit of each group.
1233: Normal sudoku rules apply. Friendly cells must contain digits which match at least one of the row, column, or box number. Two cells separated by an X must contain digits adding up to 10 and must contain exactly one friendly cell. Two cells separated by a V must contain digits adding up to 5 and must contain exactly one friendly cell. Not all X’s and V’s are necessarily given.
1234: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a king's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. Neighbouring digits on a green line must have a difference of at least 5. Digits on a purple line form a set of consecutive, non-repeating digits (which can be in any order).
1235: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Divide the digits 1-9 into three different groups. Digits with the same letter must be in the same group. Two digits from the same group may not touch orthogonally.
1236: Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid shows the sum of the digits sandwiched between 1 and 9 in that row or column. Digits in column 1 indicate in which column the digit 1 is placed in the respective row. So, for example, if r7c1 was 6 then 1 would be placed in the sixth column of that row ie r7c6. Columns 5 and 9 have the same rule for the digits 5 and 9 respectively. Each red stripe contains exactly the same sequence of nine digits in the same order (the “slot machine”). The sequence can start at any point along a red stripe, and when it reaches the bottom, it wraps around again to the top.
1237: Normal sudoku rules apply for the 9x9 grid. A cell outside the grid is a numbered room clue, to be determined by the solver. It indicates the digit which has to be placed in the Nth cell in the corresponding direction, where N is the digit placed in the first cell in that direction. Digits in a white circle must appear (at least once) as a sudoku digit or as a numbered room clue in the four cells around the circle. Digits in a black circle must NOT appear as a sudoku digit or as a numbered room clue in the four cells around the circle.
1238: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells in the same relative position in different 3x3 boxes cannot contain the same digits. (So, for example, the top left cells in each 3x3 box must all be different.) Digits on a circle have to be placed in the same circular order in the four cells that are touched by the circle. The circle has to be rotated 90° clockwise N times from the current position. N is the digit in the cell inside the circle. Eg, if R2C8=6, then R1C8=8 and R2C9=4.
1239: Normal sudoku rules apply. In some rows/columns there are extra clues (one at each end) outside the grid. One of these clues gives the sum of the digits sandwiched between the 1 and the 9 in that row/column. The other clue gives the sum of the digits sandwiched between the 5 and 7 in that row/column.
1240: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each cell in the grid should be coloured blue (for water) or green (for land). For cells containing arrows, the digit in that cell shows how many cells share the same colour with the cell in the given direction, NOT including the arrow cell itself. Note that these same-colour cells need not be connected to the arrow cell. Not all arrows are given. The water occupies a single orthogonally connected region of the grid but no 2x2 area can contain only water cells. An island is an orthogonally connected region of at least 3 land cells. All land cells must be part of islands (so land cells are always in groups of three or more orthogonally connected cells). Islands may touch each other diagonally. Land cells forming any island must contain different digits.
1241: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each cell in the grid should be coloured blue (for water) or green (for land). For cells containing arrows, the digit in that cell shows how many cells share the same colour with the cell in the given direction, NOT including the arrow cell itself. Note that these same-colour cells need not be connected to the arrow cell. Not all arrows are given. The water occupies a single orthogonally connected region of the grid but no 2x2 area can contain only water cells. An island is an orthogonally connected region of at least 3 land cells. All land cells must be part of islands (so land cells are always in groups of three or more orthogonally connected cells). Islands may touch each other diagonally. Land cells forming any island must contain different digits.
1242: Normal sudoku rules apply and some snakes are hiding in the grid. A snake has a one-cell wide path. The head and tail cell of each snake need to be determined. A snake can touch itself diagonally but cannot touch itself orthogonally or revisit any cell twice. The cells not covered by snakes form exactly 8 orthogonally connected areas in the grid, one of each size from 1 cell to 8 cells. These areas are called 'snake eggs'. Each egg of size n contains the digits from 1 to n exactly once. Eggs must not touch orthogonally, but they might touch diagonally. The given digits in the grid indicate the position of the highest number of each snake egg. The snakes must connect to each other to form a single orthogonally connected area of snake cells, where no 2x2 region is covered entirely by snakes. Separate snakes might orthogonally connect anywhere, including the head cells. The head and tail cell of each snake must contain the same digit. (This digit might be different for different snakes.) Digits along the snake are not restricted: they might repeat, and the digit in the snake's head cell might be found elsewhere on the snake.
1243: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle.
1244: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a knight's or king's move in chess cannot contain the same digit. Digits in the Nth column indicate in which column the digit N is placed in the respective row.
1245: Shade the grid by standard Hitori rules using the pencil marks as clues. Use the shaded cells' pencil marks as clues to shade the grid by standard Akari rules. If a shaded cell contains a pencil mark greater than 4, it acts as a 0 for Akari. If a cell contains a light bulb and it's corner mark is not 8 or 9, its pencil mark can be placed in the grid as part of the solution. Shade the grid by standard Nurikabe rules using the placed numbers as clues. (The pencil marks on shaded "water" Nurikabe cells are no longer needed.) Solve the grid as a standard Killer Sudoku where the cages are the Nurikabe islands, and the sum of the digits in the cage equals to the sum of the corner pencil marks in that cage. (The previously placed numbers remain in the grid.) In the solved Killer Sudoku, place 2 stars in every row, column and 3 by 3 region according to standard Star Battle rules. Cells with 4 or 5 must not contain stars.
1246: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. At least one of the four corner cells (in pink) must contain a 3. Digits cannot repeat in the yellow "spotlight" cages and each such cage must contain a 3.
1247: 3x3 middle box solve with digits 1-3 and retain 1,2,3 belonging to the rows. 5x5 middle box plus phistomefel ring solve with digits 1-5 and retain digits 1,2,3,4,5 associated with their rows. Middle box plus two outer rings use digits 1-7 and retain 1,2,3,4,5,6,7 relating to their rows. 9x9 Normal sudoku rules apply. Maximum cell, kropki and anti-king rules still apply. German Whispers: Adjacent digits along the marked lines have a difference of at least 5.
1248: Normal sudoku rules apply (ie place the digits 1 to 9 exactly once in each row, column and box). In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. Digits cannot repeat along the (blue) marked diagonal.
1249: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Along thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb end. Digits along the main diagonal (marked in blue) must not repeat. The clue outside the grid gives the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. Digits may repeat along this diagonal if allowed by other rules.
1250: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each row, column and box contains exactly one “deflection” cell. Each deflection cell contains a different digit. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits on the indicated diagonal. Digits may repeat along this sum. When a diagonal hits a deflection cell, the diagonal gets deflected clockwise by 90° ("makes a right-turn"). If a diagonal passes the same cell multiple times, that cell's value is counted multiple times towards the clue sum.
1251: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits may not repeat within a cage. Every digit, except the digit in the centre (r5c5), has a 'partner digit' that is always placed in the cell 180° rotationally symmetrical to its own, rotated around the centre of the grid. Which digits are paired up must be deduced by the solver. (eg If the digits 1 and 2 turned out to be a rotational pair and r2c4 is a 1, r8c6 must be a 2.)
1252: Place the digits 1-9 exactly once in each row, column and thick-outlined region. Digits separated by a white dot have a difference of the indicated number. Digits separated by a black dot have a ratio of the indicated number. All cages are Magic Squares: In a Magic Square, all rows, columns and length-3-diagonals sum to the same total. Digits may repeat in Magic Squares.
1253: Label some cells with numbers to form a single orthogonally-connected group of labelled cells; no 2×2 group of cells may be fully labelled. Each bold region must contain at least one labelled cell. Each number (including any given numbers) must equal the total count of labelled cells in that region. When two numbers are orthogonally adjacent across a region boundary, the numbers must be different.
1254: Normal sudoku rules apply. The digits in each cage do not repeat and sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage (if given). On a grey line, the digits sum to the same total as the two circles connected to the line. All double arrows in the grid are straight lines (ie. they do not turn at intersections).
1255: Normal Fillomino rules apply. ie Divide the grid along grid lines into regions. Into each cell, write the size of that cell's region.
