No two orthogonally adjacent regions can have the same size. The total sum of the numbers on the diagonals indicated by red question-marks is 77. The diagonals indicated by white question-marks cannot contain more than five regions of size 1 in total (but they may contain less).
1256: Normal Sudoku rules apply. Digits connected by a white dot are consecutive. Digits connected by a black dot are in a ratio of 2:1 (ie one digit will be double the other). Not all dots are necessarily given. Coloured lines in the grid are “Renban” lines. Digits on a Renban line form a set of non-repeating, consecutive digits – these digits can appear in any order. All Renban lines in the grid move orthogonally between neighbouring cells, do not branch and do not overlap each other. Each line has a unique colour. The grid is covered with fog. Correctly placed digits will clear the fog around that cell.
1257: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by an X contain digits summing to 10. Not all Xs are given. Shade some cells in the grid such that all the following conditions are fulfilled: 1) All shaded cells are orthogonally connected, without creating a 2x2 area of shaded cells. 2) Groups of orthogonally connected unshaded cells form ‘islands’. Each island has exactly one circle, and the number in the circle shows the size of the island. Each island contains digits 1 to N without repeats, where N is the size of the island. Each island is of a different size.
1258: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage.
1259: Divide the grid into rectangular regions of orthogonally connected cells, each containing exactly one clue. A plus shaped clue means that the region it belongs to is a square. A line shaped clue means that the region it belongs to is a rectangle with the longer edge parallel to the line. Four regions may never share the same corner.
1260: Normal sudoku rules apply. On each diagonal (marked in blue) digits cannot repeat. Some cages show their sums, and digits cannot repeat within a cage. A digit inside a white circle must appear in at least one of the four cells surrounding that circle. Digits in cells with a shaded square must be even. Digits in cells separated by a black dot have a 1:2 ratio (ie one digit must be double the other).
1261: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow much sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Adjacent digits on a green line must differ by at least 5.
1262: Normal Sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a black dot are in a ratio of one to two. Not all dots are given. Clues outside the grid are both sandwich and little killer clues. They indicate the sum of the digits between the one and the nine in that row or column, and also the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. Digits may repeat on the diagonals.
1263: Place the digits 0 to 8 once each in every row, column and box. Digits on arrows must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle.
1264: Normal sudoku rules apply. The sum of the digits on a line within a box (the line's 'region sum') must be the same for each box that line passes through. Dots apply to the lines in this puzzle, not cells. Lines separated by a white dot have consecutive region sums. Lines separated by a black dot have region sums in a ratio of 1:2.
1265: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages do not repeat, and sum to the number in the top left corner of the cage if given. Cells that are a (chess) knight's move apart cannot contain the same digit.
1266: Normal sudoku rules apply. The black dot between two cells indicates that one of the digits is double the other. Each line contains a set of non-repeating consecutive digits. Adjacent digits on these lines must have different parity (odd digits must be next to even digits and vice-versa).
1267: Normal sudoku rules do NOT apply! The digits 0 to 8 appear once each in each row, column and 3x3 box. Digits on an arrow sum to the number in that arrow's circle.
1268: Normal sudoku rules apply. Lines are Region Sum Lines: The sum of the digits on a line within a 3x3 box must be the same for each 3x3 box that line passes through. If a line passes through a 3x3 box more than once, each time it passes through counts separately. Lines do not branch or cross. The grid is partially covered in fog. Placing correct digits will clear the fog from surrounding cells.
1269: Put the digits 0 to 6 – once each, into every row, column and box. To enable this, one cell in every row, column and box is a “Schrödinger cell” that contains two digits. This cell counts as the sum of its digits for the following rules. One cell in every row, column and box is a doubler. This cell counts as double its value for the following rules. Each of the digits 0 to 6 appears exactly once in a doubler cell. The sum of the cell values on a line within a 2x3 box must be the same for each box that line passes through. Eg the values of r4c2+r3c3 = the values of r2c4+r1c4+r2c5
1270: Place 1-6 in each row, column and marked region. One cell in each row, column and box is a doubler. The value of this cell counts as double its digit for the other rules. Each digit appears once in the set of doublers. Digits along an arrow sum to the value in that arrow's circle. Digits in a black circle must not appear AS VALUES in the surrounding four cells. For example, a black circle containing a 4 excludes both a regular 4 and a doubled 2, but not a doubled 4.
1271: Normal Sudoku rules apply. Each (marked) diagonal has the digits 1-9 once each. Digits in cages sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. The blue cells in box 9 sum to 10. The grey line forms a palindrome ie it should read the same backwards and forwards. The three cells with grey squares in them contain even digits. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. Digits can repeat along these diagonals.
1272: Normal sudoku rules apply. The contents of each coloured cage in the grid are either a single digit number or form a two-digit number, read left to right or downwards. These numbers act as the arrow clue of their colour such that the digits on the indicated diagonal, which can include repeats, sum to that number.
1273: Normal sudoku rules apply. Additionally, there are some empty cages in the grid. In these cages, digits do not repeat, and somewhere within them is their cage total i.e. their sum, which is always two digits next to each other, read left to right or up then down as a 2 digit number. It is up to the solver to determine what each cage's sum is. Consecutive cages (ie cages that share an edge) cannot sum to 63.
1274: Normal sudoku rules apply. The clues in the grid correspond to sandwich clues of the same letter on the outside of the grid. Each clue in the grid is either a 2 or 1 digit number, read left to right or up down and must be determined by the solver. Clues outside the grid ("sandwich clues") show the sum of the digits "sandwiched" between the 1 and the 9 in that row/column.
1275: Normal sudoku rules apply. There are three "rings" in the grid, or increasingly larger squares, with some breaks in them, represented by the yellow lines. Along these rings, digits must touch at least one other consecutive digit on the ring, except in the 'breaks' of the ring (where there is no line), where digits must not touch another digit consecutively on its ring. (so r1c4 can never be consecutive with either r1c3 or r1c5). These rules do not apply to cells on different rings that touch each other. Black dots show that the 2 joined cells have a 1:2 ratio, and not all possible black dots are given.
1276: Normal sudoku rules apply. For the red cells, the sum of their orthogonal neighbours (which can include repeats) equals the sum of the clue in the cell and its correct digit (so the clue shows the difference between the cell and the sum of its neighbours).
1277: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each green line contains a set of consecutive, non-repeating digits in any order. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage (where given). Digits cannot repeat within a cage.
1280: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb. The marked square on the central thermo is "broken", meaning the thermo functions without that digit, but not with it. The broken cell may repeat a digit from elsewhere on the thermo. The center squares of the upper and lower 3x3 boxes contain all of the digits in the coloured squares of the central 3x3 box. The digit in the broken square of the central thermo is equal to the highest digit of exactly one of the other six thermos.
1281: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a single knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. Create a one-cell wide path in the grid to form a single loop that starts and ends in the central cell. The path must orthogonally touch each grey cell at least once but cannot enter any grey cell. The path cannot touch itself orthogonally. The central cell contains the lowest digit that can appear on the path. The path must visit each of the cells with a circle in them on them in strictly ascending order along the path (a cell is "visited" the first time the path orthogonally touches the cell).
1282: Normal sudoku rules apply. In addition, there is an orthogonally-connected path starting at Frogger (R9C5) that collects all flies in the grid and ends at one of the colored frogs (small circles) in the first row. The path cannot touch itself orthogonally, but can touch itself diagonally. The path also cannot go through the bushes (green cells) in the first row. Cars and logs are found in the road and the river, respectively; they appear in those regions wherever two horizontally adjacent digits sum to 10. Frogger cannot go through cars, and can only hop across logs in the river.
1283: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits inside grey bubbles must be odd. Digits separated by a white bubble are consecutive. Digits separated by a black bubble have a ratio of 1:2. Not all bubbles are given.

1287: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits along blue lines must differ by at least 5. Purple lines contain a consecutive series of digits (in any order).

1299: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits cannot repeat in cages, and sum to the number in the upper-left corner of the cage (if given). Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in its circle. Digits may repeat along an arrow if allowed by other rules.

1303: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage.

1306: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. 1307: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on a grey line must be between the digits on that line's circled ends. Digits on a purple line must be consecutive (in any order). 1308: Each row, column, region and marked diagonal must contain the digits 1-9. Numbers along an arrow must sum to the number shown in the circled cells. 1309: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits must not repeat in a cage. The numbers in a cage must sum to the given total in the top left corner. Numbers along an indicated diagonal must sum to the given total.
1310: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the number in the circle. Digits along the indicated diagonal sum to the given total.
1311: Normal sudoku rules apply. Every 2x2 square of cells must contain a digit from each of three sets (A,B,C)-(D,E,F)-(G,H,I) however, the digits in each entropy set must be deduced by the solver. Numbers that appear in the cells with a white dot between must be consecutive, AND from the same entropy set. Numbers that appear in the cells with a black dot between must have a ratio of 2:1, AND from different entropy sets.
1312: Normal sudoku rules apply. The sequence of digits on a gray line reads the same from both directions. Circles are either quadruples or anti-quadruples, meaning: Each of the digits in a circle must appear in at least one of its four surrounding cells, OR Each of the digits in a circle must NOT appear in any of its four surrounding cells. 1313: Normal sudoku rules apply. A digit X in a cage points to a second digit Y located X cells away in its row or column. The number in the top left corner of the cage gives the sum of X+Y. Numbers that appear in the cells with a white dot between must be consecutive. Numbers that appear in the cells with a black dot between must have a ratio of 2:1.
1314: Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid indicate that that clued digit X has to be placed in the Nth cell in the corresponding direction, where N is the digit placed in the first cell in that direction and N will always refer to the first occurrence of X. The arrow determines the diagonal direction of the clue AND once it hits the edge of the grid, it reflects at 90 degrees and continues until it hits the next edge at which it stops (so there are always nine possible cells for each clue). Eg if r1c5 was a 6 then r6c2 would be a 5. Any set of three sequential cells along a beige line must contain a low (123), middle (456), and high (789) digit. Any set of three sequential cells along a blue line must NOT contain a low (123), middle (456), and high (789) digit.
1315: Normal sudoku rules apply. Gold lines are "nabner" lines; ie they cannot contain repeated digits and no two digits along a line may be consecutive. Eg If a line contains a 2, there cannot be a 1 or 3 anywhere along the line. Any two lines that cross each other will each proceed straight through the intersection. The inequality points to the smaller of the two digits it separates.
1316: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells that's are a Knight's move apart from each other cannot contain the same digit. Cells along a grey line must form a palindrome. Clues outside the grid indicate the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. Digits may repeat along these diagonals (providing digits do not repeat in a 3x3 box).
1317: Normal Sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. Grey circles and squares must contain odd and even digits respectively. Digits along a solid grey line must form a palindrome. Digits along arrows must sum to the total in their white circle. All of the digits 1 to 9 must appear on both main diagonals. The number outside the grid indicates the sum of the digits along its diagonal. Digits may repeat along the diagonal.
1318: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a knight’s move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. The digits on an arrow path add to the digit in the arrow's circled cell. Digits along a thermometer must increase from the bulb end. A clue outside the grid indicates the sum of the digits along its diagonal.
1319: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. Digits along arrows must sum to the total in the their white circle. Digits may repeat along arrows if allowed by other rules. Along, thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb end.
1320: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along themometers digits must increase from the bulb end. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Digits in cells connected by a white dot are consecutive. Digits in cells connected by a black dot have a ratio of 1:2. Each coloured line must contain the digits 1 to 9 once each, in any order.
1321: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. Neighbouring digits on a red line have a difference of at least 5. Cells separated by a black dot contain digits in a ratio of 1:2. Cells separated by a white dot must contain consecutive digits. Not all possible dots are shown.
1322: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along the 'cue' increase from the butt/bulb. Digits connected by a black dot have a 1:2 ratio. The white circle (cueball) contains an odd digit, the blue square (chalk) an even digit. The two cages contain 2-digit numbers that sum to 147, and the perimeter of the grid also sums to 147. Each of boxes 2 to 7 includes a horizontal domino containing 1N, where N is the box number. The 1 always comes first.
1323: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is partially covered in fog. Placing correct digits will clear the fog from that digit’s surrounding cells. No domino in the grid sums to 3. The perimeter cells of the grid sum to 172. Digits along a thermometer must increase from the bulb end. Adjacent digits along a green line must differ by at least 5. Cells separated by a black dot must contain digits in a 1:2 ratio (ie one digit is double the other). Cells separated by a white dot must contain consecutive digits.
1324: It's classic sudoku, but put a digit in the grey cell: 1 if you are capable, 2 if you are advanced, 3 if you are expert. Honestly!
1325: Normal Sudoku rules always apply. For Knight Sudoku, a chess knight's move cannot connect identical digits. Alternatively, for King Sudoku, a chess king's move cannot separate identical digits. And alternatively, for Queen Sudoku, a chess queen's move cannot separate 9's!
1326: You can't fit a 4x4 magic square into a regular sudoku! But Cam Dennis can.
1327: Normal sudoku rules apply, and digits represent the minimum distance they can be away from an identical digit diagonally.
1328: Normal sudoku rules apply, and cages show the sum of their digits and cannot include repeats. Each digit from 1-9 has a “buddy” which appears in the cell with its co-ordinates swapped – so if 1 and 4 are ‘buddies’, a 1 in r1c3 must be matched by a 4 in r3c1, and a 4 in r6c9 must be matched by a 1 in r9c6. This constraint applies to every digit in the grid. A digit’s ‘buddy’ can be itself.
1329: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits may not repeat along each of the marked diagonals. Cells separated by a "taxicab" distance of 4 may not contain the same digit. A "taxicab" distance from cell A to cell B is the minimum possible distance from cell A to cell B when traversed only through orthogonal cells. In other words if two cells are H horizontal moves and V vertical moves away from each other, their taxicab distance from one another is H+V.
1330: Normal sudoku rules apply. A clue outside the grid shows the sum of the indicated diagonal, which may include repeats. Each digit (1-9) has a "buddy" that appears in all of the cells where the row and column indices are swapped. For example, if 1's are buddies with 4's and there is a 1 in r5c2, then there must be a 4 in r2c5. A number may be its own buddy. Figuring out the buddies is part of the puzzle.
1331: Normal sudoku rules apply. Identical digits cannot be a knight's move apart. Digits along (green) thermometers increase from the bulb. Digits along arrows sum to the number in the attached circle.
1332: Normal sudoku rules apply, and blue cells contain the sum of their (orthogonally) neighbouring cells.
1333: Normal sudoku rules apply. The two-digit pills contain distinct two-digit numbers and the three-digit pills contain their squares, where all numbers are read from left to right and the leftmost digits of a two-digit number and its square are on the same column.
1334: Normal Sudoku rules apply. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. The digits in each cage sum to the same total.
1335: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb to the tip.
1336: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Cells separated by a knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit.
1337: Each row, column, and region must contain the digits from 1 to 9 exactly once. The regions must be orthogonally connected and determined by the solver. Clues outside the grid show the sum of the two digits separated by the first region border seen from that direction in that row/column. (A row or column with a clue cannot be occupied by a single region.) For example; if the regions were the regular 3x3 boxes, then the clue at the top of column 6 would be the sum of R3C6 and R4C6, and the clue at the bottom of column 6 would be the sum of R6C6 and R7C6.
1338: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits cannot repeat and sum to the cage total where the cage totals of two cages that share an edge must differ by at least 5.
1339: Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid represent any positive integers and they show the sum of the first X digits from that direction where X is the first digit and they also show the sum of the digits sandwiched between the 1 and the 9 in that row/column.
1340: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow’s circle. Digits in a cage do not repeat, and the clue in a cage indicates its sum. Digits separated by a white dot have a difference of one; digits separated by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio.
1341: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along grey thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb end. Cages show their sums. White dots join consecutive digits; black dots join digits with a 1:2 ratio. Neighbouring digits differ at least by 5 along the green line.
1342: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits within a cage cannot repeat, and must sum to the small clue in the top left corner (if given). Cages are referred to as "crime scenes" in the following rules. WATCH OUT! A serial killer is on the loose and is leaving crime scenes and dead digits all over Sudokutown. Luckily, Sudokutown's #1 Detective is on the case, and a few brave citizens have stepped forward to provide eye-witness accounts. But will the killer be caught in time? One of the digits is a serial killer. All instances of the serial killer digit appear on a single, 1-cell wide orthogonally connected path (Snake). The serial killer's path starts in the largest crime scene (44 Killer Cage, total of 8 cells), then moves to the next largest crime scene (7 cells), then the next largest crime scene (6 cells), and so on. Exactly two adjacent cells on the serial killer's path appear in each crime scene, with one cell containing the serial killer and the other cell containing a "dead" digit. Once a digit is "dead," that digit cannot appear in any future crime scenes. After the final digit is "dead," the serial killer escapes off the edge of the grid. Additionally, the serial killer appears on both ends of the path. The serial killer's path may not touch itself orthogonally or diagonally. The serial killer and "dead" digit may appear within a crime scene in any order. The serial killer never re-enters a crime scene. Some instances of the serial killer digit will appear outside of crime scenes—those instances may appear anywhere along the path, as long as the serial killer travels through the crime scenes in descending order (in other words, the serial killer can "take a break" between crime scenes). One of the digits is Sudokutown's #1 Detective. The detective digit is trying to catch the serial killer but keeps failing. The detective digit cannot appear in crime scenes, cannot appear on the serial killer's path, and cannot appear orthogonally adjacent to the serial killer digit. The detective digit appears in the cell with a star. Some witnesses have spotted the serial killer's path. The clues outside the grid show the sum of the digits on the corresponding diagonal that are on the serial killer's path (digits that are not on the serial killer's path are not counted toward the sum).
1343: Normal 6x6 rules apply to each grid. Place the digits 1-6 into each cell of each grid so that each digit appears once in each row/column/box. 2) Normal rules for white/black dots, XVs, arrows, renban, German Whispers, and killer cages also apply. There are no negative constraints of any kind Note that German Whispers in this puzzle require a difference of at least 5, like in a 9x9 Grid. 3) Additionally, in each grid, one cell in every row, column, and box contains a doubler. For purposes of clues, a cell with a doubler counts for twice its value. 4) No two of these six puzzles contain doublers in the same cell. Some examples with doublers: a 2 cell 8 killer cage could contain a 4 and a 2 with a doubler or a renban could contain a 3, a 3 with a doubler, a 4 and a 5.
1344: Normal sudoku rules apply, and digits increase along thermos (orange) from the bulb. Palindromes (blue) read the same both ways, and cages show their sum totals.
1345: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cages show their sums. X/V join cells that sum to 10 (X) or 5 (V) - all possible Xs and Vs are given.
1346: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits increase along thermos from the bulb. Clues outside the grid sum the indicated diagonal, which may include repeats. Cages' sums are given.
1347: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along thermometers, digits strictly increase from the bulb. Clues outside the grid show the sum of the indicated diagonal, which may include repeats.
1348: Normal sudoku rules apply, and identical digits cannot appear within a knight's move of each other. Cages cannot include repeat digits, and show their sums.
1349: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along thermometers increase from the bulb. Clues outside the grid show the sum of digits between the 1 and the 9 in that row/column.
1350: Normal sudoku rules apply, Along thermometers, digits increase from the bulb. Grey circles without lines represent odd digits. Neighbouring cells along green/orange lines must have a difference of at least 5. Clues outside the grid show the sum of the indicated diagonal, which may include repeats.
1351: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along gray thermometers must increase from the bulb to the tip. Neighboring digits along green lines must differ by at least 5. Digits connected by a black dot must have a ratio of 1:2. Digits connected by a white dot must be consecutive. Not all dots are given.
1352: Normal sudoku rules apply. Circled digits equal the sum of all digits on their attached arrow. Digits may repeat on arrows. No two cells which are a chess knight's move apart may contain the same digit.
1353: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the upper left corner of the cage. Cells separated by a knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. Cells separated by a white dot must contain consecutive digits. Cells separated by a black dot must contain digits with a 2:1 ratio.
1354: Normal Sudoku rules apply. Circled digits must equal the sum of the digits on their attached arrow. Cells separated by a knight's move (in chess) may not contain the same digit. Bifurcation is not necessary!
1355: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each caged cell must be part of a region that: a) contains X orthogonally connected cells, where X is the digit placed in the caged cell; b) the cells of which sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the caged cell; c) does not contain any repeated digits. 1356: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage (if given). Digits cannot repeat within a cage. 1357: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage (if given). Digits cannot repeat within a cage. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. Digits can repeat along such a diagonal if allowed by other rules.
1358: Normal Sudoku rules apply. External clues show the digit which repeats most along the indicated diagonal. No other digit may repeat equally as often on that diagonal.
1359: Fill every row, column and bold-outlined region with the digits 1-9 once each. Cells separated by an X must contain digits summing to 10. Shade one tetromino in each region such that all shaded cells form one orthogonally connected area. Tetrominoes of the same shape may not share a border (counting rotations and reflections as the same). No 2x2 area may be entirely shaded. Additionally, each tetromino must contain digits summing to less than 13.
1360: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits cannot repeat on either of the main diagonals (marked in blue). In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage (if given). Digits cannot repeat within a cage.
1361: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage (if given). Digits cannot repeat within a cage. The path does not touch itself orthogonally or diagonally.
1362: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. Adjacent digits on a green line must have a difference of at least 5. Along the thermometer, digits must increase from the bulb end.
1363: Normal sudoku rules apply. A clue outside the grid shows the sum of the digits "sandwiched" between the 1 and the 9 in the corresponding row/column. Draw a loop through every cell except the cells that contain the digit 1. The loop is not allowed to branch, intersect or cross itself.
1364: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits cannot repeat in a cage, and sum to the number shown (if given).
1365: Normal sudoku rules apply. (ie Every row, column, and 3x3 box must contain the digits 1-9 with no repeats.) Digits on an arrow spell out the coordinates for the digit that is their sum. 1366: Normal sudoku rules apply. Within each cage, digits cannot repeat and must sum to the small clue in the top-left corner of the cage (if given)
1367: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb end.
1368: Each column contains the digits 1-9 once (with no repeats), plus one empty cell (which can be shaded green when found). Additionally, no digit may be repeated along any diagonal. Eg: the 3 in the magic column has exactly three 3s in its row (including itself.) Digits along a thin blue line always add up to 10. Blue lines never pass through any empty cells.
1369: Normal sudoku rules apply. The digits in each grey region sum to 45. Using different colours, colour 5 separate paths of orthogonally connected cells, each starting and ending at a different grey circle. No cell sits on more than one path (paths must not overlap each other or the grey regions). The digits along each coloured path must also sum to 45. Cells connected by a white dot contain consecutive digits. Not all white dots are necessarily given.
1370: Normal sudoku rules apply but using the digits 0-8 instead of 1-9. Find and colour the 24 hidden cages, which do not overlap. Each cage has a different total between 1 and 24 – the total for each cage is given on one of its cells (by a red clue). Digits MAY repeat within cages. All cages are triominoes (ie consist of 3 orthogonally connected cells) apart from one, which is a pentomino (containing 5 orthogonally connected cells.) Cells with a large snowball in the central 3x3 box count as double their value for the purposes of their cage totals (if they reside within a cage). Cells separated by a small white dot contain consecutive digits. Cells separated by a small black dot contain digits with a ratio of 1:2 (ie one is double the other.) Not all possible black and white dots are given.
1371: 1-9 must be placed in each row and column. No 3s are allowed in the corner cells, or in the spotlight (the white central area). A purple line contains a set of non-repeating consecutive digits, in any order. Digits connected by a diagonal equals sign are identical. All possible such equals signs are given.
1372: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each of the seven line types listed below appears once in the grid. You must determine which line is which. RENBAN LINE: Contains a set of non-repeating consecutive digits, in any order. GERMAN WHISPER LINE: Adjacent digits along the line have a difference of at least 5. THERMOMETER: Digits are arranged in ascending order, from one end to the other, without repeats. REGION SUM LINE: Along the line, digits within each 3x3 box have the same total. The line visits at least two different boxes. PALINDROME LINE: The sequence of digits along the line reads the same in either direction. PARITY LINE: All digits on the line have the same parity. UNLUCKY LINE: Adjacent digits along the line sum to at least 13.
1373: Normal sudoku rules apply. Any cages that have the same total are cage friends. A circled digit in a cage indicates how many friends that cage has. The blue, pink and purple cages each have no friends :(
1374: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each line within a 3x3 box has the same total, which is displayed in yellow in that box. (2-digit yellow totals read from left to right.) The digit in the purple square indicates how many of the yellow totals have the same parity (oddness/evenness) as itself (ie the purple square digit).
1375: Normal sudoku rules apply. A circled digit indicates exactly how many circles contain that digit. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow's circle.
1376: Normal sudoku rules apply. A clue outside the grid shows the sum of the indicated diagonal, which may include repeat digits.
1377: Normal sudoku rules apply, and identical digits cannot be a chess knight's move apart. Digits in a cage sum to the total given in the top corner and must not repeat.
1378: Normal Sudoku rules apply. Digits can not be next to another consecutive digit. Digits cannot be a knight's or king's move apart.
1379: Normal sudoku rules apply. On thermometer shapes, digits must increase from the bulb end.
1380: Normal sudoku rules apply. In addition, place the eight thermometers into the grid. The thermometers must be placed into the grid in their original orientation (see the puzzle link). They may not be rotated or reflected. The thermometers may not overlap each other. However, they may overlap the given digits in the grid. Along each thermometer digits must increase starting from the bulb.
1381: Normal Sudoku rules apply. Each number outside the grid is the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. Digits may repeat within a sum.
1382: Normal sudoku rules apply. 1 is treated as a poker ace. A greater-than symbol joining two cages indicates which cage is the higher-ranking hand in poker. Digits MAY repeat in a cage but cards may not repeat in a cage (but they may repeat in the grid). Eg a cage may not contain two cells with the 3 of hearts , but there may be two cells in the grid that both contain the 3 of hearts . Treat the cards and values exactly as you would in a game of poker. For example, an ace (1) ranks higher than any other card, but can be used as part of the lowest-ranking straight or straight flush: 12345. On the other hand, 6789A is not a straight.
1383: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along thermometers, the digits must increase starting from the bulb.
1384: Divide the grid along the indicated lines into areas - galaxies with rotational symmetry. Each cell must belong to one galaxy, and each galaxy must have one circle at its center of rotational symmetry.
1385: Divide the grid into regions formed of adjacent squares. Each region should contain two given numbers. The size of each region should be a value (in unit squares) between the two numbers inside that region.
1386: Locate a snake in the grid whose head and tail are given as circles. The snake can touch itself diagonally but not orthogonally. The remaining cells must form exactly nine white areas from size 1 to 9. Numbers in the grid must be part of white areas of the indicated size.
1387: Blacken some white cells then draw a single closed loop through all remaining white cells.Grey cells cannot be part of loop and indicate how many blackened cells that exist in that direction of the grid.
1388: Draw a single closed loop passing through some empty cells in the grid. The grid contains bordered/coloured cells that cannot be part of the loop. Black cells must be outside the loop. White cells must be inside the loop. Arrows in cells indicate the number of loop segments in that direction.
1389: Shade cells to create a single orthogonally connected region. No 2x2 region can contain shaded cells. Numbers outside the grid represent groups of consecutive shaded cells in that row/column. * is any size except zero.
1390: Divide the grid into pentominoes (five-cell regions) so that no two pentominoes of the same shape (including rotations/reflections) share an edge. A cell with a letter in it must be part of the pentomino shape normally associated with that letter. An inventory of pentominoes is given below the puzzle but not all shapes must be used.
1391: Divide the grid along the dotted lines into regions called polyominoes so that no two polyominoes with the same area share an edge. Inside some cells are numbers; each number must represent the area of the polyomino it belongs to. A polyomino may contain zero, one, or more of the given numbers. (It is possible for a “hidden” polyomino — a polyomino without any of the given numbers — to contain a value that is not present in the starting grid.)
1392: Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid (without arrows) give the sum of the cells sandwiched between the 1 and 9 in that row/column. Clues by arrows outside the grid give the sum of the cells along the indicated diagonal. Digits can repeat along these diagonals.
1393: Normal sudoku rules apply. The sum of the digits along the path of each arrow must equal the digit in the circled cell. Digits can repeat within an arrow shape.
1394: Normal sudoku rules apply, and digits along arrows sum to the (1- or 2-digit numbers) in the 'circles' from which they originate.
1395: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow’s circle.
1396: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow's circle.
1397: Normal sudoku rules apply, and digits increase along thermometers from the bulb. Digits along arrows sum to the numbers in the 'circles', which may be 2-digit numbers.
1398: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the value in the top-left corner of the cage. Digits may not repeat in cages. The marked diagonal must contain each digit from 1 to 9 exactly once. Cells that are separated by a knight's move (in chess) may not contain the same digit.
1399: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. Digits along arrows sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. Digits may repeat along such a diagonal if allowed by other rules.
1400: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage (if given). Digits cannot repeat within a cage. Each main diagonal (marked in blue) cannot contain a repeated digit.
1401: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage (if given). Digits cannot repeat within a cage.
1402: Each cell is part of a region of N cells (N can be 1 or higher). Regions of the same size can touch each other diagonally but not orthogonally. Cells on thermometers are in regions of strictly increasing size, starting from the bulb end (e.g. if the bulb is in a 2-cell region, the next cell along the thermo is in a region of at least 3 cells).
1403: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digit must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Adjacent digits along a green line must differ by at least 5.
1404: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits cannot repeat, and sum to the number in the top-left corner of the cage.
1405: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the number in the circle. Digits directly joined on a green line must have a difference of at least 5.
1406: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Digits on a purple line form a non-repeating consecutive set (which can appear in any order). Grey opaque circles (without arrows) contain the sum of all their orthogonally adjacent cells.
1407: Normal sudoku rules apply. The digit in the grey circle is odd. In each set of outside digits, exactly one digit is found in the corresponding row or column in the second box from the clue. All other digits in the set will be found within the first three cells in the row or column from the clue. For instance a '12' clue above column 1 could mean that '1' is found in r123c1 and '2' is found in r456c1, or vice versa.
1408: Normal sudoku rules apply. Rush Hour mechanics apply to car movements; given digits on cars move with the cars. Digits on pink lines and pink cars must form a set of consecutive numbers in any order. Adjacent digits on green lines and green cars must vary by at least 5. Digits adjacent on black dots and black cars must form a 2:1 ratio. Cars may not permanently park adjacent/touching a black dot. (Example: in row 6 starting positions, the black car is touching, but the pink car is not). Initially no cars may leave the caged 6x6 Region. Move the Red Car through the Cage opening and into the red outlined Parking Space to allow the other cars to move outside this initial cage. (Press the button that appears to release the cars.) Other cages in the grid are Reserved Parking spaces. Park the correspondingly coloured cars in their space. Reserved Parking have hidden given digits to be discovered while driving. Revealed digits do not move.
1409: Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells in the grid. Shaded cells cannot share an edge with each other. The unshaded cells must form a single orthogonally-connected area. The digit contained in each circle indicates how many cells must be shaded in that 3x3 box. A contiguous line (vertical or horizontal) of unshaded cells cannot span two 3x3 region borders. The digits in a cage may not repeat and must sum to the value given in the top left of the cage. Shaded cells do not contribute to the total.
1410: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on a grey line must increase or stay the same from bulb to tip. A digit contained in a large white circle must appear at least once in the four cells it touches. Digits connected by a black dot must be in a 2:1 ratio. Digits connected by a white dot must be consecutive. Not all dots are necessarily given. Each set of three digits along a yellow line must comprise a full set of the digits modulo 3, i.e. one each of [147], [258], and [369].
1411: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits connected by white dots are consecutive. Digits connected by black dots are in a 1:2 ratio. Not all dots are necessarily given. JENGA blocks are Killer Cages. Ie The digits within a block must sum to the total (if given) in the top left corner of the block. Some block totals are replaced with the letters JENGA and must be determined by the solver. The values of the letters increase alphabetically. (i.e. A is less than E.) [Note that two blocks have fallen and are skewed, the cage totals and dots apply within the blocks - imagine they only cover the two cells diagonally]
1412: Normal sudoku rules apply. Colors used in this puzzle are pink and yellow. The clues outside the grid indicate the order of runs of contiguous cells found in that row or column that must be shaded the color of the clue. The number in the clue indicates the sum of the cells in the run. There must be at least one unshaded cell between runs of the same color, though there is no need between runs of differing colors. All runs are given. The black dot separates digits in a 1:2 ratio. Digits on the pink line are consecutive.
1413: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on “region sum lines” (marked in blue) must have an equal sum N within each 3x3 box they pass through. (eg r7c3 [box7] = r6c2 + r5c2 [box 4]) Cells separated by a V must contain digits summing to 5. Not all V clues are necessarily given. Digits cannot repeat along the marked purple diagonals.
1414: Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade the grid using two colours, such that all instances of each colour are orthogonally connected, and no 2x2 area is completely one colour. Blue lines must have an equal sum N within each colour they pass through. If a blue line passes through a colour multiple times, each individual pass sums to N. All lines must cross colours at least once. Two digits separated by a black dot have a ratio of 2. Not all dots are given.
1415: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Cells containing filled grey circles must contain odd digits. The value of r8c7 is less than that of r8c8.
1416: Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells in the grid such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected. The digit in a circle gives the number of shaded cells within its 3x3 box. Not all circles are given. Within each 3x3 box, every separate orthogonally connected group of shaded cells must sum to N, where N is the same for all boxes.
1417: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Cells separated by a chess knight's move cannot contain the same digit.
1418: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle.
1419: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on a blue line must have an equal sum N within each 3x3 box the line passes through. If a line re-enters a 3x3 box, each segment sums to N separately. eg r3c1+r3c2=r4c2=r3c3+r2c3=r2c4=r1c2+r1c3
1420: Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells in the grid such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected. Within each 3x3 box, every separate orthogonally connected group of shaded cells must sum to N, where N is the same for all boxes. Circles can be shaded or unshaded, and the digit in a circle is the number of shaded cells in its 3x3 box. Squares are shaded, and the digit in a square is the number of shaded cells “seen” horizontally or vertically combined from that cell (including itself), where unshaded cells block vision. Diamonds are unshaded, and the digit in a diamond is the size of the orthogonally connected group of unshaded cells that it belongs to.
1421: This TOP SECRET sudoku has had all its digits redacted. Every redaction is either a Renban, German Whispers or Anti-Factor line. All I can tell you is that row 1 uses exactly two Renban lines, and every other row, column, and 3x3 box uses at least two different types of line. Digits along a Renban line form a set of non-repeating consecutive digits in any order. Consecutive cells along a German Whispers line contain digits which differ by at least 5. Digits along an Anti-Factor line of length n may not be any multiple or factor of n (other than the digit 1), and must sum to a multiple of n. eg a line of length 4 could not contain 2,4 or 8 (but could contain 1).
1422: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in large circles must appear in the surrounding 2x2 area. Digits separated by white dots are consecutive. Digits separated by black dots have a 2:1 ratio (ie. one is double the other). Not all such dots are shown. Shade some cells such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected and all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected and no 2x2 area is fully shaded or unshaded. Digits in caged cells indicate how many cells of the same colour (shaded or unshaded) are seen orthogonally from that position, including itself. The "other" colour blocks vision. All dots lie on the boundary of the Yin-Yang pattern (ie. each dot touches one shaded and one unshaded cell). Finally, the grid is partially covered in fog. Placing correct digits will clear the fog from surrounding cells, possibly revealing more clues.
1423: Fill the grid with nine non-overlapping 3x3 square regions, such that each region contains the digits 1-9 once each and no digit repeats in any row or column. Cells outside regions do not contain digits. Cages show the sum of their digits, and digits cannot repeat within a cage. Digits along arrows sum to the digit in the connected circle, and can repeat if allowed by other rules.
1424: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along grey thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb end.
1425: Normal sudoku rules do NOT apply. Fill the grid with digits 1-9, such that no digit repeats in any row, column or box. The set of digits in each row or column is unique, eg. if a row contains the digits 1234, no other row or column may contain exactly those digits. The digits in every row, column and box sum to x, where x has to be determined by the solver. Digits separated by an X sum to 10. Digits separated by a V sum to 5. Not all Xs and Vs are necessarily given.
1426: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a knight's move (as in chess) cannot contain the same digit as each other. Digits on a purple line form a set of non-repeating, consecutive digits in any order. Adjacent digits along a green line must have a difference of at least 5. Digits along an arrow sum to the number in the circle.
1427: Divide the grid into two areas of orthogonally connected cells. One of the areas is a Meidjuluk (N=9), the other is a Fillomino. Divide the Meidjuluk area into 9 regions, one of each size 1 to 9. A Meidjuluk region may not contain repeated numbers, and it may only contain factors of its size (eg a region of size 6 may contain any combination of 1,2,3, and 6, including none of them). Divide the Fillomino area into orthogonally connected regions such that no two Fillomino regions of the same size share an edge, and enter a number into each cell equal to the size of its region.
1428: Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid indicate pairs of digits that must be adjacent in that row or column.
1429: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along a thermometer, digits must increase from the bulb to the tip. Place 9 straight, vertical thermometers, each of different lengths, in the grid. All the thermometers must start from row 9 of the grid. Ie the thermometers all have their bulbs in row 9. No two 9s in the grid share a diagonal. The clues outside the grid are skyscraper clues ie they indicate how many numbers can be "seen" when looking into the grid along the column. A number is visible only when it is larger than all numbers that appear before it along the line of sight.
1430: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits along a green line must differ by at least 5. Each grey line consists of one or more non-overlapping groups of consecutive cells, each of which sums to 10.
1431: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a circle appear at least once each in the four surrounding cells. From left to right, top to bottom, the following lines have the following properties: Whisper (green): Adjacent digits differ by 5 or more. Thermo (gray): Digits increase from the bulb to the end. Renban (purple): The line contains a set of consecutive digits (not necessarily in order). Between (gray): Digits on the line are between the values in the circled ends. Region Sum (blue): Digits on the line have the same sum in each box the line is in. 10 Line (gray): The line consists of one or more contiguous groups of cells, each of which sums to 10. Groups cannot overlap. Nabner (yellow): No two digits may be consecutive. Parity (red): Adjacent digits alternate between odd/even parity. Modular (black): Every set of three sequential digits contains one digit from {1,4,7}, one from {2,5,8}, and one from {3,6,9}. Entropic (orange): Every set of three sequential digits contains one digit from {1,2,3}, one from {4,5,6}, and one from {7,8,9}.
1432: Normal sudoku rules apply. Blue lines are “region sum lines”: Along a line, each line segment within a different 3x3 box must sum to the same total. Different lines may have different totals for their line segments.
1433: Clues outside the grid are Parity Party clues and give the sum of the digits up to and including the first even digit or up to and including the first odd digit from that side. Single digit clues might give the first digit only. (i.e. a 7 clue could mean the first cell seen contains a 7, the first two cells contain an even and an odd that sum to 7, or the first two cells have a 24 pair and the third cell contains a 1.) Digits within cages cannot repeat, and sum to the small number shown. This puzzle is solved in two stages: Stage 1: Each 3x3 box is solved independently as a 3x3 “mean mini”. (ie each box uses exactly three digits from 1-9 without repeating in the rows or columns of that box.) Outside clues are for the first box seen in this stage (ie they “work” for the box next to the clue). Stage 2: Delete all digits except for the central cell of each 3x3 box. then solve the puzzle as a regular 9x9 sudoku using the remaining digits as givens. Outside clues can now see further than just the first box seen.
1434: Into each non-gray cell place a digit from 1-9. Digits cannot repeat within a row, column, or box. Every digit in the puzzle is part of an orthogonally connected clump of digits that sums to 10. Digits may repeat within clumps if allowed by other rules. Clumps do not overlap with other clumps. A circled cell gives the number of clumps in the up to 9 surrounding cells (including itself).
1435: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits may not repeat within cages. Cages show their sums. Digits along a thermo increase, starting from the bulb end.
1436: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the number in its circle. Adjacent digits on a green line have a difference of at least 5. The digit in the gray circle is odd. A black dot joins digits with a 1:2 ratio. A white dot joins consecutive digits. Each dot shown is black or white or both.
1437: Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a loop (one cell wide) of orthogonally connected cells, which does not touch itself, not even diagonally. Each digit on the loop indicates exactly how many times that digit appears on the loop. Eg: If there's a 5 on the loop, it means there are five 5s on the loop. The loop must pass through the bulb of every thermometer. Digits along a thermometer increase from the bulb end. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive.
1438: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage cannot repeat and must sum to either exactly one more than the given sum or one less than the given sum.
1439: Normal sudoku rules apply. A digit in an arrow shows the distance to a cell containing an 8 or a 9 in the indicated direction (not necessarily the 8 or 9 closest to it). For example a 1 points to the cell directly adjacent to it. Not all arrows are necessarily given.
1440: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each line must be completely divided into one or more non-overlapping strings of adjacent digits which add to 20. Note that repeats are still allowed within these sums within the normal constraints of sudoku. Digits separated by a black dot have a 1:2 ratio.
1441: Normal sudoku rules apply. All clue types are standard. However, exactly one instance of every clue type is lying to you! Constraints that do not lie work as follows: Between Lines: Cells along lines between two blue circles must have values between those in the circles. Black Kropki: Cells separated by a black dot contain digits with a ratio of 1:2. Even: A cell with a grey square must contain an even digit. German Whispers: Adjacent digits along a green line have a difference of at least 5. Odd: A cell with a grey circle must contain an odd digit. Renban: Cells along a purple line must contain a set of consecutive digits. Sandwich: Clues outside the grid give the sum of digits sandwiched between the 1 and 9 in that row/column. V: Cells separated by a V must contain digits summing to 5. White Kropki: Cells separated by a white dot must contain consecutive digits. X: Cells separated by an X must contain digits summing to 10.
1442: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in red-shaded cells in column 1 indicate the position of 1 in that row. The same is true in columns 5 and 9 for 5's and 9's respectively. Digits in a Quadruple circle must be placed at least once in the four cells touching that circle.
1443: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits cannot repeat on the indicated diagonal. Digits along blue lines have the same sum within each 3x3 box the line enters. Digits in cells with a shaded square must be even. Digits in cells with a shaded circle must be odd.
1444: Normal sudoku rules apply. Yellow lines are 'Same Difference' lines. Each pair of adjacent digits on one of these lines has the same difference. However, this 'difference value' may be different for different lines. A digit in a circle indicates exactly how many circles contain that digit.
1445: Normal sudoku rules apply. Grey lines are "between lines"; the digits along the line must have values between the digits in the grey circles at the line's ends. Digits in a black circle must appear at least once within the four cells touching the circle.
1446: Normal sudoku rules apply. A number in a circle gives how many times that number appears in circles (anywhere in the puzzle). A clue outside the grid gives the sum of the first X digits from that direction where X is the digit next to the clue.
1447: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on an arrow sum to the digit in the circle of that arrow.
1448: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits may not repeat on the marked diagonal. Digits on a purple line form a set of nonrepeating consecutive digits, which may be in any order. Any three consecutive cells on an orange line must all have different remainders modulo 3 (ie in three consecutive cells there must be one digit from [147], one digit from [258] and one from [369]. Digits along a thermometer line increase from the bulb end. Digits in a cage sum to the indicated total. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Digits separated by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio (ie one digit is double the other).
1449: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits may not repeat on the marked diagonal. Digits in a cage do not repeat and sum to the small number in the top left corner of the cage.
1450: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages may not repeat and must sum to the total in the top left corner. A line may contain no digit that is a multiple or factor of its length, other than the digit 1; and the digits along a line must sum to a multiple of its length. Digits may repeat along a line if allowed by the other rules.
1451: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits on a turquoise line must have the same difference, though this difference can be different for different lines. Each quad (ie black) circle contains all the digits in the surrounding 4 cells. Unfortunately these quad clues have all been written in white text, and so are invisible. Digits in a grey circle must be odd. A digit in a circle (odd or quad clue) shows how many times that digit appears in a circle. E.g. if there is a 5 in a quad clue, then there must be 5 total appearances of 5s in quad clues and odd circles combined.
1452: Normal sudoku rules apply. Any three adjacent digits along a yellow line include one digit from each entropy group, i.e. one digit from [1,2,3], one digit from [4,5,6] and one digit from [7,8,9]. If the line is only 2 cells long, both of its digits have different entropy. Digits do not repeat along the indicated diagonal. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Digits separated by a black dot are in a ratio of 2:1.
1453: Normal sudoku rules apply. Divide the grid entirely into '15-clumps' - non-overlapping orthogonally connected groups of cells, each of which contains no repeated digits and sums to 15. An arrow in a grid indicates that exactly N 15-clumps can be seen in the direction of the arrow, where N is the digit in the arrow's cell. The arrow's cell is not counted, though that cell's clump may be counted if other cells in it are visible in that direction. Two arrows in the same cell are counted as independent clues.
1454: Normal sudoku rules apply. Four yellow killer cages are hiding in the fog. Enter correct digits to clear the nearby fog. No guessing is necessary (or allowed!) Digits in a killer cage sum to the small number in the top left corner of that cage. Digits CAN repeat within a cage. In fact, a digit in a cage indicates exactly how many times that digit appears in that cage. Eg a 5 in a cage means that there are five 5s in that cage. Grey lines are bulbless thermometers ie Digits along a grey line must be arranged in ascending order, from one end to the other. Cells separated by a white dot must contain consecutive digits.
1455: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage cannot repeat and sum to the given total. Numbers cannot repeat along the diagonals. Gray lines are palindromes that read the same forwards and backwards. The digits separated by the white dot have a difference of one.
1456: Normal sudoku rules apply. The sum of two neighbouring digits on a grey line is always either 7 or 9.
1457: Normal sudoku rules apply. No digit can appear a chess knight's move away from itself. Place two thermometers into the grid, one of 6-cell length and the other of 9-cell length. Both thermometers have their bulbs in column 1 and are straight traveling in a south-easterly direction. Numbers increase from the bulb to the end of the thermometers.
1458: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Each main diagonal must contain all of the digits 1 to 9. Along thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb end. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in its circle. Digits may repeat along an arrow.
1459: Normal Sudoku rules apply. A 1-cell-wide python, which may not touch itself, even diagonally, begins and ends at the red squares. Digits on the python form a palindrome, with the purple square at the midpoint. The grey cells (stones) are NOT python. Each stone shows how many of its surrounding cells (INCLUDING the stone itself) are NOT python. All stone digits are different. The blue cells may be python. Each blue cell shows how many of its surrounding cells (INCLUDING the cell itself) are python. ALL possible coloured cells are given.
1460: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle.
1461: Normal sudoku rules apply. The main diagonal (marked in blue) cannot contain a repeated digit. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. The cell containing a grey circle must contain an odd digit.
1462: Place the digits 0-9 in the grid so that every row, column, and 3x3 box contains every digit exactly once. To enable this, there is a single Schrödinger cell (S-cell) in each row, column and box, containing a superposition of two different digits. Each S-Cell is a Kakuro clue to the right or downwards, showing the sum of digits between that cell and the edge of the grid. A number outside the grid is also a Kakuro clue, showing the sum of digits between the edge of the grid and the next S-clue eg if an S-Cell contains the digits 12, the clue must be twelve or twenty one. Kakuro clues can be zero or have a leading zero. R2c1 contains an even digit.
1463: Normal sudoku rules apply. The marked diagonal must contain all of the digits 1-9. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage.
1464: Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid indicate the sum of the digits sandwiched between the 1 and 9 in that row/column. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow’s circle (ie in this puzzle all arrow tips must contain the same digit as their circle!).
1465: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Cells containing an opaque grey circle contain odd digits. Cells containing an opaque grey square contain even digits.
1466: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a knight’s move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. Digits on an arrow must sum to the value in the attached circle. Adjacent digits on a green line must differ by at least 5. Digits do not repeat in cages, which sum to the given total.
1467: Normal sudoku rules apply. A purple line contains a string of non-repeating consecutive digits in any order. Digits in a cage must sum to the total in the top left corner, and cannot include repeats.
1468: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along the ORANGE line indicate the column in which the digit 5 appears in that ROW (from left to right). Digits along the BLUE line indicate the row in which the digit 5 appears in that COLUMN (from top to bottom). Adjacent digits along a GREEN line must differ by at least 5.
1469: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on an arrow sum to the value in the attached circle. A clue outside the grid indicates the sum of the digits along the marked diagonal.
1470: Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a loop that travels around the grid orthogonally through the centre of cells. This loop must pass through each 3x3 box at least once. No 2x2 area can fully contain loop cells and adjacent digits upon the loop must differ by at least 5. In a cage digits must sum to the total (z) in the top left corner of the cage if given. Additionally, each cage will reveal a coordinate (Row X Column Y, with X being the uppermost/leftmost digit and Y being the lowermost/rightmost digit) whereby Z must be placed. Each cage's coordinate cell must be part of the loop, and cages are allowed to reference the same cell multiple times throughout the puzzle. The given '6' cage is unique; no other cage can sum to 6!
1471: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each segment of a line within a different 3x3 box must sum to the same value. If a line re-enters the same box it must also sum to the value for that line. For example, r5c7 + r5c8 = r6c6 = r7c7 + r8c7. Different lines may have different sums.
1472: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells with the same relative position within a 3x3 box must contain different digits. For example, all cells in the top-left corner of each box must contain a different digit. Digits cannot repeat along the indicated diagonal. Along a blue line, each line segment within a different 3x3 box must sum to the same total. Blue lines may have different totals to one another!
1473: Normal sudoku rules apply, and the marked diagonals each contain 1-9, as do the blue cells. The Little Killer Clue shows the sum of the indicated diagonal. Box 3 (red) is a Magic Square. All the rows, columns, and diagonals sum to the same number. Box 5 (green) uses all the numbers, 1-9 in forming 2-digit Prime Numbers reading across (left-to-right) or down. Box 9 (purple) contains all the 2-digit Square Numbers reading across (left-to-right) or down.
1474: In this puzzle ‘2-digit numbers’ read from left to right or downwards. Box 1 (NW) will contain all the 2-digit square numbers (16, 25, 36, 49, 64, and 81), which may overlap but must be entirely contained within the box. Box 9 (SE) is a clone of box 1, rotated through 180°. In each of boxes 3 (NE), 5 (centre) and 7 (SW), each digit will contribute to at least one 2-digit prime number contained within that box. Box 4 (W) is a magic square, with each row, column, and 3-digit diagonal summing to the same total. In each of box 6 (E) and 8 (S), the two 3-digit diagonals sum to the same number (NB box 6's number may be different from box 8's number).
1475: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a thermometer must increase from the bulb. Neighbouring digits along a green line have a difference of at least 5. Digits on the orange line sum to 26.

1493: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on the blue line have an equal sum, N, within each 3x3 box through which it passes. 1508: Oh, no! The Wicked Witch Lorena has cursed you with forgetting all numbers! Each double arrow has its own colour. Elements of the same colour are connected. Digits in killer cages sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage (if given) and cannot repeat. Each killer cage has its own colour. Elements of the same colour are connected. Additionally the grid is partially covered in fog. Placing correct digits will clear the fog from surrounding cells, possibly revealing more clues. (And a pair of missing shoes)!
1584: After it gets dark Nala loves to go outside and look for new friends in our backyard. Will she find one today? Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a thermometer increase from the bulb end to the tip. There is only one tip for each thermometer and each thermometer has its own colour. Elements of the same colour are connected. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Digits separated by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio. Not all possible dots are given. Additionally the grid is partially covered in fog. Placing correct digits will clear the fog from surrounding cells, possibly revealing more clues.
1585: It has to be somewhere, right? Nala knows that she will get something for her birthday and secretly searches in all the rooms. She hates to wait until her birthday for the gift reveal. Will she find her present or is it hidden well enough? Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits may not repeat in a cage; cages show their sums. A palindrome line reads the same from both directions. Each palindrome has its own color and lines of the same color are connected. A clue outside the grid indicates the digit which has to be placed in the Nth cell in the corresponding direction, where N is the first digit. The grid is partially covered in fog. Placing correct digits will clear the fog from surrounding cells, possibly revealing more clues.
1586: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each of the digits 1-9 appears as a „Doubler“ exactly once in the grid. There is only one „Doubler“ in each row, column and 3x3 box. Digits that appear as a „Doubler“ have a value that is double their size. The value of digits in a cage must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits may not repeat within a cage, although values may. The value of digits along an arrow must sum to the value of the digit in the attached circle. Each arrow has its own colour. Arrows of the same colour are connected. Additionally the grid is partially covered in fog. Placing correct digits will clear the fog from surrounding cells, possibly revealing more clues.
1587: Normal sudoku rules apply: Place the digits 1-9 in every row, column and box exactly once each. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow’s circle. Each arrow has its own colour. Arrows of the same colour are connected. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Digits separated by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio. Not all possible dots are given. One cell in the grid is your newly found “motivation”. Cells must increase in value as they move away from this point in every straight-line direction (i.e. vertically, horizontally and diagonally) until they reach the edge of the grid. Once found, everything will start to flow again. Additionally the grid is partially covered in fog just as your thinking might be impaired sometimes and not allow clear thoughts. Placing correct digits will clear the fog from surrounding cells, possibly revealing more clues.
1588: Normal sudoku rules apply: Place the digits 1-9 in every row, column and box exactly once each. Digits in a dashed cage must sum to the value in the top left corner of the cage (if given). Digits may not repeat within their own cage. Nori Nori Christmas: Shade exactly two cells in each cage. Each shaded area forms a domino (cookie), not necessarily within a cage. Shaded dominoes may touch diagonally, but not orthogonally. A shaded domino functions as a black Kropki dot, i.e. digits in a shaded domino are in a ratio of 2:1. It is possible for unshaded dominoes to be in a 2:1 ratio. Digits separated by a white sugar decoration dot are consecutive. Not all possible dots are given. Additionally the grid is partially covered in fog. Placing correct digits will clear the fog from surrounding cells, possibly revealing more clues.
1589: Normal sudoku rules apply. Every digit that appears in a circle must also appear in at least one of its 4 surrounding cells. If an arrow is present in a cell, the digit in the cell the arrow comes from appears in the grid in the direction of the arrow at a distance of N cells, where N is the digit in the arrow's cell. (Not all arrows are necessarily given - there is not negative constraint.) Example: If R3C4 had an arrow pointing to the left and was a 3, and the digit below that arrow in R4C4 was a 5, then another 5 would be placed in R3C1. The grid is partially covered in fog. Placing correct digits will clear the fog from surrounding cells, possibly revealing more clues.
1590: Normal sudoku rules apply. In the final grid all clues need to be wrong. A clue is wrong when the placed digits cause it to be invalid. Placing digits that successfully make clues invalid will help clearing the fog from surrounding cells, possibly revealing more nonsense (clues). Clues are valid if: Digits in a cage sum up to the number on its top left (if given) and do NOT contain repeated digits; digits on arrows sum to the digit in the attached circle. (Each arrow is a separate clue, even if multiple arrows share the same circle); digits on a slow thermometer increase or stay the same as they move from the bulb to the tip; adjacent digits on a green line have a difference of at least 5; adjacent digits on an orange line have a difference of at least 4; digits in an orange shaded circle are odd; digits in a blue shaded square are even; all digits in a (larger) white circle appear in the 4 cells touching it; digits joined by a white dot are consecutive; digits joined by a black dot are in a ratio of 1:2.
1591: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits an equal distance from the centre of a lavender “Zipper Line” sum to the same total. For odd-length lines, the total is the digit placed in the line's (circled) centre. Digits may repeat on a Zipper Line.
1592: Place digits from 1-9 in every cell, so that no digit repeats in a row, column, or 3x3 region. The dashed lines indicate the boundaries of regions, and cells on the lines are simultaneously part of the regions on both sides of the line. Adjacent digits on a green line differ by at least 5. On a blue line, the sum of digits on the line is the same in each region the line passes through. Cells on a region boundary count toward both regions' sums.
1593: Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected, and all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected (a 2x2 area MAY be fully shaded or unshaded). For each N, row N and box N both have exactly N shaded cells, which contain exactly the digits from 1 to N. Adjacent cells on the red line have different parities i.e. one digit is odd and the other digit is even.
1594: Normal sudoku rules apply. Numbers in circles show the difference between the adjoining pair of digits. Digits separated by a V sum to 5. Digits separated by an X sum to 10. Not all such differences, Xs or Vs are shown.
1595: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits within each cage must sum to either 6 or 9. By rotating the grid through 180° each cage sum is also rotated such that 6 becomes 9. For example, the cage at r1c234 must have a different value to the cage at r9c678. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Not all possible dots are given.
1596: Normal sudoku rules apply. Additionally the solver must find a single snake of orthogonally connected digits beginning at the given 1 which does not touch itself (even diagonally), does not touch any white dots but must visit each 3x3 box in the grid. Each digit on the snake is the sum of the previous two digits modulo 10 (eg 5+7 = 2). NB The second snake digit after the given 1 can be any digit. Grey digits are not on the snake but show the number of snake cells in the surrounding (up to) eight cells. Cells separated by a white dot must contain consecutive digits. Not all possible dots are given.
1597: Normal sudoku rules apply. Within the grid lies a single snake of orthogonally connected cells which does not touch itself (even diagonally). The first and last cell on the snake contain the digit 9. Digits placed on circles and squares show the number of snake cells in the surrounding (up to) 9 cells including the circle or square itself if it is on the snake. Circles contain odd digits; squares contain even digits.
1598: Normal sudoku rules apply. The solver must draw a single loop which travels along the grid lines but not on the outer perimeter. The loop must not branch or touch itself. A digit in a blue cell shows the number of that cell's corners (grey dots) which touch the loop. Pairs of digits separated by the loop have a difference of 1.
1599: Normal sudoku rules apply. Eight grey palindromes, reading the same from each end, all begin at the central cell of the grid. Inequality signs ‘point’ to the lower digit of the adjoining pair.
1600: Normal sudoku rules apply. Orthogonally adjacent digits must not be consecutive. A digit in a circle or square must not be a multiple or divisor of any orthogonally adjacent digit. Grey circles contain odd digits. Grey squares contain even digits.
1601: Normal sudoku rules apply, and digits increase along thermometers from the bulb. If the U shapes were "unrolled" into a straight line (leaving their central three cells fixed), they would still have the same digits as they do in their current shapes.
1602: Beginning in the yellow cell, create a 1-cell wide path that cannot cross itself or touch itself orthogonally, but can touch itself diagonally; the path must alternate between circles and coloured cells (beginning with yellow) until all circles and all coloured cells are taken. The grey cells are walls. The digit in a wall cell indicates the number of path cells in the 8 cells around that wall. Circle cells are different odd digits, square cells (the 4 coloured cells) are different even digits. Row 5 and Column 5 wrap around, meaning the path can pass through one end and come out on the other side (like in Pac-Man).
1603: Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the cells along the indicated diagonal. Digits may repeat along these diagonals. Cells separated by a V must sum to 5; cells separated by an X must sum to 10. (There is no negative constraint ie it is still possible for cells without an X/V to sum to 5/10.)
1604: Normal sudoku rules apply, and lines in the grid are palindromes, which can be read the same either way. White dots separate cells with consecutive digits, and the black dot separates cells with a 1:2 ratio. No negative Kropki constraint applies, so other neighbouring cells can also contain consecutive digits or digits with a 1:2 ratio.
1605: Normal sudoku rules apply, and digits do not repeat within cages. V and X show differences of 5 (V) or 10 (X) between the sums in the cages they separate. Other instances of differences of 5 or 10 between cages may not be marked.
1606: Normal sudoku rules apply. Grey lines are palindromes ie they read the same from both directions. Along thermometers digits must increase from the bulb end. In each cage, digits must sum to 9 or 6. Digits may not repeat in cages.
