2203: Draw a non-intersecting loop through the centers of some cells that passes through every circle and moves orthogonally between cells (ie never diagonally). The loop must turn on black circles and travel straight through the cells on either side. The loop must go straight through white circles, and turn in at least one of the cells on either side. All orthogonally connected groups of non-loop cells must be connected to the edge of the grid. For the solution check function to work, enter a 1 into every non-loop cell and 2 into every cell in which the loop turns.
2204: Normal 6x6 sudoku rules apply. Digits along a diagonal marked by an arrow sum to the digit on the arrow, if one is given. Any digit along an 'arrow diagonal' indicates exactly how many arrow diagonals contain that digit. Eg: if there is a digit 3 somewhere along an arrow diagonal, then exactly 3 arrow diagonals contain at least one 3.
2205: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits may not repeat in a cage. The totals of cages an equal distance from the central cage along a lavender line must sum to the total of the central cage. Eg For the line beginning in r7c1 there are five cages along the line left-to-right; labelling these cages A, B, C, D & E, the central cage C (comprising r8c5&r8c6) sums to the same as the cells in cages B+D and the same as the cages A+E. The digit in the cell marked with a square is even.
2206: Normal LITS rules apply. Ie Shade one tetromino in each region. (A tetromino is a shape of four orthogonally-connected cells.) No two tetrominoes of the same shape may share an edge - reflections/rotations count as the same shape. All tetrominoes must form a single orthogonally connected area. No 2x2 area of the grid can be completely shaded. Additionally, each row, column and region must contain exactly one white star and one black star. Black stars must be located on tetrominoes, and white stars must not. Regardless of colour, stars may not touch each other - not even diagonally.
2207: Divide the Fillominosaurus into regions of orthogonally connected cells with a maximum size of 9 cells such that regions of the same size do not share a border, and fill every cell with a digit equal to the size of its region (ie the number of cells that region contains). A thick black line is a region border. Adjacent digits on a dark green line differ by EXACTLY 5. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. The digit in the circle shows how many times it appears in that circle. The eight cells with teeth attached all contain different digits. (Please note that the teeth themselves are not part of the grid for the purpose of the Fillomino! It is the eight "gum" cells that must contain different digits!)
2208: In this puzzle, a Latin Square is defined as an NxN grid of cells that contain only the digits 1 to N where N is greater than 1, in which digits do not repeat in a row or column. This puzzle contains exactly three Latin Squares: one within another within another. Cells separated by a knight's move (in chess) may not contain the same digit. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive; digits separated by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio (ie one digit is double the other).
2209: Nala lost her Toy in the fog (again). Can you help her find it? Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow must sum to digit in that arrow's circle. Elements of the same colour are connected. The grid is partially covered in fog. Placing correct digits will clear the fog from surrounding cells. Nala will be thrilled about your help!
2210: Normal sudoku rules apply. Divide the grid into an ocean and islands of one or more orthogonally connected cells such that each island contains a set of digits summing to 9. Digits may repeat on an island but each island must contain a unique set of digits. Islands must not touch each other (even diagonally) except at cells joined by a line, each line marks a bridge between two islands. All cells not part of an island are in the ocean which must be a contiguous region of orthogonally connected cells that never completely fills a 2x2 area. A digit in a circle counts the number of cells in its own region (island or ocean) seen in its row and column combined, including itself, where cells in other regions block vision and are not seen.
2211: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is divided into 9 snakes. Each snake is a path of length 9, starting at its tail in the southwest and moving orthogonally north or east — never west or south — to its head in the northeast. Three heads (red diamonds) and two tails (green squares) are shown, pointing to the next cell in that snake. Digits in a snake cannot repeat. The snake that contains the blue dot is a thermosnake, with digits increasing from its tail to its head. Adjacent digits connected by a dot differ by 1 if the dot is white, and have a ratio of 1:2 if the dot is black.
2212: Normal sudoku rules apply. In graves (cages), digits must sum to the day, month or year of the date of the day before or after the date on the grave. Digits cannot repeat within graves. Escape the graveyard by carefully plotting an orthogonally connected path between the green and red cells. The path may not cross the highest or lowest digits in a grave. All dates use the international standard Gregorian calendar in the DD/MM/YY format.
2213: Normal sudoku rules apply. Finkz the rat must reach the cupcake by finding a path through the maze. The path must not visit any cell more than once, cross itself, or pass through any thick maze walls. As well as moving orthogonally, Finkz may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. Digits separated by a green grape have a difference of at least 5. In this experiment, dotted box borders divide the correct path into 'index lines'; In any box, the Nth cell visited by Finkz is called 'position N'. (So, for example, in box 7, r9c2 is position 1.) The digit in position N always indicates which position along that segment contains the digit N. Eg: In a box, Finkz might visit the digits 35142 in that order. The first digit being a 3 indicates that the third digit is a 1, the second digit being a 5 indicates that the fifth digit is a 2, and so on.
2214: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a thermometer increase from the bulb end. The digits in a cage sum to the number shown, if given. Digits may not repeat within a cage. Shade some cells such that the shaded cells and the unshaded cells each form a single orthogonally-connected region. No 2x2 area can be completely shaded or unshaded (Yin-Yang rules). In a cage, even digits are always shaded, odd digits are always unshaded. On a thermometer, odd digits are always shaded, even digits are always unshaded.
2215: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a single knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. Diagonal cell pairs (sharing a corner) must have a difference of at least 2.
2216: Normal sudoku rules apply. A black dot joins digits with a ratio of 1:2. Not all dots are given. A digit in a circle must have a value between the digits on both ends of the row. A digit in a green cell must have a value between the digits on both ends of the column. All possible circles and green cells are given.
2217: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each thick grey line can be divided into one or more non-overlapping segments. Each segment contains digits that sum to 10. Eg 513173 is a valid fill for a length 6 line, because it can be broken into 5131 and 73, each of which sum to 10. Digits on a purple line form a set of non-repeating, consecutive digits. These digits can appear in any order. Digits along a thin grey line connecting two circles must have values between the digits in the circles. Eg if the two circles at a line’s ends contain 3 and 8 then digits on the line itself must be selected from [4567]. Digits separated by a black dot have a 1:2 ratio, meaning one digit is exactly double the other. Not all dots are necessarily given.
2218: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage do not repeat and sum to the clue in the top left. Moreover, if cages are adjacent to each other (i.e. share an edge), they must contain at least one common digit.
2219: Normal sudoku rules apply. AIM OF EXPERIMENT: Finkz the rat must reach the cupcake by finding a path through the maze. The path must not visit any cell more than once, cross itself, or pass through any thick maze walls. As well as moving orthogonally, Finkz may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. NULLIFIERS: In each row, column and 3x3 box there is one 'nullifier' cell to be located. The value of a nullifier cell is zero. Each nullifier cell contains a different digit. MOTION SENSORS: The value on a pink motion sensor indicates how many of the (up to 9) cells immediately surrounding the sensor are visited by Finkz. The sensor itself is counted, if visited. BLACKCURRANTS: Values connected by a blackcurrant have a 1:2 ratio. GRAPES: Values connected by a green grape have a difference of at least 5. FORBIDDEN DOORS: Values connected by a red X sum to 10. Finkz may not pass directly through a red X. TEST CONSTRAINT: In this experiment, if a row / column / box is visited by Finkz, then the values of ALL the visited cells in that row / column / box must sum to exactly 13 (even if the cells aren't all adjacent on the path.)
2220: Normal sudoku rules apply. The first digit on a diagonal seen by a camera indicates how many times that digit appears on that diagonal. Any leftover digits on the diagonal (the ones not equal to the first digit) are sorted from lowest to highest, i.e. they appear in non-decreasing order moving away from the camera. Speech bubbles all say the same odd digit.
2221: Fillomino: Divide the grid into orthogonally connected regions such that no two regions of the same size share an edge, and enter a number into each cell equal to the size of its region. Cave: Shade some cells in the grid such that all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected, and all shaded cells are orthogonally connected by other shaded cells to an edge of the grid. Each region must either be entirely shaded or entirely unshaded. If a clued cell is unshaded, the clue indicates the sum of numbers seen orthogonally from that cell; region borders block vision. If a clued cell is shaded, the clue indicates the total sum of numbers in its group of orthogonally connected shaded cells (which could include more than one region).
2222: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each pair of digits connected by a line segment must either differ by at least 5, or sum to at most 5.
2223: Every cell is either water or land. All water cells must be orthogonally connected, and no 2x2 area may be entirely water. Groups of orthogonally-connected land cells form islands, which do not touch orthogonally, but may touch diagonally. Draw a non-intersecting loop through the centres of some cells which passes through each island exactly once. The loop may only visit one cell in each island. If a clue is on a land cell, it indicates the size of its island. Every island must contain exactly one clue. If a clue is on a water cell then the loop must pass through that cell and the clue indicates how many water cells are visited by the loop between the previous island and the next island. Every water section of the loop must pass through exactly one clue. A '?' can represent any non-zero value.
2224: Draw four 3x3 boxes in the grid that don't overlap, and fill them with the digits 1-9. Digits can't repeat in a row, column or 3x3 box. Cells that are not in any box are empty, and their value is 0. Digits can't repeat in a cage, and sum to the clue given in the top-leftmost cell of that cage. Draw four snakes, each existing completely inside one of the 3x3 boxes. Each snake is a one cell wide path that only moves orthogonally, and must pass through every cell of its box. Adjacent digits along a snake sum to 10 or 11.
2225: Normal sudoku rules apply. Orthogonally adjacent digits cannot be consecutive. Digits along a line form a set of non-repeating, consecutive digits in any order. The sum of the digits along a diagonal, indicated by an arrow, sum to X, where X must be determined and is the same sum for all arrows.
2226: Fill each row, column and region with the digits 1-6. Each letter corresponds to a unique digit. A cell with one letter in contains the appropriate digit. Digits in a cage sum up to the double digit number represented by two letters inside that cage. Digits may repeat in cages. The digit in the grey square is even.
2227: Normal sudoku rules apply. Finkz the rat must reach the cupcake by finding a path through the maze. The path must not visit any cell more than once, cross itself, or pass through any thick maze walls. As well as moving orthogonally, Finkz may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. Digits connected by a blackcurrant have a 1:2 ratio. All cages have the same total, to be deduced. An electricity symbol indicates the cage's ‘shock value’. Finkz may not enter any cage with a shock value of 5 or higher. Cages with a shock value lower than 5 are safe to enter. In this experiment, dotted 3x3 box borders divide the correct path into segments. The total of each segment must be higher than the total of the previous segment on Finkz' path.
2228: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along each separate grey line (lengths: 3, 5 or 7) the product of the digits is 80. Each cage contains a 2-digit prime number (read left-to-right). A+B = C+D = A+C = B+D = 80
2229: Normal sudoku rules apply. The value of a digit on a line between two circles must be between the two values of the digits in those circles, eg if the two circles joined by a line contain 3 and 6, the digits on the line could be 4 or 5.
2230: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by an X add up to 10. Digits separated by a V add up to 5. If digits are separated by a black dot, one is double the other. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Not all possible dots or X/V clues are necessarily given.
2231: Normal sudoku rules apply. Every cage has the same sum.
2232: Normal sudoku rules apply. The digit on one end of each line is the sum of the other digits on that line. A clue outside the grid gives the sum of the first X grid digits starting from the clue where X is the nearest, eg if R5C1 is 4 then the sum of R5C1-4 is 15.
2233: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is partially covered in fog. Placing correct digits reveals clues in the surrounding 3x3 area. No guessing is required. Shade some cell such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected, all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected and each 2x2 area contains shaded and unshaded cells. The value of an unshaded cell is its digit. The value of a shaded cell is double its digit. Values along an arrow sum to the value of the attached circle. Arrows don't overlap.
2234: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent cells cannot contain consecutive digits. A clue outside the grid indicates the sum of the digits along that diagonal path. Cells separated by a black dot are in the ratio 1:2.
2235: Normal sudoku rules apply. In any cell that contains a digit that is smaller than the digit in the diagonally adjacent upper right cell, the sum of those two digits is given, where a question mark can be replaced by any sum ranging from 3 to 17
2236: Normal sudoku rules apply. Some correctly-entered digits clear fog from certain cells, but those cells may be in other parts of the grid. Other digits, even when entered correctly, do not clear fog at all. When the puzzle is fully solved, all the fog will be cleared. Digits in a cage sum to the small clue in the cage's top left corner, and digits cannot repeat within a cage. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in the attached circle (and these digits can repeat if allowed by other rules). Arrows do not cross or overlap, and all arrow sums are single-digit. Digits in cells separated by an X sum to 10. Digits in cells with a shaded square must be even. Digits in cells separated by a white dot are consecutive. If digits are separated by a black dot, one is double the other.
2237: Normal sudoku rules apply. Finkz the rat must reach the cupcake by finding a path through the maze. The path must not visit any cell more than once, cross itself, or pass through any thick maze walls. As well as moving orthogonally, Finkz may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through the rounded end / corner of a wall. If digits are connected by a blackcurrant one digit will be double the other. Not all possible blackcurrants have been given. Entering a teleport will cause Finkz to be instantly transported to the matching coloured teleport. From there she can continue her journey. Matching teleports always have identical digits, but teleports that don't match always have different digits. Finkz' path is formed of one or more segments. Any uses of teleports will divide Finkz' path up into physically separate segments, ie; if a teleport is used, the current path segment ends at the entry teleport, and a new separate path segment begins at the matching exit teleport. Any path segment must function as a “renban” ie it must consist entirely of a set of non-repeating, consecutive digits, which can be arranged in any order along the path segment.
2238: Fillomino: Divide the grid into polyominoes so that polyominoes of the same size don't share an edge. Each cell contains a number equal to its polyomino's size. Draw a loop that moves orthogonally from one cell to another through the grid. The loop must not touch itself orthogonally; however, it can touch diagonally. Along the loop, any three consecutive cells must contain numbers congruent to 0 mod 3, 1 mod 3, and 2 mod 3. (In other words, one of the numbers is from the set {3, 6, 9, 12, …}, one is from {1, 4, 7, 10, …}, and one from {2, 5, 8, 11, …}. Numbers on cells with arrows refer to the total amount of loop cells seen in the indicated direction or, if more than one arrow, in the directions combined.
2239: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each line in this puzzle is either a Renban Line or a Nabner Line. The solver must determine which is which. Digits along a Renban line must form a set of non-repeating consecutive digits in any order. No two digits along a Nabner line can be consecutive, regardless of their position on the line. Digits in cells separated by a black dot are in a 2:1 ratio. Digits in cells separated by a white dot are consecutive. Cells marked with a grey square contain even digits. Cells marked with a grey circle contain odd digits.
2240: Use exactly six digits from 1-9 to fill the grid, with each digit appearing once in every row, column and box. A digit in a diamond is the square root of the sum of the digits along the arrow.
2241: Normal sudoku rules apply. A clue outside the grid gives the sum (or the parity (Odd or Even)) of the sum of the digits on the indicated diagonal. Cells separated by a white dot contain consecutive digits. Cells separated by a black dot contain digits in a ratio 1:2.
2242: Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade the entire grid using two colours, so that each colour forms a single orthogonally connected area, and no 2x2 area is entirely one colour. An arrow in a cell indicates that the digit in that cell equals the sum of the contents of all cells of the opposite colour in the direction of the arrow. If a cell contains multiple arrows, each arrow is summed separately.
2243: Normal sudoku rules apply. Similarly colored blocks are clones and must contain the same digits in the same positions. Digits in a cage do not repeat and sum to the number shown. A clue outside the grid indicates the digit which has to be placed in the Nth cell in the corresponding direction, where N is the digit placed in the first cell in that direction.
2245: Normal sudoku rules apply. Antidiagonal Sudoku: No more than three different digits appear on each diagonal line.
2249: Digits cannot repeat in a cage. Cages show their sums, and are colored purely for decoration.
2251: Place 0-9 in each row, column and outlined region. A cell with a slash features two digits, the digit with the smaller value appearing above the larger one. The orientations of the slashes are purely decorative.
2252: Normal sudoku rules apply. Orange bars in the grid sit between ALL adjacent pairs of consecutive digits.
2253: Divide the grid into nine non-overlapping regions each consisting of nine orthogonally connected cells. Place the digits 1-9 once in each row, column, and region. The grid is covered in fog. Placing a correct digit in a cell lifts fog in that cell and possibly other cells; revealing new clues. Some cells contain a grey square inside them. The digit in such a cell is equal to the sum of the (up to 8) surrounding digits that are in different regions. Digits separated by a white dot differ by 1 and belong to the same region. A digit N on an arrow counts how many cells it sees of its region in the indicated direction, including itself. Region borders block vision. Additionally, the digit N+1 must appear immediately behind the first seen region border. Each arrow MUST therefore see a region border within the grid.
2254: Normal sudoku rules apply. The digits X, Y and Z in pill shapes (reading left to right) signify that rXcY = Z. Eg, if a pill read [825], then the cell in row 8 column 2 would have to be the digit 5. Digits along the negative diagonal (thin blue line) must not repeat. Any set of three sequential cells along the thick teal line must contain one digit from [1,4,7], one digit from [2,5,8] and one digit from [3,6,9]. Cells separated by an X sum to 10. Not all Xs are given.
2255: SCHRODINGER CELLS: Fill each row, column and box with the digits 0-9 once each. To make this possible, each row, column and box contains one Schrödinger cell, which contains two digits. The value of a Schrödinger cell is equal to the sum of its two digits. AIM OF EXPERIMENT: Finkz the rat must reach the cupcake by finding a path through the maze. The path must not visit any cell more than once, cross itself, or pass through any thick maze walls. As well as moving orthogonally, Finkz may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. BLACKCURRANTS: Two values separated by a blackcurrant have a 1:2 ratio. ONE-WAY DOORS: Finkz may only pass directly through a purple arrow in the direction it is pointing. A purple arrow always points to the smaller of the two values it sits between. TEST CONSTRAINT: In this experiment, dotted box borders divide the correct path into segments that each contain at least 2 cells. The values of two adjacent cells within the same segment always have the same difference, and this difference is unique for every segment. Eg: if a segment has a sequence of values 1, 3, 5, 7, then its 'same difference' is 2, and so no other segment may have a 'same difference' of 2.
2256: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits MAY repeat in cages if allowed by other rules. The sum of digits in each cage must be a two-digit number that acts as a valid “look-and-say clue” for that cage. Eg if the sum is 21, there must be exactly two 1s in the cage along with any combination of other digits (such that, overall, the digits in the cage sum to 21). Eg2 if the sum is 17, there must be exactly one 7 in the cage along with any combination of other digits (such that, overall, the digits in the cage sum to 17).
2257: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along a thermometer, digits must strictly increase from the bulb. The sum of the digits in each cage is given. The digits on a line must strictly be in between the digits connected on the attached empty circles. Full grey circles (but not necessarily thermometer bulbs) contain odd digits.
2258: Place exactly one queen in every row, column and coloured region. Two queens cannot touch each other. Not even diagonally.
2259: Normal sudoku rules apply. Nine cells (one in each row/column/3x3 box) are "doublers", and have a value of double their digit. Each digit appears in exactly one doubler. Values along a thermometer increase from the bulb end. Values in a cage sum to the given total. Digits may not repeat in a cage, but values may.
2260: Normal 6x6 sudoku rules apply. (Place the digits 1 to 6, once each, in every row, column and 2x3 rectangle). Every indicated diagonal has the same product.
2261: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along a thermometer digits must not decrease from the bulb to the tip(s).
2262: Normal sudoku rules apply. Finkz the rat must reach the cupcake by finding a path through the maze. The path must not visit any cell more than once, cross itself, or pass through any thick maze walls. As well as moving orthogonally, Finkz may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. Each rectangular trapdoor has a different total (the sum of its two digits.) Finkz should not step on a trapdoor without first locking it shut, making it safe to cross. To make it safe to step on a trapdoor, Finkz must first press all the circular buttons that match the colour of the trapdoor. A digit on a coloured button indicates how many buttons of that colour contain that digit. In this experiment, the correct path will be entropic, ie; every group of 3 adjacent cells along the path must contain one low digit (1, 2 or 3), one medium digit (4, 5 or 6) and one high digit (7, 8 or 9).
2263: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a line sum to the same value for each row the line passes through.
2264: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is covered in fog. Placing a correct digit in a cell lifts fog in that cell and possibly other cells. The vertical dashed lines are folded onto each other so that columns 1, 2, 8 and 9 form a secondary grid (as if the other columns disappear). In this grid all clues are still valid. Digits in a cage don't repeat and sum to the total given in the top-left corner. Cages don't overlap. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Not all dots are given. Clues outside the grid give the sum of all cells that contain a digit equal to the distance of that cell from that clue in the row or column. For example, a 4 in Row 2, Column 4 would count towards the 10 clue in row 2, and any other number would not. Horizontal distances in the folded 4x9 grid are limited to 1-4.
2265: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells that are a knight's move away are not allowed to contain identical digits. Both digits (which can be equal) on the endpoints of a line form a look-and-say clue. For example, if the digits on the endpoints are 5 and 3, then there have to be exactly five 3s AND three 5s on this line. The different line colors are only used to avoid confusion regarding line crossings.
2266: Normal sudoku rules apply. A border square is a 2x2 square that crosses at least one 3x3 box border. For all border squares exactly 2 digits are the same. The middle 3x3 box in the grid is a magic square i.e. the sum of digits in each row, column and main 3-cell diagonal in that box is N (where N must be determined by the solver). There are exactly N ‘friendly’ cells in the grid. A cell is friendly if its digit is equal to at least one of its row number, column number or box number. (Rows are numbered top to bottom; columns are numbered left-to-right; boxes are numbered in normal reading order.) Digits separated by a black dot must be in ratio 1:2 (ie one digit is double the other). Not all dots are necessarily given.
2267: Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a 1-cell-wide loop of orthogonally connected cells, which does not branch or touch itself, not even diagonally. Circled cells are not on the loop, and the digit in a circle indicates how many of the up to 8 surrounding cells are on the loop. For each pair of adjacent digits along the loop, the larger digit is an integer multiple of the smaller digit. The cell with the rectangle is on the loop.
2268: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits may not repeat within a cage.
2269: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells along lines between two circles must have values between those in the circles. Digits in white circles must be present at least once in the cells the clue touches.
2270: Normal sudoku rules apply. The digits along each arrow must sum to the number in its circle. There are six different colors of lines in this puzzle. Each color corresponds to a different one of these constraints: - Dutch Whispers (adjacent numbers on the line must differ by at least 4); - Entropic (any three adjacent digits on the line must be one each of 1-3, 4-6, and 7-9); - German Whispers (adjacent numbers on the line must differ by at least 5); - Palindrome (the numbers on the line form the same sequence no matter which end you start from); - Region Sums (if the line passes through multiple regions, the sum of the digits on the line must be the same in each region); - Renban (the line contains a set of consecutive digits in any order with no repeats).
2271: Place the digits 1-9 once into each row, column, and 3x3 box. Digits must not repeat along the marked diagonal. The grey lines are palindromes and must contain the same sequence of digits in both directions along the line. The purple lines are Double Renban lines. Each such line contains two equal-sized sets of consecutive digits. The sets might overlap partially or completely, and the digits can be in any order along the line. For example, 123123, 172839, and 142332 are each valid ways to fill a six-cell Double Renban line.
2272: Draw nine 3x3 boxes within the grid and place the digits 1-9 once into each box. Digits within boxes (the Sudoku digits) must not repeat in any row or column of the grid. Divide the remaining cells (outside of the nine boxes) into orthogonally contiguous regions and fill them according to Fillomino rules: every cell contains the size of its region, and no two orthogonally adjacent regions may have the same size. No Fillomino region may be larger than nine cells. The clues outside the grid give the sum of the Fillomino digits in the indicated row or column. (Sudoku digits are not included in the sums.) Additionally, a Fillomino digit must not be orthogonally adjacent to an identical Sudoku digit. Clues inside the grid begin hidden by fog; the fog clears when correct digits are entered. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in the attached circle; all arrows have single-digit sums and do not branch or overlap. Digits separated by a white dot must be consecutive, and digits separated by a black dot must be in a 1:2 ratio; not all dots are given. The purple lines contain a set of consecutive, non-repeating digits in any order.
2273: Place the digits 0-9 once into each row, column, and region. Identical digits may not be separated by a knight's move. The digits 0 and 9 may not be orthogonally or diagonally adjacent to each other or themselves. A clue outside the grid is either an X-Sums clue or a Sandwich clue, but not both, i.e. exactly one of the following is true: the clue gives the sum of the digits between the 0 and 9 in the indicated row or column; or the clue gives the sum of the first X digits in that row or column, starting from the digit next to the clue, which is equal to X. The ? may be any valid clue.
2274: Place the digits 0 to 9 once into each row, column, and 3x3 box. One cell in each row, column, and box is an S-cell containing two digits. The value of an S-cell is the sum of its digits; no two S-cells contain the same pair of digits. Fog covers some cells, and will be cleared when a correct single digit is placed in a cell; S-cells do not clear fog. “Renban loops” contain a set of consecutive values in any order. Each loop is a different colour of thick line, and does not cross or intersect itself. The value in a circle is equal to the sum of the values along the attached arrow. Each arrow is a different colour of thin line, and does not branch. The values in cells surrounding an X sum to 10, and the values in cells surrounding a V sum to 5. A cell with a grey square contains an even value.
2275: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along the green line, adjacent digits must differ by at least 5. A clue outside the grid gives the sum of the digits between the 1 and 9 on the indicated diagonal. The base paths are double arrows: the digits on each path have the same sum as the bases at the ends of the path. The bases contain four different digits.
2276: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is covered in fog. Placing correct digits reveals clues in the surrounding 3x3 area. Adjacent digits along an orange line have a difference of at least 4. Each orange line is in the shape of a square. Cells separated by a black dot are in the ratio 1 to 2. Not all black dots are necessarily shown.
2277: Normal sudoku rules apply. AIM OF EXPERIMENT: Finkz the rat must reach the cupcake by finding a path through the maze. The path must not visit any cell more than once, cross itself, or pass through any thick maze walls. As well as moving orthogonally, Finkz may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. TELEPORTS: Entering a teleport will cause Finkz to be instantly transported to the matching coloured teleport. From there she can continue her journey. Matching teleports always have identical digits, but teleports that don't match always have different digits. MIRROR CELLS: Each row, column and box contains exactly one mirror cell. Mirror cells may not contain teleports. The value of a mirror cell equals the digit in that cell subtracted from 10. Eg: a 2 in a mirror cell is 'mirrored' on the 1-9 scale, and has a value of 8. Every mirror cell contains a different digit. ONE-WAY DOORS: Finkz may only pass directly through a purple arrow if moving in the direction the arrow is pointing. An arrow always points to the smaller of the two values it sits between. TEST CONSTRAINT: In this experiment, the values of any two physically adjacent cells along the path (ie; not separated by teleportation) must have a difference of at least 5.
2278: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along a thermometer, digits must increase from the bulb end. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Cells separated by a (single) king's move in chess cannot contain the same digit.
2279: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits must not repeat in cells that are a single knight's move apart (in chess). The digits in a cage must sum to the small clue printed in the top left corner of the cage. Digits may not repeat within a cage. Adjacent digits along each green ‘German Whisper’ line must have a difference of at least 5. Lines and cages do not overlap. The grid is partially covered with fog. Correctly placed digits will clear the fog around that cell. No guessing is required.
2280: Normal sudoku rules apply. Color every cell in the grid one of two colors such that all cells of each color are orthogonally connected and no 2x2 region is a single color. A digit in a square indicates how many cells of the same color are seen orthogonally from that position, including itself, where cells of the other color block vision. Diagonally adjacent cells may not contain the same digit.
2281: Normal 4x4 sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio. The difference between two adjacent digits on a coloured line indicates exactly how many pairs of adjacent digits along that line have that exact difference.
2282: Normal 6x6 sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio. The difference between two adjacent digits on a coloured line indicates exactly how many pairs of adjacent digits along that line have that exact difference.
2283: Normal 9x9 sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio. The difference between two adjacent digits on a coloured line indicates exactly how many pairs of adjacent digits along that line have that exact difference.
2284: Normal sudoku rules apply. A digit in a circle indicates how many circles contain that digit. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Digits do not repeat along the marked diagonal.
2285: Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected and all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected. No 2x2 area may be fully shaded or fully unshaded. Along a line, any changes in shading divide that line into segments of fully shaded or fully unshaded cells. On each line, each such segment (shaded or unshaded) must have the same sum as all other segments. Within the shaded areas, adjacent digits along the lines must differ by at least 5. Within unshaded areas, any string of 3 or fewer digits along the lines must be from a different set of (147), (258) and (369).
2286: Normal sudoku rules apply. The sum of the digits on a line strictly between two circles is equal to a concatenation of the two values in the circles, in some order. For instance, 3_346_1 could be a valid split pea line, as 3+4+6=13, which is 1 concatenated with 3. A circled digit indicates exactly how many circles contain that digit. Note: This also includes all circles which are bounding the split pea lines. If, for example, a 3 appears in a circle, then there must be exactly 3 circles that contain a 3.
2287: In this experiment, nine letters of the alphabet (to be determined) must be used to fill the grid so that no letter repeats in any row, column or 3x3 box. AIM OF EXPERIMENT: Finkz the rat must reach the cupcake by finding a path through the maze. The path must not visit any cell more than once, cross itself, or pass through any thick maze walls. As well as moving orthogonally, Finkz may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. DYNAMIC FOG: Entering correct letters may clear fog somewhere in the maze. No guessing is necessary. CUE CARDS: Each pink cue card sits between two letters that both appear on that cue card. BRAINWAVE MONITORS: The faint light of 11 blue monitors are visible through the fog; Finkz must visit all of these before reaching the cupcake. With any luck, they will provide an insight into her thoughts. TEST CONSTRAINT: 3x3 box borders divide Finkz' path into segments. If a segment contains more than one cell, then the cells must be visited in alphabetical order.
2288: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits along orange lines must have a difference of at least 4. A digit in a white circle must appear once in the four surrounding cells. Any two cells which are in the same relative position within their respective 3x3 boxes must contain different digits. For example, if 7 was placed in the top-left corner of box 1, then no other boxes could have a 7 in their top-left corner.
2289: This is a 9x9 map of the ocean - there are ocean cells and island cells. Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage with nine or fewer cells. Cells separated by an X must contain digits summing to 10. Not all Xs are given. HOWEVER, 18 cells - two in each box, row and column -are 'island' cells - these do not count toward the cage totals. Only 'ocean' cells count towards cage totals. There can be as many island cells as needed in any cage.
2290: Normal sudoku rules apply. The sum of the digits in each cage has a unique total. The grey square contains an even digit.
2291: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells a (chess) knight's move apart cannot contain the same digit. Placing a correct digit will clear some fog in the grid. A number in the corner of a cell gives the sum of all digits along one of the diagonals containing the cell. Which diagonal must be deduced by the solver. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in the bulb. All arrows are 2 cells long.
2292: Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells so that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected, and all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected. No 2x2 region can be completely shaded or unshaded. Each cell in one region has a value of its digit plus 1. Each cell in the other region has a value of its digit minus 1. The sum of the values of cells on lines connecting two circles is equal to a concatenation of the two values in the circles, in some order. For example, 3_346_1 is valid, as 3+4+6=13. Leading zeros are allowed. Every line between two circles is summed separately.
2293: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is partially covered in fog. Placing correct digits will clear some of the fog in the grid. No guessing is required (or recommended). Shade some cells so that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected, and all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected. No 2x2 region can be completely shaded or unshaded. R5C5 is neither shaded nor unshaded in the final grid. The sum of the digits on a line strictly between two circles must be equal to a concatenation of the digits in that line's circles. For instance, 3-346-1 could be a valid split pea line, as 3+4+6=13, which is a concatenation of 3 and 1. (ie One circle contains the ‘tens’ digit of that line’s sum; and one circle contains the ‘units’ digit of that line’s sum.) Each circle in the puzzle indicates the number of cells along each line directly connected to the circle, including the bounding circles, which are of the same shading as the circle. All lines travel orthogonally. Lines may not branch or cross, except at circles. Digits separated by an X sum to 10. Digits separated by a V sum to 5. Not all X or V are given.
2294: Normal sudoku rules apply (ie place the digits 1-9, once each, in every row, column and 3x3 box). Along a thermometer, digits must increase from the bulb end. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle.
2295: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits along a green line have a difference of at least five. Box borders divide a blue line into segments with an equal sum.
2296: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits along the holly outline (green) differ by at least 5. The 3x3 box borders divide the bell outline (yellow) into segments that sum to the same value. Digits on baubles (pink) form a consecutive sequence in any order. Digits in white circles must appear at least once in the surrounding 2x2 cells.
2297: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is partially covered in fog. Entering correct digits will clear the fog from surrounding cells. The number in the top left corner of a red cage (if given) indicates the sum of the digits sandwiched between 1 and 9 in that row. The number in the top left corner of a blue cage (if given) indicates the sum of the digits sandwiched between 1 and 9 in that column. The digit in a cage indicates how many digits (including the crust of 1 and 9) the corresponding sandwich sum contains. “?” can represent any number at all.
2298: Normal sudoku rules apply. AIM OF EXPERIMENT: Finkz the rat must reach the cupcake by finding a path through the maze. The path must not visit any cell more than once, cross itself, or pass through any thick walls. (The walls have been decorated with red tinsel.) As well as moving orthogonally, Finkz may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so. DYNAMIC FOG: Entering correct digits may clear fog somewhere in the maze. CHRISTMAS LIGHTS: An orange Christmas light indicates that any digits visited by Finkz in its row or column are odd. A blue Christmas light indicates that any digits visited in its row or column are even. TELEPORTS: Every teleport is part of a matching pair. Entering a teleport will cause Finkz to be instantly transported to the matching coloured teleport. From there she can continue her journey. Matching teleports always have identical digits, but teleports that don't match always have different digits. BLACKCURRANTS: Blackcurrants sit between two digits with a 1:2 ratio. BAUBLES: The number on a gold bauble gives the total of any cells it touches. TEST CONSTRAINT: In this experiment, any two cells that are adjacent along the path contain consecutive digits (except when separated by teleportation, where the digits are identical.)
2299: Normal sudoku rules apply. Within a cage, digits may not repeat, and the sum of their values is equal to the expression in the top left corner. There are nine vampire cells and nine prey cells in the grid, one of each in every row, column and box. Every digit from 1-9 appears exactly once in a vampire cell, and exactly once in a prey cell. A vampire cell steals the value of the digit in the prey cell in the same box and adds it to its own digit to create its value. The value of the digit in a prey cell is 0.
2300: Divide the grid into square-shaped regions. Fill each region of size NxN with the numbers 1-N, such that no number repeats in any row or column of the region. Same numbers cannot touch orthogonally, even across region borders. Additionally, the following constraints apply: Numbers along an arrow must sum to the number in the attached circle; numbers along a grey thermometer must increase from the bulb end; and numbers along a pink line must form a non-repeating consecutive sequence - these numbers can appear in any order.
2301: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits on a green line have a difference of at least 5. A pink line contains a sequence of consecutive digits in any order. Digits along an arrow sum to the number in the attached circle.
2302: Normal sudoku rules apply (place 1-9 in each row, column and marked 3x3 box).
2303: Normal sudoku rules apply. Divide the grid into galaxies: orthogonally connected groups of cells that have 180 degree rotational symmetry about their centers (marked with a small dot). All cells must be part of a galaxy; no galaxies overlap. Grey dots mark "renban" galaxies: those with two or more cells, whose digits form an unbroken consecutive sequence in any order. White dots mark galaxies whose digits do NOT form a consecutive sequence. Digits may not repeat within a galaxy. There is one "dark star" (a single cell galaxy) that is not marked. As per Galactic Map Standards: All galaxies with at least TWO cells indicate their SMALLEST digit with a diamond icon. All galaxies with at least SIX cells indicate their LARGEST digit with a circle icon. The Galactic Census requires that all galaxies with at least THREE cells must report their star system count (sum of digits in the galaxy).
2304: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each blue line is both a "region sum line" and a "10 line". Region sum line: box borders divide each blue line into segments with the same sum. 10 line: the line consists of one or more contiguous groups of cells, each of which sums to 10 – these groups cannot overlap.
2305: For each 4x4 quadrant of the grid, choose 4 of the digits from 0-9, and use them to fill that quadrant so that no digit repeats in any marked 2x2 box. In the overall 8x8 grid, no digit may repeat in any row or column. Digits on the pink line form a non-repeating consecutive sequence which can appear in any order along the line. Box borders divide a blue line into segments whose digits each have the same sum. Digits along a green line have a difference of at least 5. No two digits anywhere on a yellow line may be consecutive or the same.
2306: Normal sudoku rules apply. The digits in a cage sum to the value indicated. No adjacent run of three cells may be all odd or all even, horizontally or vertically.
2307: Normal fillomino rules apply (ie divide the grid along grid lines into non-overlapping regions of orthogonally-connected cells such that no two regions of the same size touch each other orthogonally; and fill each cell in each region with that region's size ie the number of cells in its region). Use only the digits 1 to 9 and the digit N cannot appear in row N or column N. Digits on the marked diagonals cannot repeat and must sum to the total (if given). The grid is covered by fog. Correctly placing digits may clear fog somewhere in the grid.
2308: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits may not repeat in cages. If a cage contains a clue in the top left corner, that cage must be comprised of 1-, 2-, 3-, and/or 4-digit numbers that sum to that value. Numbers are made from either horizontally adjacent digits read left-to-right; or vertically adjacent digits read top-to-bottom (ie numbers cannot bend!). Every digit within a cage must be part of exactly one number, and numbers may not cross cage borders.
2309: Normal sudoku rules apply. Numbers outside the grid are both Sandwich Clues and X-Sum Clues. A sandwich clue shows the sum of digits between the 1 and the 9 in that row or column. An X-Sums Clue shows the sum of the first X digits, where X is the first digit, from that direction. Shaded circles are odd numbers. The grid is partially covered with fog. Placing correct digits will remove the surrounding fog.
2310: Divide the grid into nine regions each containing 9 orthogonally-connected cells, such that each cell is part of exactly one region. Some region borders have already been given. Fill the grid with the digits 1-9 such that no digit repeats in any row, column or region. From each circle, draw some arrows that travel in a straight line either horizontally only or vertically only. The number in the bottom right corner of a circle cell indicates the number of arrows that must be drawn from that circle. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in the attached circle. Additionally, all cells along arrows must be part of the same region as the circle they originate from. If an arrow doesn't reach the edge of the grid, the cell directly after the tip must be in a different region than the arrow.
2311: Normal sudoku rules apply. Box borders divide a blue line into sequences with the same sum. Adjacent digits along a red line have a difference of at least six. If digits are separated by a red cherry, one is double the other.
2312: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a single knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. The 3x3 boxes in the grid are numbered in normal reading order. In odd numbered boxes, odd digits appear in ascending order (with respect to position within that box). In even numbered boxes, even digits appear in ascending order (with respect to position within that box). (Cells within 3x3 boxes are also numbered in normal reading order.) In cells separated by a black dot, one digit is double the other.
2313: Normal sudoku rules apply. The sum of the digits along an arrow is equal to the digit in that arrow’s circle. A purple line contains a non-repeating set of consecutive digits – these digits can appear in any order. Digits in cells separated by an X sum to 10. Digits in cells with a shaded square must be even.
2314: Normal 6x6 sudoku rules apply. (Place the digits 1 to 6, once each, into every row, column and 2x3 bold-outlined rectangle). Each finger has lost its gold ring! Can you find them? Every row, column and box contains one gold ring, and none of them are located on a finger. Each gold ring contains a different digit. The digits ABC along a finger, reading towards the fingertip (the C goes on the fingernail), indicates that row A column B contains that finger's missing gold ring, which contains the digit C.
2315: Normal sudoku rules apply. In the positive diagonals (ie the blue marked diagonal and the diagonals parallel to it), the difference between two neighboring digits is only 4 or 5. Along the blue marked diagonal all digits are different.
2316: 𝗗𝗲𝗰𝗼𝗻𝘀𝘁𝗿𝘂𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻: Place 9 non-overlapping 3x3 boxes in the grid. Fill each cell in a box with a digit from 1-9 such that digits don't repeat in rows, columns or boxes. A cell that is not in any 3x3 box should be left blank but its value for the purposes of the loop/palindrome is zero. 𝗗𝘆𝗻𝗮𝗺𝗶𝗰 𝗙𝗼𝗴: The grid is covered in fog. Placing a correct digit in a cell lifts fog from that cell and possibly other cells; revealing new clues. 𝗪𝗵𝗶𝘀𝗽𝗲𝗿 𝗟𝗼𝗼𝗽: Draw a loop through the centers of some cells that moves orthogonally from cell to cell (never diagonally). The loop may touch itself diagonally, but not orthogonally. Adjacent values along the loop differ by 5 or more. 𝗖𝗶𝗿𝗰𝗹𝗲𝘀: Circles are on the loop and in boxes. Their digit counts the number of loop-cells in their box. 𝗣𝗮𝗹𝗶𝗻𝗱𝗿𝗼𝗺𝗲𝘀: Cells an equal distance to the circled center of a line have the same value.
2317: 1-6 must be placed in each row, column and marked 3x2 region. Digits on the line 𝘴𝘵𝘳𝘪𝘤𝘵𝘭𝘺 𝘣𝘦𝘵𝘸𝘦𝘦𝘯 the two circles sum to a two-digit number, where the "tens" digit is in one circle and the "ones" digit is in the other. Also, digits on the line, 𝘪𝘯𝘤𝘭𝘶𝘥𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘤𝘪𝘳𝘤𝘭𝘦𝘴, sum to a two-digit number, where the "tens" digit is in one circle and the "ones" digit is in the other.
2318: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits an equal distance from the centre of a lavender 'Zipper Line' sum to the digits in the middle of that line. Digits on a white dot are consecutive. Not all dots are given. Nine cells in the grid (one per row, column, and box) are Doublers, which count as double their value on Zipper lines. Each digit appears in exactly one Doubler. Doublers aren't necessarily on Zipper lines.
2319: Normal sudoku rules apply. Neighbouring digits along the line must differ by at least 5. Two of the cells covered by the circle contain the same digit.
2320: Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells such that all shaded cells are connected orthogonally by other shaded cells to the edge of the grid, and the remaining unshaded cells form one orthogonally connected area. Note that 2x2 areas that are entirely shaded or entirely unshaded are allowed. Digits in circles cannot be shaded, and represent the total number of unshaded cells seen horizontally and vertically from that cell, including itself. Shaded cells block the vision. Digits in cells separated by a white dot must have consecutive values. Additionally, one of those cells must be shaded and the other must be unshaded. Every set of orthogonally connected unshaded cells within a 3x3 Sudoku region acts as a Renban line: ie those cells must contain a nonrepeating set of consecutive digits in any order. 2321: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is covered in fog. Placing a correct digit in a cell lifts fog from that cell and possibly other cells. All lines and attached circles are “split pea lines” and, between the circles, the lines function also as “index lines”.
2322: Normal sudoku rules apply. Box borders divide each blue line into segments with the same sum.
2323: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along grey (TEN) lines must be broken into one or more non-overlapping segments that each sum to ten. Digits may repeat within such sums if allowed by other rules. For example, 513173 is a valid fill for a length 6 line, because it can be broken into 5131 and 73, each of which sum to 10. Any set of three sequential cells along an entropic (ENT) line must contain a low digit (1-3), middle digit (4-6) and high digit (7-9). Digits may repeat on an ENT line, if allowed by other rules. Digits on a purple (REN) line form a set of non-repeating, consecutive digits in any order. Digits do not repeat along a gold (NAB) line. Additionally, no pair of digits anywhere on a gold line can be consecutive. Along green (GW) lines, adjacent digits must differ by at least 5. Digits separated by a black dot have a 1:2 ratio, meaning one is exactly double the other. Not all dots are necessarily given.
2324: Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid indicate the sums of runs of contiguous cells that must be shaded. The shaded runs must be separated by at least 1 non-shaded cell. The imposter has messed up this Japanese Sums Sudoku! The imposter changed SOME column/row clues to represent the runs of UNshaded cells instead of the shaded ones! And he even erased one of the clues (row 5)! All I remember is that there are less shaded cells than unshaded. Note: a row or column clue will only give you a clue about one type of cell: shaded or unshaded. There are no mixed clues within a column or row.
2325: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each line must contain a digit equal to half the sum of its digits. Digits may repeat on a line if allowed by other rules.
2326: Normal sudoku rules apply. Neighbouring digits along an orange (Dutch Whispers) line differ by at least 4. A pink (Renban) line contains a set of consecutive digits in any order. Starting at the bulb end, successive digits on a dark grey (slow) thermometer do not decrease. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive.
2327: Normal sudoku rules apply. A digit in a circle indicates how many circles contain that digit. On an “index line”, the digit in the Nth cell along the line (starting from the diamond) indicates the position along the line where the digit N appears. Eg: 3214 would be a valid line; the 1st digit, 3, indicates that the 3rd cell contains a 1, the 2nd cell a 2, and so on.
2328: Normal sudoku rules apply. Colour every cell in the grid light or dark. Cells of the same colour are orthogonally connected. Every 2x2 contains both colours. On an “index” line, the digit in the Nth cell along the line (starting from the diamond) indicates the position along the line where the digit N appears. Eg: 3214 would be a valid line with 3 as the diamond; the 1st digit, 3, indicates that the 3rd cell contains a 1, the 2nd cell a 2, and so on. All cells that reference their own position on a line (the digit N is in position N) should be dark. Cells that are not “self-referencing” should be light. Eg for the line 3214 with 3 as the diamond, the 2 and 4 would be dark and the 1 and 3 would be light. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive and have the same colour. Not all such dots are necessarily given.
2329: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is covered in fog. Placing a correct digit in a cell lifts fog in that cell and possibly other cells; revealing new clues. On an “index line”, the digit in the Nth cell along the line (starting from the diamond) indicates the position along the line where the digit N appears. For example: 3214 would be a valid line with the 3 on the diamond; the 1st digit, 3, indicates that the 3rd digit is a 1, and so on. Inequality signs point to the smaller of the two digits. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Digits separated by an X sum to 10. Not all such symbols are necessarily given.
2330: Normal sudoku rules apply in the main 9x9 grid. The grid is covered in fog. Placing a correct digit in a cell lifts fog from that cell, potentially revealing new clues. Placing correct digits in the main 9x9 grid may reveal additional cells. Digits outside the grid (excluding the corners) must be filled and count how many digits are 'seen' looking into the grid in the row/column. Digits are visible when they are larger than all digits before them. Digits in cages never repeat. For each total (in the top-left corner) exactly 3 cages display that total. Two of them sum to that total, one does not.
2331: Normal sudoku rules apply. For each set of 3 lines that are the same colour (and line styling), two of those are index lines and one is a thermometer. No line can be ambiguously both. Digits along a thermometer must strictly increase starting from the bulb. The digit in the Nth cell along an index line (starting from the bulb) indicates the position along the line where the digit N appears. For example, 3214 is a valid index line, the 1st digit, 3, indicates that the 3rd digit is a 1, and so on.
2332: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is partially covered in fog. Placing correct digits will clear the fog from surrounding cells. One cell in each row, column and box is lighter than normal. Lighter cells have a value equal to half of their digit. Each digit from 1 to 9 appears once in the set of lighter cells. One cell in each row, column and box is heavier than normal. Heavier cells have a value equal to one and a half times their digit. Each digit from 1 to 9 appears once in the set of heavier cells. No cell is both lighter and heavier. Box borders divide a line into segments whose values sum to the same number. Lines do not branch, cross or share cells.
2333: Divide the grid into nine regions, each containing 9 orthogonally connected cells such that each cell is part of exactly one region. Fill the grid with digits 1-9 such that no digit repeats in any row, column or region. Thermo knots: From each big circle, draw straight horizontal or vertical thermometers in all possible directions, such that each thermo occupies at least two cells (including the circle). Digits along a thermo must increase, starting from the circle. Additionally, all cells along thermos must be part of the same region as their circle. If a thermo doesn't reach the edge of the grid, it MUST keep extending until it reaches the edge of its region, and the cell directly after the tip must be in a different region and must contain a SMALLER digit than the tip. Cells separated by a small white circle must be in DIFFERENT regions and contain consecutive digits.
2334: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along green lines, adjacent digits differ by at least 5. Along pink lines, digits form a consecutive sequence in any order. Digits in cages must sum to the given total.
2335: Normal sudoku rules apply. Mus the mouse must reach the cupcake and Felix the cat must reach the escape hole finding paths through the maze. Individually, their paths must not visit any cell more than once, cross itself, or pass through any thick maze walls. As well as moving orthogonally, both Mus and Felix can move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. Importantly, the paths of Felix and Mus can cross each other. This can only happen on even digits and if it does happen, both paths MUST continue on to another cell in a straight line. Mus and Felix may only pass through black arrows if moving in the direction the arrow is pointing. An arrow always points to the smaller of the two values it sits between. Cells connected by a blackcurrant have a 1:2 ratio (one is double the other.) Not all possible blackcurrants have been given. Digits separated by a green grape have a difference of at least 5. Not all possible grapes have been given. For Mus, the path within each box must be a thermometer with the bulb being the first square entered and the tip being the last square in the box. Digits along a thermometer increase from bulb to tip. Repeat visits to the same box are considered separate thermos. For Felix, adjacent cells along the path must be of different parity (odd/even).
2336: Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw 9 straight diagonal lines, each through the centres of at least 3 cells: Every line contains exactly one Bull and one Red Flag; Different lines do not cross or share cells; The grid is a torus, i.e. row 1 wraps around to row 9 and column 1 wraps around to column 9 as shown. No two Bulls contain the same digit; The digit on a Bull is the average (mean) of all digits on its line. No two Red Flags contain the same digit; The digit on a Red Flag is friendly, i.e. it equals its own row, column or box number (rows, columns and boxes are numbered 1-9 from top to bottom, left to right, and in reading order respectively).
2337: Normal sudoku rules apply. Entering correct digits may clear fog somewhere in the grid. No guessing is necessary. In this puzzle, coloured lines are 'edge thermos'... these run along cell edges. Any cell edge covered by a thermo contains a thermo spot. The value of a thermo spot equals the sum of the digits in the two cells it sits between. Values of spots along a thermo strictly increase moving away from the bulb (the large spot at one end.) Each thermo is a different colour, and they don't overlap or intersect each other.
2338: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits along a green line must differ by at least 5. Each grey line can be split into contiguous, non-overlapping segments each of which sums to exactly 10. If allowed by other rules, digits inside a segment may repeat. For example, a valid “ten line” could read 37424 where the segments 37 and 424 both sum to 10.
2339: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow’s circle. Digits in a cage cannot repeat and must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage (if given). Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. In cells separated by a black dot one digit must be double the other. Not all dots are given.
2340: Normal sudoku rules apply. Placing correct digits will clear the fog from surrounding cells. Digits in cages do not repeat, and sum to the small clue, if given. Pink strips (of at least 2 cells in length) are hidden in the fog. Digits in a vertical strip in column N indicate the column in which the digit N appears, in the corresponding row. Digits in a horizontal strip in row N indicate the row in which the digit N appears, in the corresponding column. For example, if r2c3 is in a horizontal strip, and contains a 7, then r7c3 contains a 2.
2341: 𝗖𝗵𝗮𝗼𝘀 𝗖𝗼𝗻𝘀𝘁𝗿𝘂𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻: Divide the grid into 9 regions of orthogonally connected cells. Place the digits 1-9 once each in every row, column and region. 𝗔𝗻𝘁𝗶-𝗖𝗮𝗺𝗲𝗹: Digits separated by a camel move (in fairy chess) may not contain the same digit. A camel moves 3 steps forward and 1 step to the side. 𝗜𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗻𝗮𝗹 𝗫-𝗦𝘂𝗺𝘀: A digit in a circle counts the number of cells it sees of its own region in its row and column combined, including itself. Region borders and elephants block vision. If given, a 2-digit number in a rectangle gives the sum of all 'seen' digits.
2342: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each purple line contains a set of non-repeating consecutive digits, which may appear in any order on the line. The digits in a cage sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage.
2343: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a thermometer must increase from the bulb end.
2344: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a grey thermometer increase from the bulb end. Thermometers contain exactly 4 digits, only move horizontally and vertically (never diagonally) and don't branch or overlap. Thermometers are partially invisible (even after the fog is cleared). The grid is covered in fog. Placing a correct digit in a cell lifts fog from that cell and possibly other cells. Every 2x2 area in the grid contains at least one digit from each of the sets (123), (456), and (789).
2345: Normal sudoku rules apply. Box borders divide each blue line into segments with equal sums. Different lines may have different sums. Adjacent digits on a green line must differ by at least 5.
2346: Fill the grid with the digits 1-9. Each row N and column N contain exactly N distinct digits, with the rest of the row / column being filled with repeats. Divide the grid into 9 regions, each containing 9 orthogonally connected cells. The finished pattern of regions will have 180 degree rotational symmetry. The digit in a circle indicates how many distinct digits appear in its region. Eg: A 6 in a circle indicates that the region includes 6 distinct digits (and 3 repeats.) No two circles contain the same digit. Region borders divide blue lines into segments, each of which have the same sum. Each blue line must cross at least one region border.
2347: Place the digits 0 to 8 exactly once each in every row, column and 3x3 box. The grid is partially covered in fog. Placing correct digits will clear the fog from surrounding cells, possibly revealing more clues. Digits separated by a V sum to 5. Digits separated by an X sum to 10. Not all Vs and Xs are necessarily given. Every horizontal domino which sums to 5 must have either the two cells directly above it summing to 1 or the two cells directly below it summing to 9 (it could have both, but it doesn't need both).
2348: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits along a green line must differ in value by at least 5. The lines and hexagons are double arrows ie Digits on each line sum to the same number as the sum of the digits in the hexagons at the ends. Values at equal distance to the center of a lavender line sum to the central value.
2349: Normal 6x6 sudoku rules apply ie Fill the outlined grid with the digits 1-6 such that no digit repeats in a row, column or region. Numbered Rooms: Fill all circles with digits from 1-6. A digit N in a circle indicates that the Xth cell in that row or column, viewed from the direction of the clue, contains the digit N, where X is the digit in the cell next to the clue. Digits placed a chess knight's move apart cannot be the same. (This includes digits in circles.)
2350: Normal sudoku rules apply. Box borders divide blue lines into segments with the same sum. Different blue lines can have different sums. If two digits (called x and y) are neighbors along a blue line, then x as well as y has to be an integer multiple of the difference between x and y. For example, 6 and 4 are allowed to be adjacent on a blue line since both 6 and 4 are a multiple of 2 (the difference between 4 and 6).
2351: Normal-ish Sudoku rules apply ie place one of the digits 0-8 in every empty cell so that there are no repeated digits in any row, column or 3x3 box. Every 3-cell sequence on a teal line contains one digit from {0,3,6}, one from {1,4,7} and one from {2,5,8}. Digits an equal distance to the hat on the lavender line sum to the hatted digit. Digits joined by eyes are in a 1:2 ratio (ie one digit will be double the other). Digits joined by a small white dot differ by 1. Digits joined by an X sum to 10.
2352: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on a line sum up to a two digit number made out of the digit in the line's circle repeated twice. For example, 245 on a line (sum: 11) would have a 1 in its circle.
2353: Normal sudoku rules apply. Every cage in the grid is paired with exactly one other cage of the same colour. Digits may not repeat within a pair of cages, and when combined, sum to a concatenation of the two numbers in the top left corners of the cages. For example, if a 1 cage was paired with a 3 cage, the digits in both cages would sum to either 13 or 31. 0 is allowed to be the leading digit for sums in this puzzle. Digits separated by a white dot must be consecutive. Not all possible dots are necessarily shown.
2354: Normal sudoku rules apply. A clue outside the grid gives the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. The cell with the opaque grey circle contains an odd digit.
2355: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each 3x3 box contains a circled digit which is equal to the addend of that box. The addend applies to all cells of the box it lies within. The value of each cell is equal to the digit placed in the cell added to the addend of its box. The nine circled cells contain a different digit. Cells separated by a black dot have values in which one is double the other. Not all black dots are necessarily given. Box borders divide the blue lines into segments whose values have the same sum. Different lines may have different sums.
2356: Normal sudoku rules apply. Identify two "indexer" cells in each row, column, and box, with one indexing in the row and the other indexing in the column. The digit in an indexer cell indicates the position of the other indexer cell in its row or column. Positions are counted left to right in rows and top to bottom in columns. The value of an indexer cell is the digit in the cell it indexes. For all other cells, their value is their own digit. All lines are region-subset lines: ie 3x3 box boundaries divide each line into segments. For any pair of segments on the same line, the values on one of those segments must all appear on the other segment. Examples: i) If () represents an indexer cell, then 12(6)34(7)598 would be a valid row of digits, because there are exactly two indexer cells, and one of the cells indexes the other: the (7) is in position 6, and the other indexer cell contains a 6. The value of the (6) cell would be 7, because that is the digit in the cell it indexes. Given that this is a row, we would also know that r7c6 must be an indexer cell, because the (7) cell indexes it. ii) A region-subset line could contain the values 189-8-98-918, where a dash represents a box boundary. This is valid because (8) is a subset of (89) and (189), (89) is a subset of (189), and (189) is a subset of itself.
2357: Normal sudoku rules apply. The sum of the digits in a white bulb equals the sum of the digits on each attached arrow.
2358: Mark and Simon have just finished a game of Connect 4. They are both too clever for each other, and so it resulted in a draw; the board became full of an equal number of red and yellow discs without either of them managing to get any horizontal, vertical or diagonal connected line of 4 discs of their colour. Recreate the end board state by colouring the holes red and yellow. The first two moves have been shown. Fill the discs with the digits 1-7 so that no digits repeat in any row or column. A digit on an arrow disc indicates the total number of discs in the indicated directions (combined) that match its own colour. (The arrow disc itself isn't included in the count.) Two orthogonally adjacent red discs must be of different parity (one odd digit and one even digit.) Two orthogonally adjacent yellow discs must have a difference of at least 3.
2359: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells a chess knight’s move away from each other must not contain the same digit. Box borders split blue lines into segments where the digits on each segment have the same sum. This sum may be different for different lines.
2360: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits do not repeat along gold Nabner lines. Additionally, no pair of digits anywhere on a Nabner line can be consecutive. The digits along each arrow must sum to the digit in the circled cell. A black dot between cells indicates cell values with a 2:1 ratio (ie one digit will be double the other). A white dot between cells indicates cells with consecutive values. Not all possible dots are shown.
2361: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits along the green line have a difference of at least five. No two orthogonally connected cells can sum to 5. Cells separated by a black dot have digits in which one is double the other.
2362: Normal sudoku rules apply. All lines in the grid are German Whispers lines (regardless of color). Adjacent digits along the line must have a difference of at least 5. Digits separated by a white football are consecutive. Digits separated by a black football have a 1:2 ratio, meaning one is exactly double the other. Not all footballs are necessarily given.
2363: Normal sudoku rules apply. In addition, each unique letter of "FOURTH OF JULY" represents a unique digit from 1-9. The two-letter sandwich clue represents a two-digit number where the first letter is the tens digit and the second letter is the units digit. Along thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb end. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the cells "sandwiched" between the 1 and 9 in the relevant row/column.
2364: Normal sudoku rules apply. The circles given in the grid are the centers of pointsymmetric "galaxies", which function as cages for the Killer Sudoku. The numbers inside the circles indicate the sum of the digits in the cages. In addition, each cage is a "thermometer". Along thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb end, but the bulb end is not given. The cages/thermometers cannnot "branch". Thermometers are also symmetrical about their circles. The digits in a cage/thermometer may not repeat. Not every cell in the grid has to be part of a galaxy.
2365: Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid function as BOTH Sandwich and X-Sums Clues. In addition, Queen and King sudoku rules apply. 1. X-Sums: Numbers outside the grid indicate the sum of the first X digits in the corresponding direction. X is the first digit in the corresponding direction. 2. Sandwich: Numbers outside the grid indicate the sum of the digits between the 1 and the 9. 3. King: No digit can lie a "king's move" away from an equal digit (i.e. no digit can be adjacent to an equal digit, even diagonally). 4. Queen: You cannot repeat the number 9 within a "queen's move" (ie along the same diagonal).
2366: Normal sudoku rules apply, and neighbouring cells cannot contain consecutive digits. Clues outside the grid show the sum of the first X digits from that direction, where X is the first digit seen.
2367: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. If there is a digit in a cage outside of the 9x9 grid, it has to contain a number from 1-9. This number cannot be two-digits or 0. These digits outside the sudoku grid are sandwich clues and indicate the sum of the numbers between 1 and 9 in that row or column. [Cells outside the 9x9 sudoku grid are not subject to sudoku rules (ie sandwich totals can repeat!)].
2368: in each 3x3 box, the numbers 1,2,3,4 form a tetromino.
2370: Normal sudoku rules apply. Additionally, each cell must be orthogonally adjacent to a number greater or lower by 1. Each inequality symbol between two cells points to the lower cell with its "pointy" end.
2371: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along thermometer shapes digits must increase from the bulb end. Blue rectangles (“whimsical wind”) outside the grid indicate that the first 3 digits in that row/column must be unordered (ie neither increasing or decreasing). Yellow rectangles (“Rays of sunshine”) outside the grid indicate that the first 3 digits in that row/column must increase from the innermost to the outermost cell.
2372: Each row, column and 9-cell region must contain all digits from 1 to 9. Additionally, each digit must see one or more identical digits by a chess knight's single move. For example, if cell R1C2 has value of 7, then at least one of cells (potentially many) R3C1, R3C3 or R2C4 must also contain a 7.
2373: Normal sudoku rules apply. Normal thermo rules DO NOT apply. Each thermo consists of at least two numbers (each possibly multi-digit, with the unit digit towards the tip) that increase - at least doubling and at most tripling each time. Cells with an arrow pointing to an adjacent thermo cell must indicate how many digits the adjacent number on the thermo has. In cages, digits must sum to the clue in the top left corner of the cage.
2374: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits cannot repeat and their sum must equal the product of “corner cell” digits of that cage. A “corner cell” in a cage includes a horizontal and vertical dotted line.
2375: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells with a blue circle contain the number of neighboring odd digits, orthogonally and diagonally, excluding the cell itself. Along thermometers, digits must increase from the round bulb to each end. Cells separated by a white dot must contain consecutive digits.
2376: Normal sudoku rules apply. There are nine doubler cells in the grid, one in every row, column and box. Each digit from 1-9 appears in a doubler cell exactly once. A doubler cell's value counts as double its digit. Along a green line, values of neighboring cells must differ by at least 5. For cells separated by an ‘x', the two cells' values must sum to 10.
