The line starts with a small digit followed by a consecutive digit. From there, every next digit will be the sum of the previous two digits. For example, 1-2-3-5-8 or 4-5-9 are both valid.
2787: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits along a green line must differ by at least 5. Each pink line contains a set of consecutive, non-repeating digits, which can appear in any order. Each gray line consists of one or more contiguous groups of cells, each of which sums to 10. These groups of cells cannot overlap; every cell is part of exactly one group. Lines may share endpoints, but otherwise don't overlap.
2788: Normal sudoku rules apply. Quadruples: Digits in circles must appear at least once in the four surrounding cells.
2789: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is covered in fog. Correctly placing a digit will clear any fog in its own cell, and potentially clear fog in other cells too. Each row, column, and 3x3 region contains exactly one given digit whose exact location is to be deduced. No two givens are identical digits, i.e. each of the digits 1 to 9 is given exactly once. A clue outside a row or column indicates the sum of all digits up to the given digit (the given digit itself is not included in the sum). Digits on an arrow sum to the digit in the circle from which the arrow emerges. Digits joined by a black dot have a 1:2 ratio. Digits joined by a white dot are consecutive.
2790: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each line is divided into multiple segments, with the divisions at each point where the line changes region or enters/exits the grid. On a given line, each segment has the same sum (different lines may have different sums). Numbers on lines outside the grid (to be determined) are Hitpoints clues: a clue's value equals the sum of all digits in that row/column which equal their distance from the clue.
2791: Normal 6x6 Sudoku rules apply. ie Place the digits 1-6, once each, in every row, column and 2x3 rectangle. Draw a path along interior gridlines from the robot to the exit. The path cannot touch itself. The robot computes the difference between each pair of digits it passes between, and writes these differences to the grey memory cells in reading order. (All memory cells must be written to and no difference goes unrecorded).
2792: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits increase along thermometers from the bulb.
2793: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle.
2794: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow's circle.
2795: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along a thermometer, digits must increase from the bulb end.
2796: Normal Sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage.
2797: Normal sudoku rules apply (ie place the digits 1-9, once each, in every row, column and 3x3 box). The purple line contains a set of consecutive digits in any order. The digits in a cage sum to the small clue in the cage’s top left corner. Digits may not repeat in a cage.
2798: Normal sudoku rules apply (Place the digits 1-9, once each, into every row, column and 3x3 box). Cells separated by a single knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. The digits along a thermometer increase from the bulb end.
2799: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is partially covered in fog; placing a correct digit will clear the fog in that cell and possibly elsewhere in the grid. Each of the following constraint types may contain no repeated digits anywhere in the puzzle. E.g., if a parity line contains a 5, then no other parity line cell in the puzzle may contain a 5: 1) Digits in a cage must sum to the total given; 2) Digits joined by an X sum to 10; 3) Adjacent digits along a red parity line (PR) must alternate between odd and even digits; 4) A purple renban line (RB) must contain a set of consecutive digits in any order; 5) A yellow nabner line (NB) must contain a set of nonconsecutive digits in any order; 6) Any set of three digits along an orange entropic line (ENT) line must contain one digit from each of the following sets: 123; 456; 789; 7) Any set of three digits along a teal modular line (MOD) must contain one digit from each of the following sets: 147; 258; 369; 8) Pairs of digits equidistant from the centre of a pink zipper line (ZIP) must sum to the digit in the centre of that line, notated by a small circle. Lines in the puzzle never intersect or share cells.
2800: Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a single snaking line connecting two particular cells (to be discovered) which forms a palindrome, ie; its sequence of digits reads the same in either direction. The palindrome line should pass through the centres of cells, and may move both orthogonally and diagonally, but may not branch or cross itself. A digit on an arrow indicates how many cells it sees (in the indicated direction) that are NOT ON the palindrome. The arrow cell itself is not included in the count. Digits in a cage do not repeat, and the clue in the top left corner indicates the total of any digits in the cage that are NOT ON the palindrome.
2801: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages do not repeat, and sum to the small clue, if given. Grey circles contain 1 or 9. One grey loop is Entropic, one is German Whisper, and one is Region Sum; the solver must determine which is which. Entropic: every 3 cells along the line contain one low digit {123}, one middly digit {456}, and one high digit {789}. German Whisper: adjacent cells along the line differ by at least 5. Region Sum: box borders divide the line into segments with the same sum.
2802: Normal sudoku rules apply. Every 2-cell red or blue line can be read as a square number in one direction or the other (eg 25 or 52). The central grey cell is also a square number.
2803: Latin Square rules apply (ie place the digits 1-9, once each, into every row and column). The grid is covered in a checkerboard pattern of yellow and blue cells. Each digit appears in one of the colours exactly as many times as its value. For example, 7 will appear either exactly seven times in blue or exactly seven times in yellow. Digits may not repeat along any negative diagonal (those going from the top left to the bottom right). Cells separated by a single knight’s move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. Digits in grey circles must be odd.
2804: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in adjacent cells separated by a white dot differ by exactly 1. Adjacent digits on a green line differ by 5 or more. The digits in a cage sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage.
2805: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells a king's move apart are not allowed to contain identical digits. The digit in the central cell of each box is less than or equal to the box number. Boxes are numbered in normal reading order. Each horizontal 3x1 region that is completely contained in a single box sums to the same value. Each vertical 1x3 region that is completely contained in a single box sums to the same value. The digit in the top-left cell and the digit in the bottom-right cell of the grid sum to 3.
2806: Normal sudoku rules apply. A digit in a black circle must appear in one of the four cells touching that circle. A digit in a blue circle indicates how many blue circles contain that digit. Digits along a pink circle form a non-repeating consecutive sequence. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive.
2807: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the number in the attached circle. Digits do not repeat along each of the indicated diagonals.
2808: Normal sudoku rules apply. (ie Place the digits 1-9, once each, into every row, column and 3x3 box). Penrose Lines: On a pink line, a sequence of increasing digits repeats from the bulb end. The sequence must fully complete and repeat at least once (and, each time it repeats, it must repeat fully). For example, along a penrose line, digits could read: 137137137.
2809: Divide the grid into eight non-overlapping 2x4 regions, which can each be placed either horizontally or vertically. It must be determined which one of the digits 1-9 is missing from the grid. The other eight digits should each appear once in every row, column and region. RENBAN (pink) - digits along the pink line form a non-repeating consecutive set, which can appear in any order. NABNER (yellow) - no two digits on the yellow line may be consecutive (or the same.) REGION SUM (darker blue) - on the blue line, digits in each region have the same total. GERMAN WHISPER (green) - adjacent digits on the green line must have a difference of at least 5. PARITY (red) - digits on the red line must alternate between odd and even. PALINDROME (grey) - the string of digits on the grey line reads the same in either direction. SAME DIFFERENCE (turquoise) - each pair of adjacent digits on a turquoise line has the same difference. This difference value can be different for different turquoise lines. KROPKI - two digits connected by a black dot have a 2:1 ratio (ie one is double the other.)
2810: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each line can be divided into one or more segments such that every segment in the grid sums to the same total. (For the avoidiance of doubt, this means that segments from both the 78-cell line and the 2-cell line have the same sum!) The digit in the grey square is even.
2811: Normal sudoku rules apply. The cell with the gray square is even. Every 5 must have a 1 directly above it or a 9 directly below it. It may have both, but it doesn't need both. Digits in column 1 indicate the column in which the digit 1 appears in that row (e.g. if r4c1 is a 6, r4c6 is a 1). The same is true of column 5 and the digit 5, and column 9 and the digit 9. An X between two cells means that the digits in those cells must add up to 10.
2812: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. Along the indicated diagonal, digits cannot repeat.
2813: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by a white dot cannot be consecutive. Digits separated by black dot cannot have a 1:2 ratio. Digits separated by X may not sum to 10. Digits separated by V may not sum to 5. Digits in a cage may not sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits along a red line may not form a palindrome. Digits in a yellow “max” cell must be smaller than ALL the orthogonally adjacent cells. Digits in an orange “min” cell must be bigger than ALL the orthogonally adjacent cells. Digits in a circle cannot ALL appear in the surrounding cells and no digit in the 4 surrounding cells can repeat. Along each grey thermometer is a bulb (it is NOT the current one and has to be found); digits must increase from that bulb to the extremities and may not repeat. Digits along a purple line may not repeat and must not form a set of consecutive digits. Clues outside the grid must not give the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. A cell with a blue square must not contain an even digit.
2814: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a thermometer must increase from the bulb end. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. Digits cannot repeat on the main diagonal (marked in blue). Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle.
2815: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid 'wraps around' (the top connects to the bottom, and the left edge to the right edge). DUTCH CELLMATES: Every digit in the grid needs to have a digit at least 4 greater in the cell below it, or a digit at least 4 smaller in the cell above it. It may have both, but doesn't need both. KILLER CAGES: Cages chained to each other have the same sum.
2816: Normal sudoku rules apply. Every three-cell-segment of a teal modular line contains one digit from the groups {147}, {258} and {369}. The sum of the digits on a thin gray line equals the sum of the digits in the attached circles. Adjacent digits on a green line differ by at least 5. Purple lines contain a set of distinct consecutive digits in any order. Digits in cages do not repeat. Gray circles indicate odd and gray squares even digits. The digits on the MARKed diagonal sum to 60.
2817: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on blue lines can not be between or equal to the digits in the diamonds at the ends of the line. The digits in the diamonds at the ends of a line must differ by at least 4. A diamond terminates a line segment.
2818: Normal sudoku rules apply. German whispers: Adjacent digits on a green line must have a difference of at least 5. Digits in grey circles must be odd and digits in grey squares must be even. In cells separated by a black dot, one digit must be double the other. Not all dots are given. Renban: Digits placed on purple lines must be a non-repeating set of consecutive digits, in any order. Digits separated by an X must sum to 10. Not all Xs are given.
2819: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each digit in column 1 indicates the position of the 1 in its row. (eg if R5C1 is a 6, then R5C6 is a 1 as the 1 must appear in the 6th position). Column 5 operates the same way for the digit 5; and column 9 for the digit 9. Each digit in row 1 indicates the position of the 1 in its column. (eg if R1C5 is a 6, then R6C5 is a 1). Row 5 operates the same way for the digit 5; and row 9 for the digit 9. On thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb end. Along the marked diagonal, digits must not repeat.
2820: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits must not repeat in cages. Digits on thermometers increase from the bulb end. Digits on lines must be between the digits in the circles on each end. These lines also act as thermometers i.e. digits on lines must increase from the "low" circle to the "high" circle.
2821: Normal sudoku rules apply. The central 3x3 box is a magic square (each row, column and diagonal in that box sum to the same number). Digits on the thermometer increase from the bulb end. Cells connected by a purple line sum to 10. In the cage, digits that are a (chess) king's move apart from other caged digits must not repeat and must not sum to 5, 10 or 15.
2822: Normal sudoku rules apply. Lines contain digits in order with a constant difference (e.g. 1-2-3, 4-6-8, 7-4-1). Lines of the same colour cannot contain repeated digits. Cells separated by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio (ie one digit will be double the other).
2823: Normal sudoku rules apply. Box borders divide the blue line into segments. Along this blue line, each segment’s digits sum to the same total. The sum of all digits on the blue line and pink line combined is 89. A black dot between two cells indicates that one digit is double the other.
2824: Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells blue (“water”), such that all water cells are orthogonally connected, but water may not fully cover a 2x2 area. Shade the remaining cells green, which represent islands. Digits may not repeat within an island. Each island contains exactly one numbered clue, which gives the product of i) the sum of the digits on the island and ii) the size (number of cells) of the island, e.g. an island filled with 346 would have a "39" clue (13x3). A "?" may represent any single, double, or triple-digit number. A cell with an arrow(s) may be land or water, and the digit gives the total number of island cells in the indicated directions combined, not including itself. Not all arrows are given.
2825: Divide the grid into polyominoes and fill each cell with a number equal to the size of its polyomino. Polyominoes of the same size may not share an edge. Shade some cells such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected and all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected. No 2x2 area may be fully shaded or unshaded. All odd polyominoes are shaded, while all even polyominoes are unshaded. Numbers on cells with an arrow indicate the number of polyominoes of the SAME shading/parity seen in the direction of the arrow. Arrows do not count their own cell, but may count their polyomino if a cell within its polyomino is visible in the direction of the arrow.
2826: Cave: Shade some cells such that all orthogonally connected groups of shaded cells (the wall) touch the edge of the grid, and all unshaded cells (the cave) are orthogonally connected. Suguru: Each orthogonally connected group of shaded (wall) cells contains the digits 1-N (where N is the size of the group). Suguru digits may not repeat in a row, column, or shaded group. Fillomino: Divide unshaded cells into polyominoes and fill each cell with a digit equal to the size of its polyomino. Polyominoes of the same size may not share an edge. All numbers in the puzzle are 1-9. A Fillomino Polyomino may not border a Suguru digit with the same value. An unshaded circled clue indicates the total number of unshaded cells seen in the four orthogonal directions, including the clue cell. A shaded circle clue indicates the size of the shaded region.
2827: Masyu: Draw a closed, non-branching, non-crossing loop along dotted gridlines. The loop must visit all given circles and follow these rules for movements: The loop must turn on black circles, and go straight through at least one vertex on both sides of the turn. The loop must go straight through white circles. It must also turn on at least one of the vertices it visits on either side of the white circle. Gray circles act as either a black or a white circle (the solver must deduce which). Star Battle: The Masyu loop divides the grid into regions. Place exactly one star into each row, column, and region, such that no two stars touch, not even diagonally. For the solution check to work, place a 1 into every cell containing a star in the final grid and a 0 into all other cells.
2828: Normal sudoku rules apply. Nurikabe: Shade some cells (representing water) such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected, but never fully cover a 2x2 area. Groups of orthogonally connected unshaded cells form islands. Two separate islands cannot touch one another orthogonally, but may touch diagonally. Digits may not repeat on an island. Each island contains exactly one numbered clue, which gives the product of the sum of the digits on the island and the size (number of cells) of the island, e.g. an island filled with 346 is would have a '39' clue (13x3). A '?' may represent any number (not necessarily single-digit). A cell with arrow(s) may be land or water, and the digit gives the total number of island cells in the indicated directions combined, not including itself. Not all arrows are given.
2829: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits may not repeat along the indicated diagonal. Numbers outside the grid are simultaneously full rank clues and sandwich clues. A '?' can be any number. Full rank Each complete row and column can be read from both directions to form 36 distinct 9-digit numbers. The clues outside the grid give the rank of the 9-digit number read from that position when all the numbers are ranked from smallest (1) to highest (36). Sandwich: A number outside the grid represents the sum of the digits sandwiched between the '1' and '9' in its respective row or column.
2830: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a marked diagonal cannot repeat. Digits separated by an X sum to ten. Digits separated by a V sum to five. Not all XV pairs are shown. Numbers in a cage must be a perfect square (2-digit cages read left-to-right), and each perfect square can be used only one time.
2831: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage cannot repeat and must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage.
2832: Normal sudoku rules apply. Neighbouring digits on the green line have a difference of at least 5. Digits do NOT repeat on the green line. Neighbouring digits on the orange line have a difference of at least 4. Digits may repeat on the orange line. A purple line contains a set of consecutive numbers in any order. The cage shows its sum.
2833: Normal sudoku rules apply. The central 3x3 box of the puzzle forms a magic square. Ie each 3-cell row, column and main diagonal of that 3x3 box must sum to the same total. Digits in cages sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. Cells separated by a white dot must contain consecutive digits. Cells separated by an X must contain digits summing to 10. Cells separated by a V must contain digits summing to 5.
2834: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along thermometers, digits increase from the bulb end. Digits in cages sum to the number given. Adjacent digits on an orange line have a difference of at least 4. The blue is the water, and has no effect on the puzzle.
2835: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits cannot repeat on marked diagonals. Digits joined by a white dot are consecutive. Digits joined by a black dot are in a ratio of 2:1.
2836: Normal sudoku rules apply. Numbers on an arrow sum to the number on the arrow's origin (circle or pill). Pills are read from left to right. Some circles and pills do not have an arrow. Pink pills are the sum of the two pills or circles below them. Digits with a white dot between them are consecutive. Digits with a black dot between them are in a ratio of 2:1.
2837: Normal sudoku rules apply. Numbers in circles and pills are CONSECUTIVE powers (first power, second power, third power, etc.) of the number in the top circle in each of the three stacks. Numbers in pills are read from left to right. Digits in cages do not repeat and sum to the number shown. Digits joined by a white dot are consecutive.
2838: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits outside the grid give the sum of the digits between 1 and 9. Mozarts birth and death must be placed diagonally downwards. Mozart was born: 1756 Mozart died: 1791
2839: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits outside the grid give the sum of the digits between 1 and 9. Digits may not repeat on the diagonals.
2840: Normal sudoku rules apply, Clues outside the grid show the sum of the digits between the 1 and the 9 in that row/column. The grey shape is a palindrome.
2841: Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the cells "sandwiched" between the 1 and the 9 in the row/column. Einstein's birth year and death year must appear in the finished solution. The dates must read diagonally downwards (and the two dates can overlap).
2842: Normal sudoku rules apply. A clue outside the grid shows the sum of the digits between the 1 and the 9 in that row/column. No two 5s in the grid have the same digit in the cell immediately above.
2843: Normal sudoku rules apply. Box borders divide the blue Region Sum Lines into segments with the same sum. Gold Palindrome lines must read the same forwards or backwards.
2844: Place the digits 1-9, once each, into every row, column and irregularly-shaped marked nine-cell region. Cells separated by a black dot contain two digits where one digit is double the other. A magic square is a square of NxN cells in which each row, column and both main diagonals sum to the same total. (In this puzzle digits CAN repeat in a magic square.) The entire 9x9 grid is a magic square. In the centre of the 9x9 magic square is a 7x7 magic square. In the centre of that is a 5x5 magic square. And in the very centre is a 3x3 magic square. The dotted lines clarify the positions of the magic squares.
2845: Normal sudoku rules apply. The 3x3 box borders divide a blue line into segments. Each segment along a line has the same sum. (This segment sum can be different for different lines).
2846: Normal sudoku rules apply. Orthogonal neighbours (ie cells sharing an edge) are never consecutive. In the positive diagonals (ie diagonals sloping from SW to NE), the sum of neighbours is at most 11.
2847: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits along a green line have a difference of at least five. Digits increase from the bulb to the end of the thermometer. A digit in a square counts the number of odd digits (including itself) on its line or thermometer.

2849: Normal sudoku rules apply. Colour each cell in the grid either red or blue, such that no 2×2 square is a single colour and the cells of each colour form a single orthogonally connected region. Every line that passes through at least one red cell is an alternating-parity line (i.e. each pair of consecutive digits along the line must include one even and one odd digit). Every line that passes through at least one blue cell is a region-sum line (i.e. box borders divide the line into segments with equal sums; these sums may vary between lines). Any line that passes through both red and blue cells is also a renban (i.e. it contains a set of consecutive, non-repeating digits in any order).
2850: Normal sudoku rules apply. Box borders divide each blue line into segments with equal sums (the sum may vary between different lines). The black dot connects two digits, one of which is double the other.
2851: Normal sudoku rules apply. Exactly nine cells in the grid are "rooters". The value of a rooter equals the square root of its digit (in all other cells, the value equals the digit). No two rooters share a row, column, box, or digit. A black dot connects two cells where one value is double the other (not all such dots are necessarily given). Values on thermometers strictly increase from bulb to tip. The sum of the values along an arrow equals the value in the attached circle. Along green lines, neighbouring values differ by at least 5. On each purple line, the set of values consists of consecutive integers in any order. All cages have the same product of values (digits or values may repeat within a cage if allowed by other rules). The grid is partially covered in fog. Entering correct digits may clear some fog (not necessarily beneath or around the entered digit). No guessing is required.
2852: Normal sudoku rules apply. All blue (“+”) cages have the same SUM; all yellow (“×”) cages have the same PRODUCT. Both constants are to be determined by the solver. Digits may repeat within a cage if allowed by sudoku. The grid is partially covered in fog. Entering correct digits may clear fog somewhere in the grid. Usually a correct entry will clear its own cell, but not always — some fog is extra dense! No guessing is required.
2853: Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a one-cell-wide loop of orthogonally connected cells. The loop may not touch itself, not even diagonally. The loop acts as a German Whispers line (i.e., adjacent digits on the loop must have a difference of at least 5). Cells with small numbers in the corner are on the loop. This number gives the sum of all loop cells (including itself) seen from that cell in all horizontal/vertical directions combined, where non-loop cells block the vision. Digits may repeat in a sum if allowed by other rules.
2854: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along SLOW thermometers digits stay the same or increase as they move away from the bulb.
2855: Normal sudoku rules apply. The 3x3 box borders divide a blue line into segments. Each segment along a line has the same sum. (This segment sum can be different for different lines). Digits on a pink line form a set of non-repeating consecutive digits – these digits can appear in any order. Adjacent digits on a green line must have a difference of at least 5. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow’s circle.
2856: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each of the following constraint types may contain no repeated digits anywhere in the puzzle E.g., if an orange line cell contains a 5, then no other orange line cell in the puzzle may contain a 5. Constraint types: 1) A digit in a grey square is even; 2) A digit in a grey circle is odd; 3) For digits in cells separated by a white dot, one must be one greater than the other; 4) For digits in cells separated by a black dot, one must be double the other; 5) Adjacent digits along an orange line must differ by 4 or more.
2857: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a (chess) knight’s move cannot contain the same digit. Any three consecutive cells along a green (modular) line must contain one digit of each residue class modulo 3: {147}, {258} and {369}. Digits joined by a black dot are in 1:2 ratio, digits joined by a white dot are consecutive, and digits joined by a green dot are both in the same residue class modulo 3.
2858: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along the slow thermometer line increase or stay the same starting from its only bulb. The position of the single bulb is to be determined and it is on one of the cells marked with circles.
2859: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells a chess knight's move apart may not contain the same digit. Digits joined by a white dot are consecutive. All possible white dots are given. Digits joined by a V sum to 5. All such pairs are given. The grey line is a palindrome: its digits read the same in either direction.
2860: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by one move of a chess knight may not contain the same digit. For each line, the digits in the two cells marked with dots are ‘look-and-say clues’ ie in at least one way of reading them, one digit indicates how many times the other digit appears on the line. (eg if the marked cells contain 78 it can mean the line has seven instances of 8, or eight instances of 7). Adjacent digits along an orange line must have a difference of at least 4.
2861: Normal sudoku rules apply. Doppel-Dög loop: Draw an orthogonal non-branching closed loop that doesn't cross or touch itself, not even diagonally. The loop "starts" at the cell marked with the dog and is considered to be oriented in the direction indicated by the arrow (i.e. r6c6 and r6c7 are in the loop). A cell on the loop with a digit D will have a value equal to the cell D steps away along the loop in the orientation given by the arrow. Cells not on the loop will have a value equal to the digit in them. Adjacent digits (not values) along the loop must have a difference of at least 5. Values in a cage sum to the indicated total. Cells marked with a circle are not part of the loop and have a digit that equal to the count of the, up to 8, neighbouring loop cells. Clues outside the grid show the sum of the values of the loop cells in the indicated row/column.
2862: Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade each cell light or dark so that cells of the same colour are orthogonally connected and each 2x2 contains both colours. Dark cells have double their digits as values. (Light cells are unaffected.) Dots split lines into segments with equal value-sums. Values may repeat on segments but digits may not.
2863: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits may not repeat along the marked diagonal. Digits an equal distance from the centre of a lavender line sum to the central digit of that line.
2864: Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. Digits separated by a white dot have a difference of one, while digits separated by a black dot are in a 1 to 2 ratio (ie one digit will be double the other). Not all possible dots are given. Cells separated by a single knight's move (in chess) do not contain the same digit. Cells separated by a single king's move (in chess) do not contain the same digit.
2865: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is partially covered in fog; placing a correct digit may clear fog somewhere in the grid. Each of the following constraint types may contain no repeated digits anywhere in the puzzle. E.g., if a renban line contains a 5, then no other renban line cell in the puzzle may contain a 5: 1) Little Killer: Black numbers with an arrow outside the grid give the the sum of the digits on the indicated diagonal; 2) X-Sums: Red numbers outside the grid indicate the sum of the first X digits in that row or column, where X is the first digit in that row or column; 3) Digits on a purple Renban (RB) line form a non-repeating set of consecutive digits NB All Renban lines are exactly three cells long; 4) Neighbouring digits on a green German Whisper (GW) line must have a difference of at least 5; 5) The 3x3 box borders divide blue Region Sum (RS) lines into segments. Each segment along a line has the same sum.
2866: Normal sudoku rules apply. In each cage, there is one digit that equals the sum of the other three digits in that cage. Digits may repeat in cages if allowed by sudoku rules.
2867: Normal sudoku rules apply. If a white dot separates digits, they are consecutive. If a black dot separates digits, one is double the other. Adjacent digits along a green line have a difference of at least 5.
2868: Normal sudoku rules apply. Two cells separated by a single Chess knight's move must contain different digits. Digits within a cage must sum to the clue in the cage’s top-left corner. The clue outside the grid gives the sum of all digits along the indicated diagonal. Digits may repeat on this diagonal if allowed by the other rules.
2869: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages must sum to the number in the top left corner of the cage. Digits may not repeat within a cage. The numbers outside the grid give the sum of the digits between the 1 and the 9 in that row or column.
2870: Normal sudoku rules apply: Place the digits 1-6 once each in every row, column, and 2x3 box. Doublers: Place one Doubler in every row, column, and box. Each Doubler must contain a different digit. The value of a Doubler is 2 times the digit in its cell. The value of a non-Doubler is the digit in its cell. Standard Region Sum Line, Renban, Nabner, Thermo, Kropki, XV, and Quadruple rules apply, with respect to cell values ie: Region Sum Line: Box borders divide the blue line into segments with equal sums of values. Renban: Values along the pink line must form a set of non-repeating consecutive values in any order. Nabner: The two values on the yellow line must have a difference of at least 2. Thermo: The value on the tip of the thermometer must be larger than the value on the bulb. Kropki: Values separated by the white dot are consecutive. Values separated by a black dot are in a 2:1 ratio. V: Values separated by the V sum to 5. Quadruple: The value 2 must appear at least once in the four cells surrounding the white circle.
2871: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells along gray lines between two filled circles must have values between those in the circles. The sum of the digits along a red line connecting two circles is equal to the sum of the digits in the circles. The digit in the circle is odd. The digit in the square is even. Digits may repeat on lines of either type if allowed by other rules.
2872: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb end. The purple line contains a set of consecutive digits in any order. Adjacent digits on a green line differ by at least 5.
2873: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each grey line is a "slow thermometer" with an invisible bulb at one end. Digits on a slow thermometer either increase or stay the same, as they move away from the bulb, but they never decrease.
2874: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits along a green line must differ by at least 5. Each pink line contains a set of consecutive, non-repeating digits, which can appear in any order. Each grey line consists of one or more contiguous groups of cells, each of which sums to 10. These groups of cells cannot overlap; every cell is part of exactly one group. Lines may share endpoints, but otherwise don't overlap.
2875: Fill the grid with digits from 1-9 so that no digit repeats in any of the 9 rows, 11 columns, or 9 boxes. Along each of the 6 grey lines, digits increase in one direction. If a line has a bulb, the bulb is the smaller end. Digits touching a white dot are consecutive. Digits touching a black dot are in a 2:1 ratio. (For clarity, thermometer and kropki clues "connect up" as if the grid were un-skewed).
2876: Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage.
2877: Divide the grid into 9 regions, each consisting of 9 orthogonally connected cells. Place the digits 1-9 exactly once in every row, column, and region. The digits along the arrow sum to the three-digit number displayed in the attached pill. The arrow passes through the centres of all cells that are not part of the pill (note that consecutive arrow cells are not necessarily adjacent; for example, a portion of the arrow follows r7c1 → r7c3 → r8c1). The arrow functions as a ‘region sum line’: along the arrow, every maximal sequence of digits within the same region has the same sum. I.e. when all non-pill cells are arranged in sequence according to the order in which the arrow visits their centres, this sequence will be composed of disjoint contiguous segments with equal sums. Two consecutive cells in this sequence belong to the same segment if and only if they are part of the same region. The inequality sign points to the smaller digit.
2878: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is covered in fog. Placing a correct digit will remove the fog from its cell and possibly other cells in the grid. One cell in each row, column and box is a doubler. The value of a doubler cell is equal to twice its digit. Each of the digits from 1 to 9 appears in a doubler cell. On each of the constraints below, values do not repeat anywhere in the puzzle. For example, if there is a 2 on a parity line, 2 or double 1 can't appear anywhere else on a parity line, but double 2 could because it has a value of 4. 1) Adjacent values on a thin green line differ by at least 5; 2) Values on a thick purple line form a set of consecutive numbers with no repeats; 3) Adjacent values on a hollow red line must alternate between odd and even; 4) A value on an orange circle must be greater than 5; 5) A value on a blue square must be lower than 5.
2879: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits are not allowed to repeat on any positive diagonal (i.e. any diagonal going from the lower-left part of the grid to the upper-right part of the grid). A digit x in a black circle indicates exactly how many of the up to 8 neighboring cells (i.e. orthogonally and diagonally adjacent cells) contain a digit that is in a 1:2 ratio with x. All black circles are given. The sum of the digits in Phistomefel's ring (marked by the cage) is prime.
2880: Normal sudoku rules apply. INFLUENCER CELLS: The grid contains nine 'influencer cells', each in a different row, column and box, and each containing a different digit. Every cell in the grid has a value equal to its own digit plus the digits in any orthogonally adjacent influencer cells. Eg: a cell containing a digit 2 would have a value of 10 if it neighbours an influencer 3 and an influencer 5, because 2 + 3 + 5 = 10. CAGES: The small clue in the corner of a cage indicates the total value of the cells in that cage. REGION SUM LINES: 3 x 3 box borders divide blue lines into segments. The values on each segment have the same sum, though this sum can be different for different lines.
2881: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits along an orange line have a difference of at least four. Each cage has digits that sum to 3. The central digit of the puzzle is even.
2882: Normal sudoku rules apply. The purple lines in the grid are “renban” lines. Ie Digits on a line form a set of non-repeating, consecutive digits in any order.
2883: Normal sudoku rules apply. A digit N placed inside a circle or semicircle indicates that exactly N full circles in the grid contain the digit N. Two semicircles together count as one full circle. For example, if there are four semicircles containing the digit 5 and three full circles containing the digit 5, then the total count is 2+3=5 circles with the digit 5.
2884: Normal sudoku rules apply. The sum of the digits along an arrow is equal to the digit in that arrow’s circle. German Whispers: Adjacent digits along a green line must differ in value by at least 5. Renban: Purple lines contain a non-repeating set of consecutive digits – these digits can appear in any order.
2885: Normal sudoku rules apply. Yin Yang: Shade some cells in the grid such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected and all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected. No 2x2 may be all shaded or all unshaded. A cell that is a ‘doubler’ has value equal to twice its digit. Two Truths and a Different Truth: For all the following constraints, if shaded cells are treated as doublers and unshaded cells are normal then two of the clues are correct and the third is incorrect. If unshaded cells are treated as doublers and shaded cells are normal then the same two clues are incorrect and the third is correct: a) Renban: Values on a pink line form a set of consecutive numbers with no repeats; b) Arrows: Values on an arrow sum to the value in that arrow's circle; 3) Values on an X sum to 10; 4) Values on a white dot are consecutive. Values on a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio (ie one is double the other); 5) A value on a grey circle is odd. A value on a grey square is even.
2886: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells that are a knight's move apart in chess cannot contain the same digit. Digits on a line of any color form a set of non-repeating consecutive numbers (in any order).
2887: Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a snake connecting the two green spots. The snake must be one cell wide, may only move orthogonally, and may not touch itself (not even diagonally.) Adjacent digits along the snake must have a difference of at least 5. A digit in a coloured circle indicates how many times that digit appears in a circle of that colour. All circles of one colour are on the snake. All circles of the other colour are not on the snake.
2888: From each clue outside the grid, draw a path which begins in the nearest cell of the grid and then travels orthogonally from cell to cell until arriving at a fish. All empty cells must be used by a path. Paths may not cross themselves, each other, or fish. A number at the beginning of a path indicates how many cells in the grid the path occupies, including the cell with the fish. To avoid confusion among the anglers, no two fishing lines of the same length may touch. This includes both orthogonal and diagonal touching. Answer Check: For each ? clue, fill each cell along the corresponding path with the digit equal to the length of the path. If the length is a double digit number, fill the cells with the one's digit of the length.
2889: Normal sudoku rules apply. The 3x3 box borders divide blue lines into segments. The digits on each segment of the same line must sum to the same total. Digits on pink lines form a non-repeating, consecutive sequence in any order.
2890: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each cage must appear cloned somewhere in box nine, without rotations or reflections. All cages marked with x must have the same total, to be deduced by the solver. Cells separated by a grey dot must either be consecutive, or have a 2:1 ratio (ie one digit would be double the other).
2891: Normal sudoku rules apply. Every run of five digits on the yellow line contains a digit from {1,6}, a digit from {2,7}, a digit from {3,8}, a digit from {4,9}, and the digit 5. The grey line consists of one or more contiguous groups of cells, each of which sums to 10. These groups of cells cannot overlap. Digits an equal distance from the centre of the purple line must sum to the digit in the centre of that purple line. Adjacent digits along the green line must differ by at least 5. Digits on the pink line form a set of consecutive integers in some order.
2892: Normal sudoku rules apply: Place the digits 1-9 once each in every row, column, and 3x3 box. Draw a 1 cell wide loop through the centers of some cells. The loop only moves orthogonally and cannot branch or touch itself, even diagonally. A digit in a circle on the loop indicates how many circles on the loop contain that digit. Similarly, a digit in a circle off the loop indicates how many circles off the loop contain that digit. Black dots separate digits where one is double the other. Additionally, exactly one cell touching a black dot is on the loop, and the other is off the loop. White dots separate consecutive digits. Additionally, the two cells touching a white dot are either both on the loop, or both off the loop. Not all dots are necessarily given.
2893: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. The two main diagonals each contain every number from 1 to 9 exactly once. The cells on a purple line contain a set of non-repeating consecutive digits, but not necessarily in order.
2894: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages sum to the number in the top left corner of the cage. Digits do not repeat within a cage. Digits separated by an V sum to 5.
2895: Normal Sudoku Rules. In cages, digits must sum to 12. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits sandwiched between the 1 and 9 in that row/column. The 5 gold rings are all sandwich “crusts” (ie the digit 1 or 9). Some of the clues have been replaced with letters. Each letter represents a different digit.
2896: Normal sudoku rules apply, and yellow lines are separate palindromes, reading the same in each direction. Numbers ascend along the (grey) thermometers, from the bulb to the end(s). The grid contains one hidden, 9-cell, straight thermometer occupying one whole row, column or diagonal.
2897: Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid show the sum of digits sandwiched between the 1 and 9 in that row/column. Some flies have got into some of these sandwiches. Each cell with a fly (Ѫ) is either 'sandwich filling' (included in the sandwich sum) or 'sandwich crust' (1 or 9) for one of the clued sandwiches. The grid also contains a couple of 'palindromic worms. The digits along the worms read the same starting at either end. Some of the clues have been replaced with letters. Each letter represents a different digit from 1-9.
2898: Normal sudoku rules apply. A clue outside the grid shows the sum of the first X digits along that row/column where X is the first such digit. Digits on a bauble or star (circle) contain the difference between the sum of all the digits on one of the attached lines and the sum of all the digits on the other.
2899: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each circle has a value equal to the four digits around the clue arranged in ascending order. Eg if the four digits were 4,3,6,4 then the value of the circle would be 3446. Assign each circle a rank according to its value's position in a list of the all of the circles' values. The lowest rank would have rank 1, the next lowest would have rank 2 etc. Place each circle's rank into the cell at the tip of the arrow emerging from that circle. NB clues with the same value would have the same rank and would have the same digit in the tip of their circle's arrow. Digits in a cage sum to the given total.
2900: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow’s circle. Within a cage, digits do not repeat and sum to the total given. All cages sum to 7 or 13.
2901: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells with squares in them contain even digits. In this grid, the digit '4' is the only even digit that is allowed to see itself diagonally.
2902: Place the digits 0-8 in every row, column, and 3x3 box of the grid without repeats. Digits separated by an X sum to 10, digits separated by a V sum to 5. All Xs and Vs are given. Digits may not repeat along either marked diagonal. Digits placed on a purple line must be a non-repeating set of consecutive digits – these digits can appear in any order.
2903: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits connected by an olive dot must be from different parities (1 even/1 odd) and differ by at least 5. Digits connected by a lavender dot must be consecutive and from different entropic sets (123/456/789). Digits in killer cages do not repeat and must sum to the number in the top left of the cage.
2904: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits on green lines differ by at least five and each line contains exactly one repeat digit. Once a digit has appeared on a line as a 'repeat digit,' it may not do so again. Digits cannot be a knight's move (in chess) away from themselves. Digits in a cage do not repeat and sum to the total in the top left corner.
2905: Lines: Draw two non-branching lines in the grid - one green and one blue - that connect the centres of cells. The lines must only move orthogonally (i.e. not diagonally). Neither line may touch itself, even diagonally. The two lines may, however, touch or cross each other, but only at discrete points (i.e.if the two lines meet in the centre of one cell they cannot continue in the same direction into the centre of their next cell). The green line must form a closed loop; and, the ends of the blue line may not be on any intersections with the green line. Projected Sums: Clues outside the grid give the sum of digits on lines along the indicated direction. Coloured clues count only the line of that colour. Black clues count digits on both lines. If both lines pass through a cell, that cell's digit only counts once in the projected sum. German Whispers: Along the green line adjacent digits must differ by at least 5. Modular Lines: Along the blue line, in every run of three cells, the three digits in those cells must each have a different remainder when divided by 3. Clones: The two cages are exact clones of each other. They contain the same digits in the same positions and they contain the same lines (including colour) in the same positions. Digits may repeat within the clone if otherwise allowed.
2906: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage do not repeat and sum to 23.
2907: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits may not repeat in a cage and must sum to the number in the top left corner of the cage. Adjacent digits along a thicker orange line must differ by at least 4. The 3x3 box borders divide the thinner blue line into segments, each of which has the same sum. Digits in orange circles count the total number of odd digits along the line connected to the circle, including the circled cell. Digits on a thin green line with circles at both ends sum to a two-digit number; the 'tens' digit of this sum is in one circle and the 'units' digit is in the other circle.
2908: Normal sudoku rules apply. Every constraint in the puzzle is a straight line: every horizontal line is a renban, every vertical line is a German whisper, and every diagonal line is a region sum line. Different lines of the same type do not share cells. The grid is partially covered in fog. Entering correct digits may clear fog somewhere in the grid. No guessing is required. A renban line contains a set of consecutive, non-repeating digits in any order. Adjacent digits on a German whisper line must differ by at least 5. Box borders divide a region sum line into segments each of which must have the same total (different lines may have different totals).
2909: Normal sudoku rules apply. Yin-Yang: Shade some cells in the grid so that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected, all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected, and no 2×2 region is entirely shaded or entirely unshaded. A shaded cell containing digit x has value x+10; an unshaded cell has value equal to its digit. Region sum lines: Blue lines are divided into segments by box borders. All segments along a single line must have the same sum of values (this sum may differ between lines). Cells connected by a black dot have values, one of which is double the other. Not all dots are necessarily given. The grid is partially covered in fog. Placing correct digits reveals their own cell and may also lift fog elsewhere in the grid. No guessing is required.
2910: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Digits separated by a black dot have a 1:2 ratio.
2911: Normal sudoku rules apply in the 9x9 central grid. Numbered Rooms: All outside cells on the thermo must contain a digit. That digit must also appear in the Nth position looking into the grid in the row/column, where N is the digit in the first position. Slow Thermometer: Digits on the slow thermometer must not decrease, starting from the bulb end (the circle). The white dot separates consecutive digits. The black dot separates digits where one is double the other. The X separates digits that sum to 10.
2912: Standard Fillomino rules apply: divide the grid into regions of orthogonally connected cells, and place a number in every cell equal to the size of its region (ie the number of cells that region contains). Regions of the same size cannot share an edge. Some numbers are already given. Every Fillomino region contains a unique cell (called the Top Right Boi!): looking at the region, there can be no cell in the region that is either further to the east or further to the north than the Top Right Boi cell.
2913: Place the digits 1–9 exactly once in each row and each column of the grid. Draw a directed path that moves orthogonally between cell centres and visits every cell of the grid exactly once. Each of the 27 cages can be entered by the path at most once (i.e. the path must visit all cells of a cage in a single continuous run before leaving it). The path acts as a thermometer with respect to cage totals: as the path moves away from its starting cell, the sums of the cages it visits must strictly increase. Digits may not repeat within a cage.
2914: Place a digit from 1-7 in each cell. Each digit must appear exactly once in each row, column, and box, except for the digits 1 and 3, which may appear any positive number of times. Every 1 and 3 must be part of at least one adjacent pair of cells which reads as '13' either from left to right or from top to bottom. Digits in a cage do not repeat (including 1 and 3) and sum to the total shown in the top left corner.
2915: Normal sudoku rules apply. No digit can appear a chess knight's or a chess king's move away from itself. Digits along an arrow sum to the number in the oval which is a 2-digit number reading left-to-right. Adjacent digits along the arrow (including the oval) have a difference of at least 4.
2916: Normal sudoku rules apply. Identical digits may not be a chess knight's move apart. Each pink line contains a set of consecutive digits in any order. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits between 1 and 9 in that row or column.
2917: Fill the grid with the digits 1-9, plus the letters R, B and C, so that no letter or digit repeats in any row, 3x4 box, or column. 3x4 boxes are numbered 1-12 in normal reading order. The value of an R equals its row number. The value of a B equals its box number. The value of a C equals its column number. BLACK KROPKI: If two values are joined by a black dot, one is double the other. RENBAN: Values along a pink line form a non-repeating consecutive sequence, arranged in some order. GERMAN WHISPER: Adjacent values on a green line have a difference of at least 5. ARROWS: Values along an arrow sum to the value in the attached circle. SAME DIFFERENCE: Adjacent values on a turquoise line have the same difference. This difference may be different for different turquoise lines.
2918: Fill each cell (octagons and squares) with a digit from 1-9. Cells sharing an edge can't have the same digit. Each horizontal row and vertical column contains a non-repeating consecutive set of digits (like 2345678) in any order. A value in an external cell represents the rank of the number formed by reading the digits in the indicated 5-cell diagonal from that direction, where (1) is the lowest such row or column and (20) is the highest. If two ranks are tied, the value in both external cells is the lower of the two ranks being shared.Eg, if the lowest four ranks are '12453', '13524', '13524' and '15432', the values in the relevant external cells would be (1), (2), (2) and (4) respectively.
2919: Each ball may move sideways or downwards (diagonally or straight) any number of times, but may NOT move upwards, on its journey. Balls may not enter any cell more than once. Balls may not enter a grey shaded cell or a "bumper" cell (given digit). Each ball must visit both of the "target" cages (shaded yellow) along the way. No path shares any cells, and while they may cross other paths diagonally, no path crosses itself. Box borders divide the BLUE path into segments with the same sum. Adjacent digits along the GREEN path must differ by at least 5. Digits along the RED path must be 5 or higher.
2920: Normal sudoku rules apply. Colour each cell in one of two different colours, where cells containing the same digit must have the same colour. If an orthogonally connected group of cells of the same colour has one or more circles in it, the circled cell(s) contain the size of that group.
2921: Fill the grid with nine non-overlapping 3x3 regions, such that each region contains the digits 1-9 once each and no digit repeats in any row or column. Digits along a marked diagonal sum to the clue outside the grid. Blank cells don't count towards the total.
2922: Normal sudoku rules apply. Reading from the bulb to the tips, digits along a thermometer must either increase or stay the same. Adjacent digits along the green line have a difference of at least five. Box borders divide each blue line into segments with the same sum. Each cage has digits that sum to 8.
2923: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in its black circle. Digits may repeat along an arrow if allowed by other rules. A digit x in a circle (including black arrow circles and red circles) indicates exactly how many of the up to 8 neighboring cells (i.e. orthogonally or diagonally adjacent cells) contain a digit that differs by at least 5 from x.
2924: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. A black dot sits between two digits where one is double the other. Not all dots are necessarily given. Inequality signs between two cells point towards the smaller digit.
2925: Divide the grid into five regions, each containing 5 orthogonally connected cells. Place a digit from 1-5 in each cell so that digits do not repeat in a row, column or region. 'Marbles' join cells that share a region, and no two marbles share a region. Draw a 'Marble Run' from any cell in the top row to a 3 in a bottom corner. The marble run line is formed entirely of L-shaped line segments: a downwards movement (to gain speed) and then a horizontal movement of the same distance. Adjacent cells on the Marble Run are in different regions. Use the pentomino information provided around the grid to discover a secret code and enter it at the top of the grid to reveal the final rule.
2926: Place each digit 1–7 exactly once in each row and column of the 7×7 grid. The grid is covered by 16 jigsaw pieces. Each piece covers the same sum. If a cell is covered by more than one piece, its digit is split between those pieces proportionally to the area covered. Eg if R4C4 contains the digit x, then this cell contributes ¼·x to the sum of the piece covering R3C3, ½·x to the sum of the piece covering R3C5, and ¼·x to the sum of the piece covering R5C5.
2927: Within the main grid (inside the thick border), fill every cell with a digit from 1-5 such that digits do not repeat in a row or column. Full Rank: A value in an external cell represents the rank of the number formed by reading the digits in that row or column from that direction, where (1) is the lowest such row or column and (20) is the highest. Mod 3 lines: Any 3 adjacent cells along a line must contain a complete set of residues modulo 3 (there will be a residue 0, 1, and 2, with residue defined as the remainder of the cell value after dividing by 3). N.B. If two ranks are tied, the value in both external cells is the lower of the two ranks being shared. For example, if the lowest four ranks are "12453", "13524", "13524" and "15432", the values in the relevant external cells would be (1), (2), (2) and (4) respectively.
2928: Normal sudoku rules apply. The sum of two orthogonal neighbours is at most 13 (ie no domino in the grid can sum to more than 13). The sum of two 'point symmetric' cells is always 10. (Point symmetric cells are pairs that are mirror images of each other across the exact centre of the 9x9 grid (the middle of the central 3x3 box). ie Rotating the grid 180° around this central point maps a cell directly onto its symmetric partner). So, for example, r7c1's symmetric counterpart is r3c9.
2929: Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected and all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected. No 2x2 area may be fully shaded or fully unshaded. If two digits are separated by a black dot one digit is double the other. Additionally, a black dot always separates a shaded and an unshaded cell. Not all dots are necessarily given. Shaded digits in the grid represent skyscrapers of that height, with taller skyscrapers obscuring smaller ones. A clue outside the grid shows the number of all visible skyscrapers from the clue's direction. Unshaded digits do not affect the outside clues.
2930: Normal sudoku rules apply. Placing a correct digit may clear fog somewhere in the grid. Adjacent cells cannot sum to 10. Grey lines are palindromes that read the same in both directions. If two digits are separated by a black dot one is double the other. Not all possible black dots are necessarily shown. A cell marked with a grey circle contains an odd digit. No guessing is required.
2931: Normal sudoku rules apply. Outside clues are Sandwich clues, indicating the sum of the cells between the lowest & highest values (usually 1 & 9) seen in their row or column. R0C0 applies this to each of row 0 & column 0 individually. Apart from value 0, every Sandwich clue is unique. (If multiple instances of 0 are seen by R0C0's clue, which is 'lowest' is to be determined by the solver.) Cells across white dots contain consecutive values. Cells across black dots contain one value double the other (1:2 ratio).
2932: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each row, column, and 3x3 box contains two 'indexer' cells: a 'row indexer' and a 'column indexer'. The digit in a row indexer gives the position of the column indexer in that row. The digit in a column indexer gives the position of the row indexer in that column. Positions are counted left-to-right in rows and top-to-bottom in columns . Digits in a cage sum to the small clue in the upper left corner, if given. Indexer cells cannot appear in cages.
2933: Normal Sudoku rules apply, but once again strange things are afoot... Fog has filled the land, thicker than ever before, and within it, lurk many Creatures of the night! Yet fear not! If you can find them, friendly Wisps will aid you in navigating the fog. There is one Wisp in each row, column, and 3x3 box, marked by a pale blue dot. Cells containing a Wisp contain either their row, column or box number (read in normal reading order). No two Wisps can contain the same digit. Fog cleared by Wisps leaves an eerie blue light. The Monsters: Zombies: marked by a green dot, zombies have an infectious bite. Orthogonally adjacent cells are even when the zombie's number is even, or odd when the zombie's number is odd. Vampires: marked by a red dot, vampires suck the power from their victims. Orthogonally adjacent cells sum up to the vampire's number. Headless Horsemen: marked by an orange dot, horsemen have a knight's reach. Cells a chess-knight's move away from the horseman can't contain the same digit as the horseman's number. Poltergeists: marked by a grey dot, poltergeists throw everything into disarray. Orthogonally adjacent cells are either all higher than the poltergeist's number, or all lower. Fog: the land is covered in dynamic fog. Putting in correct digits will clear the fog for that cell. Finding a Wisp will clear more fog. No guessing is required. The monster under your bed will know if you cheat!
2934: Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a directed path through the centres of some cells in the grid, starting in one blue circle and ending in the other. The path may move only orthogonally north (↑), orthogonally east (→), or diagonally southwest (↙), and it may not visit any cell more than once. The path must function both as an entropic line and as a region sum line. Every black dot in the grid must be crossed by the path. A white dot joins two cells - neither of these cells may be visited by the path. Along an Entropic line, every set of three consecutive cells along the line must contain one low digit (1,2,3), one middle digit (4,5,6), and one high digit (7,8,9). Along a Region sum line. the 3x3 box borders divide the line into segments; and all such segments must have the same sum. A white dot between two digits means they must be consecutive. If two digits are separated by a black dot one is double the other. One of the dots contains an inequality sign pointing to the smaller digit.
2935: Normal sudoku rules apply. Exactly one cell in each row, column, and box is a "doubler", and doubler cells contain a complete set of the digits 1-9. A cell's value is equal to its digit, except that a doubler cell may or may not have a value equal to its digit multiplied by two. The same cell may have different values for the purpose of different clues. The sum of the values inside each cage is shown. The sum of the values along an arrow is equal to the value in the connected circle. Box borders divide each blue line into segments with the same sum of values. Along a green line, values differ from their neighbors by at least 5. A purple line contains a non-repeating set of consecutive values in any order. Values in cells separated by a black dot have a 1:2 ratio.
2936: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is partly covered in fog. Placing correct digits may clear fog revealing other clues. No guessing is required. A digit in a square indicates the total number of digits smaller than itself that it 'sees' in all the four cardinal directions (North, East, South, West) along its row and column. In each direction, it 'sees' ALL digits smaller than itself until vision is blocked by a digit greater than itself or the edge of the grid. (For clarity it does not see itself). If a black dot separates two digits, one of those digits is double the other.
2937: Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a 1-cell wide loop that moves strictly orthogonally and doesn't branch or intersect itself. The loop doesn't touch itself, not even diagonally. Neighbouring digits on the loop must have a difference of at least 5. A digit in a circle indicates how many times that digit must appear in circles. The circled digits also indicate how many of the (up to 8) surrounding cells are on the loop. Circles are never on the loop. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Digits separated by a black dot have a 1:2 ratio.
2938: Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a 1-cell wide loop that moves strictly orthogonally and doesn't branch or intersect itself. The loop doesn't touch itself, even diagonally. The loop acts as a German whispers line. Neighbouring digits on the loop must have a difference of at least 5. A digit in a circle indicates how many times that digit must appear in circles. The circled digits also indicate how many of the up to 8 surrounding cells are on the loop. Circles are never on the loop.
2939: Normal sudoku rules apply. (Place the digits 1-9, once each, into every row, column and 3x3 box.) Cages within the same 3x3 box must sum to the same total. Any cage can only contain either all odd digits or all even digits.
2940: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each cage has a two-digit total to be placed by the solver inside the cage. Place the tens digit in the leftmost cell of the topmost row of the cage, then write the total from left to right. If the cage shape doesn’t allow a left-to-right placement, write the units digit directly below the tens digit instead. If the total consists of two identical digits (e.g., 22, 33, 44), write only a single digit. Digits may repeat within a cage, provided normal sudoku rules are not broken. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in the attached circle.
2941: Normal sudoku rules apply. A binary code is a sequence of numbers (“bits”) that are either on or off. In this puzzle, Odd digits represent bits that are 'OFF'(O) and Even digits represent bits that are 'ON'(E). This gives us the following representation of the digits 1-9: 1 → OOOE 2 → OOEO 3 → OOEE 4 → OEOO 5 → OEOE 6 → OEEO 7 → OEEE 8 → EOOO 9 → EOOE The digit in an arrow cell dictates the parity (odd or even) of its four orthogonal neighbours. These four neighbours must match the binary code of the digit with the small arrow. The arrow points to the first bit of the binary code. (read from left to right.) The full code must wrap around the central cell clockwise. Eg If a 6 is placed in an arrow cell, its code is OEEO. Therefore, its four neighbours (starting from the arrow direction, moving clockwise) must be Odd, Even, Even, Odd.
2942: Fill each cell with a digit from 1-9. Cells sharing an edge can't have the same digit. Each horizontal row and vertical column contains a non-repeating consecutive set of digits (like 23456) in any order. The blue circles and red squares combined form a complete set of the digits 1-9. A digit in a blue circle indicates how many of that digit appear in the entire puzzle. A digit in a red square indicates that the digit does not appear exactly that many times in the puzzle. EG if there were four 4s and six 5s in the grid, the 4 would go into a circle and the 5 in a square.
2943: Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a one-cell-wide loop of orthogonally connected cells. The loop may not touch itself, not even diagonally. The loop acts as an entropic line. Each set of three adjacent digits along the loop must be one low [123], one medium [456], and one high digit [789]. The loop must enter every cell of every cage. The sum of all digits in any given cage is the same for every cage (that sum must be determined by the solver).
2944: Dr. Norma L. Dokes! A virus is spreading and causes people to eat each others brains! Please perform some measurements in the village and bring the results to the hospital. We need to see how severe the spread is. But be careful - It is highly contagious! NORMA L DOKES - Normal sudoku rules apply. INFECTIONS - The 3x3 boxes are numbered in normal reading order, 1 to 9. Each digit matching its own box number is a 'patient zero'. Each row and column contains a 'patient zero'. Patient zeroes are infected. Infected cells infect every orthogonally adjacent cell with a smaller digit. Infections keep spreading until no infected cell has a smaller uninfected orthogonal neighbour. (Every infected cell can be traced back to one or more patient zeroes.) PATH - Draw a 1-cell wide path from the doctor () to the hospital (). The path only moves orthogonally and may not touch itself, not even diagonally. The path may not contain infected cells. MICROSCOPES () are on the path and count the number of infected cells in the (up to 9) surrounding cells. KROPKI TABLETS (white dots) join consecutive uninfected digits.
2945: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages must sum to the number in the corner of the cage. Digits in cells separated by a black dot must be in a 2:1 ratio, digits in cells separated by a white dot must be consecutive - not all dots are shown. Digits along a purple Renban line must be a set of consecutive digits in any order. Digits along a red palindrome must read the same forwards or backwards. Digits along the blue diagonal line must not repeat.
2946: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits cannot repeat along the marked diagonal. Every 2×2 square of cells must contain all three possible remainders modulo 3 (i.e. at least one digit from each of the sets {1,4,7}, {2,5,8}, and {3,6,9}). Draw a path starting in the top-left corner cell and finishing in the bottom-right corner cell, visiting every 3×3 box at least once. In a single step, the path may move only east (→) or southwest (↙). Any three consecutive digits along the path must have three different remainders modulo 3. Box borders divide the path into segments; each segment is a renban, i.e. it must contain consecutive, non-repeating integers in any order.
2947: Normal sudoku rules apply. The cells in the grid are numbered from 1 to 81 in normal reading order ie 1 at the upper left, ..., 9 at the upper right until 81 at the bottom right. The digit in a cell with a square number is itself a square (1,4,9) while the digit in a cell with prime number is a prime (2,3,5,7). In addition, any vertical or horizontal straight line of three cells never contains a consecutive set of digits.
2948: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on a line between two circles must have values between the digits in those circles. Each circle digit must be consecutive with at least one digit on the line. For example, (2)-7-3-5-(8) is a valid fill for a Snug Between Line.
2949: Normal sudoku rules apply. The two digits on an arrow give the coordinates of a particular target cell somewhere in the grid. The digit on the arrow's shaft indicates the target cell's row, and the digit on the arrowhead indicates the target cell's column. The difference between the two digits should be placed into the target cell. No two arrows target the same cell. Also: A pink arrow contains two consecutive digits; a green arrow contains two digits with a difference of at least 5; and, on a black arrow, one digit is double the other.
2950: Normal sudoku rules apply. One cell in each row, column and region is a nullifier cell. Nullifier cells have a value of zero. In graves (cages), values must sum to the day, month or year of the date on the grave. Digits cannot repeat within graves. Escape the graveyard by carefully plotting an orthogonally connected path between the green and red cells. The path may not cross the highest or lowest values in a grave.
2951: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. Digits on a (slow) thermometer do not decrease from the bulb end. Adjacent digits on a green line differ by at least 5. A cage shows its sum. A purple line uses a set of consecutive digits in any order. Digits on an arrow sum to the digit in the connected circle. Digits separated by an X sum to 10. Digits separated by a V sum to 5.
2952: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage sum to the number given in its corner. Digits may not repeat within a cage. In any row or column, no more than two consecutive digits may have the same parity (i.e., be both odd or both even). Eg A sequence such as 2–4–5–7 is valid; but 2–4–6–3 is not valid, since three even digits appear consecutively.
2953: Normal sudoku rules apply. Box borders divide the blue line into segments whose values have an equal sum. Consecutive digits along the orange line have a difference of at least four. Consecutive digits along a green line have a difference of at least five. If cells are connected by a black dot, one is double the other. A cell with a gray circle contains an odd digit.
2954: Place the digits 1–9 exactly once in each row and each column. Shade some cells so that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected, all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected, and no 2×2 area is entirely shaded or entirely unshaded. Within each cage, the sum of the shaded digits equals the sum of the unshaded digits. Digits MAY repeat within a cage. The corner cells with grey diamonds contain the same digit.
2955: Normal sudoku rules apply. Nurikabe: Shade some cells such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected (water), but no 2x2 area is entirely shaded; groups of orthogonally connected unshaded cells form islands. An island may be of size 1. Every cell with a circle clue is unshaded, and each island contains exactly one circle cell. The digit in this circle cell gives the size of the island. Note that an island may occupy a full 2x2 area (unlike water). Digits may not repeat within an island. Every blue line must contain at least one shaded and at least one unshaded cell. Switching between shaded and unshaded cells divides each line into segments with the same sum. Different lines may have different sums. Digits may repeat on a line if allowed by other rules.
2956: In each NxN grid, place the digits 1-N once in every row, column and box; in the slanted 6x6 grid, digits should be entered only in the middle of cells. A digit may not appear in the same position in multiple 4x4 grids. Each arrow contains a 2-digit number, with the 10s digit on the shaft and the 1s digit on the head; the number on an arrow gives the sum of the first X digits seen in a straight line in the indicated direction, where X is the first digit seen. Arrows only see cells that contain digits, i.e. blank spaces, such as those not belonging to any grid, are not seen.
2957: Normal sudoku rules apply. Circle a digit in each row, column, and box. Each circled digit must be different. Shade some cells, such that within any row, column, or box, the number of shaded cells is equal to the circled digit. A digit in a diamond is not circled, and equals the sum of the circled digits in its row and column. Shaded digits within a cage sum to the value given in the top left of the cage.
2958: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is covered in fog. Placing correct digits reveals clues in the surrounding 3x3 area. The digits 1 to 9 appear once each on both blue diagonals. The digits along an arrow sum to either a single digit number in that arrow's circle or a two digit number (reading left-to-right) in that arrow's oval.
2959: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages sum to the small total given in the top left corner of the cage. A clue outside the grid gives the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. Within the grid, digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Grey lines are palindromes which read the same forwards and backwards. Digits separated by a white dot have a difference of one. Not all possible dots are given.
2960: Normal sudoku rules apply. Some cells contain ghosts. Not all ghosts are visible! Each ghost with the digit N is staring at another ghost with the digit N, exactly N diagonal steps away. A headstone shows the sum of the ghosts in its column. (For the avoidance of doubt, the eyes indicate the direction the visible ghosts are staring in!)
2961: Normal sudoku rules apply. The 3x3 boxes are numbered in normal reading order. Each digit matching its box number is an "inoculation site". Each row and column contains an inoculation site. They are infected. Infected cells infect every orthogonally adjacent cell with a smaller digit. Infections keep spreading until no infected cell has a smaller uninfected orthogonal neighbour. (Every infected cell can be traced back to one or more inoculation sites.) All uninfected cells form one orthogonally connected area. Each orthogonally connected group of infected cells touches the grid's edge. A digit in a blue circle is uninfected and counts the number of infected cells in its 8 surrounding cells. Green lines connect 2 infected digits that differ by 5 or more. Pink dots join consecutive uninfected digits.
2962: Normal sudoku rules apply. No domino in the grid can contain digits summing to 10. There is some fog in the grid; placing a correct digit might remove it. No guessing is required. Digits in a grey box cannot repeat. There are lines in the grid that connect boxes; the digits in a box are summed to arrive at a value. That value applies to the following rules: 1) Zipper: when box values equidistant from the centre box on a pink line are summed together, they are equal to the centre box's value on that line.
