3142: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits along an orange line have a difference of at least 4. Digits on an arrow sum to the digit in the circle of that arrow.
3143: Normal sudoku rules apply. Finkz and Phinx must both reach different cupcakes by finding a path through the maze. 3144: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grey region must contain each digit 1-9 exactly once. The digits on each arrow must sum to the digit in the attached circle.
3145: Normal sudoku rules apply. The 3x3 box borders divide the blue lines into segments with the same sum, but the sum may be different for different lines. 3146: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a pink line form a set of non-repeating consecutive digits in some order. A clue outside the grid indicates the digit which has to be placed in the Nth cell in the corresponding direction, where N is the digit placed in the first cell in that direction.
3147: Normal sudoku rules apply. Finkz and Phinx must both reach different cupcakes by finding a path through the maze. 3148: Place the digits 1-6 once each in every row, column and 2x3 box. Adjacent digits along a green line must differ by at least 3. Digits on an arrow sum to the number in the circle. Cells separated by a V sum to 5. On a black dot, one digit is double the other.
3149: Normal sudoku rules apply. There is one zombie cell in every row, column, and box. There are no duplicate numbers in the zombie cells. 3150: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a single knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. For all rules below: Do not duplicate any digit within a ruleset. 3151: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is covered in fog. Entering correct digits may clear fog. No guessing is required. There is one Eraser Cell in every row, column, and 3x3 box. Values along a thermometer increase from bulb to tip. Values in cells joined by a V sum to 5. Values in a cage may not repeat and sum to the total given in the cage’s top left cell. Digits MAY repeat in a cage. If two cells are joined by a green line the values in those cells must have a difference of at least 5.
3152: Normal sudoku rules apply. There are nine Middler cells in the grid, one in each row, column, and 3×3 box, each containing a different digit. The value of a Middler cell is 5, regardless of the digit in the cell. If two cells are joined by a green line, the values of those cells must have a difference of at least 5. Cells joined by a V have values that sum to 5. Cells joined by an X have values that sum to 10. Cells separated by a white dot contain consecutive values. The values along the gray line read the same forwards and backwards.
3153: Normal sudoku rules apply. Find nine Nudge cells in the grid, one in each row, column, and 3×3 box, each containing a different digit. 3154: Normal 6x6 sudoku rules apply. (Place the digits 1-6, once each, into every row, column and 2x3 rectangle). Each digit in a circle must appear in the surrounding 2x2 area. 3155: Normal sudoku rules apply. A white drop indicates how many digits in the indicated direction differ from it by 1. A black drop indicates how many digits in the indicated direction are double or half its value.
3156: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each pink line is a renban: it contains a set of consecutive digits (in any order). No two pink lines have the same digit sum.
3157: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages sum to the expression or value in the top left corner. X and Y are positive integers such that X is greater than Y. 3158: Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid provide the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. Digits may repeat along a diagonal if allowed by other rules. Digits in cages sum to the value in the top left corner. Digits along a golden palindrome line are read the same from either direction. In addition, the central digit on the line marked by a golden circle is the same as the digit on the ends of the line.
3159: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells with the same colour circle contain the same digit. Cells touched by a “Sum Dot” add to the indicated value. Digits may repeat within a dot if allowed by other rules.
3160: Numbers may not repeat within cages. Within the inner 5x5 grid: Place the digits 1 to 5 such that digits do not repeat in any row or column. Considering all rows and columns as 5-digit numbers read from the direction of the clue and ranked from lowest (1) to highest (20), a clue cell represents where in the ranking that row/column lies. (The clue cells are those with grey outlines orthogonally adjacent to the row/column they rank.) There are no ties in rank. Within the rest of the 15x17 grid: Divide the grid into regions, each consisting of orthogonally connected cells. Regions cannot overlap. Fill each cell with a number that is the size of the region. Regions of the same size cannot share a cell edge.
3161: Normal sudoku rules apply. All the 2x2 areas of the grid, when read in normal reading order, make a total of 64 four-digit numbers. Clues in the centre of a 2x2 area show its rank among those 64 numbers, where the lowest is 1 and the highest is 64. The two “X”s are the same number. One or more equal numbers are considered to be at rank N when there are N-1 numbers of strictly lower rank. (Eg, if there are three equal numbers which have 19 numbers lower than them then these three numbers would be rank 20 and the next rank will be 23, i.e. the ranks could go ⋯, 19, 20, 20, 20, 23, ⋯)
3162: Normal 9x9 Sudoku rules apply. Blockers: Digits in diamonds can never be used on a different clue type than the clue type the diamond lives on. Renban: Digits on a purple line form a set of consecutive digits in any order. Dutch Whispers: Two adjacent digits on an orange line must differ by at least 4. German Whispers: Two adjacent digits on a green line must differ by at least 5. Region Sum: The 3x3 box border divide blue lines into segments; each segment along an individual line must have the same sum.
3163: Normal sudoku rules apply. If two digits are separated by a black dot then one digit is double the other. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Not all dots are given. Deducing the digit in the highest visible checkpoint (marked with a green square and a number) will reveal new cells and potentially a new checkpoint. Each line follows the rules of one specific constraint type from the following list. It is up to the solver to determine which line belongs to which type. Each line constraint type may contain NO REPEATED DIGITS anywhere in the puzzle. At the start of the puzzle, all lines are Region Sum Lines (ie the 3x3 box borders divide the lines into segments; each segment along an individual line has the same sum). When a new checkpoint is revealed, remove the determined line types and all entered digits EXCEPT those on checkpoints. You are now allowed a new line constraint! Checkpoint 1: Additionally, the lines can now be German Whisper lines (Adjacent digits differ by at least 5) Checkpoint 2: Additionally, the lines can now be Parity lines (Digits alternate between odd and even digits) You have completed the puzzle when all 3 checkpoints are revealed and the complete grid is filled.
3164: Normal sudoku rules apply. Finkz and Phinx must both reach different cupcakes by finding a path through the maze. The paths must not visit any cell more than once, share cells, cross themselves or each other, or pass through any thick maze walls. As well as moving orthogonally, they may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. A purple arrow may only be passed through in the direction it's pointing. An arrow always points to the smaller of the two digits it sits between. If a redcurrant sits between two digits, one is odd and the other is even. In this experiment, any digit on Finkz' path indicates exactly how many times that digit appears on Finkz' path. The same rule applies separately for Phinx' path.
3165: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along every positive diagonal (ie from south-west to north-east) the difference between neighbouring digits is at least 2. Every green line contains only odd digits. The central 3x3 box is a magic square (ie each row, columns and 3-cell diagonal of this box must sum to the same total).
3166: Normal sudoku rules apply. The 3x3 box borders divide each blue line into segments; along an individual line each of those segments must have the same sum.
3167: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits along an orange line have a difference of at least four. The gray lines are palindromes, reading the same from both directions. Cells separated by an X sum to ten.
3168: Normal sudoku rules apply. Every 5 in the grid must have a 1 directly above it or a 9 directly below it. It may have both, but it doesn't need both. Each horizontal blonde line sums to a 2 digit number. These two digits are at the start and end of its row, in some order. Each vertical brunette line also sums to a 2 digit number. These two digits are at the top and bottom of its column, in some order.
3169: Normal sudoku rules apply. The sum of the digits inside the cage is equal to the small number in the cage’s top left corner. The sum of the digits along an arrow is equal to the digit in that arrow’s circle. Digits in cells separated by a white dot are consecutive.
3170: Normal sudoku rules apply. Finkz and Phinx must both reach the cupcakes by finding a path through the maze. The paths must not visit any cell more than once, cross themselves or each other, or pass through any thick maze walls. The paths may not share cells except for where they meet at the cupcake cell. As well as moving orthogonally, they may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. There is one booster cell in every row, column and box, and each contains a different digit. The value of a booster cell equals its digit, plus its row number, plus its column number. Eg: If r7c3 is a booster cell and contains a 6, it will have a value of 16 (7+3+6). If two cells are joined by a blackcurrant then the value of one is double the value of the other. The sum of the two values joined by a starfruit is always the same, and must be deduced. In this experiment, both rats visit the same number of cells, and the sequence of VALUES along both paths are identical. Eg: If the first five values visited by Finkz are 7, 4, 12, 3, 8 (in that order) then the same must be true for Phinx.
3171: Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected, all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected, and no 2x2 area is fully shaded or fully unshaded. A digit in a cell with an arrow counts the total number of shaded cells seen in the direction of the arrow (not counting the cell itself). For every 2x2 area in the puzzle, no two shaded cells can be from the same modulo 3 set. In other words, in any given 2x2 area, there can only be one shaded cell with a digit from [147], one from [258], and one from [369].
3172: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a single knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. The following constraints operate in this puzzle: 1) Cells connected by an X must sum to 10; 2) Cells connected by an V must sum to 5; 3) Digits in a cage sum to the small number in the cage's top-left corner; 4) Digits on an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow's circle; and 5) Digits on a thermometer must increase from the bulb end. Within any single constraint type listed above, digits may not repeat. (Eg If one caged cell contained a 1, no other caged cell anywhere in the puzzle can contain a 1.)
3173: Normal sudoku rules apply. 𝗗𝘆𝗻𝗮𝗺𝗶𝗰 𝗙𝗼𝗴 hides some clues. Placing a correct digit clears fog from its cell and possibly other cells. For each clue type listed below, there are three clues of that type in the grid which don't share cells. Two of them are correct, and one is incorrect ('lying'). For each clue type, all cells clued by that type (incl. the liar) contain different digits. 𝗖𝗹𝘂𝗲 𝗧𝘆𝗽𝗲𝘀: 1) 𝗖𝗮𝗴𝗲𝘀: Digits in a cage sum to the total in the top-left. 2) 𝗩: Each V joins two digits that sum to 5. 3) 𝗗𝗼𝘂𝗯𝗹𝗲 𝗔𝗿𝗿𝗼𝘄𝘀 (DA): If two circles in different cells are connected by a line, the sum in the circles is equal to the sum of the remaining (0+ cell) line. 4) 𝗔𝗿𝗿𝗼𝘄𝘀 (A): Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in the attached circle. 5) 𝗥𝗲𝗻𝗯𝗮𝗻 (R): Digits on a hollow line form a single consecutive sequence (like 234) in any order. 6) If two digits are joined by a black dot then one is double the other.
3174: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage cannot repeat. Some cages show their sum. A number outside the grid shows the sum of the cells on the indicated diagonal. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Cells separated by a (chess) king's move cannot contain the same digit.
3175: Normal sudoku rules apply. On a white dot, digits are consecutive; on a black dot, one is double the other. Digits in cells separated by an X sum to 10, digits separated by a V sum to 5. Digits in a cage sum to the value in the corner of the cage.
3176: Normal 6x6 sudoku rules apply. Digits may not repeat in a cage. Numbered Rooms: All outside cells on a clue must contain a digit. That digit must also appear in the Nth position looking into the grid in that row/column, where N is the digit in the first position.
3177: Normal sudoku rules apply. Finkz and Phinx must both reach different cupcakes by finding a path through the maze. The paths must not visit any cell more than once, share cells, cross themselves or each other, or pass through any thick maze walls. As well as moving orthogonally, they may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. If a blackcurrant sits between two digits, one is double the other. If a redcurrant sits between two digits, one is odd and the other is even. Entering a yellow teleport will cause a rat to be instantly transported to the other yellow teleport. The teleports have identical digits. The digit on a pink motion sensor indicates the number of cells that are visited (by either rat) within the (up to 9) cells immediately surrounding the sensor. The sensor itself is counted, if visited. In this experiment, for any row or column, the digits visited by Finkz must have the same sum as the digits visited by Phinx. 3178: Normal sudoku rules apply. Colour each cell in the grid one of two colours such that: Each colour forms a single orthogonally connected region; and no 2×2 block of cells is entirely one colour. The digits along each line sum to the same total (which must be deduced). Along each line, the colouring separates odd and even digits; that is, all odd digits on a line are one colour and all even digits are the other colour. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive.
3179: Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a single loop that travels orthogonally and passes through the centers of cells. The loop may go straight through a cell or turn within a cell, but it cannot branch or cross itself. Adjacent digits along the loop differ by at least 5. A digit in a circle indicates how many of the four surrounding cells contain turns of the loop. The digit also indicates that at least one of those four surrounding cells contains that digit.
3180: Place the digits 1-6 once each in every row and column. Every cell has exactly two orthogonal neighbours that differ from it by at least 3. On the grey line, one cell is the sum of the other two.
3181: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage sum to the number in the top left corner of the cage.
3182: Normal sudoku rules apply. The blue "R" is split by a box border into two segments whose digits have the same sum. Each pair of adjacent digits on the red "A" must contain one odd and one even digit. Each pair of adjacent digits on the green "H" must have a difference of at least 5. A digit on a Fibreglass Acoustic Diffuser (mushroom) shows how many times that digit appears on Fibreglass Acoustic Diffusers. For each Fibreglass Acoustic Diffuser, digits may not echo (repeat) in the up to 4 orthogonally adjacent cells.
3183: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each cell in the grid belongs to exactly one terrain: Either island (green) or water (blue). All water cells in the grid must form one orthogonally connected region. Each 2x2 region in the grid contains at least one cell from each terrain. Each island contains exactly one clue, which equals the product of the size of the island (i.e. the number of cells that belong to this island) and the sum of the digits in all cells belonging to this island. Digits within an island do not repeat. Islands are not allowed to touch each other (neither orthogonally nor diagonally). A digit in a circle equals the size of the island. Not all possible circles are given.
3184: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a single knight’s move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. The digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow’s circle. Digits do not repeat along gold “Nabner” lines. Additionally, no pair of digits anywhere on a Nabner line can be consecutive. Digits along each magenta line must be a set of non-repeating consecutive digits – these digits can appear in any order.
3185: Normal sudoku rules apply. Finkz and Phinx must both reach cupcakes by finding a path through the maze. The paths must not visit any cell more than once, share cells, or pass through any thick maze walls. No diagonal moves are possible in this maze. If two digits are joined by a blackcurrant, one is double the other. If two digits are joined by a redcurrant, one is odd and the other is even. If two digits are joined by a goldenberry, they are non-consecutive. If two digits are joined by a grape, they have a difference of at least 5. A digit on a motion sensor indicates exactly how many cells in the (up to 9) surrounding cells are visited by a rat. In this experiment, some clues are fake! (A fake clue breaks its rule in the list above.) All clues that Phinx passes through are fake. All other clues are truthful (ie; those passed through by Finkz, and those unvisited by either rat.) It is to be determined which rat is which.
3186: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits are grouped into entropic sets: Low → {1, 2, 3}; Mid → {4, 5, 6}; High→ {7, 8, 9}. A digit placed in a circle indicates the size of the orthogonally connected group of cells that all contain digits from the same entropic set as that digit. No region contains more than one circled cell. Not all regions contain a circle. Digits separated by a white dot must be consecutive. If two digits are separated by a black dot then one digit is double the other.
3187: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits on any pentomino must differ in value by at least 5.
3188: Normal sudoku rules apply. Black dots separate cells with a 1:2 ratio. Not all dots are given. Cells a knight's move or a king's move apart must be different. Orthogonally adjacent cells cannot be consecutive.
3189: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a single move of a chess king must contain different digits. In a cage, digits may not repeat and sum to the total in the top left corner (if given). On a green line, adjacent digits differ by at least 5. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. If two digits are separated by a black dot, one is twice the other. Not all dots are necessarily given.
3190: Normal Sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits on a green German Whisper line differ by at least 5. Digits on a pink Renban line form a consecutive set with no repeats. The central cross is a single line. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Where digits are separated by a black dot, one is double the other. Not all dots are given (no negative constraint).
3191: Normal sudoku rules apply. On an orange Dutch Whisper line adjacent digits differ by at least 4. The digits on a pink Renban line form a consecutive set with no repeats. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Where digits are separated by a black dot, one is double the other. (Not all possible dots are necessarily given.)
3192: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits on a green German Whisper line differ by at least 5. The digits on a pink Renban line form a consecutive set with no repeats.; The central cross is a single line. If two digits are separated by a black dot, one is double the other. Two digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Not all dots are given.
3193: Normal 6x6 Sudoku rules apply. Digits may not repeat in cages. Skyscrapers: All outside cells in a cage must contain a digit. That digit counts how many digits are 'seen' looking into the grid in that row/column. Digits are visible when they are larger than all digits before them.
3194: Normal sudoku rules apply. AIM OF EXPERIMENT: Finkz and Phinx must both reach different cupcakes by finding a path through the maze. The paths must not visit any cell more than once, share cells, or pass through any thick maze walls. HOT AND COLD ZONES: Divide the grid into two zones of orthogonally connected cells, one hot and the other cold. No 2x2 area may be completely in one zone. INVISIBLE WALLS: A few maze walls are visible, but the rest are invisible and must be located. If two orthogonally adjacent cells are in different zones, a wall exists between them. If they are in the same zone, no wall exists between them. Because no 2x2 spaces exist fully within one zone, no diagonal movements are possible in this maze. BOX BALANCE: • The value of a hot cell equals its digit +1. • The value of a cold cell equals its digit -1. • In each 3x3 box, the total value of hot cells must equal the total value of cold cells. CURRANTS: • If a BLACKCURRANT sits between two cells, then the value of one is double the value of the other. • If a REDCURRANT sits between two cells, then one has an odd value and the other has an even value. • Two cells joined by a currant are both in the same zone. TEST CONSTRAINT: In this experiment, Phinx must stay in the hot zone and Finkz must stay in the cold zone.
3195: Fill each row, column, and box with the digits 0-6 once each. Exactly one cell in each row, column, and box is a "Schrödinger's cell," which contains two digits. Two Schrödinger's cells cannot contain the same pair of digits. A cell's value is equal to the sum of its digits. For final solution check purposes, if a cell's value is from 0-9, enter the digit equal to its value; otherwise, the cell may be left empty (in-progress solution-checking doesn't work properly in this puzzle). Cells with red squares are index cells. If an index cell in column X has a value of Y, then the cell in column Y in the same row has a value of X (e.g. if r3c1 has a value of 5, then r3c5 has a value of 1). An index cell may contain two digits, but may not have a value greater than 6. If an index cell has a value of zero, the value being indexed does not appear in the row. Nothing in these rules prevents a value from repeating in a row, even if one instance of that value is referenced by an index cell. The sum of the values along an arrow is equal to the value in the connected circle.
3196: Normal sudoku rules apply. Any sequence of five cells along the long purple lines must contain a run of five consecutive digits in any order without repeats. Lines shorter than five cells must contain a run of consecutive digits in any order without repeats.
3197: Normal sudoku rules apply. Yin Yang: Shade some cells such that i) all shaded cells are orthogonally connected; ii) all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected; and iii) every 2x2 contains both shaded and unshaded cells. Yin Yang Split Lines: Yin Yang borders split lines into 2 or more segments with the same sum. (If 2 cells are adjacent along the line, they are in the same segment if and only if they have the same shading). Digits may not repeat within a segment. Every line contains shaded and unshaded cells. Segment Counters: A digit in a circle on a line indicates how many total segments that line has.
3198: Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a single 1-cell-wide loop of orthogonally connected cells into the grid that does not branch or enter any cell more than once. The loop must pass through all given dots, and all given dots must be in the middle of a straight loop segment (i.e., the distance from a dot to the next turn along the loop must be identical in both directions). Digits separated by a grey dot are consecutive or one is double the other. Adjacent digits on the loop not separated by a dot must NOT be consecutive or where one is double the other.
3199: Normal sudoku rules apply. MODULAR ARROWS: A digit on an arrow counts how many cells in the indicated direction have the same remainder mod-3 as itself, including itself. (Eg a 4 on an arrow would indicate that exactly four digits (including the 4 itself) in that direction were selected from the digits 1, 4 & 7 (because each of 1,4 & 7 have the same remainder (ie 1) when divided by 3).
3200: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each letter from ABCDEFGHZ stands for a different digit from 1-9. Each labeled gray letter cell in the grid contains that digit. Where a ? is used, it always represents a two digit total. Ie the leading question mark is never 0. Digits in cages sum to the total given. Digits cannot repeat within cages. Digits along indicated diagonals have the indicated sum. Digits may repeat along such diagonals. Circles within the grid are quadruples. The indicated digit appears in at least one of the four surrounding cells. Digits with a door are numbered rooms. The indicated digit appears a number of cells into that row or column given by the first number in that row/column. Digits with a building are skyscrapers. They indicate how many digits are seen from the perspective of the clue if digits are only seen if they are the highest digit encountered so far.
3201: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells are either 'sea' or 'land'. No 2x2 block is filled with just sea or land. All sea cells are connected orthogonally. Cells with arrows are dead ends, that is, sea cells that point to the only other sea cell they touch. Land cells form 'islands' that don't touch each other, even diagonally, comprising four orthogonally adjacent, different digits, summing to 14. On an X, the two digits sum to 10, and on a red dot, they sum to 12. All arrows, X's, and red dots are shown. On an X, the two cells are both sea or both land.
3202: Normal sudoku rules apply. Finkz and Phinx must both reach different cupcakes by finding a path through the maze. The paths must not visit any cell more than once, cross themselves or each other, share cells, or pass through any thick maze walls. As well as moving orthogonally, they may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. If a blackcurrant sits between two digits, one is double the other. If a redcurrant sits between two digits, one is odd and the other is even. If a grape sits between two digits, they have a difference of at least 5. The digit on a grey camera indicates the total SUM of the digits in any visited cells that the camera's lens points towards (before a wall is reached, which blocks vision.) A video camera cell itself may not be entered. In this experiment, all of the low digits in the grid (1s, 2s and 3s) must be visited, but none of the high digits (7s, 8s, and 9s) may be visited. The two rats' paths must be perfect reflections of each other across the positive diagonal (marked with a thin pink line).
3203: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits a king's move, as in chess, away must be different. Adjacent digits on a green line differ by at least 5. Purple lines contain a set of distinct consecutive digits in any order. Black dots indicate some places where one digit is double the other, white dots indicate consecutive digits.
3204: Normal sudoku rules apply. Two adjacent digits on a purple line must have consecutive values. Two cells separated by a single knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit.
3205: Normal sudoku rules apply. The 3x3 box borders divide blue lines into segments with the same sum. Different lines may have different sums. An inequality sign points to the lower of the two digits it sits between.
3206: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a pink line must form a non-repeating group of consecutive digits, but they may appear in any order along the line. Using red, green, and blue, colour all circles such that: Orthogonally adjacent circles are different colours; and the digit inside a circle appears that many times in circles of that colour.
3207: Normal sudoku rules apply. The 3x3 box borders divide each blue line into segments; each segment along an individual line must have the same sum.
3208: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along each line, the hexagon is referred to as 'position 1', the next cell along is 'position 2' and so on. Digits never repeat along a line. PURPLE LINES are thermos. Digits along thermos always increase as you move away from the hexagon. Eg: 24579 would be a valid thermo. TURQUOISE LINES are index lines. On an index line, the digit in the Nth position indicates the position along the line where the digit N appears. Eg: 32154 would be a valid index line. The 3 in the 1st position indicates there is a 1 in the 3rd position, and so on. LIGHT BROWN LINES are hitlines. Digits can be in any order on a hitline, but the digit in the hexagon indicates how many digits along the hitline match their position number. Eg: A hitline might read 27315. The 2 on the hexagon indicates that exactly two digits match their position number; in this case, 3 in the 3rd position and 5 in the 5th position. SHENANIGANS: One of the digits 1-9 (to be determined) is the 'mischief digit.' Every line follows one (AND ONLY ONE) of the three line rules above, but any line containing the mischief digit has been painted the wrong colour. (Any line NOT containing the mischief digit is the correct colour.)
3209: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells along a pink line form a set of consecutive, non-repeating values in any order. A black dot separates two cells where one is double the value of the other. Place Werewolf cells into the grid so that there is exactly one Werewolf cell in each row, column and box; each Werewolf cell must contain the digit that matches its Box number (counted from left-to-right, top-to-bottom); the value of a Werewolf cell is unique from other Werewolf cells and is selected from the remaining digits within its box (e.g. if the digit 1 in Box 1 has a value of 4, the digit 2 in Box 2 could have neither a value of 2 nor 4).
3210: Normal sudoku rules apply. AIM OF EXPERIMENT: Finkz and Phinx must both reach different cupcakes by finding a path through the maze. The paths must not visit any cell more than once, cross themselves or each other, share cells, or pass through any thick maze walls. As well as moving orthogonally, they may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. BLACKCURRANTS: If two digits are joined by a blackcurrant, one is double the other. REDCURRANTS: If two digits are joined by a redcurrant, one is odd and the other is even. TELEPORTS: Entering a teleport will cause a rat to be instantly transported to the matching coloured teleport. Matching teleports always have identical digits, but teleports that don't match always have different digits. TEST CONSTRAINT: In this experiment, for any path segment connecting two teleports, no other cells along the segment may equal either of the two teleport digits at its ends, or lie numerically between them. Eg: if a path segment joins two teleports with the digits 3 and 6, then the other digits along this path segment may not include a 3, 4, 5 or 6.
3211: Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid indicate the sum of the first X digits, where X is the first seen digit. A and B represent two numbers to be determined by the solver. Any three adjacent digits along a teal modular line have different residues modulo 3 (i.e. one digit from {1,4,7}, one from {2,5,8}, and one from {3,6,9}).
3212: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits cannot repeat on the thin blue main diagonal. Cells that appear in the same relative position of their 3x3 box may not contain the same digit. So, for example, r5c1 (the middle left cell of its 3x3 box) could not contain the same digit as r8c7 (the middle left cell of its 3x3 box.) Digits in a cage sum to the small clue in the cage’s top left corner. Digits on a pink line form a set of non-repeating, consecutive digits in any order. The 3x3 box borders divide the thick blue lines into segments; each segment along an individual line must have the same sum.
3213: Place a digit from 1-9 in each cell of the main 7x7 grid. Digits may not repeat in a row, column or 3x3 box of this grid. The grid contains nine 3x3 boxes, which overlap at the dashed lines. Clues in pills refer to the digits missing from the associated row or column, but pills do not need to be filled. Thick purple pills are X-sum clues, i.e. the digits missing from that row or column can form a 2-digit number, which is the sum of the first X digits from the direction of the pill, where X is the first digit seen. The digits missing from a row with a pill containing a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio (ie one is double the other); The digits missing from a row with a pill containing a white dot are consecutive; The digits missing from a column with a pill containing an X sum to 10.
3214: Normal sudoku rules apply. There's a one-cell wide 'river' of orthogonally-connected cells snaking from R9C9 to R1C2 without branching or touching itself orthogonally (but it may touch diagonally). Digits along the 'river' differ by at least 5. All remaining cells are 'land'. 'Bridges' (=) only cross single 'river' cells, and are the sum of the two 'land' cells at each end of the 'bridge' (e.g. if the river cell was a 5, the two land cells could be 2&3 or 1&4). Diagonal 'bridges' only cross 'river' corners. Placing a correct digit will clear fog in its cell, and may also clear fog in other cells.
3215: Normal sudoku rules apply. Any sequence of four cells along the thinner purple lines must contain a run of four consecutive digits in any order without repeats. The thicker red line contains a set of consecutive digits in any order. Cells separated by an X sum to ten. Cells separated by a V sum to five.
3216: Normal sudoku rules apply. If the digit N appears in any of the four cells adjacent to a circle then it appears exactly N times adjacent to a circle across the grid. The 3x3 box borders divide blue lines into segments; each segment along an individual line has the same sum. Adjacent digits on red lines alternate between odd and even. Adjacent digits on green lines differ by at least 5. Digits on a pink line form a non-repeating consecutive set in any order.
3217: Normal sudoku rules apply. The sum of the digits along a 'double arrow' line is equal to the sum of the digits in the attached circles. Digits do not repeat along the marked diagonals.
3218: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a single knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. Along a thermometer digits must increase from the bulb end. Each purple line contains a set of non-repeating, consecutive digits in any order.
3219: Normal sudoku rules apply. Fog will clear when neighboring digits are filled in. Neighboring digits along the grey line must have a difference of at least 5. Digits separated by an X sum to 10. Digits separated by a V sum to 5. Each letter (except X and V) corresponds to a unique digit. A cell with a letter in it contains its corresponding digit.
3220: SOMEDOKU: Fill the grid with the digits 1-9 so that each row N and column N contain exactly N distinct digits, with the rest of the cells in that row / column being repeats. For example, only 3 distinct digits appear in row 3, and any of these can be repeated multiple times in order to fill the row. AIM OF EXPERIMENT: Finkz and Phinx must both reach the cupcakes by finding a path through the maze. The paths must not visit any cell more than once, cross themselves or each other, or pass through any thick maze walls. The paths may only intersect at the cupcake cell. As well as moving orthogonally, they may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. BLACKCURRANTS: If a blackcurrant sits between two digits, one is double the other. REDCURRANTS: If a redcurrant sits between two digits, one is odd and the other is even. GRAPES: If a grape sits between two digits, they have a difference of at least 5. CAGES: Digits may not repeat within a cage. Each cage has the same total, to be deduced. If the digit on a cage's electricity symbol is 5 or higher, the cage may not be entered. TEST CONSTRAINT: In this experiment, both rats visit the same number of cells. Any pair of cells (one on each path) that are an equal distance from the cupcake cell sum to the digit on the cupcake cell. Thus, both paths combined form a valid 'zipper' line, with Finkz and Phinx at the ends and the cupcake cell in the middle.
3221: Normal sudoku rules apply. All arrows act as both modular arrows and entropic arrows. A digit on a modular arrow counts how many cells in the indicated direction have the same remainder mod-3 as itself, including itself. A digit on an entropic arrow counts how many cells in the indicated direction are in the same entropic group (123, 456, 789) as itself, including itself.
3222: Normal sudoku rules apply. Lines in the puzzle act as both Zipper lines and Nabner lines. Ie On these lines, digits at equal distance from the lavender central cell must sum to the digit in that central cell. Additionally, along each gold Nabner line, no two digits may be consecutive, and digits do not repeat along the line.
3223: Normal sudoku rules apply. Yin Yang Doublers: Shade some cells in the grid such that all shaded cells are orthoganally connected and all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected. No 2x2 may be all shaded or all unshaded. A shaded cell has a value equal to twice its digit. An unshaded cell has a value equal to twice its digit minus one (double the digit first, then subtract one). Uniqueness: On each of the constraints below, values do not repeat anywhere in the puzzle. For example, if there is a shaded 5 (value 10) on a renban, shaded 5 can't appear anywhere else on a renban, but unshaded 5 could because it has a value of 9. Renban: Values on a purple line form a set of consecutive numbers with no repeats. Arrows: Values along an arrow sum the value in that arrow's circle. X: Two cells joined by an X have values that sum to 10. Black Dots: Two cells joined by a black dot have values where one is double the other.
3224: Normal 6x6 sudoku rules apply. Digits on the slow thermo may not decrease starting at the bulb. Outside clues on the slow thermo must contain a digit, and that digit indicates the length of the first ascending sequence in that direction. For example, a row with 142536 gives a left clue of 2 (1, 4) and a right clue of 1 (6). ie a sequence can be only one cell.
3225: Every gold circle contains a different digit. In any row or column, its circle indicates the number of distinct digits that appears in that row or column. Any of these digits can be repeated any number of times in order to fill the row / column. Eg: one particular row has a circle containing a 3, meaning that row only contains three distinct digits - a valid example would be 173777131. Entering a correct digit may clear fog somewhere in the grid. No guessing is necessary. Along a lavender line, digits that are the same distance from the central spot sum to the digit on that central spot. Adjacent digits along a green line have a difference of at least 5. If a red dot sits between two digits, one is odd and the other is even. If a black dot sits between two digits, one is double the other.
3226: Normal sudoku rules apply. Within cages, digits cannot repeat. Each cage has a value equal to the sum of all the digits it contains. Color each cage 1 of 4 colors. Cages of the same color cannot share sides, though they may touch corner-to-corner. All cages with the same color have sums whose prime factorizations contain the same set of prime factors. [E.g. If a red cage is 20 = 2x2x5, then all other red cages must have a prime factorization of 2^X*5^Y. For example, 10, 20, 40, 50, 80, 100, etc could all be valid. 25 would not be valid (no 2's). 30 would not be valid (2x3x5 has a 3). Any other colored cage could not have a 2 nor 5 in its prime factorizations.]
3227: Normal sudoku rules apply (ie place the digits 1-9, once each, in every row, column, and 3x3 box). In cages, digits do not repeat and sum to a value that must be deduced. Each cage shares a side with exactly one other cage with the same sum.
3228: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells that are orthogonally adjacent cannot contain consecutive digits. Digits on a grey line read the same forwards and backwards. Correctly placing the first digits in the grid will reveal the hidden cell in the Eye of the Storm.
3229: Normal sudoku rules apply. A pink line contains a set of consecutive, non-repeating digits, in any order. A number outside the grid indicates the sum of all the digits sandwiched between the 1 and 9 in that row or column.
3230: Normal sudoku rules apply. A solid pink line contains an unordered set of consecutive digits, without repeats. A hollow green line’s adjacent cells have a minimum difference of 5. A dashed blue line is divided by 3x3 box borders into segments with equal sums. On a black dot, one digit is double the other. On a white dot, the digits are consecutive.
3231: Normal sudoku rules apply. The product of the digits along a hollow orange line is equal to 300. Every set of three sequential digits along a teal modular line contains digits with three different remainders when divided by 3. (I.e. one digit from {1,4,7}, one from {2,5,8}, and one from {3,6,9}). Additionally, the total sum of the modular lines is equal to 300.
3232: Normal sudoku rules apply. Arrows indicate the direction in which the first three digits in that row or column (nearest the arrow) increase or decrease. For instance, r7c1 is less than r7c2 which is less than r7c3. If no arrow appears adjacent to a row or column, the three nearest digits must not be in increasing or decreasing order (that is, the central digit must be the highest or lowest).
3233: For the final preliminary 'free-roam' trial, the nine shortlisted rats were placed in a 9x9 space, and their movements were observed and recorded. Each of the digits 1-9 appeared in each row and column. OBSERVATIONS: Every cell in the grid was visited, exactly once; No rat's path contained any repeated digits; No rat chose to move diagonally at any point; Every 2x2 area was visited by at least 2 rats; No two rats started on the same digit; No two rats ended on the same digit; All blackcurrants and redcurrants were eaten; and No grapes were eaten. If a blackcurrant sits between two digits, one is double the other. If a redcurrant sits between two digits, one is odd and the other is even. If a grape sits between two digits, they have a difference of at least 5.
3234: Sudoku: Fill all rows, columns and marked 3x3 boxes with the digits 1-9 without any repeats. Chaos Construction: Divide the grid into 9 additional regions of 9 orthogonally connected cells. Each extra region contains the digits 1-9 without repeats. Circles: A digit in a circle indicates how many cells (including itself) overlap between its 3x3 box and its additional region.
3235: Normal sudoku rules apply (ie place the digits 1-9, once each, in every row, column and 3x3 box.) Digits in a cage do not repeat and sum to the number given in its upper left corner. Cells surrounding a white circle must contain at least one copy of the digits within the circle.
3236: Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a 1-cell wide loop in the grid, passing through the centres of some orthogonally adjacent cells. The loop does not touch itself, not even diagonally. A digit on the loop indicates how many times that digit appears on the loop. A digit in a cell containing an arrow counts how many loop cells are in the indicated direction (not including the cell with the arrow). Multiple arrows in the same cell count loop cells independent of one another (so if r6c4 is a 3 then there are three loop cells to its north and three loop cells to its north east).
3237: Oskode says: I placed a bunch of constraints in my puzzle but I was stupid enough to use the same colors for similar looking constraints... Can you help me check if the puzzle is still solvable? I know that: Normal sudoku rules apply. One cage sums to 15; the other one is a Look-and-say cage, that says it has “one 5”. One of the orange dots joins consecutive digits; the other joins digits with a 1:2 ratio. One of the Y's joins two digits that sum to 5; the other joins two digits that sum to 10. Along one of the blue diagonals digits may not repeat; box borders divide the other one into segments with the same sum. One red line contains a sequence of digits, in any order; along the other one adjacent digits have a difference of at least 5. Along one of the lines connected to the grey bulb digits increase from the bulb; along the other the digits sum to the digit in the bulb. One orientation of the grey triangles (pointing up/down) contains even digits; the other orientation contains odd digits. One dark blue line reads the same in both directions; along the other each three digits include one from {147}, one from {258}, one from {369}. On one green line digits on the line must be between the number in circles; on the other digits on the line sum to the total of the two circles.
3238: Normal sudoku rules apply. A letter indicates the same whole number whenever it appears (eg the letter B could represent the number 10 throughout the puzzle); and each letter represents a different number. Digits in a cage sum to the total in the cage’s upper left corner. Red numbers outside the grid indicate the sum of all digits along the indicated diagonal. Black numbers outside the grid indicate the sum of the first N digits in that row or column (counting from the direction of the clue), where N is the digit in the first cell in that row or column (closest to the clue.)
3239: Normal sudoku rules apply. Placing a correct digit may clear fog somewhere in the grid – no guessing is required. The digits along a purple line contain consecutive digits in any order without repeats. Each purple line is in the shape of a square. Similarly, the digits along a grey line contain consecutive digits in any order without repeats. Each grey line is also in the shape of a square. Cells separated by an X sum to 10 and, in cells separated by a black dot, one digit is double the other.
3240: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along SLOW thermometers, digits either stay the same or they increase as they move away from the bulb. Along green lines, adjacent digits differ by at least 5.
3241: Fill the grid with the digits 1-9 so that digits don't repeat in any row, column or box. Each row contains a 6-digit number reading forwards and another reading backwards. Each column contains a 6-digit number reading downwards, and another reading upwards. These 24 numbers are ranked from 1-24, from lowest to highest. There are no tied ranks, so none of the numbers are the same. A purple circle contains the rank of the 6-digit number it points at (reading in the direction the arrow is pointing.) If two digits are joined by a black dot, one is double the other. If two digits are joined by a red dot, one is odd and the other is even. If two digits are joined by a yellow dot, they are NOT consecutive.
3242: Normal sudoku rules apply. The difference between the sums of two linked sausages on a chain must be exactly equal to the number of sausages in that chain.
3243: Normal sudoku rules apply. The values of the digits along a line must lie between the two values of the circles at either end of that line.
3244: Normal sudoku rules apply. The 3x3 box borders divide each blue line into segments; each segment along an individual line must have the same sum.
3245: Fill the grid with the digits 1-9, so that in each row and column, one of the digits 1-9 is missing, and one of the digits is repeated. Every digit from 1-9 is missing from exactly one row and one column, and repeated in exactly one row and one column. Use the orange arrows to keep track of missing digits, and the blue arrows to keep track of repeated digits. Finkz and Phinx must both reach different cupcakes by finding a path through the maze. The paths must not visit any cell more than once, share cells, cross themselves or each other, or pass through any thick maze walls. As well as moving orthogonally, they may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. A red X may not be passed through, and sits between two digits that sum to 10. If a blackcurrant sits between two digits, one is double the other. If a redcurrant sits between two digits, one is odd and the other is even. If a grape sits between two digits, they have a difference of at least 5. If a goldenberry sits between two digits, they are not consecutive (or the same.) In this experiment, a rat's path is divided into segments by any fruit she eats. The digits on each segment have the same sum, to be determined. This 'segment sum' may be different for Finkz and Phinx.
3246: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage may not repeat and sum to the two-digit number in the two left-most cells in the top row of that cage.
3247: Normal sudoku rules apply. Nine copycat cells exist in the grid. They all contain the same digit (to be deduced), but they all have a different value. You can use the circles at the bottom to keep track. The value of a copycat cell equals the digit in the cell that is 180° rotationally opposite itself. Eg: If r1c3 is a copycat cell, then its value equals the digit in r9c7. For two adjacent values along a grey line, one can always be divided by the other to give an exact integer - ie; one is a multiple of the other. If a black dot sits between two cells, the value of one is double the value of the other. If a yellow dot sits between two cells, their values are not consecutive or the same.
3248: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along each length-3 line, the digits ascend from one end of the line to the other. In every 3x3 box, the digits in every horizontal or vertical threesome are never consecutive in some order.
3249: Normal sudoku rules apply. A clue outside the grid gives the sum the digits between the 1 and 9 in that row/column. Cells separated by a white dot are consecutive. On a black dot, one digit is double the other. Adjacent digits along a green line differ by at least 5. Adjacent digits along a red line include one odd and one even. Digits in a cage sum to the total given. The grey line reads the same in both directions.
3250: Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells so that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected, and all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected. No 2x2 area may be completely shaded or unshaded. The shading splits the line into segments with equal sums. Digits may not repeat within a segment.
3251: Normal sudoku rules apply. On each line the sum of the odd digits equals the sum of the even digits. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. The digit in the grey square must be even.
3252: Normal sudoku rules apply. Within a cage, digits must not repeat and they sum to the small number in the top left corner.
3253: Normal 6×6 sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the two-digit number shown in the attached pill (read left to right in base 10).
3254: Normal sudoku rules apply. In every row, column, and 3x3 box, one cell has a value of ten. These cells form a complete set of the digits from 1 to 9. The sum of the values in each cage is unique.
3255: Normal sudoku rules apply. Finkz and Phinx must both reach different cupcakes by finding a path through the maze. The paths must not visit any cell more than once, cross themselves or each other, or pass through any thick maze walls. There is no space to move diagonally in this maze. If two digits are joined by a blackcurrant, one is double the other. A purple arrow always points to the smaller of the two digits it sits between, and may only be passed through in the direction it's pointing. In this experiment, any two digits visited adjacently along a path must be different parities (one is odd and the other is even), and also have a difference of at least 5.
3256: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each arrow indicates that the sum of the odd digits must equal the sum of the even digits in the first x cells seen in the direction of the arrow where x is the digit in the cell next to the clue.
3257: Place the digits 1-6 once each in every row, column, and irregular region. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits between the 1 and 6 in that row or column. If two digits are either side of a V, the V ‘points’ to the smaller digit.
3258: Place the digits 1-6 once each in every row, column, and irregular region. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the first X digits in that clues row or column, where X is the digit in the cell next to the clue.
3259: Normal sudoku rules apply. Finkz and Phinx must both reach different cupcakes by finding a path through the maze. The paths must not visit any cell more than once, share cells, cross themselves or each other, or pass through any thick maze walls. As well as moving orthogonally, they may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. Much of the grid is obscured by fog. Entering correct digits may clear fog somewhere in the grid. No guessing is necessary. If a blackcurrant sits between two digits, one is double the other. If a grape sits between two digits, they have a difference of at least 5. If a starfruit sits between two digits, they always have the same sum, to be determined. Every coloured circular button must be visited. The digit on a button indicates the number of cells that the rat moves after the button to arrive in a different 3x3 box. (Eg: if the rat moves immediately from the button into a new 3x3 box, the button would contain a 1.) A digit on a path may not be consecutive with the digit visited immediately before it.
3260: Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is partially covered in fog. Placing correct digits will clear the fog from the surrounding area. Shade all cells either brown (chocolate) or yellow (banana) such that all chocolate areas are rectangular, and no banana areas are rectangular. All lines move orthogonally and end in circles on either end. Lines do not cross, branch, or share cells. Circles may be contained in either chocolate or banana cells. Circles indicate the size of the area in which they are contained. The digit in a circled cell with a line attached also gives the number of cells of the same shading as the circled cell along the line, including the endpoints. Digits along a line must sum to a two-digit number, where the 'tens' digit is in one circle and the 'ones' digit is in the other. Cells separated by an X sum to 10. Cells separated by a V sum to 5.
3261: Normal sudoku rules apply. Box borders divide each blue line into segments with the same sum. Digits in a circle must appear at least once in the surrounding four cells.
3262: Normal sudoku rules apply. The 3x3 box borders divide the blue lines into segments; each segment along an individual line must have the same sum.
3263: Normal sudoku rules apply. Anti-giraffe: cells (1,4) apart cannot contain the same digit. (eg the digit in r1c5 cannot appear in r2c1/r2c9/r5c4/r5c6.) Cells joined by black dots contain digits in a 1:2 ratio (ie one digit will be double the other); cells joined by a white dot contain consecutive digits. Along a thermometer, digits increase from the bulb end. The digits in the black cage sum to 12. The blue cages contain the same pair of digits.
3264: Place a digit from 0-8 in each cell such that no digit is repeated in any row, column or 3x3 box. 5x5 Latin Square: The digits in red circles are all from the same set of five of the numbers from 0-8 (which five are to be determined). None of these repeat in any of the diagonal lines of red circles. Each diagonal of the 5x5 latin square can be read as a 5-digit number and the 20 resulting numbers (each line is read from both directions) can be ranked in numerical order. The position in the rank (lowest is 1, highest is 20) of some of the diagonals are given by the blue cages attached to that diagonal. N.B. Two-digit numbers are read from left to right and do not start with 0. There are no tied ranks in this puzzle. The two digits separated by the white dot differ by 1.
3265: Normal sudoku rules apply. Orange lines are both index lines and entropic lines. Index lines: starting with the diamond at position 1, the digit at position N along the line indicates the position of the digit N on the line. Entropic lines: every set of 3 consecutive digits along the line contain one low digit (1,2,3), one medium digit (4,5,6) and one high digit (7,8,9). The arrow points to the smaller of the digits in the cells it occupies.
3266: Normal sudoku rules apply. The sum of the digits inside a gold cage (which may repeat) equals the sum of the digits in the cells outside which share an edge with cells inside.
3267: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each question mark acts as a stand-in for a digit, which must be deduced for each question mark. Each circle contains 2 digits. The 2 digits must appear in at least one of the four cells surrounding that circle (if a digit repeats in a circle, it must appear twice). Digits along an arrow sum to a two-digit number. This number is a concatenation of BOTH digits in the attached circle. For clarity: A circle with the digits {1, 9} would be surrounded by at least one copy each of the digits 1 and 9 and could have arrows that summed to either 19 or 91. Its arrows could not sum to 11 nor 99, this would require a {1, 1} circle surrounded by two 1s or a {9, 9} circle surrounded by two 9s respectively.)
3268: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by a yellow safety strip are in a 2:1 ratio (ie one is double the other.) Extend the 'gap' (ie the grey lines) along cell edges so that it forms a single loop, which cannot touch itself. Even and odd digits may not touch except across the gap. Draw a path from cell centre to cell centre from the blue dot to the red pin, which may move orthogonally or diagonally. It can't cross or touch the gap, except at yellow safety strips. Adjacent digits on the path differ by at least 3.
3269: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a black dot contain digits that are in a 1:2 ratio. Cells separated by a white dot contain consecutive digits. Neighboring digits along a green line must differ by at least 5. Neighboring digits along an orange line must differ by at least 4. A pink line contains a set of non-repeating consecutive digits in any order. Along a gray thermometer, digits must strictly increase from the bulb end. Each set of three consecutive cells along a peach entropic line must contain one low (123), one medium (456) and one high (789) digit. Box borders divide the blue region sum line into segments with the same sum. The sum of all digits that belong to one constraint type (e.g. all digits on black dots) is the same for each of the eight constraint types in this puzzle and must be deduced by the solver.
3270: Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid indicate the sum of all continuously diagonally adjacent digits with the same parity, up to (and not including) the first digit with the opposite parity along the indicated diagonal from the direction of the clue (digits may repeat if allowed by other rules).
3271: Normal sudoku rules apply. On lines, the sum of the even digits and the sum of the odd digits are almost equal - that is, they are off by one. Digits may repeat on lines if sudoku allows.
3272: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each line contains a square number reading from left to right (or in the case of the line in r3c1, from top to bottom). eg If r8c7 was a 2 then r7c8 must be a 5 (to give the square number 25). (As an aide memoire, all 2-digit squares and 3-digit squares (without zeroes or a repeated digit) are: 16, 25, 36, 49, 64, 81, 169, 196, 256, 289, 324, 361, 529, 576, 625, 729, 784, 841, 961).
3273: Place the digits 1-6 once each in every row, column, and irregular region. A clue outside the grid gives the digit that must be placed in the Nth position in that row or column, where N is the digit in the cell next to the clue.
3274: Place the digits 1-6 once each in every row, column, and irregular region. The grey regions contain the same set of digits in the same arrangement. Adjacent digits on a green line differ by at least 3. Digits on a magenta line form a non-repeating, consecutive set in any order. Digits on a grey thermometer strictly increase from bulb to tip. Digits in a cage do not repeat, and sum to the small number in the top left of the cage. A clue outside the grid gives the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. Digits either side of a white dot are consecutive. On a black dot one digit is double the other.
3275: Normal sudoku rules apply. Solid pink lines contain an unordered set of consecutive digits, without repeats. Hollow blue lines are divided by 3x3 box borders into segments with sums of equal value. Cells separated by a black dot have one digit double the other. Cells separated by a white dot have consecutive digits.
3276: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each cage contains a letter. The same letter represents the same pair of digits across the grid. Different letters must represent different pairs. The order of digits within cages does not matter.
3277: Normal sudoku rules apply. No 5 in the grid may be a chess queen's move away from another 5. Every set of 4 adjacent digits on a hollow peach line must contain a digit from each of the X-pair (ten-pair) subsets of {1,9}, {2,8}, {3,7}, and {4,6}. A 5 may not appear on a peach line. A white dot between two digits indicates that those digits are consecutive. A black dot between two digits indicates that one digit is double the other.
3278: The digit in each red cell is greater than each orthogonally adjacent neighbour in a white cell. Each digit in a blue cell is less than each orthogonally adjacent neighbour in a white cell.
3279: Divide the grid into 9 non-overlapping regions, each consisting of orthogonally connected cells. Place the digits 1–9 exactly once in each row, column, and region. A digit in a circle equals the number of distinct columns occupied by its region. There are 9 circles in total, and exactly one pair of circles share the same digit. A digit in a square equals the number of distinct rows occupied by its region. There are 9 squares in total, and exactly one pair of squares share the same digit. A digit in a diamond equals the number of distinct regions that appear anywhere in its row or column, including its own region (regions seen in both the row and column are still counted once). The sum of every circled and squared digit within a region is the same for each of the nine regions. The grid is covered in fog, placing correct digits clears the fog somewhere in the grid.
3280: Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits along a green line have a difference of at least 5. The sequence of digits along a gray line reads the same in both directions. A clue outside the grid gives the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. Digits in cells joined by a white dot are consecutive.
3281: Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a single road that travels orthogonally from cell to cell, never branching, crossing, or overlapping, and which eventually closes into a loop. The road must pass through every house. Borders marked with traffic lights are controlled intersections that the road cannot cross. The bold 3×3 borders divide the road into segments. Within each segment, all digits must be pairwise prime (that is, any two digits in the same segment share no common factor greater than 1). A digit in a house equals the length of the segment containing it, while a digit in a speed camera counts how many road cells appear in the ENTIRE row of that camera, including the camera cell itself. Note: A segment does not necessarily contain a house. Any segment of length 1 must contain the digit 1.
3282: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Draw a single route that travels orthogonally from cell to cell, never branching, crossing, or overlapping, which eventually closes into a loop. The loop must pass through every planet. Thick black borders represent black holes that the route cannot cross. A digit in a satellite dish equals the number of loop cells in the 3×3 box centred on that cell. Along the loop, one parity forces the route to turn (making a 90° angle) while the other forces it to continue straight (making a 180° angle), it is up to the solver to determine which parity corresponds to which behaviour. Any two cells that are adjacent along the loop must contain non-consecutive digits unless the loop is passing through a white dot (where consecutive digits may appear).
3283: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Draw a single electricity cable that travels orthogonally from cell to cell, never branching, crossing, or overlapping, which eventually closes into a loop. The loop must pass through every hut. Water drops mark river borders that the loop cannot cross. Any two cells that are adjacent along the loop must contain non-consecutive digits, unless the loop is passing through a white dot (where consecutive digits may appear). Any two huts directly connected by the loop form a segment (including both huts). A digit in a hut equals the length of the longest segment containing it.
3284: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits a king's move (in chess) apart must be different. Adjacent digits on a green line differ by at least 5. Digits on a purple line do not repeat and are a set of consecutive digits in any order. On a black dot, one digit is double the other. Red cells indicate the position of the cell's column number in that row, e. g. a 4 in r6c3 implies a 3 in r6c4.
3285: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells containing a grey square must contain even digits. Three adjacent cells in any direction (orthogonal or diagonal) never contain three consecutive digits in some order.
3286: Finkz must reach the cupcake by finding a path through the maze. The path must not visit any cell more than once, cross itself, or pass through any thick maze walls. As well as moving orthogonally, Finkz may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. Fill the grid with the digits 0-9. Divide the maze floor into pentomino shaped regions (groups of five orthogonally connected cells.) Every cell belongs to exactly one pentomino region. Every thick maze wall sits between two separate regions. All five cells of a region must be filled with the same digit. Regions that touch along an edge (even through a wall) may not contain the same digit, and must not be the same shaped pentomino (rotations and reflections count as the same shape.) Most of the maze is obscured with fog. Correctly filling a pentomino will clear some fog somewhere. No guessing is necessary. A purple probe is a diamond shaped device built into a wall between two neighbouring pentomino regions. The digit on the attached circle indicates the total number of cells visited within those two neighbouring regions. If a blackcurrant sits between two digits, one is double the other. If a redcurrant sits between two digits, one is odd and the other is even. If a grape sits between two digits, they have a difference of at least 5. If a goldenberry sits between two digits, they are not consecutive (or the same.) A purple arrow sits between two different digits and points towards the smaller digit. Finkz may only pass through a purple arrow in the direction it's pointing. If a floor panel is illuminated with a blue square, it lies on Finkz' path and indicates that a spike in brain activity was detected in response to that digit. Two cells visited adjacently along the path may never sum to a prime number. (Note: 0 and 1 are not prime.)
3287: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a thermometer must strictly increase from the bulb end. Additionally, the sum of the digits along a thermometer must be divisible by the number of cells the thermometer uses.
3288: Normal sudoku rules apply. Totals of orthogonally adjacent cages differ by at least 7. No two cages have the same total.
3289: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cages show their sums. Digits increase along thermos, from the bulb. The digit 1 never touches two of the same digit (including diagonally).
3290: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along (grey or red/blue) thermometers, digits increase from the bulb. Yellow circles have odd digits. Orange lines join consecutive digits.
3291: Normal sudoku rules apply. Circles contain odd digits. Each line contains a sequence of consecutive digits in any order. There is a hidden 9 cell ‘thermometer’ entirely contained in one box, along which digits increase from one end to the other. It only moves orthogonally and does not cross itself.
3292: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a pink line form a set of consecutive digits in any order. Blue/red lines are thermos, which increase, starting from the bulb. Box borders divide a grey line into segments with the same sum. The digit in a yellow circle is odd. There is a hidden thermo that begins and ends at cells α and Δ (not necessarily in that order). It only moves orthogonally, and may not cross the renban line.
3293: Normal sudoku rules apply. The two puzzles must be solved in tandem. The puzzles overlap at the Loop in R9C9 (so eg. R9C7 in North Side and R1C6 in South Side contain the same digit). All cells with an airplane contain the same digit across both puzzles. Red Line: Parity line (cells alternate in parity). Purple Line: Zipper line (digits an equal distance from the center sum to the digit in the center). Yellow Line: Nabner line (no two digits can be consecutive or identical). Blue Line: Region Sum line (box borders divide the line into segments with an equal sum). Green Line: German Whisper line (adjacent digits differ by 5 or more). Orange Line: Dutch Whisper line (adjacent digits differ by 4 or more). Brown Line: Slow thermo (moving from the bulb, each digit is the same or higher). Pink Line: Renban line (a set of consecutive digits in any order).
3294: Normal sudoku rules apply. The two puzzles must be solved in tandem. The puzzles overlap at the Loop in R9C9 (so eg. R9C7 in North Side and R1C6 in South Side contain the same digit). All cells with an airplane contain the same digit across both puzzles. Red Line: Parity line (cells alternate in parity). Purple Line: Zipper line (digits an equal distance from the center sum to the digit in the center). Yellow Line: Nabner line (no two digits can be consecutive or identical). Blue Line: Region Sum line (box borders divide the line into segments with an equal sum). Green Line: German Whisper line (adjacent digits differ by 5 or more). Orange Line: Dutch Whisper line (adjacent digits differ by 4 or more). Brown Line: Slow thermo (moving from the bulb, each digit is the same or higher). Pink Line: Renban line (a set of consecutive digits in any order).
3295: Normal sudoku rules apply. Several (invisible) killer cages are present in the grid. Digits in a cage cannot repeat, and sum to the clue in the top-left-most cell of the cage (top-most is evaluated first, followed by left-most). Cages cannot overlap. Only the number for each cage is visible, and it is up to the solver to determine the rest of the cells each cage visits. Every cage visits at least two 3x3 boxes and has an equal number of cells in each 3x3 box visited.
3296: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage must sum to the small number in the top-left corner of the cage. Adjacent digits along a rose octagon line must differ in value by at least 6.
3297: Normal sudoku rules apply. The digits along each arrow must sum to the digit in the circled cell. No digit on a golden line can be consecutive with any other digit on that line. A white dot between two cells indicates that the digits are consecutive. Not all such dots are shown.
3298: Normal sudoku rules apply. Along a line that occupies N cells, every pair of adjacent digits must have a difference of at least N. If a black dot sits between two digits, one is double the other.
3299: Normal sudoku rules apply. One cell in each row, column and box is a “doubler cell”. Doubler cells have a value equal to twice their digit. Each digit from 1 to 9 appears once in the set of doubler cells. Each grey line can be divided into one or more consecutive, non-overlapping sections each of which contains values summing to ten. Digits in a cage do not repeat. Values in a cage sum to the total in the upper left corner of the cage. Values on a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio (ie one value is double the other).
3300: Normal sudoku rules apply. Correctly placed digits clear fog from their own cell and possibly other cells – no guessing is necessary. The sum of the digits inside each cage is equal to the small number in the top left corner, and digits cannot repeat within a cage. Cage sums are in the left-most cell in the highest row reached by the cage, and all cage sums are given. Purple lines contain a non-repeating set of consecutive digits in any order. Lines do not branch or overlap.
3301: Normal sudoku rules apply. Numbers outside the grid indicate the sum of the LAST N digits, where N is the FIRST digit in the indicated row/column.
3302: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. If the digits in a cage sum to N, there are exactly N cages whose digits sum to N.
3303: Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a single knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. Digits in circles must appear in a cell that touches the circle. Digits on pink lines are consecutive.
3304: Normal sudoku rules apply. A digit in a circle equals the sum of all orthogonally adjacent cells. All circles are given.
3305: Normal sudoku rules apply. The 3x3 box borders divide blue lines into segments. The digits on each segment of the same line must sum to the same total. eg r4c9 + r5c9 + r6c9 = r7c8 + r7c9. Digits in cells joined by a yellow dot are not consecutive.
3306: Normal sudoku rules apply. The sum of the digits along an arrow is equal to the digit in the connected circle. Purple lines contain a non-repeating set of consecutive digits in any order. Along orange lines, every set of three adjacent cells contains one low digit (1-3), one middle digit (4-6), and one high digit (7-9). Digits in cells with a shaded circle are odd.
3307: Normal sudoku rules apply. All outside cells on a clue must contain a digit. That digit must also appear in the Nth position looking into the grid in the row/column, where N is the digit in the first position. The sum of the digits in the circles is equal to the sum of the digits on the attached line. Digits are allowed to repeat in the circles and on the lines as normally allowed by other rules.
3308: Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Digits in a Quadruple circle must be placed at least once in the four cells touching that circle.
3309: Normal sudoku rules apply. Box borders divide a blue line into segments with the same sum.
3310: Normal sudoku rules apply. Each digit 1-9 is depicted in this puzzle by a strange symbol. Deduce which symbol stands for which digit, and keep track using the key on the right.This grid contains numerous blob-like alien creatures, each consisting of two horizontally adjacent cells. Some blobs are shown; the others are invisible and must be located. Blobs do not overlap each other. Some blobs are clones of each other, ie: they contain the exact same two digits in the same order. A blob's left-hand digit always indicates exactly how many instances of that blob (including itself) exist in the grid. If there is a circular label in the centre of a blob, its symbol indicates the sum of the blob's two cells.
3311: Normal sudoku rules apply. No digit may appear more than once on a particular clue type. Clue types: 1) Adjacent digits on a green line differ by 5 or more; 2) Purple lines must contain a set of consecutive non-repeating digits in any order; 3) Any sequence of 3 adjacent digits along a teal line must contain a complete set of residuals modulo 3, i.e: one from (1,4,7), one from (2,5,8) and one from (3,6,9); 4) Digits along a red line must alternate between odd and even; 5) Digits may not repeat within a cage; 6) The grey circle contain an odd digit. The grey squares contain even digits. 7) Cells separated by a black dot have a 1:2 ratio (ie one is double the other); 8) Cells separated by a white dot must be consecutive.
3312: Normal sudoku rules apply. Orthogonally adjacent cells may not both contain even digits. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in its circle.
3313: Normal sudoku rules apply. Two cells connected by a green line must have a difference of at least 5. Digits on a magenta line form a set of consecutive, not-repeating digits in any order.
3314: Normal sudoku rules apply. A greater-than symbol points towards the smaller number. Draw two metro lines that travel orthogonally from cell to cell, never branching, crossing, or overlapping, either with themselves or with each other, which eventually close to form two loops. Thick black walls cannot be crossed by the lines. One loop must lie entirely inside the other, so the outer loop completely surrounds the inner loop. Every station must lie on a loop. All cells on the same loop share the same parity (the two loops may have the same or different parities). A digit in a red sensor equals the number of cells visited by either loop in the 3×3 box centred on that cell. A digit in a station equals the total number of stations containing that digit. The mirror cell has mirrored parity, meaning its parity is considered to be the opposite of its real parity. If a loop passes through it, treat the cell according to this mirrored parity.
3315: Normal sudoku rules apply. The nine marked cells contain the digits 1–9, each exactly once. If a marked cell contains the digit N, then every vertical group of N consecutive cells in its column has remainders 0, 1, ..., N−1, in some order, when its digits are divided by N. Such a group may start anywhere in the column; it does not need to contain the marked cell. For example, if a marked cell contains 4, then every four consecutive cells in its column have remainders 0, 1, 2, 3 modulo 4, in some order.
